review_text:
Dinner at I-SANG was a really nice modern Korean fine dining experience for me. Helmed by Chef @steve_ouiiii, the tasting menu reimagines Korean flavors with refined techniques, balancing tradition and contemporary finesse.

Dishes like the Perilla Oil Kal-Guksu stood out with handmade noodles, local shrimp, and nutty depth from perilla oil. The Maeun-Tang balanced chili heat with catfish and morning glory, while Ogolgye with black chicken, banana, and black garlic was as intriguing as it sounds. Even the comforting Juk felt elevated here, layered with betel leaf and jangjorim for depth.

What I enjoyed most is how every plate still carried a sense of comfort — like familiar Korean flavors reimagined with finesse. It doesn’t scream luxury for the sake of it, but quietly delivers satisfaction in a polished, modern way.

The food was very nicely thought through.  You can see that the chef has put a lot of thinking and testing with ingredients.  The chef is Korean and he was able to incorporate local ingredients into his cuisine seamlessly.  The service was great.  Overall amazing meal, the only deducted points for me was the set up.  It’s in a somewhat confusing building and rather casual.

One of the best Korean fine dining experiences, meticulous attention to detail both in food and service. Chef Steve previously opened Hansik Goo 1 star Michelin star restaurant in Hong Kong and trained at Mingles 2 star Michelin restaurant. At I-Sang he brings out his own style while paying homage to traditional Korean techniques and flavors.  We had a great dining experience for 4, the sommelier is also very knowledgeable and focused on finding the right choice for the customer rather than pushing his own preference. Thank you for a lovely evening - look forward to visiting again!

Food tastes great, very creative and a fresh take on korean food. Each dish tastes unique. Love the surprised fried chicken with sprinkles of chili on them. The service would have been better if they start serving the food faster. The first dish was served almost half an hour after we arrived. The server should also be more knowledgeable about wine and give better recommendations.

Dining at Isang felt like tasting Korean classics through a new lens — rooted in tradition, but with Thai twists that kept me curious. My favorite was the Birth (seaweed soup), one of my comfort foods from Korea, reimagined so beautifully. The stone pot rice with anchovy broth was humble yet deeply satisfying, and even the KFC came with a fun surprise. Finishing with the pandan dasik and tea was just perfect. A meal that felt both personal and refreshing.

A sophisticated dining experience with a vibrant yet elegant ambiance. The tuna and uni were truly exceptional — fresh, balanced, and beautifully presented. The carabineros, premium beef, and blue lobster showcased outstanding quality and precise execution. Service was impeccable: the team exuded warmth, enthusiasm, and professionalism, creating an atmosphere of genuine hospitality. The wine list features an impressive selection from both Italy and France, curated with care to complement the cuisine.
An excellent restaurant that combines refined flavors with heartfelt service — highly recommended.

I just had very tasty meal at this restaurant. Recommended Autumn Course (Menu as specified):

1.Scampi Tartare: Fresh scampi tartare with a delicate flavour, making for a perfect start.

2.Chesnut Gnocchi: Soft and chewy chestnut gnocchi, embodying the flavour and aroma of autumn.

3.Pasta Uni Sauce: Pasta tossed in a rich, sweet, creamy, and luxurious sea urchin (Uni) sauce.

4.Steak M5: Excellent quality M5 beef steak, meticulously grilled. The tender and succulent meat is an impressive main course, providing a superb finish to the meal.

Notes/Cautions:

You are permitted to bring an outside cake, but you are not allowed to consume it inside the restaurant.

The reservation process can be quite complicated, involving correspondence through both email and Line chat.

The staff introducing the dishes are not the chef directly. Furthermore, requests to change tables (even when the restaurant is empty) may not be accommodated.

Our beloved legendary Dusit Thani Hotel has reopened! The modern reinterpretation of the old building is simply ingenious.

Upon arrival, the security guard pointed us toward the valet parking, but after driving into the garage and back up to the entrance, there was no valet in sight. Anyway, I was here to review Cannobi Restaurant, not the parking!

The food was spectacular — both in presentation and taste. Every dish was outstanding. We had the degustation menu, seven courses of pure joy. The service was excellent, and the food was exceptional — truly worth the astronomical price.

I went there after two consecutive birthday dinners at The Normandie Grill at the Mandarin Oriental, and I must say, Cannobi definitely outshined the MO!

We had a wonderfully memorable experience at Cannubi by Umberto Bombana.

The small wine bar and lounge on the upper floor is an excellent place to begin your evening. Their signature cocktails are superb, and the atmosphere truly elevates the mood.

The tasting menu is exceptionally well-curated. If you're a party of two, ordering different options allows you to sample a wider array of dishes.
We reviewed the lunch set menu and found it less appealing, so we definitely opted for dinner.

The wine pairing was a particular highlight. The sommelier expertly selected excellent wines to complement our meal. There was one minor issue: we initially ordered five wine pairings but only received three courses. However, because we chose different dishes, we ended up with distinct wines accompanying each plate, allowing us to taste a wider variety. We also ordered some sweet wine to pair with our desserts. Our final bill correctly reflected charges for three wine pairing courses.

Service-wise, the staff was attentive and good, though there's still some room for improvement.

Overall, we were very satisfied with every aspect of our visit. We will definitely return to explore the à la carte menu.

Very impressed with the atmosphere and service; each table has its own privacy and staffs are very attentive. Great lunch course with reasonable price. Went to celebrate my birthday and the resto have me a very beautiful bouquet. One comment is that it’s unfortunate you are not allowed to eat outside birthday cakes on premise (should allow since there must be many people coming here to celebrate their birthdays) but you are allowed to have them on the table for phototaking and appreciation. That aside I had a great time.

Birthday Dinner | Oct 15

We chose Duet, The Ritz-Carlton Bangkok for my birthday dinner -the newest luxury hotel in town, and I’ve always loved The Ritz-Carlton.

Duet by David Toutain is truly a masterpiece — Michelin-star artistry you can taste and feel. Every dish tells a story, melts in your mouth, and turns dining into a form of art. Worth the visit, every single bite.

The staff were charming, attentive, and beautifully trained  and yes, all good-looking! 😄

I tried Duet by David Toutain — a new fine dining gem of The Ritz-Carlton Bangkok — offers an elevated French dining experience in an elegant glasshouse overlooking lush Lumpini Park. Come around sunset and you’ll get a stunning golden-hour view to go with your meal.

I tried the Summer Inspiration series, which was heavy on vegetables but surprisingly rich and indulgent — exactly how I love. Every course was thoughtfully composed, with seasonal ingredients transformed into dishes full of depth and flavor. I’m definitely coming back next season!

Refined, Seasonal Dining at Its Best

Had an amazing set dinner at Duet by David Toutain—an unforgettable experience from start to finish. The ambiance is elegant and upscale, with a refined but warm atmosphere that perfectly complements the food. Service was absolutely top-tier—attentive, knowledgeable, and welcoming without being stiff.

The menu is deeply seasonal and beautifully thought out, with locally sourced ingredients elevated through modern French technique. Every dish felt like a story told through flavor and texture.

Some highlights from the set:
A delicate smoked red bell pepper bite, a bright and refreshing watercress starter, and a crispy onion tart inspired by pissaladière. Loved the tomato, crab, and burrata dish—so fresh and complex. The Gambero Rosso with sweet corn was a beautiful harmony of land and sea, while the zucchini with yuzu kosho and pistachio was subtle but deeply flavorful.

Other standouts: green beans with smoky sardine and rosemary, rich artichoke with bone marrow, and a perfectly cooked fish course with fennel and black olives. The main—French pork with girolles and zucchini flower—was earthy, juicy, and incredibly balanced.

Dessert was light yet memorable: pomelo and spruce, a surprising but refreshing end to an exquisite meal.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for a fine dining experience in Bangkok that’s both inventive and rooted in quality. Would return in a heartbeat.

had the pleasure of experiencing “The Art of Two” at DUET, The Ritz-Carlton Bangkok—an exclusive collaboration between Chef David Toutain and Chef Valentin Fouache. This eight-course tasting menu explored the harmony of nature, memory, and technique in a truly elevated gastronomic journey.

Each dish was thoughtfully composed, with a modern, earthy elegance that reflected both chefs’ philosophies. Highlights included the vibrant Provence Green Asparagus with pistachio and lovage, a poetic Ostra regal oyster amuse-bouche, and a stunning pigeon with purple artichoke and black olives—each beautifully plated and rich in character.

The wine pairings, curated by The Wine Merchant, were exceptional and seamlessly matched the rhythm of the courses

Service was flawless—attentive, warm, and genuinely passionate. Every detail was looked after with care, creating a refined and welcoming atmosphere.

Impeccable service, and quality curated menu.

This is a rather late posting as the dinner was back in January during Ritz-Carlton's official opening night. Had the privilege of dining at Duet, and icing on the cake was meeting Chef Toutain himself who flew in from France to do the final checks, crossing the Ts and dotting the Is.

The curated menu was of high standards, with plating and table side presentations well prepared. Service was not just attentive, but warm and engaging. The staffs actively strike up conversations and you can feel they genuinely wanted to engage you.

Love the little cards which are presented on the table to introduce the key herb used in each dish. The main dining room, which is designed as a glasshouse, truly set a beautiful dining ambience.

Super authentic Southern Thai food bursting with flavor! The dishes are rich, spicy, and true to tradition. Love the balance between the lush garden seating and cool air-conditioned indoor area—great for any weather. Friendly service and cozy vibes make it a perfect hidden gem. Definitely worth a visit if you’re craving real Southern Thai cuisine in a relaxed, beautiful setting.

This restaurant is located in a residential area and is always busy, so be prepared to wait a little for a table. We love the variety of shrimp dishes here! This time, we had coconut curry with shrimp and rice, as well as a papaya salad with shrimp egg.

For drinks, we enjoyed fresh coconut water and a large Heineken beer. As always, both dishes tasted absolutely delicious. The service was very attentive, and the restaurant’s atmosphere is also quite nice.

We will definitely come back again!

My FAV spot for southern thai food

food is spicy and packed with flavors. The seafood is a must to order (shrimp!). I eat the same thing every time I come back here. The atmosphere is pretty nice too if it’s not hot, you can sit outside with greens. Dessert was also great especially the coconut milk pudding. Although, no parking is available so you will have to park by the street and might be difficult on the weekend. Lots of ppl on the weekend too.

Highly recommended!!!!!
The food here is incredibly authentic and uses high-quality ingredients. The service is also commendable. While it may be a bit of a trek to get here, the experience is definitely worth it!

Worthy southern food in Bangkok!

Here is a reasonable price, especially for the shrimp menu. The taste is hot and strong like the southern character.

I like fried sun-dried squid, Yellow soup, fried shrimp with Kapi, and fried sea bass. Everything I order here, I do not regret.

At the restaurant, there are outdoor and AC zones. If you wish any specific, please make a reservation in advance. Sometimes I still see people in line up.

One of the best Tom Yum Noodle gem near Charoenrat Road. Opened in 2024, Jek Tod has quickly become a local favorite among noodle lovers seeking bold, pork-driven flavors in Bangkok’s Charoenrat area. This humble shop serves one of the most satisfying bowls of tom yum noodles in town; fiery, fragrant, and deeply umami without being overly greasy. The broth balances spiciness, tang, and a hint of sweetness, perfectly coating every strand of chewy egg noodles.

The highlight here is the generous use of premium pork cuts - from minced pork and boiled sweet pork to homemade pork balls, all adding texture and richness to each spoonful. For an upgrade, add an onsen egg; its silky yolk melds into the noodles, creating an extra layer of creaminess that elevates the dish beautifully. I recommend flat egg noodle for ultimate experience.

Despite its casual setup, service is quick and friendly, with a crowd that ranges from office workers to late-lunch foodies. Prices are fair, portions are hearty, and the aroma alone could stop traffic literally. Just be cautious if you park along the street; the police often patrol the area. Still, for a soul-warming bowl of tom yum noodles, Jek Tod is absolutely worth the trip and the ticket risk.

Ordered the dry Tom Yum noodles and the minced pork in plum soup — both were absolutely delicious! The Tom Yum was quite spicy, so if you’re sensitive to heat, make sure to ask for a milder version. Can’t wait to come back!

Just had lunch at this casual eatery called Jek Tod, the food is very fresh and tasty (aroi makk)! Had the soy sauce pork with minced meat balls and rice, plum soup with minced meat and the rice noodles with soy sauce pork, pork balls and minced meat balls! Do stop by and have a try, you wont be disappointed! Highly recommended!

As a Tom Yum noodle lover, I have mixed feelings about this place.

I ordered 2 Tom Yum soups, one with noodles and one without. Both had top-tier ingredients, the meatballs were some of the best I've ever had. It would have been a 5 star experience for sure, but the soups were different. The one without noodles was really, really sour, while the one with noodles was perfect. That made a big difference for me. The dried rice porridge was above average, with perfectly cooked ingredients.

Noodles lover, ranked this place as one of my favorites. A special menu  is really good. Not only noodles are good but dried rice porridge so nice. Taste and meats so great and along together. Thr offal, intestine or liver no bad smell.

The food is truly something special — authentic Thai flavors but presented in such a thoughtful way. Every dish in the set menu was perfectly balanced; highlights for me were the crab curry with pickled bamboo shoots and the crispy fried fish with fish sauce.

You can tell a lot of love and preparation goes into the cooking here, and it feels like recipes passed down through generations. The atmosphere is warm and intimate, which made the evening even more enjoyable. It’s definitely not a place for walk-ins, but that makes it even more unique — everything is prepared fresh for the group.

Worth every baht, and I’d happily come back again with family or close friends. Highly recommended if you want to experience Thai food that’s both comforting and elevated.

Foong, a newly opened Thai restaurant in Thonglor Soi 19, offers a vintage-inspired setting that complements its traditional Thai recipes. The restaurant serves an 8-person Thai set menu (9,900 THB, reservation only) with a carefully curated selection of dishes.

Highlights include Foong Miang (a twist on miang kham with fish and toasted rice), fruit salad with fermented shrimp paste, stir-fried jackfruit with crispy chicken skin, and crispy salted fish rice salad. Mains feature chu chee soft-shell fish, southern-style crab & roe curry, and sweet garlic squid stir-fry. For dessert, sago pearls in fresh coconut milk provide a perfect sweet finish.

The intimate setting and well-executed dishes make it a great spot for those looking for an elevated Thai dining experience.

Foong offers a cozy, family-style Thai dining experience in a warm, inviting setting. The food is good and comforting, but not particularly memorable—I expected a bit more given the hype.

Service was friendly but a bit confused at times, which took away from the overall flow. If you’re after a casual, homey meal with a group, it’s a decent choice, but don’t expect to be blown away.

Foong is a charming Thai restaurant offering authentic home-cooked dishes in a warm and welcoming atmosphere. Parking can be a bit tricky—once the spots in front of the restaurant are full, you’ll need to park at a rental lot further away. Thankfully, the restaurant provides a shuttle service to and from the parking area. On the day I visited, it was pouring rain, which made getting to the restaurant a bit of a challenge.

The meal is served as a set, featuring around 10 traditional Thai dishes. The flavors are bold, rich, and authentically Thai, with high-quality, fresh ingredients. Each dish is crafted with care, making it a must-visit for anyone who loves authentic Thai cuisine.

If you’re looking for a delicious and satisfying Thai dining experience, Foong is a place you shouldn’t miss!

Baan Suan Aromdee is a true gem! This intimate, home-style restaurant, with limited tables, truly captures the essence of Thai home cooking. Reservations are highly recommended. They offer a set menu, but are wonderfully accommodating to dietary preferences – just communicate your needs.
While slightly pricier than your average Thai eatery, the exceptional quality and variety of dishes justify every baht. Expect fresh, vibrant flavors that taste like they came straight from a family kitchen.
Parking is limited to two cars; however, they kindly suggest a nearby larger parking lot and offer a pick-up service or a short walk. The warmth and hospitality are truly unmatched. This is a must-try for authentic, heartfelt Thai cuisine.

Old thai style food. Very good vibe Food is small portions but very good test. It a bit far from town. You need to come by car. Price is Mid to high price class. Have a lot of old traditions thai food that you can’t find elsewhere in this time.
Beautiful setting in a restored Thai wooden house.  Good selection of carefully prepared Thai dishes.  Wait staff are very attentive.

⸻

Poon Daeng Kaeng Ron
This place feels homestyle, but the flavors are anything but ordinary 🌶️🍲
The curries live up to the name—steaming hot, bold, and full of spice. Every bite tastes like sitting down for a family meal in a bustling Bangkok evening market.

The food is straightforward Thai classics—red curry, green curry, stir-fries—but each dish is rich, layered, and generous with herbs and spice. Nothing watered down, everything full-on, just like a market cook who never skimps on ingredients 🥘🔥

Prices are friendly, the kind that make you feel full and satisfied without thinking twice. Perfect spot whether you come with friends, family, or even solo for a comforting meal.

Bottom line: If you’re craving hot rice with real-deal Thai curries, this place will not let you down 🙌
A hidden Gem. Food is delicious. Price little over  average, but taste speek for itself. The place has very charming atmosphere with good attentive service. Highly recommended.
Love the vibe feeling so homies. The food is great prices are reasonable too

Actually 5 stars for the service. We were one of the last tables and they were very kind to us, offering free soup.

The bitterness of the raw buffalo was not my style but I know it fits the palate of local people. Reasonable prices of around 50 THB per laab plate.

If you want a real THAI CUISINE with 100% taste really good by Thai standard, please come and try to dine here!

It was a great culinary experience, unique and reflects the Thai culture especially with the Larb, just wow! There are some dishes that we will never forget the taste. There is no vegetarian option but if you are a meat lover or somehow a pescetarian like me (they have fish options), this is a good place to go. The vibe of the place is also cozy and would be perfect to dine in with family. All good!

tasty food however papaya salad was not so impressive as the papaya was too ripe. service was attentive. for atmosphere, many people come here to drink so the noise was a bit loud. they charge ฿20 per pax for ac room fee

Good northern (and northeastern) style food. Crowded during typical mealtime and you might have to wait for some dishes that need to be slowly cooked, e.g. grilled meat. But overall, serving waiting time is ok.

Very spicy and tasty Northern style dishes. Recommend to those who are not compromising with authentic spicy local food. Larb Khua (stir-fried mince pork with spices and herbs) is the must. Others are also good. Don’t forget to eat together with steamed sticky rice.

Very good atmosphere. Food was amazing, we just arrived 45 minutes before closing and the staff kindly served us!
Food has quality and price is completely fair.
Must try their craft beers if you are into.
Make sure to ask for normal spicy in case you do not like it, otherwise, go for Thai spicy 😉

Wow - better tasting Thai food than most hotels, which tends to water down Thai flavors for fear tourists can’t handle real Thai food.  We’ve been to Thailand for over 20 years and the Thai food here is as good as any good Thai restaurants in Bangkok!  They got a really good chef here - some of our fav dishes are the tom yum shrimp soup, the fried turmeric fish & the sliced beef over flavored steamed rice.
The restaurant is in the lobby of the cool & modern ASAI boutique hotel (a Dusit brand/property, barely 5 minutes walk from the Saint Louis BTS skytrain station.
Staff (Khun Guide, Elle, & Nae Nae were great) speak English well & are welcoming & friendly/helpful. We’ll be back!

A clean and cosy boutique hotel that is value for your money. The breakfast is delicious and I especially like the Crispy Chicken & Egg set and the Chicken Boiled Rice. The staff is friendly and helpful. The room is well maintained and kept clean and tidy. Overall a good experience if you intend to have an affordable and nice accommodation for your stay in Bangkok.

Fantastic restaurant. We loved att he food we tried (Massamam beef, turmeric seabass, thai ice tea, mango sticky rice). But what makes this place so amazing is the friendly, attentionate and genuinely nice staff. We visited with our 2-year old and felt very welcome and had an amazing meal.

Love the cooking experience hosted here at Asai. The chef Knot and supervisor Guide are both very friendly and informative about Thai cooking and culture. Highly recommended for cooking enthusiats or someone who just wanna get some hands on activity. Good past time for a hot or rainy afternoon.
Excellent Boat Noodles. Must order the grilled pork/beef balls and chives .

The unique boat noodle restaurant is hidden in the small alley under the big tree next to the canal. The restaurant has a small parking lot around the house, which can pack up to 10-15 spots. The atmosphere overall was nice and homey. The boat noodle (both soup and dry) are just perfect. The grilled pork ball and the sauce are a good appetizer too. Overall 5 stars great place to visit !!!

It was fun! We were the only foreigners but the owners made sure we were welcomed. They gave us a number and waited around 40 minutes. In total we ordered 1 passion fruit juice, 1 water, 6 noodles bowl (3 pork, 2 beer and 1 dried noodles). We received 4 and were all beef 😂 Bless them 🫶 The noodle were amazing and the beef was soooo good but we wanted to try the pork. We ordered again one pork and one dry noodle and only received the dry noodles 🙈 It was good but again no pork 😂 Anyway, the food is delicious regardless if we revived our order or not. The only thing is that the drink took way longer and received it when we finished to eat. For the rest it was good. 20thb per bowl!
Like the taste even though not that very authentic. Good ambient. Parking is okay. The plus is the sweet menu.
It was good about beef noodles and reasonable price but the meatball not much recommend.

If you're craving Pad Thai in Udon Thani, this spot is a must-try. Despite limited parking, it's worth the hassle. It's an outdoor place.

Open every day, it's convenient for any schedule. The highlight? Their Pad Thai is top-notch, with a variety of choices to suit every palate. What sets it apart is the ability to customize your dish to perfection. Whether you prefer it spicy, loaded with veggies, or with extra protein, they've got you covered. The flavors are authentic, leaving you satisfied with every bite. The ambiance adds to the experience, making it perfect for a casual lunch or dinner outing. However, be prepared for potential parking challenges, especially during peak hours.

Despite this drawback, the quality of the food makes it a go-to spot for Pad Thai enthusiasts in the area. Overall, if you're in Udon Thani and craving delicious Pad Thai with options galore, this place won't disappoint.

Was blown away by the affordable pricing, quality, portion and taste. Usually would not find this kind of portion at this price in Bangkok.  Highly recommended.

Limited street side parking for cars.

Pad Thai บัวแดง is a fantastic restaurant located on the main road, making it very convenient to find. If you’re a fan of Pad Thai, this place is a must-visit. The restaurant offers a wide variety of delicious Pad Thai dishes that are sure to satisfy your taste buds. You can choose from different types of meat, including shrimp, scallop, fish, grilled pork, crispy pork, and beef. This variety ensures that there’s something for everyone, no matter what your preferences are.

One of the best things about Pad Thai บัวแดง is the 10% discount they offer to students. If you have a student ID, make sure to bring it along to enjoy this special offer. This makes the restaurant an excellent choice for students looking for a great meal at a reasonable price.

When it comes to drinks, Pad Thai บัวแดง offers free water, which is a nice touch. You don’t have to worry about extra charges for your drink, and you can stay hydrated while enjoying your meal.

The restaurant accepts both cash and cashless payments, making it very convenient for customers. Whether you prefer to pay with cash, credit card, or another cashless method, Pad Thai บัวแดง has got you covered. This flexibility is a big plus in today’s increasingly cashless society.

Another important aspect of any restaurant is the cleanliness and quality of its facilities. Pad Thai บัวแดง has a good toilet, which is clean and well-maintained. This attention to hygiene and comfort adds to the overall positive experience of dining at this restaurant.

In summary, Pad Thai บัวแดง is an excellent choice if you’re looking for tasty Pad Thai on the main road. With a variety of meat options, a student discount, free water, and flexible payment options, it’s a convenient and affordable place to enjoy a meal. The clean and well-maintained toilet is an added bonus that enhances the overall dining experience. Whether you’re a student, a local, or just passing through, Pad Thai บัวแดง is definitely worth a visit.
Tasty Pad thai! They have 3 sizes, the regular, extra for 10 baht and jumbo for 20 baht.

Taste was good and original with the flavor of the noodles fried in a wok and not greasy and a touch of lime and lemon. Great taste at 80 baht per plate. I ordered prawn and another pork. It is authentic Thai without adding sweetener.

2nd time here and never disappointed.
A bit spicy but you can tell them for step you can take.
Brought my expat friend here and they loved it! They can enjoyed watching chef cooking on open kitchen. Fusion Thai dishes like the appetizer here are unique and flavorful.
My fav dish this time is grilled pork neck.

RARK is an absolute gem! Every dish here is a testament to quality and freshness. The ingredients are clearly top-notch, and the flavors are incredible - perfectly balanced, making every dish a standout. The chef's dedication to using fresh, high-quality ingredients shines through, transforming classic Thai recipes into something truly memorable.

The service is warm and welcoming. The staff and chef go above and beyond to make you feel at home, adding a personal touch that makes the experience even more enjoyable. If you're looking for a Thai restaurant that delivers both exceptional food and friendly, attentive service, RARK should be at the top of your list. Highly recommended!

Home-cooked Thai restaurant that captures the taste of childhood. The taste is like eating in the past and the seasonings are not lacking. Ranjuan curry that I miss the salty and sour taste of pork and beef. Overnight sour curry with a strong taste, very delicious soft vegetables and tender pork. Traditional glass noodle salad with crispy dried shrimp and peanuts for contrasting tastes. It is a good food experience. The shop is cute like eating at a friend's house and a friendly work team. I would like to come and eat more often.

Really enjoyed my meal here. Much more intimate vibes than some of the ‘nicer’ Michelin restaurants, but just as good if not better cooking and ingredients going on here. Would absolutely recommend this restaurant and return on my next visit.

Honestly, compared to how difficult it is to get the table, I expect more. However many dishes totally got me! The beef curry was so beautiful and very tasty, the scallops on curry curd also very good 👍 Most of all, Chicken salad with rose apple was a bless 🤩
The two chefs did a good job overall. So if you are able to get a table, do not hesitate to come ☺️

Such a lovely experience! The restaurant has a wonderfully homey and cozy atmosphere. The food is not only delicious but also beautifully plated — very photogenic!
We really enjoyed the vibe in the evening. Great taste and great setting.

Been here three times, and incredible every time. The ingredients are so fresh and perfectly cooked. The atmosphere is amazing..a beautiful traditional Thai wooden house. And the owners give us such a warm welcome. It truly feels like you’re dining at a friend’s home. Highly recommended!

What a truly special evening!

A magical place that enchants not only with its atmosphere but with the love poured into every detail. The kitchen is outstanding – guided by two wonderful people and a lovely team who clearly do what they love.

Each dish was a culinary delight, full of heart, creativity, and perfectly balanced flavors. As a guest, you can truly feel the passion behind it all – in the food, the service, and the unique ambiance of the place.

We wholeheartedly recommend it – visiting this little gem should be a must!

Thank you so much, Chanan & team, for such an unforgettable evening!

AMAZING! MUST GO! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
This is such a special place - truly a hidden gem. A light spot on a dark road.
Nestled in a cute little garden with fairy lights, is an intimate restaurant. Reservation only. We were two of only 14 dinner guests that night. Three groups there total.
Menu is set by the kitchen based on seasonal ingredients and catches of the day, so it's a lovely surprise! About 800 baht per person and totally worth it.
Started with the house cocktail - Passion Maree (rum and passionfruit - yum!).
The crab and water chestnut crab cakes wrapped in bean curd were AMAZING. The mangosteen and prawn salad was INSANE. The grilled fish in banana leaf was tasty and the fried Mexican kale was delicious. Squid with the ink was funky and sooo tender and delicious! Sagot to end was warm and lovely.
Each dish is made and served with care. The owner speaks perfect English (he is Thai) and explained each dish and the origin of all the ingredients, most local or from a region in Thailand. There were mosquitoes but a fan, repellent and even an electric racket are provided!
It was such a beautiful dining experience and I highly recommend it to anyone going through Koh Phangan!!!

No booking, no eat! Love the concept of the restaurant where they locally source ingredients daily. No fixed menu nor fixed price. Heard the place it’s super busy everyday. Especially during high-season. We were just lucky to get to dine at the place this trip. Highly recommended ☺️
Great place for northern style food. The service was fast and the restaurant was clean. Good price.

This is a great place to have lunch or dinner.  The staff were very pleasant, the food delicious, and the ambience is peaceful and calm/quiet which I loved. It has a very traditional feel, and the prices are reasonable. Will go back again.

A must visit while in Chiang Mai - you can try an extensive range of authentic northern Thai food. The restaurant is air-conditioned and quite comfortable. There is a lot to choose from on the menu. I particularly like the sticky rice with chilli paste, pickled vegetable, and meat of you choice. The pork in lemongrass is so tender it falls apart. There's 2 types of hung lay, as well as assorted chicken dishes. The flavours blow the tastebuds away - so delicious. For the 2 of us we order 3 dishes plus rice (sticky or steamed is available). Good range of non-alcoholic drinks, as well as alcohol. The restaurant is near the Cultural Centre, separate from where the kantok dinner is held. We've not had problems parking our motorbike, but noticed that on nights when the kantok dinner is busy the parking lot has a lot of tour buses. Definitely worth a visit so you can try authentic northern Thai food.

Great lunch
It’s definitely authentic northern food
The service was excellent and the atmosphere is very elegant and friendly.
Definitely worth a try for authentic food

A nice little old-style northern restaurant. The food is very tasty (for Thai people). However, the staff are not always on-site when I visit, so I need to call them to place an order, especially since there aren’t many customers around 4 PM.

Recommend the Laarb and แกงคั่วหอย

We had the chance to enjoy a rare traditional Thai menu, the kind that is hard to find these days. We didn’t book in advance, but luckily a table was available, so the chef prepared a special set menu for us.

The flavors reflected authentic Central Thai cuisine—slightly on the sweet side, yet perfectly balanced and harmonious. Every dish felt natural and wholesome, crafted with quality ingredients and without unnecessary additives.

The chef shared the stories and details behind each dish in such an engaging way that it made the dining experience even more special. At 950 THB per person, the price felt reasonable, especially given the generous portions. We couldn’t finish everything, so we even got to take some home.

5/5 what a fantastic meal - totally the highlight of my Thailand trip. Seasonal & local ingredients packed with flavors. Chef is very amicable. Good vibe, good service. Unlike other places with pretentious “set menu”, Chawee won’t left you go without eating too much…with super reasonable price

Great hidden gem in Chiang Mai. We had the restaurant choose the dishes for us and everything was delicious. You have to pay the whole amount at the time of booking but this is understandable given they only have 3-4 tables. Will surely return!

I had a fantastic time visiting Chawee.
It had a very laid back, retro feel,  as if you're dining in someone's (very stylish) home with a great sound track adding to the relaxed vibe.

The food was incredible. I encountered a tasting menu, I tried  various dishes, things i wouldn't have thought to order, it was an education. The dishes were prepared with love and cooked to perfection, incredibly fresh food and produce.

I asked Tan (the owner) about the food preparation and where the ideas for dishes came from. I was told these dishes were inspired from family recipes and made with ingredients bought that morning,fresh and local in season and cooked that day- and it shows. Incredible flavours and spices. Great wine selection too, I had red wine -shiraz which absolutely complimented my meal. A complete taste sensation.

I urge you, whenever you visit chiang mai, your visit is incomplate without a visit to Chawee. Thank you Tan / Chawee!

Chawee is a small restaurant located along Chang Phueak Road in Chiang Mai. It offers modern Thai cuisine that meticulously blends flavors from various regions into perfectly balanced Thai dishes. Each menu item is delicious, featuring dishes like Kai Palo (braised eggs in sweet soy sauce), traditional Moo Satay (grilled marinated pork skewers), and Khao Tang (crispy rice crackers). Before each dish is served, the chef shares its story, adding a unique touch to the dining experience. The restaurant's ambiance is cozy and inviting, with warm hospitality from the owner and staff, ensuring excellent service.
In summary, **this is a must-visit restaurant!** Reservations are highly recommended, and it’s best to select your menu choices in advance.

I first visited Bo.Lan in 2016, and ever since, it has been a must-stop whenever I’m in Bangkok. I often dined there with local friends—many of whom hailed it as the best Thai food they had ever tasted. The only time I missed a visit was in 2017, the year Bo.Lan received its Michelin star—reservations were simply impossible to get.

Then came COVID-19, and with it, a long pause in travel. It’s been years since I last stepped into Bo.Lan.

Returning now, I find that Bo.Lan has transformed—beautifully and meaningfully. Before the pandemic, Bo.Lan was focused on gastronomical experience, offering a deep dive into the refined traditions of Thai cuisine. Today, Bo.Lan brings forward the taste of home, the flavour of love, and a genuine passion for food—all shaped by resilience through challenge and change.

There are many fine dining restaurants that can impress with technique and presentation. But few, if any, serve food that so clearly speaks of identity, conviction, and heart. Dining at Bo.Lan today is not just a meal—it’s a journey, a reflection of life’s own complexities and joys.

Huge respect to Chef Bo and Chef Dylan.

I’ll most certainly be back.

First off this should be six stars.  This is one of my top tier restaurant of all time.  I’ve been coming here since my first visit to Thailand almost ten years ago and if I’m in the country I AM GOING HERE.  I haven’t met Bo but have met Dylan on multiple occasions and he’s always been absolutely fantastic to me and my company.  The staff is all impeccable.

I’ve rarely had the same meal twice but old favorites do show up from time to time and they are always welcome.  It just keeps getting better and better over the years.

Just a warning, it is spicy.  But Never to the point where I feel it’s a detriment to the flavor, it’s always just an enhancement to the complex flavors.

I beleive they told me they changed the menu every 3 months?   I only wish I could come for every single one. ❤️❤️❤️

We were so excited to have the opportunity to experience Bo.Lan, which is truly wonderful in every way! We’d planned to come about 5 years ago, but weren’t able to make the trip due to the pandemic. The food is delicious (portions are fairly generous, so come hungry and pace yourself!), service is spectacular, and ambiance is perfect. Highly recommend!

Bo.lan is one of the most authentic fine-dining Thai experiences in Bangkok. Every dish reflects deep respect for Thai traditions — bold spices, complex herbs, and perfectly balanced textures. The restaurant focuses on sustainability and locally sourced ingredients, which makes every bite feel honest and pure. The tasting menu takes you on a culinary journey through Thailand. Service is warm yet sophisticated. A must for serious food lovers.

Very expensive (4,800 + 17% service charge & VAT ~ 5,600 per person)... But then the place is busy so can't blame them for charging what they can.
The building is amazing, really nice decor making for a nice ambience.
They only do a tasting menu so tried a huge variety of Thai (mainly isaan derived) dishes but couldn't honestly pick one out as being that great which is disappointing at this price point. You could find nicer tasting examples of each dish at a random food stall anywhere in BKK...  But the place is selling the whole dining experience etc so unfair comparison I guess...
Reading more online afterwards, I'm guessing the place is living off it's Netflix appearances and Michelin stars which were presumably gained through saying the right stuff about sustainability, environment etc

Couldn't honestly recommend it but at the same time, there's obviously a market for this kind of place because it's 5k per person and seems busy...

restaurant_name: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling)
review_text:
Great Desserts, Average Ice Cream
Khanom Mo Kaeng Mae Yai is highly recommended for its traditional Thai desserts. They are delicious, with just the right level of sweetness that isn't overpowering. The signature Khanom Mo Kaeng itself is a definite highlight and lives up to its reputation.
However, the ice cream available here is quite average and not particularly outstanding.
In summary, visit Khanom Mo Kaeng Mae Yai for the excellent Thai sweets, but the ice cream is just so-so.

restaurant_name: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling)
review_text:
Located near Ayutthaya’s famous floating market, Khunom Mo Kaeng Mae Yai is widely celebrated for its charming, nostalgic take on traditional Thai sweets. The shop doubles as both a café and a souvenir haven, making it a perfect stop for dessert lovers and gift hunters alike.

•	Khunom Mo Kaeng (Thai custard) comes in classic flavors like egg, taro, and mung bean, priced around ฿60. The texture is smooth and rich, not overly sweet—perfectly balanced with aromatic coconut and subtle palm sugar  ￼.
•	The vendor also serves a variety of other Thai desserts including bua loi (rice dumplings), sankhaya (taro custard), sticky rice with toppings, and more. According to one review:
“We tried the custard pots, bua loi, and taro sankhaya—each was pleasantly sweet without being cloying. Absolutely recommend the bua loi!”

Will recommend this place for first time Thai Khamin for everyone.

restaurant_name: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling)
review_text: There were variety of Thai desserts. You could select for having in the shop or takeaway. It was nice decorating and cozy place. The parking lot was available.

restaurant_name: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling)
review_text: The mango and sticky rice is delicious. The sticky rice has the perfect flavor combo of sweet and savory.  The rice texture has a nice crisp and when combined with the mango, you are gifted a paradise for the tongue.

restaurant_name: Khanom Mho Kaeng Mae Yai (Phai Ling)
review_text:
Driving around in Ayuthaya Thailand, came across this amazing shop selling Thai sweets. Most of these would have been made in Thailand, for at least a century. The history of such Thai delicacies reveals that,  many of them originated in the royal palaces. Those were the days when food including Thai sweets, were supposed to taste and look good. Times have changed but back in the old days, it was only natural colors from leaves and flowers that were used.

The shop had a kitchen next door, an open air place to sit down and relish your Thai sweets. Also at the same place, an air conditioned coffee and cold beverage shop. All these belong to the same owner.

Amazing traditional Thai food. Wish I discovered this place earlier in my stay. The food is fresh, full of flavour and at a reasonable price. I highly recommend the cashew chicken . We also had the sea bass with sweet and sour sauce and the papaya salad which were both really good.

Had lunch there every day while we stayed nearby. The food was sooooooo good and we tried different dishes every time. Each dish is about 100-180THB, portion is big. We ordered 2 dishes each - food was that good!
They also adjusted the spicy level, perfect yam won sen and tom yum without burning my mouth! Everyone where was so nice, definitely recommend!!!
Very nice place with great food and wonderful service. Would highly recommend. I ordered the crispy pork with salt and chilli which was very tasty with great crispy pork skin.
This is a very excellent Thai restaurant. I recommend you to come and eat at this restaurant. The food tastes good and the staff are friendly.

Amazing food! The best fresh fried fish we had in all our trip in Thailand!! Best papaya salad too.. kids friendly! the staff is amazing, good quality of food in fair prices. we came almost every day to eat there.. we sure will come again!

Beautiful place, good service, chefs know what they are doing. Unfortunately for us the Isan chocolate beef dry age wasn't available tonight but only fresh, the taste was good but I will try again when the dry age come back should be more interesting! Tasty squid very tender.
The dry age duck was banging definitely on my top 10 of the dishes I had in Thailand ! Well done guys, keep rocking, learning and enjoying your job and you'll be the best place in town.
Top end view and food. A skillful chef has taken some Isaan standards and done amazing things. Beef, duck and squid are all amazing. Our staff Gift and Bill were knowledgeable and super helpful.
Perfect food and service, great ambience.  If you only have steak on occasion, this is one of the best.  Located on the 27th floor of the Ad Lib hotel.  The upstairs cocktail lounge is great as well.
The food itself is nice but there are not much options to order.
You'll be greeted with Unbelievable service, along with a gorgeous view to enjoy delicious food and drinks! Perfect for a romantic evening!

Exceptional omakase experience with well paced courses, each accompanied by Chef Tiago's commentary on ingredient origins, seasonal availability, and preparation techniques.

The menu showcased highly seasonal and quality sourced ingredients.

The staff was attentive, smoothly clearing plates and refilling drinks, and their attention to detail complemented the intimate, relaxed atmosphere.

Every aspect of the space had a story, from the selection of fish to the type of wasabi sourced, the use of raw sanded wood for the counterspace, and the wabi-sabi style plating. The chef really showed how much he cares about his craft which led to an enjoyable experience. (He really knows a LOT about the dishes, history, techniques, which is really great for people that appreciate this aspect as well as the dining experience)

A new omakase restaurant just opened in Bangkok, run by a foreign chef. Even though he’s not Japanese, the sushi he makes is really interesting and tastes amazing.

Sitting at the counter watching the chef work is a whole experience—you get to take in the sights, smells, flavors, and even the sounds.

The ingredients are top-notch. I was impressed from the very first bite. Each piece is crafted with care and comes with a good variety of flavors. The sushi leans toward bold, well-seasoned tastes.

Personally, I loved the strong flavors at the beginning, but by the end, it started to feel a bit salty. And the dessert made with sake lees didn’t really hit the spot for me—just not quite to my taste.

The small course is just the right amount for me—not too much, not too little.
Service was great—attentive and friendly.

The chef here is Portuguese, but his skills are just like those of a true Japanese chef. I really love, especially the rice, which comes in two different colors. Red vinegar rice is paired perfectly with Akami. The fresh wasabi at this place is absolutely amazing. It makes every piece of sushi delicious. It’s creamy, fragrant, and has just the right amount of spiciness. Truly outstanding!

The chef is Portuguese, but he has deep respect for Japanese sushi and culture. He explains the background and story of each ingredient and fish in English, which made me feel that he understands Japanese culture even more than some Japanese chefs.

For the omakase course, you can enjoy several types of nigiri. All of them were incredibly delicious, and both my friend and I were very satisfied.

Among the sushi, I especially loved the akami, uni, negitoro maki, and kohada. They also served awabi as a special item, which was also excellent.

The atmosphere in the restaurant is very quiet and relaxing, allowing you to fully concentrate on the omakase experience.

If you’re looking for a high-quality omakase experience in Bangkok, I highly recommend this sushi restaurant.

One of the most unforgettable sushi experiences I’ve had in Bangkok.
As someone from Japan, I have to say Chef Thiago completely impressed me. His technique and the way he talks about the ingredients, and his respect for Japanese culture is so genuine that you forget he’s not from Japan.
The atmosphere is calm and intimate. Everything, from the raw wood counter to the handmade plates, feels intentional and personal.
The fish quality is unreal. The rice he used was a blend of two different varieties, specially selected and balanced by Japanese top rice meisters, and it had the perfect softness and chew. Even the pickled ginger stood out. It was so good I wanted to take it home. And the fresh Nagano wasabi he picked himself in Japan was amazing. No gimmicks. Just honest, incredible food prepared with so much love and care.

Via Emilia has been on my list for a while after several recommendations, but I just never got around to visiting until recently. I went on a Saturday evening for dinner and booked about two days in advance. Getting a reservation was quite easy, though the restaurant was already buzzing by the time I arrived.

The atmosphere felt warm and inviting — very family-friendly, with that unmistakable charm of an authentic Italian spot. The food itself tasted genuinely Italian, with rich flavors and generous portions.

Parking is limited to roadside spaces, but it wasn’t too difficult to find a spot if you arrive around 5:30 to 6 PM. Overall, it’s definitely a place worth visiting, especially if you’re looking for comforting, homestyle Italian food in a lively yet relaxed setting.

One of the best Italian restaurants in Bangkok. A great discovery for a last-minute dinner! It’s best to book in advance, as the place is usually full. The food is excellent, with authentic Italian flavors. The desserts are simply outstanding! I’ll definitely come back soon to enjoy another meal here.

Via Emilia is truly a gem! I went with friends and everything was absolutely excellent — from the warm service to the authentic Italian ambience that makes you feel like you’re right in Italy.

The food is outstanding. The cold cuts and cheese selection are top quality, the pizza is one of the best I’ve had in years, and the grill section is equally impressive. The menu is huge, offering plenty of delicious options, and the wine list is excellent and very affordable.

A special mention goes to Manager Carlo — he’s a great guy, always coming to our table to check in and making sure we were well taken care of. His personal attention made the evening even more enjoyable.

It’s the perfect spot for families and friends — casual, easygoing, yet full of character. Prices are very reasonable for the quality you get. Highly recommended! Just a little tip: make sure to book in advance as it’s a very popular place.

I had saved this place for a while after seeing a review, and finally chose it to celebrate my friend’s birthday.

We adored every dish we ordered—even one of my friends who isn’t usually a fan of Italian food ended up loving it. My personal favorite was the pizza: the crust was perfectly baked, with fresh ingredients and not greasy at all. Honestly, if I hadn’t already had four dishes before, I could have finished the whole pizza myself!

For wine lovers, the restaurant offers a long list of excellent red and white selections. And don’t miss the desserts—they were just as delightful, so be sure to save some room.

A very popular Italian restaurant in Bangkok, so it can get a bit noisy when crowded, but the lively atmosphere adds to its charm. The menu offers a wide variety of dishes, which makes it easy to find something new to try. The risotto was slightly undercooked for my taste, but the meatballs with wine sauce were well balanced and full of flavor. The pizza stood out. I tried the Patate Scamorza e Pancetta for the first time and loved the crust, which was both chewy and crispy. The piadina was also great, soft yet flavorful. Overall, it’s a great spot if you’re looking for authentic Italian food with lots of options in a bustling setting.

Review of Yakiniku Sudo Bangkok: A Meat Lover's Delight

Yakiniku Sudo Bangkok is a fantastic destination for steak lovers, offering a delightful dining experience with a focus on high-quality meat prepared in traditional Japanese style. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it a great spot for both casual meals and special occasions.

The course menu is well-crafted, showcasing a variety of meats that are expertly grilled to perfection. Each dish highlights the flavors and quality of the ingredients, making for a satisfying meal.

However, I did find the kimchi to be a bit off; the flavor was unusual and didn’t quite match my expectations. Additionally, while the overall course was enjoyable, I felt that having two rice options was excessive. The set includes rice with the main dishes, and then you also get hamburg with rice, which felt like overkill.

Despite these minor setbacks, Yakiniku Sudo remains a solid choice for those seeking a delicious steak experience in Bangkok. With its quality meat and inviting atmosphere, it's worth a visit for any meat enthusiast!

Love the experience, the beef was very good. I thought the meal was going to be a bit too fatty but it actually balanced very well. The chef was also very nice too, he gave us a good explanation of every course that was being served to us. Will definitely come again👍

Tried the Bangkok Signature Course for 2,200++. The Japanese beef was incredibly tender, but the Thai beef was a bit tough— the chef did mention it in advance so it was understandable.
Overall, the flavors were well-balanced and flowed nicely throughout the course. Worth trying for the price.

Delicious food with a wonderful atmosphere.
The beef and tongue were incredibly tender – the tongue was my favorite! :)
Finished off with dessert, which was excellent. Truly impressed and satisfied!

I had the 4200++ course. The food was excellent, quality of the beef is top tier. The chefs are extremely friendly and kind. My personal favorite was the sirloin, very rich and flavorful. Will definitely come back soon.

A wonderful evening from start to end. A beautiful and charming building filled with style and character. Unique and custom artwork representing all corners of India. The menu is a culinary journey. Dishes prepared in a homely way, yet presented with upscale elegance. Chef / proprietor was around and ensured everything hit the highest standards. A wonderful evening and experience. Can’t wait to come back and to explore more of the menu.

From bite-sized bursts of flavor to bold curries reimagined, every dish here tells a story of tradition meeting innovation. Indian cuisine, each dish a celebration of India’s vibrant soul wrapped in modern artistry.. 👨‍🍳😋🤤

Celebrated my friend’s birthday here as we wanted to try a fancy Indian place in BKK. We tried most recommended menu with colorful fried crisp rice it’s a lovey one, cracked it once before you eat. All plates were delicious, intensive with herbs and intense ingredients. I like the lamp curry most. Would recommend for couples who need a romance moment as it’s easy to talk and impress for the vibes and quality of food. I deduct one point as a bit pricey. The rest was perfect and friendly staff.
FYI : They just received Michelin 2025 guide too

Just had dinner in Tapori, the staffs are all friendly, the foods are all delicous! And very great atmosphere here. The owner is also very nice giving us a dessert from his side✨ if you’re in Bangkok (especially Sukhumvit) and looking for proper Indian restaurant, this is the place!🫶

Tapori curates 29+ recipes from major regions across India, to portray diversity of Indian cuisine.

We ordered 6 menus from 4 towns, 3 gastronomic regions. All dishes have unique flavors and ingredients using. We had tasty and exciting journey through this meal. However, we wish the restaurant could improve story telling a bit about dining here as gastronomic journey across India. It would be nice to order food as planing trip where on India we would visit through eating today.

The service was nice, interior was homy and charming, definitely be back to try more regional Indian food here.

Let’s Just Say, I’m in the Restaurant Business & Won The Best Of Awards For Both My Spots…I Live In Florida & Bangkok 50/50. I’m a Diehard Foodie…We Have Eaten The Michelin List & Just Noticed This Spot Won!
We Had To Try!
This Place Is Insane!! Wow
Wow! New To The Michelin Guide 2025! With its soft lighting and Northeastern-inspired decor featuring woven lampshades and wall art, KaenKrung exudes a warm atmosphere. The chef-owners present contemporary Isan flavours from Khon Kaen in a menu of well-balanced Thai and Isan dishes. Made with local ingredients, the signature Hao Dong, comprising grilled pork tossed in a fragrant herb and spice mix, delivers bold, spicy, smoky notes with a refined finish. Perfect for those who love strong, punchy flavours.

HOUSE BLEND “KAEN” TEA (ROSE, LAVENDER, CLOVE, LIQUORICE AND ROSELLA)

SALTED CRISPY PORK SKIN WITH GRILLED TOMATOS RELISH

( MICHELIN GUIDE)
GRILLED PORK NECK SPICY SALAD WITH CUMIN LEAF (LONG-LOST RECIPE)

CHARCOAL-GRILLED SQUID WITH SEAFOOD SUACE

LAAB Duck Confit (Deboned & Mixed To Perfection)!

We Will Be Back!!!! Tastebuds Are Dancing! Aroi Mak!!!

The pork rinds here are a thing of beauty. It was great in my Luang Prabang som tum, and I’m sure it was great in the tomato relish dip dish that every other table seemed to be ordering. The assam river prawns reminded me of a dish that my grandma used to cook. And the sirloin skewers, despite not being charred enough, still managed to be wonderfully moreish and flavourful.

I think this restaurant has lots of potential. Didn’t order much as I wasn’t very hungry that day, but I’ll be back soon to try more of their menu. Their focus on sourcing, from breeds of local pork for the sausages, down to the different kinds of rice, is admirable and something I wish we’d see more of in the context of casual restaurants like this.

Absolutely loved my experience at Kaenkrung! The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and the staff were incredibly friendly and attentive. The food was the highlight — full of flavors, beautifully presented, and serve with fresh local ingredients. Will definitely be coming back soon!

Loved the food here. As a newbie to Thai cuisine, this was a great introduction to Isaan food. The hosts were very kind, the interior was cosy and the flavours were so balanced! The confit duck was my favourite.
One of the best meals of my life. The atmosphere and food were phenomenal. I would recommend to anyone visiting Bangkok.

Sooooo good! Authentic home cooked with chill vibe. Super cool owner as well. All the dishes are very yummy! My mum loves this place so much. Feel like coming to grannys place for food. Bonus point : They also welcome dogs too, the staffs were very attentive brought the furbabies water with ice cube too.

One of my favourite Thai food restaurant. The food taste is authentic , delicious and most importantly the price is very reasonable. The portion size is good. My favourite dish was basil beef , super tender and the Panang curry beef too . It’s so nice to go with rice. The fried fish and fried bread with pork , both were very unique. All the menu in this restaurant all worth a try . If you want to experience authentic , non commercial home made food in Thailand . This is one of the best selection . The interior vibes is so very homey, there are indoor and outdoor . The staff service is very polite and welcoming. For car parking it’s in the photo . Free Street parking , first come first serve . For wheelchair customer , please check photo for attention. There is some steps to go in the indoor restaurant. This place suitable for family and kids . Vegetarian menu is available but limited . Highly recommend this place , and I will definitely come back for next visit .

This restaurant has an indoor dining area, but it appears to be fully booked sometime. However, they do offer a meal at the opposite restaurant, which is owned by the same owner.

The food itself is decent, but the chili and vegetable dishes are a bit ordinary. The chili lacks the spiciness and kick that thai food usually have. The egg and prawn dishes are also not particularly extra nice, decent taste. The soup is sour which is nice and has fried fish, but it’s not served hot enough. Maybe because too many people.

The vegetables look plentiful, but below is actually the egg . A tad salty

Overall, this place is a good option for a meal, but it’s not particularly special compared to other Thai food places in Bangkok.

I recommended to visit this place if you loved Thai cuisine. I ordered pans beef (stewed beef in red curry), minced pork with salted fish, fried pork ribs and spicy clear soup with stewed beef. They were delicious with good ingredients. The atmosphere was like home. The staffs were nice with service mind. The parking area was on the side of road.

Highly recommended Thai restaurant in Rama 9 area with homemade style. The restaurant's atmosphere made me feeling like dinning in grandparent or family house. We may have some difficulties to find car parking at side of street. Top 3 dishes do not miss when you are here that red curry beef, stir fried mince pork with salted fish and fried beef with garlic. Their staff fully provide attentive service and always anticipate customer needs.

Beautiful restaurant with warm lighting and lots of greenery.

The food was amazing,  a perfect mix of Thai and Western flavors, and beautifully plated.

The desserts were very nicely decorated, and the overall atmosphere made it perfect for a special night out.

The restaurant is located right next to the river, making it a lovely place to watch the sunset while enjoying the relaxing background music. Will definitely come back!

Great and original food , great atmosphere and excellent service. Just got a distinction in the Michelin , and that’s well deserved. Highly recommend to food enthusiasts , good for romantic dinner or group of friends. Family also welcome. Million thanks to the chef, cooks and waiters, we had a memorable night and even order take away for the next day lunch

Good location and good vibe indeed, recommend to book in advance for seats. They do have both indoor and outdoor zone.
Variety of foods and more like Thai fusion style. I ordered some simple dishes like Thai omlette with chopped pork, soup with tofu & veggie, chef made it delicious though. I would also recommend salmon in red curry is also great!
The only thing i would recommend them is to have high chair for kids, as the restaurant is also good for families gathering, but they did not have that and my baby needed to sit on the lap for dinner.

A Must-Visit for Authentic Thai Cuisine!

Tub Ping Restaurant is truly a hidden gem and an absolute must-visit for anyone who appreciates excellent Thai food. The dishes are authentic, bursting with flavor, and beautifully presented. Highly recommend trying their Pad Thai, Khao Soi with Beef, Shrimp Curry, and Fish with Black Pepper—each one was outstanding.

Prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion size. The restaurant is clean, well-maintained, and offers great service with friendly and attentive staff. They also have a spacious van for group transport and a surprisingly good wine selection, which paired perfectly with our meal.

Highly recommended and definitely a place I will return to again!
Very good and authentic Thai food! The staff are knowledgeable and clearly well-trained — really impressed with their service. Lovely vibes by the Ping River. Definitely coming back!”

🍽️ This visit to Gong Kham Local Food Mae Rim was an experience of authentic Lanna flavours in a wonderfully shady and friendly wooden house setting. The restaurant truly excels with its traditional local dishes that are rich in flavour and spices.

🏡 Atmosphere
The restaurant maintains the feeling of eating at a friend's country home in Chiang Mai. The atmosphere is relaxed and airy, with a Lanna-style wooden house design, allowing us to fully unwind and enjoy the meal.

🌶️ Dishes Sampled (Highlights on the table)
The menu we ordered today was a comprehensive collection of the restaurant’s best local dishes:

1. Larb Khua (Northern Thai Spicy Minced Meat Salad):
* The pork Larb Khua was crumbly, fragrant with spices toasted until aromatic, and offered a bold, rich flavour typical of the "Khon Muang" (local people). Topped with crispy fried shallots (and pork crackling), this dish is best enjoyed with hot sticky rice or steamed rice for the full experience. It was genuinely "fully flavoured."

2. Sai Ua (Northern Thai Herb Sausage):
* The Sai Ua here appeared packed with herbs, sliced into perfect bite-sized pieces, and had an appealing colour. The flavour was intensely herbal, neither too oily nor too dry. It is a must-order dish for anyone having Northern Thai cuisine.

3. Kaeng Hung Lay (Burmese Style Pork Curry):
* (The thick, rich curry topped with shredded ginger) This was one of the rumoured "must-try" dishes! The pork was stewed until incredibly tender and succulent. The Kaeng Hung Lay gravy was thick and rich, fragrant with spices and ginger, offering a balanced sweet and spicy flavour. It is excellent mixed with hot steamed rice.

4. Cho Phak Kat (Green Cabbage Soup with Pork):
* (The clear soup topped with fried shallots and a dried chilli) This traditional soup had a perfect sweet and sour taste characteristic of authentic Cho Phak Kat. The Cantonese cabbage was tender, making it easy to sip and offering a feeling of healthy comfort food that was still delicious.

5. Steamed Pork (Jîn Nêueng / Mǔu Nêueng):
* (The sliced steamed pork resting on a banana leaf) This steamed pork dish looked tender and juicy, served with a sharp dipping sauce (either Nam Phrik Khàa or Nam Chim Jaew). It did a great job of highlighting the natural flavour of the meat.

6. Fresh Vegetables (Phak Sod):
* Essential for any Northern Thai meal, a generous serving of fresh vegetables including cabbage, cucumber, and other local greens was provided to accompany the chilli dips (which we ordered separately), making the meal complete and preventing it from becoming too heavy.

✨ Summary
Gong Kham Local Food Mae Rim absolutely confirms its reputation for maintaining the standards of authentic Northern Thai cuisine. All the dishes we ordered today were "fully flavoured" and delicious, especially the Larb Khua and Kaeng Hung Lay, which were particularly impressive. If you are looking for genuinely authentic Northern Thai food in a comfortable setting, you should not miss this restaurant on your trip to Chiang Mai!

We had such a wonderful experience enjoying authentic Northern Thai food here. The flavors were rich and traditional, with every dish.

If you are looking to experience real Northern Thai cuisine beyond the usual tourist menus, this restaurant is an absolute must-try. We will definitely come back again on our next trip!

Northern Thai cuisine. Nice good with good atmosphere. I found many dishes that are quite hard to find in local markets. Had a good experience to restaurant is large and spacious. They offer quite a large variety.

I recently visited this northern-style restaurant in Chiang Mai and was really impressed. The food tasted so authentic — rich flavors, perfectly balanced herbs and spices, just like true northern home cooking. Every dish was delicious, especially the signature ones, Sai Oua and Namprik Num. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, with friendly staff and local vibes. Definitely a must-try if you want genuine northern Thai taste!

A very local restaurant, they do have English menu but you have to order on a piece of paper which is all in Thai. The staff here are very friendly but they basically speak zero English. The fried chicken wings and steam chicken tasted like they were made from fresh chicken instead of frozen chicken. For people who doesn’t eat spicy, they will have limited choice here as this is a really local Thai restaurant so most of the food are quite spicy. Price wise is very cheap and affordable. Cash only, no credit card.

We had a wonderful dining experience at Ma Maison, a truly elegant restaurant offering refined Thai cuisine. The atmosphere is simply beautiful — both indoors and outdoors. We chose to sit outside and enjoyed the pleasant evening breeze surrounded by a serene, charming ambiance.

The staff were exceptionally attentive and courteous throughout our meal. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of authentic flavor. We particularly enjoyed the pomelo salad among others: papaya salad, krapao, fried assorted mushrooms, and sweet potato spring rolls — each one delicious and thoughtfully prepared.

By the end, we were simply too full for dessert, so we settled for an espresso instead — a perfect way to conclude a magnificent dining experience.

This Thai restaurant is absolutely delicious! Every dish is flavorful and perfectly seasoned — just like homemade food. 🥰
Everything is fresh, served quickly, and the staff are friendly with a cozy and clean atmosphere.
I honestly wanted to try every single dish! ❤️ Especially the Maggie sauce marinated pork — it’s incredibly tasty and goes perfectly with steamed rice! 🍚✨

The story goes something like this: Nai Lert found this piece of land in the 1900s and bought what is now half of Bangkok. He built a small business importing ice from Singapore, then what became Thailand’s first bus company. He was a simple man. A simple man who did not like spicy food. His wife, ever enterprising, helped run his business (now one of the largest in the country) and cooked up marvelous (non spicy) food. They both came from humble means and this translates into using every single ingredient to oblivion and with remarkable adeptness. Take the “Mee Nam Park Nai Lert” for instance: it seems like a simple red Tomyum soup. But look closer, and it has leftover shrimp, fried vermicelli and a sweet sour kick. Pure perfection. Nai Lert and his wife have long passed but their legacy lives on through her and her recipes. A conduit to another time, a better one. Other standouts were the beef red curry and the Yum Tua Pu.

One last anecdote: a bomb fell in the front yard of the house, and instead of pouring concrete over it, Nai Lert made it into a beautiful pond. This tells you everything you need to know. Must visit.

I’ve dined at many Thai restaurants, but this one offers a truly distinctive experience.

The flavors are well-balanced and delicious, elevated by the use of high-quality, carefully selected ingredients.

The service is absolutely outstanding, making you feel like a valued guest.

The atmosphere is relaxed and surrounded by an air of luxury, with a view of a serene green garden that’s pleasing to the eye.

Excellent meal here last night. Nice looking restaurant, great atmosphere and good service. The food was really good and very reasonably priced, especially for the quality. We were so impressed we’re going again tomorrow.
Everything is excellent except the noisy blender. Watch out for the spicy seafood sauce from the grilled mushrooms. Brought my non vegan friend here and she was surprised how good it was

I’d say the taste was even better than the real Esarn food ( I’m still dazed how they did so well with the vegan plara , I was told they used fermented beans )
Will definitely be back

I flew around half the globe to have my vegan culinary full-circle moment here.
My father is lao and when I was a kid, we always went to these grill garherings with his close friends. It was one of the very few moments in my childhood, where I truly connected with his culture. I remember the food very vividly, from the first time trying som tam to all these amazing flavors.
This place brought me back to these memories, but in a peaceful and harm-free manner.
I will definitely come back and wish the business great success & all the best!

Great vegetarian dishes. I love all som tam dishes, spicy soups and fruit frappe. There are some menu that we couldn’t try this time as we have ordered many dishes already. We will definitely come back to try their summer menus.
Isaan vegetarian food is really hard to find. I only know of one other restaraunt near Santi Asoke on Nawamin. So this place is special. The food is good and unique. A treasure hidden in Thonburi.

Not sure if this is the authentic Hainan-style rice noodles — I’ve never had the original.
But this one? Tastes great, easy to enjoy, and totally hits the spot.

The broth is nicely thick and flavorful, with soft noodles and generous cuts of crispy pork belly. There’s also a chunk of daikon radish that goes perfectly with the house-made shrimp paste and vinegar mix — adds a real punch of flavor.

Tip: If you’re ordering takeaway, don’t forget to add a bowl!
Taste great. Udon noodles with thick soup. Crispy pork belly is delicious. Shrimp paste sauce is good well with the noodles.

Very good and quick dishes which we got for breakfast. We arrived at opening and got a seat easily and were quickly served. The clear broth was extremely flavourful (heavy on the pepper) and the crispy pork stayed crispy in the soup
The staff was efficient and welcoming.

Fantastic pork noodles, available in two different types of gravy/sauce (clear broth or thick sauce) - both delicious. We also tried the crispy pork belly, which was also delicious, but indeed, a somewhat small portion (the noodles were also on the small side, but sufficient). Beware though, we arrived at around noon (peak lunch hour) and were informed of an estimated hour-long wait. So we took a number and came back about 40-45 minutes later and were seated soon after. If I could do it again we would order the same noodles but double the portion of crispy pork. Also, the wait was definitely worth it.

Randomly stumbled onto this spot. The noodles were freshly made (udon style) which gave it incredible chewy texture.

Got the "sticky" or "thick broth" that had immense seafood unami to it. Topped with some crispy pork belly and added their special shrimp paste sauce, which added a completely different flavor profile. Mustard greens added much needed acidity and the toasted sesame added a nutty and earthy balance.

Not well known but I know it will be.

Truly one of the best dining experiences you can have. The service, food, dish ware, and atmosphere are all top quality.

Chef Gaby and her team have created a unique dining experience that keeps true to her Mexican roots while elevating every dish with an artistic touch. You can taste the thoughtfulness and care put into every dish and drink.

Whether you need a spot for a date or a group dinner, Delia will wow your guests or date. For us, this is one of the restaurants we like to come back to over and over again. ❤️

Mexican cuisine is one of my top 5  favorite cuisines! Am very happy that “Delia” is in the Bangkok gastronomy map👏 Thanks to Chef Gaby and Chef Diego and the team for bringing Mexican flavors to Bangkok. I love the interior and decor! It’s chic and stylish. It makes me feel that am sitting somewhere in Mexico City. We enjoyed homemade corn tortillas and all the dishes we ordered were full of details, elegantly presented and very flavorful. The portions are very small and a bit overpriced but we enjoyed the experience at Delia😍
Service is very good. Staffs are friendly and English speaking.
We will definitely return!

Overall a good experience. Was recommended by a friend and upon trying a few dishes, I can see why!

But we went as a bigger group and I found the food relatively hard to share. So my recommendation would be to go in a smaller group or for a date.

Loved the area the restaurant was located in, so that really adds to the ambiance.

Super tasty! Had dinner here and absolutely loved it! The food was fresh and flavorful, the portions were just right, and the staff made us feel very welcome. A great spot for a relaxing evening meal.

I had a great experience eating at Delia! The atmosphere was warm and lively, with colorful decor and great music that really set the mood. Tacos, tostada and pastor were fresh and full of flavor.

Service was very good, and the prices were reasonable for the quality. I also tried a margarita, which was delicious.

Highly recommend this place if you’re craving authentic Mexican food. I’ll definitely be coming back.

Authentic Thai dining experience with vibrant flavors and fresh ingredients. The atmosphere is cozy, and the staff is friendly and attentive. Highly recommend the papaya salad and grilled pork neck – absolutely delicious! Perfect spot for a casual meal with friends or family.

First up, My wife (Tik) and brother-in-law (Natt) have just opened (7 September 2024) MAHN Bangkok restaurant about 20 minutes from the centre of Bangkok.  It specialises in Isaan style cuisine.  It’s family style with my wife’s Mum supervising the cooking.  Its target audience is local Thais who want good food at a great price to share in comfortable air-conditioned surroundings.

However, if you are foreign and you want great authentic Thai food in a calm friendly atmosphere, then you might want to consider MAHN.  As you would expect, in addition to the usual soft drinks, there is quality wine and cold beer which matches well with the food.  Note:  There is only one sparkling, one white and one red wine on the menu but they have been carefully selected to specifically complement Isaan style cuisine.

I enjoyed the Somtum Thai (80THB), a sweet and spicy papaya salad, Jackfruit Laab (80THB) which is outstanding, with steamed and sticky rice (20THB each), charcoal grilled marinated chicken (80THB) and fried dried and marinated pork neck (80THB).  Check out the photos.  I washed it all down with an ice cold Leo (60THB) and shared a bottle of Cono Sur Bicicleta Reserva Sauvignon Blanc (1,100THB) with the rest of the family.

As you can see, the pricing is very reasonable and you could probably get a GRAB from Bangkok city, have lunch or dinner at MAHN and ride a GRAB back and still have money left over compared to finding one of the tourist focused places close to the city.
