Or you can drive as there is plenty of free off-street parking.  And you’ll experience authentic carefully prepared great food and a relaxing and friendly ambience.  You’ll probably be the first in your circle of friends to know about this “great little restaurant in Prawet”.  Take it slow and enjoy the experience.

Don't let the strip mall location fool you, this is a hidden gem.

Don't miss the Corn Larb Salad; a very unique twist on a classic dish.

I recently visited this newly opened Isaan restaurant, and I couldn’t be more impressed! The owner is incredibly welcoming and passionate about the food, which really shows in the quality of every dish. The flavors are authentic, fresh, and absolutely delicious, all at very reasonable prices.

The service was top-notch—friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home. The decor is beautifully done, with a cozy, homey vibe that makes you want to stay longer. It’s the perfect spot for a relaxed meal with friends or family. Highly recommend this place! I’ll definitely be coming back.

Honest Review

- Shop: Very beautiful. I really like this style of restaurant. Comfortable and chill, not stuffy. 10/10
- Menu: It might not be a huge selection, but it's not a small selection either. I ended up ordering several items. The grilled khao jee was all gone, and the grilled fish was all gone. 7/10
- Taste: The papaya salad was delicious and flavorful, but the crying tiger was tough and dry. I finished it all because I was hungry. The om curry was delicious. The plates and bowls were very cute. 7/10
- Service: I was a little confused, but that's okay, we can gradually learn. 7/10
- Staff: The auntie was yelling at the young man in front of customers all the time. This wasn't okay. 1/10

Overall, it's not bad, but it's not amazing. I think with improvement, the restaurant will definitely be a hit.

A hidden gem that brings together Chaozhou and Southern Thai flavors with charm

The food is packed with personality. Prawn fried rice has that perfect wok-char, and the clam omelette is crispy and fresh. Also don’t miss the Thai dessert

The cozy atmosphere makes you want to linger. Service is friendly and quick, and the unique building gives this place real character

"The ambience perfectly combines classic and modern Chinese elements, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. While a few dishes had a slightly fishy taste, the overall dining experience was enjoyable and satisfying."

Nice cozy place to have dinner and the food variety on the menu are good. The taste is quite southern Thai , very nice. Liked the shrimp stir fry vegetables, prawn basil. The curry is not spicy enough but nice taste. Fish is fresh and nice soup, not very sour surprisingly.  Overall, this is a nice place. Too bad they cannot cater to request like to cook without the smelly bean .

Nice decorated Southern Thai-Chinise restaurant. Come in medium portion. Taste is good, like home cooking. Not to rich, not too salty. Order many dishes, all are quite ok except Moo Hong (southern style braised pork) which is not tender enough.
Price is quite high but acceptable by the ingrediants, atmosphere, decoration and services.
Service is good, about 20 free parking spaces.

🍲🍗🥘🥣
If you seek for nice Thai restaurant you should have a visit at this place. Actually, this place is also famous for Thai Southern food. Unfortunately, my stomach cant tolerate to very spicy food these days.

Anyway, I ordered deep fried sea bass with turmeric, deep fried soft tofu and minced pork mixed with salted fish. The sea bass was great and fresh. The portion was big. The garlic on top of the fish was very tasty. Next time I will ask for extra garlic. 🤣
Soft tofu was way beyond what I expected. You dont even have to chew it. Minced pork mixed with salted fish was also good as a standard.

💳💰🪙
The price was reasonable, not too expensive.

🏞🏡🚕🚗
The atmosphere was nice. It's a restaurant in a pretty house. The parking space is available onsite.

A quiet and elegant setting as we were the only diners.
Service was attentive with frequent plate changes, but the meal pacing was far too rushed. Multiple dishes were delivered to our table in quick succession, resulting in three dishes arriving while we were still on our second course. No napkins were provided until we used our own.
The food was a letdown given the hype. Starters were overly salty; the fish maw soup lacked depth. The fried crab, char siu, and squab were delicious, but the seafood fried rice was mediocre. The coconut dessert was excellent.
For a meal over 7,000 THB, it didn't feel worthwhile. Perhaps Chef Vicky's true craft is only found at Wing.

The food was nice, though it didn’t exceed my expectations.
However, the service by Khun Joe and Khun Gig was truly outstanding — they explained every dish very well and took excellent care of us.

From the course menu, I especially enjoyed the soup and the roasted pork.

Personally, I feel that coming here for the food alone is just okay, but the lunch set with dim sum looks quite interesting.

Fantastic view with nice food. Love their dim sum.
Crispy taro is a must. Soy sauce and vinegar are very good, great aroma.
However, I found a piece of crab shell, reported it, but service just took it away without even a single word of apologize.

Dining at K by Vicky Cheng was nothing short of extraordinary. From the moment we stepped into the beautifully designed space—elegant, modern, and infused with subtle Chinese artistry—we knew we were in for something special. The panoramic views of Bangkok’s skyline added a magical backdrop to an already luxurious setting.

Chef Vicky Cheng’s menu is a masterclass in modern Chinese cuisine. Each dish blends traditional Cantonese and Teochew flavors with refined French techniques. The mud crab with olive leaf and garlic was a standout—bold, aromatic, and surprisingly hands-on. We also loved the char siu and fish maw, which were rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced.

Service was impeccable: warm, attentive, and knowledgeable without being overbearing. The lunch set menu was a great way to sample a variety of dishes, and the presentation was as stunning as the taste.

Whether you're a foodie or simply looking to treat yourself, K by Vicky Cheng is a must-visit. It’s not just a meal—it’s an experience.

located on the 56th floor of the empire building, definitely you get one of the most amazing view of the city. the environment is beautiful and service is meeting the expectation.

this review is from their soft-opening but i believe it’s still relevant. overall everything is delicious, good portion and satisfying. i especially liked their dim sum which are pretty authentic cantonese.

knowing the background of the chef vicky cheng, i think its worth giving this place a try if you are in BKK, at least its CP value is higher as compare to his other outlets elsewhere.

The best fish I had in Thailand maybe ever. Very moist and flavourful. All dishes were delicious and flavourful. The menu is focused on fresh ingredients so they might run out but everything is fresh. I would recommend to make a reservation since it gets packed. The place is cosy, simple and the stuff is very sweet. Fried Sea Bass with tamarind sauce was my favourite but the quality of crab was great too and they take the meat out for you. If you like it funky, try the Sato (stinky bean), it is very flavourful.

The restaurant offers home-style cooking at reasonable prices. Every dish is authentic Thai with familiar flavors, and the seafood is outstanding. Highly recommended!

PS. Booking is required. I made it just one week prior.

Very recommended to whoever wanna try authentic Thai dishes, especially seafood. You will experience the taste of home cooking with homy ambience. Pre-booking is Recommended. Foods are fresh and served in large portions, with group of 4 pax or more would allow you to enjoy various dishes. Price is fair for the great quality ingredients and served in large portions.

I have eaten here multiple times already. The food is fresh, clean, and every menu is delicious. The seafood is really big and the food is flavorful but easy to eat. Worth the price and the atmosphere is relaxed. You can park in front of the restaurant. This restaurant is highly recommended !!!🩷🩷🩷

The overall price is a bit pricy but the quality of food is so fresh and nice.

For the parking lot, please find any available slot the side of the road.

PS. I would rate for 3 stars because they accept only CASH and they allow us to pay cashless only for this time.

Rewriting my review since I have had a reservation for dinner. The food was good but the squid topping was too much it blocked the taste of the actual dish. I had about 3 different dishes with squid topping (tofu, garlic rice, yakisoba) all of them near bland because of the topping. I had to brush it to the side to taste the dish.

I ordered two different beef dishes and both were good but nothing spectacular that made you go “wow”.

The sweet potato was good and more than reasonable for its price.

Now for lunch, the beef bowl and pork neck was spectacular! The taste! The aroma! How it came nice, hot and steamy! It was definitely what I expected.

The service is good and the atmosphere as well.

I was quite excited to try Pari after hearing about its Michelin mention and unique Thai–Izakaya fusion concept. Unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations.

Starting from the booking process, everything felt overly rigid. You have to book through their website and pay in advance (around 300 THB per person, VAT not included). Seating rules are very strict and not flexible at all, which set the tone for a rather formal and slightly stressful dining experience.

When we arrived—10 minutes early—we still had to wait because they weren’t ready, even though they kept reminding us not to be late. The restaurant wasn’t even full, which made that part more disappointing.

Food-wise, it was decent and up to a standard Izakaya level, but definitely not the best I’ve had. Portions were very small compared to the price, and the variety was limited—our group of four could easily order the entire menu and still not feel full. Service was just okay; everyone seemed to be in a rush, and the whole meal felt a bit mechanical.

The place was also quite crowded and hard to park nearby, which added to the overall inconvenience. With the high price, small portions, and average quality, it feels like you’re mostly paying for the “story” and branding rather than the experience or the food itself.

In short, Pari didn’t meet my expectations. It’s not a bad restaurant, but definitely not one I’d recommend waiting or paying extra for. No worries if you haven’t tried it—you’re not missing much.

Innovative Local Flavors, World-Class Experience!!

The food is a genuine journey. The flavor profiles are truly unique and exciting, delivering a creative twist that keeps you engaged with every bite. What's most remarkable is how the kitchen beautifully elevates traditional, regional ingredients and techniques to a gourmet level. It's clear why they were included in the Michelin Guide right after opening. If you're looking for an innovative taste of the local area, this is the place to be.

Everything is over the moon! I had such a great experience here. You need to reserve a table, but the wait was less than 5 minutes to get seated. It took around 10–15 minutes for the first dish to arrive and only 5–10 minutes for the next ones. The interior is lovely, but the food is even better! I really enjoyed it and will definitely come back for sure.

The dishes at this Japanese restaurant are authentic and delicious.
The grilled fish is crispy on the outside and tender inside, full of flavor; the handmade gyoza has a golden crust with juicy filling; the corn tempura is crunchy and slightly sweet, enhanced by bonito flakes. Overall, the taste is genuine and highly recommended.
The space is quite small, so it’s best to book 3–5 days in advance.

One of the best resto I’ve been to. After being disappointed by some other over-hyped Michelin 2 star Chinese/Asian fusion in London, I was cautious at the beginning. But the chef here at GOAT really understands Thai&Chinese ingredients&flavors and how to bring the best out of them. The creativity is superb. The staff were all so passionate and proud of whatever they were serving and went out of their ways to tell the stories behind the food. I particularly loved the tour on the rooftop garden and saw how the herbs are grown. The beverage parings were even better than wine in my opinion. Overall great experience!

Everything here is simply on point – from the presentation, food, service, cocktails, to the atmosphere! A truly unique dining experience. Our host Kitty was exceptionally friendly and attentive, taking the time to explain every course in great detail. The homegrown mint tea was refreshing, and the kombucha was absolutely outstanding.

The restaurant is set in a quiet standalone house, exquisitely decorated with elegant Chinese-inspired touches. The courtyard’s lush greenery feels natural and calming, while the refined design creates a graceful atmosphere. Even more impressive, many of the organic vegetables and herbs used in the dishes are harvested from their own rooftop garden, adding freshness and authenticity to the meal. Neatly arranged cabinets of house-made pickles give a sense of order and care, reflecting the restaurant’s thoughtful philosophy.

The evening tasting menu is designed like a culinary map of Thailand, with each course showcasing premium ingredients from different regions of the country. Every dish brings out unique local flavors, turning the dinner into a true visual and gastronomic journey.

What makes Goat truly special is not only the inventive Thai-Chinese fusion, but also their commitment to the finest regional ingredients, presented with passion and precision. If you’re looking for an elevated fusion dining experience in Bangkok, Goat should absolutely be at the very top of your list!

I love the story of the GOAT as much as I love the food and experience. It was the best dining experience. One Michelin star is not enough for this gem. I love their zero waste policy and that all ingredients (inckuding the wines) are sourced in Thailand. The welcome drink, their house kombucha is delicious and certainly the best ibhave ver tasted. I am looking forward to dining their again when next I am in Bangkok

Sometimes dreams come true. Having read lots of reviews of GOAT I booked the restaurant for an important dinner. Some reviews left the impression that things were bad whereas most praised it being culinary heaven.

GOAT is for people who love exquisite cuisine and the next level of special / fine dining. If you just want the boring bland stuff of a place like Nobu, then this is not for you. Instead, if you want to see how a real one Michelin star restaurant (I guess it will be two stars soon) looks, feels and tastes, then GOAT is the place to be.

From the moment we arrived and were served an aperitif in the immaculate courtyard including shown parts of the self grown garden including how they ferment and create things like Scoby (not Scooby Doo) it was a tour of Thai cuisine.

The menu defined the 1462 km journey from Chang Mai in the north to the border with Malaysia in the south. All shown on the menu as a map like a tourist guide. My guest decided to have the soft pairing while I went for the white Wine pairing. The sommelier Gus gave a deep insight to special wines grown in Thailand which I never knew before.

Twice we had the honour of having the Owner and Mastermind behind GOAT, Mr Tan-Parkorn Kosiyapong explain the next course being served with his little pincer and that big friendly smile. It was like a surgeon telling you what will happen and how you will feel afterwards.

Having eaten over 100 Michelin stars in my life including NOMA, Alain Ducasse and others, this was by FAR the best of them all. Why? So unexpected, yet so authentic. And the most insane part is that the entire restaurant feels like an Art/hobby project. There is no chance they can make money with these prices against the ingredients used and staff on hand. I counted 14 staff (kitchen+floor) to serve max 20 guests. Most expensive bottle of wine on the card was a St Emilion for THB 9900.

Walking away that night I felt I had been paid (and maybe played) by getting such an experience for so little money (all in THB 20k for two guests).

There is one way to find out - and that is to come back! Meanwhile the plot thickens….

Small request:

Aircon - a bit too strong. Please not so cold.

Loved the service so much. Food was excellent. Everyone was warm and hospitable. Kitty has been really very kind and helpful. The gentleman who shared his knowledge about Thai wine with me was generous with his expertise. It was truly an experience I will never forget.

Authentic Thai cuisine in a truly hidden gem – Michelin recommended and well deserved!

We recently had a fantastic family dinner at Lung Shall Kitchen in Pattaya, and it was one of the culinary highlights of our trip. The restaurant itself is very modest and unassuming from the outside – you’d probably walk past it if you didn’t know it was there. But once you step inside, you immediately feel welcome. It’s simple, clean, and focused on what really matters: the food.

And the food is absolutely outstanding. Everything we tried was fresh, flavorful, and clearly prepared with a lot of care. The menu offers a great variety of traditional Thai dishes, from spicy salads to perfectly balanced curries and delicious seafood. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients – nothing felt mass-produced or reheated. It’s authentic, home-style cooking at its best.

What makes this place even more special is the fact that it’s been recommended in the Michelin Guide 2025. That’s how we found it in the first place – and it definitely lives up to the recommendation. It’s not fine dining in a fancy setting, but it delivers high-end flavor in a casual, local atmosphere.

Service was friendly, fast, and helpful, even though English is limited – but that just added to the charm. We felt very well taken care of and appreciated.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for real Thai food away from the tourist traps. We would absolutely come back!

Very tasty, full-flavloured Thai authentic food with incredibly cheap price! Becareful if you don't like spicy food but it's really worth to give it a try.

They open for lunch and dinner with gap in the afternoon so please check the timing and do come early as it's quite packed.

I decided to patronise this place after I saw Mark Weins Youtube channel which featured this local Thai restaurant. It was also not far from our home (4.1km away). Luckily, we came early and had no issues getting a table. Cos the crowd started coming in after we arrived.

We ordered the Fish Tom Yum and Geng Khua Koong for lunch today. The food was so awesome, flavourful and inexpensive. Hence, the recently awarded Michelin Guide (Bib Gourmand).

The final bill came up to: 560 baht (with those 2 signature dishes, 2 bowls of rice and my infant sons Seafood Fried Rice and a 1.5 litre bottle of water).

I’ll definately bring my parents and guest here if they come to visit us here in Pattaya.

Came here because of the Michelline. The water sole fish was definitely the MVP but the rest are on the very oily and too sweet side.

Everything is fresh ingredients but too oily and too sweet.
Great local flavor restaurant , newly renovated could accommodate more customers. Quite far away from Pattaya town center but worth the drive

Outstanding experience just outside of Nichada, with wonderful food and service. We were absolutely delighted to celebrate our special occasion with a meal here - the most incredible Thai delicacies made with so much creativity, sustainability and care in mind. We were looked after so well, the setting is beautiful and this place is a true hidden gem; we will certainly be returning and it deserves to be very successful. We were even treated to a tour of the herb garden and to see the innovations the restaurant is making to stay as environmentally friendly as it can be. A must-visit!!

It's a place where you can go back and eat more and more. The menu changes constantly. Every time I go back, I can try something new.
The food on the menu is easy to choose from, and it is divided into curries, grills, etc.
Fresh vegetables will be served with the food. I like to try new vegetables regularly.
The atmosphere is always nice, the staff is very attentive.
I recommend the menu: Golden sheets with chicken (sorry if the name is wrong)

Amazing food, nice ambience and perfect service. They really try to create something special and it’s worth the short journey. We enjoyed some of their bugs, some beers, the set menu, some wines, and dessert tea. You can feel it is worth visiting more than just once.

Hi Akkee,
Thank you for making us experience thai food outside padthai, tom yum soup and moo krop! This is a totally new experience for us! I hope we can also try your other seasonal dishes in the future!!! :)

P.S. all the staff are nice and attentive!

It was more than just dining, but it was truly an experience!

Recently crowned a Michelin Star, Akkee is always a go-to place for me every time I visit Nonthaburi. The food, the beer and wine selections, the staffs, and the ambience and choice of music, you'd never want to leave the place!

Every month and every season, the restaurant seems to always be introducing new dishes from the roots of traditional Thai delicacies to the table and great selections of wine and beer pairing, and they never seem to disappoint.

Would recommend to everybody to come at least once, and I'm pretty sure it won't be your last time 🍚🤩⭐️

From the front, this restaurant already looks stunning. It's unique, filled with antiques and vintage collectibles. The place is huge, located right by the river. The menu has a wide selection, and everything is delicious. I was very satisfied with my meal here.

Didn’t stay here
came here after Katrina Day at temple nearby on 26 Oct 2025

had crab fried rice , a plate of sir fry veg n coconut smoothie.
Nice setting

Delicious Authentic Thai Food in a Unique Setting!

This spacious restaurant offers a memorable dining experience right by a small river (though there’s a slight odor). The quirky decor is filled with an eclectic collection of toys, creating a strangely charming—if slightly eerie—atmosphere. Walking to your table, you can’t help but be fascinated by the unusual decorations!

The food was excellent, and the prices were very reasonable. Our group of seven enjoyed multiple dishes and a drink each, all for under 2,000 THB. Highly recommended—especially if you’re visiting Chokchai Farm, as it’s conveniently nearby.

They also have a museum, though we didn’t get a chance to explore it. A great spot for tasty Thai food in a one-of-a-kind setting!

Photogenic restaurants and hotels, decorated in a vintage style collecting various kinds of stuff from the 80s to 90s. The complex of the restaurant is quite complicated and a bit confusing. Elderly and handicaps should be careful of steps. The staff are nice and friendly. Food is good at portioning.

We walked on a bridge to get to the restaurant as it is on the other side of the river. There're displays of collectible, figurines, antique, vintage stuff everywhere, including the Blues Brother and super hero figures. We ordered several dishes for dinner and they were very tasty. The breakfast buffet was also very good.

A lovely homey small family restaurant specializing in two main dishes: Pad Mee Korat (fried noodles Korat style) and Som Tum (Papaya Salad). Both in different variations and on a very high level of quality. Friendly owners and huge portions. We will happily come back as the sticky-sweet noodles fill our tummy.
Great of taste!

Pad Mee Kratok, a famous shop in Chokchai. Pad Mee with fresh shrimp, a small plate but you get a lot. The shrimp are big. There's also a lot of chicken mixed in. It's delicious. Today I found the taste to be average, not very sweet (I personally like it sweeter). I also ordered Som Tam Korat. The Som Tam was delicious. It goes well with Pad Mee. The shop owner is kind. There's parking in front of the shop. The entrance is narrow, it's a rural village road. Open Google Maps and drive there.
Pad Mee Korat, rich flavor, best eaten with papaya salad. During lunch, there are a lot of people but you don't have to wait in line.

The Pad Mee is so delicious! I have to admit that I'm usually disappointed whenever I go to a Michelin-starred restaurant. But, wow, Auntie Pliang really does it. The Pad Mee is so good that it's a real 888. Even though the papaya salad might not be up to par, I only focused on the Pad Mee. The portion is huge! Auntie is so awesome! 🤩

We had an incredible dining experience here! Every single dish was a piece of art. The ingredients were high quality and thoughtfully prepared. Service was impeccable. ​Make sure you're on time, as every guest starts eating at the same time. Booking in advance is a must

Heard about this place for a while and decided to give it a try. Wasn’t impressed that they served our welcome drinks at a table in Lord Jim’s during staff training in there that went on quite loudly. Then we got to the restaurant where the atmosphere was much better. Kaiseki dinner and sake were great. High quality ingredients and all the dishes were so tasty and complex. The head chef can speak English fluently and very friendly.

Great dining experience at Mandarin Oriental Kinu by Takagi.

It's a 10 course omakase menu. We paired  6 types of perfectly selected Sake to complement our meal.

Chef was friendly and every dish was prepared with lot of passion and love.

3 different types of Caviar was served. Every  dish was well presented and delicious.

Great intimate ambiance. Good service. Highly recommended

5 ⭐️ meal. Very delicate dishes with many ingredients/elements involved.
But the lunch course is quite small compare to the price.
The restaurant is quite small with total 10 seats.  And the restaurant serve everyone promptly at noon. So if you are not friends having lunch together, the air can be quite intense.

I was told that the head chef comes from Japan every month and luckily I booked the day the head chef is in town.
This is a real authentic Kaiseki dinner course which you don’t really see much in Bangkok as we know that omakase sushi restaurants are taking over the scene here in Bangkok.
The course here was well put together.  The amount of food served was just right.
This restaurant sets a new standard for Kaiseki meal in Thailand.

This is probably the best value Khao man gai in Chiang Mai. It's hard to still find 35 baht street food but here you can! Sure, it's not the best I have had but for the price, you can't complain. The only downside is that the outdoor seating has a lot of mosquitos. Bring your own repellant.

Chicken rice dreams do come true!
Tucked away in the heart of the city, this humble chicken rice shop has earned its Michelin Guide spot for all the right reasons. The chicken is silky and juicy, the rice is rich with just the right hint of chicken fat and aromatics, and every bite feels like a warm hug.
What really stands out is how perfectly they balance quality, quantity, and price — it’s rare to find such honest cooking that still feels so generous.
This isn’t just a meal, it’s a love letter to simple, honest flavors done right. If you’re chasing the soul of real comfort food, you’ll find it here, one delicious spoonful at a time.

I went there for the Michelin star rating, but it wasn't as good as the chicken rice I had at a food court in Singapore. The sauce was good, but the chicken was a bit tough, dry, and tough. It wasn't quite what I was looking for. But the price is really cheap.

One of the best chicken rice we’ve ever tried! The chicken was extremely soft, tender, and uniquely flavorful. Sauce was great too. Great portion and totally deserving of its Michelin nod. The queue system is well-organized too. A must-try in Chiang Mai! This is definitely one of the best local Michelin pick.

Some of the best chicken and rice I’ve had (and I’ve had a lot)! Flavorful broth, the chicken is moist and tender, dipping sauce is near perfect, and the rice was perfectly cooked. We each got the 45 baht portion and it was very filling. They were closing up around 12:30 so get there early…absolutely worth visiting! Just look for the big chicken on the side of the road 🤩

Must have reservations to eat at this establishment. Best Thai food I had in a long time! Known for the papaya salad. Recommend the corn and salmon salad and all the yum-type salads. So fresh tasting and so good!
The food taste so good authentic E san food , love every dishes we ordered , highly recommended everyone

If anyone has a desire for a gourmet feast of อีสาน food, I truly appreciate this restaurant, it’s highly recommended for the pungent aroma and the piquant taste of the cuisines. Every dishes that we order is scrumptious! The Yam Talay was cheap and I really enjoyed it, with salmon, shrimp, crab sticks and crabs.you can ask for the waiter to make it less spicy, and the amiable waiters and chef will try their best to make it as what you want it to be. The roasted chicken is a non-spicy dish so it is a great pleasure for kids and other people who couldn’t eat spicy food.
You must try their fried catfish, undoubtedly, it’s one of their best dishes with an aroma of lemon and fish sauce, so if you couldn’t eat fish sauce, just tell them!
The service was excellent and food were extremely delicious, please have a go at it if you went to Ubon.

We loved our dinner here, especially the Duck Larb! A little hard to find from the street, but quiet and very professional inside. We talked to the owners a little bit too and they are extremely nice and helpful. They recommended boiled sausage which we ate for the first time. Green mango was excellent but we found the fish tasted too strong.

Great place.Good food. Wonderful service.
We will back again soon.

10/10 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Had a wonderful dining experience at Nina’s. The restaurant is surrounded by lush greenery, giving it a calm and cozy garden atmosphere — perfect for relaxing with friends and family.

The food was outstanding with a great mix of flavors:
•	Crispy pork larb – crunchy, flavorful, and full of herbs.
•	Crab dip with fresh vegetables – rich, creamy, and paired perfectly with the fresh veggies.
•	Crab-filled crispy cups – light, crunchy, and deliciously topped with sweet crab meat.
•	Salted Fish Pork Patties) – savory, aromatic, and very tasty with lime and onion.
•	Clear fish soup with Plum– refreshing, not too salty, and comforting.
•	Garlic shrimp stir with garlic – fresh, juicy, and aromatic.
•	Pumpkin tempura – lightly fried, crispy, and naturally sweet.

The presentation of each dish was beautiful, and everything tasted freshly prepared with high-quality ingredients. Service was friendly and attentive, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for authentic, flavorful Thai food in a charming garden setting. 🌿🍴

Reservation is required in the peak seasons with 1000thb deposit and preorder the menu.

Great taste, nice staff and cozy atmosphere.
Pumpkin salt egg is the must.

Recommended!

Was so impressed with the food here. Everything from the salted egg yolk crusted pumpkin to the squid was delicious and generously portioned. We also love all the cakes and desserts we ordered here. Note, kitchen closes at 19.30 so come early. This place is indoor seating with not a lot in terms of view, but the food is absolute to die for. Highly recommended!

Every dish we tried at Nina Cafe was truly impressive. The seafood was incredibly fresh, especially the squid — perfectly cooked with an excellent texture. The flavors were bold and authentic, with every plate delivering that signature Thai zest. Food also came out fairly quickly.

One tip: be sure to reserve and pre-order your preferred menu items a few hours in advance, as everything is made fresh. Also, don’t forget to ask about their seasonal or “secret” menu — they sometimes have special dishes that aren’t listed but are absolutely worth trying.

If you're craving real Thai flavors with top-quality ingredients, Nina Cafe is definitely worth a visit when in Khao Yai.
Superb local taste with very fresh ingredients! Also, don't miss their awarded Young Coconut Custard!

This used to be my family’s go-to dim sum restaurant for years. However, during our last visit, we were shocked to find a cockroach in the noodles near the end of our meal. It was extremely disgusting and raised serious concerns about the restaurant’s hygiene standards.

We immediately informed the staff, who apologized and offered a 10% discount (only on a few items, not the full bill) Given the severity of the situation, the response felt inadequate and disappointing.

Sadly, after this experience, I can no longer recommend this place, and we won’t be returning

I heard that there are many customers, so I made a reservation by phone in advance and visited.
I visited at 12 p.m. on weekdays, and there were many customers in the restaurant.
But it wasn't busy or noisy.
The cute staff who welcomed me with a shy smile were so kind.
My husband and I ordered dim sum, Xiaolongbao, and duck dishes.
The food shown in the first picture was really delicious(soy sauce served with together was really delicious), but I couldn't eat it well because it contained coriander. If you don't like coriander, be careful. I don't know if you can take out the coriander.
Shrimp dim sum and chives shrimp dim sum were also so delicious.
I can pay with a credit card, and thanks to my kind employees, I had a good meal.
Finally got a chance to stop by for a quick lunch after recommended by friend. The place is conveniently located at Soi Nimman 5. BBQ and dimsum is delicious with reasonable price.
Recommended! Number one Chinese food I love the most in Chiangmai !

Traditional Cantonese food in Chiangmai. Price may be very cheap but the quality is good. Their noodle portion is a lot, can be shared by two people. Dim sum price is good, the buns are tasty. The dumplings are also good. But better to come with many people so you can order more to share.

At the fish club located within the Andez Resort The view is amazing.  Blue sky with amazing outdoor dining environments. Staff are super friendly and pays attention to the details on the dining preference of the guests. Alaskan crab salad is quite a unique combination with avocado as the base. Fisherman’s burger is amazing. The sauce is light. Cucumber goes very well with the prawns patty as well as the crab meat.  Coconut cold brew is a must to try. Original sweetness from the coconut water and the cold brew is intense. Reasonable price and food quality is definitely worth the price. truly deserved Michelin star

Fish Club is my go-to spot every time I check in at Andaz Pattaya. Whether I’m waiting for my room or just craving a relaxing lunch by the pool, this beachfront restaurant never disappoints.

The setting is stunning—right next to the main pool with ocean views, perfect for sunny days. The ambiance strikes a great balance between laid-back and stylish, ideal for a peaceful meal.

The menu offers a mix of Thai and international dishes, with a strong focus on seafood. Many dishes I’ve tried here is fresh, well-presented, and full of flavor.

I will plan to dinner here next time when I have a chance to stay this hotel again and imagine that how the vibe in the evening is equally beautiful with the sound of waves in the background.

Highly recommend for both hotel guests and outside visitors looking for quality seaside dining.
Almond sole & bass were world class! Thank you for an excellent birthday - well back for the excellent fish and awesome service. Kap poom 🙏🏼

The food tastes amazingly really good with enough portion. Although the menu is limited, there are slightly different menus for lunch and dinner. We have early dinner by the pool and enjoy view of calm sea although it is a cloudy day in rainy season. Nice atmosphere and romantic for special vacation.

An in house guest, had multiple meals at the Fish Club.
Daytime it's great for relaxed eats by pool.  Transitions seamlessly into a seafood restaurant with beautiful sunset views.
The service team was all super friendly and engaged. Ging in particular impressed, remembering preferences from previous meals.
Good sized portions, tasty, flavourful dishes and killer sunsets.
Best to reserve a table in advance for the best views.

As a Thai but also a tourist to this area I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant's green curry, hor mok with fish, chicken laab and lod chong dessert.  The restaurant has an elegant but accessible vibe and the service was warm and attentive.  The team escorted us from the parking lot into the courtyard.  Another plus was the pandan water and beautiful banyan trees and other structures patrons can visit.  The owner not only cares about the food but is also an informed person who can tell you about the rich history in the area.  Hopefully the owner creates a vid telling the history of the area in English.  Local people nearby hold this restaurant in high regard.
You have got to go there once. Nice courtyard. Good thai food. Not the best of the best but good enough for the view and the service

Been in this restaurant advised by a local guide.
The location is so suggestive: on the riverside,inside and outside seatings,historical,cured in every detail  from the wooden swings,to the wooden benches,tables etc and very well decorated!
Service has been 5 start from the beginning to the end,very gentle and professional.
We ve been here on our 3rd day of the trip and I have to say I ve been eating better food,but is still good and defitenely worth the money
The food is very delicious. The atmosphere is very good. If you want to eat rare Thai food, you can find it here.

The first was a welcome drink!!! Nice Num Bai toey

The food is delicious and sweet…

Price suitable for the size dishes

This small, air-conditioned restaurant with only three tables provides an intimate and comfortable dining atmosphere. The dishes are exceptionally flavorful, clearly prepared with high-quality, fresh ingredients. Parking is conveniently available along the side of the owner’s house, adding a pleasant sense of local hospitality. Although the prices lean toward the higher end, the excellent taste and impressive quality make the experience worthwhile. Overall, it’s a charming spot for those who appreciate refined flavors in a cozy, tranquil setting.

Food - The flavors were absolutely spot on authentic and deeply satisfying.
Every dish was a burst of flavor and truly impressed by the quality of the seafood.

Service - The owner was very welcoming and tried her best to guide us through the menu, even though some descriptions were a bit hard to follow and not quite appropriate while she explained among two stranger customers at the same time.

Atmosphere - The space is quite small and can get a bit crowded, but it still manages to feel cozy and authentic.

A unique chef's table restaurant that I highly recommend for an authentic Thai dining experience.

It's reservation-only, and you'll need to make direct contact to book. They have some strict rules in place, which you'll learn about when you inquire, but they contribute to the focused dining atmosphere.

The menu changes seasonally, every three months, so you can experience a different set of dishes four times a year. A significant aspect is their commitment to local ingredients, particularly seafood caught daily from small local fisheries. Because of this, they're upfront about the act of nature potentially impacting pre-ordered items and ask you to select substitute options.

They focus on bringing back real local Thai dishes and cuisines. All dishes are served together, Thai-style feast, creating a communal dining experience. The chef's skill in combining ingredients and seasonings is incredible, resulting in delicious and authentic flavors.

Overall, it's a worthwhile experience to try all their seasonal menus.

This restaurant opened my mind to more knowing the local food of Thai Eastern. It isn't just the local food but it's the traditional menu and the cooking tips of family. The menu was cooking by Sea food ingredients so fresh and  increased more exciting of menu by local fruits whatever Mangoesteen, Coconut and Ma-Fai(Baccaurea ramiflora). All the bite that i've had, i can feel that Khun May and Khun Ploy (the owner and chef) made so much intend to cooking all menu which it's made me so happy and impressively. I really recommend, it's the restaurant you must try .

A small but warm restaurant, like your mother cooking for you. Fresh food, very tasty, very open experience. I like the rice topped with galangal, squid, and dried shrimp. Fresh ingredients from the boat by Chef May and Chef Ploy. #reservationonly

The restaurant offers a large selection of simple and yet very tasty Thai food, particularly for single dish meal, that has earned its place in the Michelin Guide.
Our most favourite dishes are pomelo salad, fried rice with pork crackling and acacia with pan fried mackerel, scrambled eggs with fish sauce stir-fried shrimps, and last but not least, the super tender and yummy roast duck breast with angkok. Desserts are good, but nothing exciting in our opinion.  Certainly a satisfying meal at reasonable prices. Parking is very tight and only for 3 cars.

Good taste of Thai food.
Small portions, 5-6 dishes for two.
Only private 3 car parking lot.

A restaurant that offers fine and delicious food with a pleasant atmosphere. The staff provide excellent service. However, the parking area is quite small, so during busy times, you may need to park nearby.

Jamn offers a genuine taste of Thailand with its chef's table approach that focuses on the subtle details of authentic cooking. The food is consistently impressive, with flavors that speak of the Damnoen Saduak area's unique culinary traditions.

Each dish is carefully introduced by the attentive staff, making every course informative and enjoyable. The ambiance is relaxed, making it an excellent choice for a quiet group gathering where the focus is on the shared experience of good food.

Don't miss out on the desserts—they're a highlight. And with a set menu that changes monthly, there's always a new delicacy to try. A tip for future diners: come hungry to make the most of the exceptional fare on offer at Jamn.

An understated yet memorable spot for those who appreciate the art of Thai cuisine.

A newly opened Thai restaurant with “Chef Noi” who has at least ten years of experience in cooking Thai food using original recipes from her family. The menu features delicious dishes that are hard to find in other restaurants, such as the very tasty “Gang Run Juan”. It is a must-try restaurant for Thai food lovers.

A wonderful experience with the 10-course menu. From the professional service and the chef’s confident, friendly explanations of each dish to the delicious and creative food, everything left me completely satisfied.

The restaurant area is spacious. The parking lot is large. The restroom is clean.

Truly a great experience. So much value given the price. Dishes were packed with flavor and presented so beautifully. A lot of the dishes were quite heavy and rich for me, personally, so it was really nice with a palette cleanser midway! Beautiful craft!

Been multiple tasting menus and Michelin stars, and I would say experience in the food, both eating and watching it being prepared, would say it's a Two Star Michelin. The chef really knows how to build on flavors with each course.

Culinary vision was thoughtfully carried out and represented on the journey. Chef played with both modern and classic flavors and ensured texture was a huge part of the experience.

Also the chef took her time to explain every dish and even talked to our group after dinner and explained her dream and her concent of "Friend's Table".

This is a must go if you are looking for a culinary experience.

We had a fantastic meal here. Even with all the reviews it still feels like we experienced something that’s only going to get more attention going forwards, as the quality and attention to detail is really excellent.

The owner makes a big effort to explain everything personally and I was impressed by how professionally the staff all work as a team, even if some of them are quite young.

It’s a bit of a whirlwind with ten courses in under two hours, but it didn’t feel rushed either. They close up pretty soon after the final desert, which was fine for us but maybe worth noting in case you’re expecting to stay chatting long after the meal. As other reviews mentioned, it’s a bit remote but the Grab drivers had no problem finding us.

Definitely recommend and we’d love to come back.

Had an amazing dinner at Friend’s Table. This mini vacation starts when you enter the compound where you are immediately greeted. Their is a group of 7 talented and dedicated people that support  the 10 guests where you are part of the kitchen. You can observe the details of each dish prepared. After the dishes are presented the chef goes to each table then explains each dish. This is an amazing experience in Chiang Mai. Thanks to all the people working at Friend's Table that made this a great experience.

Had a really good experience first visit at NavanNavan. Chef Van was friendly and showed a lot of passion in his food and the stories behind the food. The food was also delectable starting straight off the first course. The setting was casual also embodied by the chef’s repeated message that you can enjoy the food however you like. We had a memorable dining experience here. The transportation was slightly difficult to arrange but it’s totally worth it. Recommend to get hotel in Chiang Mai to book a 4 hour ride.

Tucked away in Martin, the place could be a bit hard to find in the evening. But NavanNavan is absolutely worth visitings. (And yes, I deliberately intentionally add the S to the “visitings”).

Bold is what I would like to describe the tasting menu of Chef Van. The dishes look simple, yet strong in the tastes. The meats, the fish, the vegetables, the fruits; they were all impeccably themselves in the best way.

My friend and I do enjoy all the dishes we had that day. We would absolutely love to be back, and I strongly recommend going to NavanNavan.

PS thank you the team for arranging such a late dinner for us. We are really glad that we made it there.

We were so happy to be here!!! At first we missed Chef Van’s a la carte but after we tried his course, we totally changed our mind! Food was incredible— natural / looks simple but have such a deep taste :)
He also has a la carte menu to order more!
Recommend to stay at Baan Myth if you would not like to drive back. Worth it!

Amazing. The finished food might be simple looking, but the journey to come about of each dish was priceless.   The team was friendly and accommodating.   The only tiny setback for me was the sequence of the dish.  But that was just my two cent.

The restaurant was a bit far out of stick.   It was already warned about the road to the restaurant.

Hideaway experience by chef Van. Located in middle of rice fields. My fav were Grill veg and cuttlefish salad that have very unique taste. Also the fish with pear as the sauce to light up the sweetness the one very good and burger as good as alway.

This restaurant at four season not has a big selection, but the dishes are impressive. I was enjoying the meal. The streaks were good. The selection of mocktail/cocktail are OK. But they were very delicious.
I think a good place to celebrate a special occasion.

Surprisingly great food, wonderful service, superb interior and a lovely, quiet ambience.

This is a true hidden gem in Bangkok.

As soon as our bums were in our faux leather booth and our ears registered the retro modern French music, we had forgotten about the traffic and the heat outside. We were transformed somewhere I can only describe as a Michelin Star chef’s private mansion in French Polynesia.

I’ll be honest, I am not normally a big fan of French cuisine. However, every dish we had at Palmier was both beautifully presented and tasty, without being overly oily.

The lobster is flown in directly from France twice a week and it was Fresh with a capital F. The steak was perfectly cooked and juicy and paired well with some incredibly well executed potato fries.

The side dishes did their job, but the true star of the meal for me was the hazelnut-chocolate ‘Paris Brest’ dessert.

A big part of the magic here is the Chao Phraya Estate - the palatial grounds housing luxury hotels and private residences by the riverside. You have to walk through the otherworldly Four Seasons hotel and its art exhibition to get to Palmier in the first place.

I came to dine at this restaurant with high expectations, as I had previously visited another restaurant in this hotel and was impressed. However, it didn’t turn out as I had hoped. The taste and presentation of the food were quite ordinary, and the prices were rather high. Personally, I don’t think it was worth the cost. That said, the atmosphere was nice, especially since I sat at a front table with a view of the river.
The food is surprisingly nice for this hidden gem. Did not see many customers during lunch, maybe that help to create the intimate ambience, where you can just have a chat with frds and order drinks.

Was there for dinner last night. The place was quiet and calm with gorgeous landscape lighting by the river. Dress was casual smart. The service was impeccable. The food (pigeon and squid in cream sauce) was outstanding. I want to go back again

A great 2025 Indian Michelin-listed restaurant. We were welcomed with a complimentary sparkling juice, which was a lovely and tasty touch. The food is excellent, with flavors that truly stand out. Prices are reasonable, and the staff is friendly and attentive. Overall, a fantastic dining experience.

We had such a lovely dinner ,everything from the flavours to the presentation was absolutely spot on.

We started with Pani Puri .Then came the set menu it was like a mini feast on a plate. Every dish was very nice.

The service was friendly, the ambiance was cozy.

I ordered bindi and asked for no onions. They put more onions than bindi. They literally gave me only onions with a little bindi inside.

I have tried to separate the bindi from the onions but it is not possible as it is all mixed.

I don’t understand how this place is highly rated. I lived in India, I know good Indian food, and this ain’t it. The staff were nice though, they let me order take away even though the restaurant had already closed. So I appreciate that.

But it was surely
not worth 500 baht. All I got were 2 rotis and mostly onions .

It's an easy 10/10. I review a lot, usually positive unless really bad. Indian by Nature has just blown me away with the quality delivered.
Chicken tikka....proper juicy, succulent, tasty chunks... and plenty of them. None of that tough rubbery nonsense.
Garlic nan....full of flavour and perfect for the sauce.
Tarka dal....probably the best I have had. Thick, creamy and super tasty. Beats the watery versions I have been used to.
It's been a few years since I was last in Indian by Nature....that was in the restaurant and was 100%....this takeaway was every bit as good....if not better.
I've tried the rest, honestly.... this is the best!

Went here as a group of 5 on march 26. Lovely place inside, great ambience. Service staff lovely, professional, attentive and kind.
Starter of chicken tikka for sure best I have had in Thailand. Samosa also superb. We all tried each others mains, the lamb maddrassi was first class. In over 20 years in Thailand this is the best Indian I have been to so far. Seriously amazing ... Cannot wait to go back.

Great food at this local spot. Soup was very tasty and the pork wontons had a great peppery flavor to them. Service was great, seated immediately and greeted. I don’t speak Thai, but we were able to communicate well enough. So far the best place off of the Michelin Guide in Phuket.
Delicious local noodle restaurant

From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere set the tone — elegant, warm, and inviting. The restaurant beautifully blends Thai and Indian cultures, especially the Baan Ruen Thai dining room and the garden room.

Each dish was a creative harmony of spice and aroma — Thai herbs met Indian masala in a way that felt both exciting and natural. The Summer curry  was unforgettable — fragrant, creamy, and perfectly balanced.

Service was attentive and knowledgeable; the staff explained the inspiration behind each dish, making the experience feel personal and thoughtful. Every detail, from presentation to plating, lived up to Michelin standards.

If you love both Thai and Indian cuisine, this restaurant is a masterpiece that celebrates both traditions while creating something entirely new. A must-visit for adventurous food lovers!

We love every single of their  crokery ！
​
​Looking forward to coming back!!!

I had the absolute pleasure of dining at this two-star restaurant, and it was without a doubt the best dining experience I’ve ever had. From start to finish, everything was flawless — the service was impeccable, attentive without being intrusive, and the staff made us feel genuinely welcome.

The ambiance was elegant yet warm, creating the perfect atmosphere to enjoy an unforgettable meal. And the menu — simply extraordinary. Every dish was a masterpiece, beautifully presented and bursting with creativity and flavor. Each course felt like a journey through taste and texture, leaving me amazed from the first bite to the last.

This restaurant truly deserves every bit of its reputation. I can’t recommend it highly enough — an exceptional experience in every possible way.

Gaa was my first fine dining experience in Bangkok and one of the more memorable restaurants I visited this year. The menu is beautifully presented, creative, and ambitious. Every dish looks refined, the service feels polished, and the experience carries a sense of occasion.

Yet for me, the food did not always land. It felt like the kitchen was trying so hard to be inventive that it sometimes missed the simple point that food should be delicious at heart. Most dishes impressed visually, but few stayed with me after the meal. The exception was the blue swimmer crab curry, which stood out as genuinely flavorful.

The desserts, however, left me disappointed. I believe the closing course in a tasting menu should deliver a moment to remember, but here it fell flat. On the other hand, the chaat at the start hinted at the meal’s potential and may have been the strongest expression of flavor.

Overall, Gaa is striking, sophisticated, and worth experiencing once. It shows a bold creative vision, even if not every plate hits the soul.

An unforgettable culinary journey at Gaa

As part of our honeymoon in Thailand, my wife and I decided to end the trip with dinner at Gaa, inspired by our deep love for Indian cuisine. We came in curious, and admittedly a bit skeptical, since for us, Indian food had always meant delicious, authentic street food. We weren’t sure how it would translate into a Michelin-star experience.

What we discovered was extraordinary. The meal was a true journey of flavors, creative, surprising, and absolutely unforgettable. Chef Garima Arora has crafted something remarkable here: a fine dining experience that celebrates the essence of Indian cuisine while elevating it to new heights.

Garima and her team were warm, professional, and attentive. We were guided by Pam, who was wonderful, knowledgeable, engaging, and truly enhanced our experience.

Thank you, Restaurant Gaa, for this exceptional evening. It was worth every baht, highly, highly recommended to anyone visiting Bangkok!

Great experience. The atmosphere and the design of the space was magnificent. We were greeted by welcoming staff and the servers were really well spoken and attended to us very well. We were impressed by a couple of dishes on the menu. By the end, we were really full but the deserts really completed the experience! We hope to be back again for the new menu!

This restaurant has some of the most flavourful Thai food I've ever had.

The dishes radiated vibrancy. You can see that there's a high attention to detail in every component of each dish. Little things like the browning on aromatics in the soup.

I recommend anyone in the area to try this restaurant. Expect flavourful, well-done dishes without any frills in decor or service.

Firstly I am posting photos of the menu as I couldn’t find it anywhere nor from any other review. Very local restaurant. Had the Pork stir fried with red chilli paste and it was delicious - also the Shrimps with chillies were  cooked to perfection ! Would definitely go back
The taste is delicious, the portions are large, it has been awarded Michelin for five consecutive years, and most of the customers are locals.
Little Michelin Bib Gourmand gem tucked away in Kathu.  Frequented by locals mainly.  Worth a visit.  Dishes are yummy.

Let’s face it, no one is here to sweat it out in a tin shack but the food is great - the southern fish yellow curry, prawns with stinky veg and fried mackerel are all winners. You won’t regret eating here but bring something to make you comfortable cos the wait is a min. of 20 mins and it’s hot in there

What a surprise. My first time in Bangkok and I directly went into this place because it smelled appetising and looked promising. We stepped in and got placed with a warm welcome. The Menu is neatly arranged and the offers sounds interesting. As a starter I had Pig Ear Terrine. A cold starter with kind of meat and asian spices and a vinaigtette with exactly my taste. My daughter had fried du k rice with mushrooms and an increable aroma of felt 100 spices with an additonal flavored fishsauce. I ha roast duck with noodles and with a full flavoured sauce with roasted peanuts. It was overwhelming as a rookie in original chinese kitchen. The price is bit higher than expected for Bangkok but absolutely worth it.

The duck meat really cooked well, not too hard when bite in mouth, it is nice and tasty. Lemon tea is too sour perhaps it has to mix with more syrups. Price of the meal is high. Environment of the restaurant designed with retro Chinese restaurant style.

Food was excellent, loved the retro Shanghainese vibes.

Perfect for meat lovers.

This place has also cool neon lights, if you re a neon lover.

Came because of the Michelin guide recommendation, was worth it!

Food was brought cold. And it’s lacking of seasoning. Sauces lack of flavor. Not authentic. Maybe good for tourist. Nevertheless the wait staff. Responded correctly and brought a second order. At the correct temperature . I wish this new restaurant all the luck and make sure the plates are hot so the food keeps warm until it’s served.

The restaurant is amazing.   Best red pork I’ve ever had.

Went upstairs after into the bar.   The tender is an alchemist and has gold in his ice in the drink.   Was amazing.
The Southern Thai food here is incredibly spicy, rich, and flavorful. Everything tastes delicious, and the quality of the ingredients is excellent.

Their fish and bamboo shoot curry is a must try (definitely super spicy and tangy). I also ordered Thai Basil Chicken, and though its not famous for that, surprisingly its one of the tastiest one I have tried across Thailand.

The “jungle curry” was quite the experience to try. It’s an extremely spicy southern sour sea bass curry with coconut shoots. Spiciest thing I had in all of Thailand. It was pretty good too, not on the level of tom yum or khao soi but it just felt so authentically thai and it’s definitely nothing i could ever get back home so I can’t not recommend it.

I also a stink bean curry with shrimp which was also very unusual to me. The stink beans had a very strange delayed aftertaste so I didn’t eat most of them, but other than that the sauce was delicious so I had no problem clearing the plate
It was introduced to me as Southern Thailand food. Michelin Guide 2025. I like the mixture of all the flavour in Thailand.

This restaurant specializes in southern cuisine. The dishes here are known for their spicy and flavorful taste. If you don't prefer spicy food, you can let the staff know when placing your order. There is a parking lot located opposite the restaurant, which can accommodate approximately 20 cars.

Absolutely worth it! Super fresh ingredients, sourced from the same supplier as Sushi Saito in Japan.

I especially love the Chirashi Don—the rice is unique and pairs perfectly with the fish.What impressed me most was how the rice temperature was adjusted for each dish to match the specific fish,showing incredible attention to detail and care.

The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, and all the staff are kind and very attentive.Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Japanese sushi. I will definitely come here again!

Loved the Uni here! The flavor is truly unique—unlike any other place I’ve tried. Highly recommend giving it a try!

Every ingredient was incredibly fresh, and the sauces were perfectly crafted to complement each type of fish. Every bite was beautifully balanced.

The chef was friendly and exceptionally attentive to every detail in the preparation.

It was my first time trying Sushi Saito—truly a 3-star Michelin experience.

The chef was warm and welcoming, and every piece was beautifully crafted.

I highly recommend booking the Full Omakase course with Uni.
It’s sweet, creamy, and has a unique flavor you won’t find anywhere else. Absolutely loved it!

An amazing Omakase course to remember. I booked in advance but it was relatively uncrowded so the experience was very private. The counter seats were great for displaying the chef's skill.

Food quality is outstanding. Every piece was fresh and high quality (especially the uni). The course was also quick for an omakase, which I quite liked. Not too slow. The Japanese chef is also highly skilled and knowledgeable.

I visited after seeing so many great reviews, and it was just as amazing as expected. Every bite was fresh and delicious.

The chef is incredibly detail-oriented, friendly, and welcoming. Some items may vary depending on the day, which makes the experience feel even more special.

The staff took great care of us, and the atmosphere was warm and relaxing. It’s also very easy to get to.
A famous Vietnamese steamed rice rolls restaurant in the province. Delicious, friendly service and affordable prices.
Fast and precise as a robot while she is making pak mor. The rice steamed flour was soft. Having with the sunny side up egg was superb for breakfast menu .

The shop we found from internet.

My partner were searching from internet as he like kind of this snack. After arrived,  no parking we have find somewhere else and walk to the restaurant instead.

Overall, just double check again.
"Pak Mor" that is eaten with sweet sauce. Strange and delicious. I've never seen anywhere. The insides are the same in every menu. Different in appearance

26 jan 2025

my first time tasting michelin guide restaurant

good food, cheap price, good service
Enjoyed thai desserts and drinks here. Custard apples in coconut cream and pumpkin dumplings with chestnut and barley were delicious. Good service.

Had time for a quick lunch and decided to give this a go. I had walked past them the day before. As I was dining alone, I could only try three dishes. I've had pomelo salads before, and even on this short trip, had it the day I arrived. The rendition here blew my mind, or rather my taste buds. No overly sweet sauce, just peanuts and fried onions. The taste was sensational and the texture as I was chewing, even more so. The beef cheek masaman curry was also very well done. The meat was soft and the tendon (or connective tissue) just melts on your tongue. The snakehead fish was good too. I always enjoy this when I can find it. All in all, a very nice way to spend my one free hour before heading to the airport.

Delicious food, located in a non busy area of the mall it gives you a much more peaceful experience than the standard mall dining.
Coconut taro dumplings with coconut milk and yam was delicious, the sauce was adequate for the amount of fish and if you like spicy many peppers are in the sauce. Perfectly cooked fish

Well, perhaps not the best of time during my visit on Mother’s Day. They could have been understaffed but looking for anyone to put in order was not the easiest when the restaurant probably had 4 tables occupied.

The decor is very quaint and they are located on the ground floor where the snack market and the gigantic food court are. I couldn’t find them the 1st round but it was easy to find coming down from the other escalator.

Everything that they put star on the menu was a safe choice from very good to excellent but the random fish’s innards soup wasn’t what I expected. I was expecting more umami and less bitter with more fish.
The crab meat in coconut milk is a must. That was delicious.
Located inside Central Embassy. The food was excellent, the plates, environment and surroundings were well decorated. It is worth a visit.

restaurant_name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
review_text: Fried Banana Rama 5 truly lives up to its reputation! Recognized with the Michelin Bib Gourmand from 2022 to 2025, this spot serves some of the best fried bananas in Thailand — perfectly crispy on the outside, soft and sweet inside, with a hint of coconut and sesame aroma. They’re surprisingly not oily at all, just light, fragrant, and delicious. Everything is freshly made and served hot. Simple, affordable, and absolutely worth the hype — a must-try local treat that represents the best of Thai street food!

restaurant_name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
review_text: If you're looking for an amazing, authentic Thai snack, this is the place. The fried bananas at Fried Banana Rama 5 are simply delicious. They are not too sweet and have the perfect crunch, with a fluffy texture inside. It's a simple snack, but they have perfected it. Worth the trip!

restaurant_name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
review_text: I tried the stall in One Bangkok food court. The quality of fried banana inconsistent, some hot and crunchy, some not. THB 60 per pack.

restaurant_name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
review_text:
Fried bananas are crunchy outside and soft inside, tasty snack. They also have lots of different delicious snacks: fried sweet potatoes, sweet potato balls (turned out to be my favorite thing here), mango muffins, lots of coconut sweets, even dumplings (delicious and fresh). There were so many things but because of language barrier we couldn’t find out what other snacks were ☺️

Good quality and cheap ☺️ we took two boats to get here and then a taxi from boat station (40 baht only) . It takes time to get here, but it was a nice boat trip with beautiful views and really cheap. This is a take out place but right across the street there’s a coffee place with aircon and cozy seats , lovely staff allowed us to eat our snacks after we bought ice drinks ☺️

They have other stores in the city but we wanted to try the original one.

restaurant_name: Fried Banana Rama 5 (Bang Kruai - Sai Noi Road)
review_text: There is a reason why this shop has a Michelin recommendation, the fried banana is crispy and not oily. And always warm and fresh, price wise very affordable, and because you need to expect a queue when you come here. While you are queueing up, you've might indulge yourself in some of other produce that they will sell.

Celebrating my 30th birthday at TAAN was nothing short of magical. From the moment my boyfriend and I stepped into the restaurant, we were enveloped in warm Thai hospitality and an atmosphere that struck the perfect balance between refined and relaxed.

We chose the 9-course tasting menu, and every dish felt like a love letter to Thailand — both familiar and completely new. The chef’s focus on locally and responsibly sourced ingredients shone through in every bite. Each course told a story about regional flavors, seasonal produce, and the people behind the ingredients.

Highlights included a stunning reinterpretation of classic Thai flavors — bold, balanced, and beautifully presented. The pacing of the meal was flawless, with just enough time to savor each course before being surprised by the next. The wine (and Thai-inspired cocktail) pairings elevated the entire experience without ever overshadowing the food.

What impressed me most was how TAAN manages to feel both deeply authentic and incredibly innovative. It’s fine dining, yes, but it’s also heartfelt — you can taste the respect for local farmers, for Thai culinary traditions, and for sustainability in every dish.

The staff made my birthday feel truly special, even adding a thoughtful personal touch to the dessert course. I left feeling celebrated, inspired, and deeply grateful for such a memorable evening.

If you’re in Bangkok and want a dining experience that celebrates the very best of modern Thai cuisine — TAAN is absolutely unmissable

Presentation and quality of food was refined and excellent. We were pleasantly surprised when the Thai Essence was served. There was good variety with so much to eat. And to top it all, we were served a delicious hazelnut chocolate cake and a special drink to celebrate our anniversary. Table service was quintessentially Thai… friendly, gentle and attentive. Thoroughly enjoyed the evening. Thumbs up!  We will be back here again when we come to Bangkok.

Amazing food with very nice view. Food was very aromatic with different use of herbs, definitely something we want to try in Thailand. The waitress explained each dish and its origin very well.

My only suggestion was that one of the junior waitress (who introduced us the water and drinks trolley) may need some training for working in a ‘fine-dining restaurant’. She seems a bit forceful without reading what their customers really want. The other lady who served us the dishes was very good.

Stunning ambience with a million-dollar view of the Bangkok skyline and excellent service from K. Suriya and team. The appetizers stood out, but the rest of the main course menu was average in flavor. Desserts were decent — the burnt cheesecake with sorbet was a highlight, though not as surprising as hoped. Overall, a pleasant evening with great conversations

Having heard much about this restaurant and seeing it listed in the Michelin Guide for several consecutive years, I came in with high expectations. Unfortunately, I found the experience a bit overrated.

Ordered the 9 course set. While the presentation and creativity of the dishes were certainly impressive, the flavors didn’t quite come together. The ingredients seemed thoughtfully chosen, but the combinations often felt forced or unbalanced, leaving the taste underwhelming despite the artistic effort.

That said, the service was attentive throughout the evening, and the atmosphere and city view was nice.

Overall, it’s a place that excels in concept and experience, but for me, the execution on flavor didn’t match the accolades. Worth a try if you’re curious, but perhaps not the culinary revelation it’s made out to be.

I came for the Peking Duck and it was outstanding! It’s served in 2 courses and I had the black pepper sautéed preparation for my second course.

The Peking duck was perfect—the grill on the skin was folded and crispy. Perfect ration of duck skin/green onion/cucumber and pancakes.

But the second course changed how I see duck for the best! The meat was so tender and juicy, the flavors well-balanced.

In 7+ years coming to Bangkok and many more of eating Peking Duck, this was a top tier meal!

**Restaurant Review: Wah Lok Restaurant in Bangkok**

If you’re seeking an exceptional dining experience in Bangkok, look no further than Wah Lok Restaurant. Renowned for its outstanding service and exquisite Cantonese cuisine, Wah Lok truly elevates your culinary experience to a top-tier level.

From the moment you step into the restaurant, you are welcomed by an atmosphere that exudes elegance and sophistication. The staff is attentive, polite, and knowledgeable, ensuring that every need is met with a smile. Their level of service is commendable, making you feel like a valued guest throughout your meal.

Now, let's talk about the food—Wah Lok’s Cantonese dishes are nothing short of spectacular. Each plate is a masterpiece, showcasing the traditional flavors and cooking techniques that define Cantonese cuisine. One dish that stands out is the Peking Duck. Cooked to perfection, the duck boasts crispy skin and tender meat, served with all the classic accompaniments. It’s a must-try that exemplifies the restaurant’s commitment to high-quality ingredients and culinary expertise.

Whether you’re a local or a visitor to Bangkok, Wah Lok Restaurant promises a memorable dining experience filled with delicious food and impeccable service. It's a true gem in the city's vibrant culinary scene!

Impeccable service at this well-known Michelin cantonese restaurant in Bangkok. Prices are reasonable for good quality cantonese cuisine, especially their Peking Duck.

Do take note that dimsum is available for lunch only, and unavailable for dinner. But there's a good selection of appetisers to choose in place of dimsum.

The food was cooked nicely and the service was good but guys - THERE IS NO MEAT IN THE DUCK PANCAKES. It is just skin! On what alternative planet / in which parallel reality is it OK to serve just duck skin for the pancakes? There is no precedent for this in China (where sometimes the prized crispy skin is served alone with sugar or garlic paste as a first course - not in pancakes) nor outside of China. How these other reviews are saying this is good or normal is beyond me. Their most famous dish is being served totally wrong and everyone is saying it’s amazing. Totally mad on all the levels and I’m genuinely worried that so many people are praising it online 😂😂😂

The Best Authentic  Chinese Restaurant in Bangkok 5 stars
Food: Good quality and tastes very nice and fantastic
Service: Good service, Professional and friendly
The Atmosphere are nice. We booked private room is quiet, clean, and comfortable.
We will come back again.

Chose Mia for a quiet yet luxurious dinner, and it was truly delivered. The ambiance was serene, perfect for a celebration. The vegetarian menu was thoughtfully curated, blending contemporary flavors with nostalgic touches that brought back fond memories. I especially enjoyed the artichoke and beetroot dishes — each bite was rich in texture and taste. The desserts were beautifully crafted, offering a perfect, indulgent finish to the meal. The service was attentive, adding to the overall exceptional experience. Mia is a must-visit for anyone seeking refined cuisine in an elegant setting.

An outstanding restaurant! Every dish is creative and full of layers of flavor. My favorite was the sea bass — the tender meat paired with curry was absolutely amazing. The main course was a bit too salty for my taste, but the bread and desserts were truly impressive and delicious — the best bread I’ve had in Thailand. I’ll definitely come back again for my birthday next year. Thank you for the warm hospitality!

Impressive! This is my third time here and the food keeps getting better and better, especially love their desserts and petit four. The food presentation and their attention to detail are outstanding. Particularly love their wine pairing, it comprises of wine from all over the world which makes it so fun and interesting. Each wine really complements each dish. The entire service team is super friendly and professional at the same time. We had a great time here and will definitely return.

Our Second Visit to Mia Restaurant – Just as Impressive as the First

This was our second time dining at Mia, and we went with the 8-course menu. Overall, the flavors of each dish were clear and well-executed, delicious, and beautifully presented.

Highlights for us included:

The Snacks: A great way to start the meal—full of bold flavors and absolutely delicious.

The Cod Fish: A standout dish. The fish was cooked perfectly, with a great texture and delicate flavor.

Dessert – White Lady: Beautiful presentation and the flavor was balanced and refined.

On top of the great food, the service was excellent. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, answering our questions in a friendly and professional manner.

Overall: Another memorable dining experience at Mia. Definitely worth coming back!

I was very satisfied with the delicious food and the calm yet pleasant atmosphere. I was surprised by the warm hospitality of all the staff and the thoughtful explanation of the dishes from the two main chefs. I’ve been to several Michelin-starred restaurants before, but I never felt such genuine sincerity.

In particular, I truly appreciated the care and attention from the server who took care of us. At first, I couldn't remember her name — she was a beautiful lady with long braids who spoke Korean — but later I found out her name was Emma, just like my English name. What a lovely coincidence!

Thanks to her, this meal will remain in my memory for a long time. And a heartfelt thank-you to the chef who cheerfully shouted “Happy 3rd Anniversary!” as we were leaving — such a fun and touching surprise.

The food was fantastic (I could have eaten ten plates of the grape cold starter alone!), but what really made this evening unforgettable was the warmth of the people. Thank you again.

It is a shop located deep in the road. When you drive in, you may feel surprised because the roadside does not look like there is a restaurant.But when you get to the shop, you will find that the shop is beautifully decorated and there are many customers.You will need to park behind the shop and walk to the front of the shop to find a table.The staff are very welcoming. There are 2 sides of the table, one with air conditioning and one without air conditioning.There are many menus to choose from. I chose a set menu that was already arranged for 1,000 baht.The set meal I chose had a total of 5 dishes, which was enough for me and my 4 friends to eat until we were full.All the food we received was very tasty.And even though the shop is in the province, it's hard to believe that the shop accepts credit cards.Overall I was very impressed and will definitely be back.

I had a wonderful experience at Khlang Na Pla Khao. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The fish dishes were especially delicious — perfectly cooked and seasoned. The atmosphere is cozy and relaxing, with a nice view of the surrounding nature. The staff were friendly, welcoming, and very attentive. Definitely a place I would recommend to anyone looking for great food and a warm, local dining experience.
