Great place for traditional Thai food, great selection and variety of dishes. Right beside some rice paddy fields, has a  lovely atmosphere in the evening, had had local guitar/band playing . Slightly off the main roads, but just follow Google maps
Every dishes are so yummy. Only thing that was quite annoying was a small piece of paper with the plate which I think they should takeout.

The shop is a little away from the main road. The route is a bit complicated, but you can follow Google Maps. It's not difficult to get to, but the roads are bad and rough. The food is delicious and the prices are reasonable. The atmosphere is good. In the middle of a rice field When it gets dark, there will be a lot of mosquitoes. But the shop has a large fan available. The air is well ventilated, not hot.

Best Thai food in Chiangmai. You can feel the love and dedication through the food. Highly recommend for pork ribs, fish coconut curry, salacca and prawn soup (which is not tom yum goong), and durian ice cream.
Worth every baht you spend there.

This is truly a Michelin-starred restaurant! The service is excellent, the staff are very friendly, the environment is great, and the food is delicious! I ordered three dishes and they were all tasty! I recommend pork eggplant, curry crab meat, and tom yum soup! The portion size is not large, so the price is a bit high, and there is no free ice water.

Nice thai food - the morning glory is good and must ask for abit spicy!

The omelette with pork is good too!
Nice ambience with friendly staff, good to cool off in a hot day!
Worth a visit!

Just great in every way - service, food, and atmosphere. Definitely Michelin worthy.
Tanya is amazing in explaining all the dishes and helping us picking additional dishes to complement our selections.
Highly recommend.

We had a blast, there make sure to eat and try some delicious food.

Tanya and Pala were very nice to us and explain a lot of the vision of the restaurant and the owner.

Food was really good, we order some Indonesian dishes.

Make sure to support and help the foundation that they support. The cute cup holders are made there.

Can wait to be back!

I celebrated my birthday here!

The food was fantastic. We initially came here because we heard the chef used to be the head chef of Water Library so we came to check it out.

Plating was beautifully done and the taste was perfect! I love that they are all small portions so we get to try a lot of dishes! Overall a great experience!

A well-deserved Michelin star for Avant! The entire meal was fantastic, showcasing a strong commitment to quality ingredients. While a few dishes felt a little crowded with too many components, the overall experience was excellent. The standouts were definitely the Unji and Akemo dishes—they were truly unique and memorable. The staff was friendly, professional, and made my birthday celebration feel incredibly special. A truly great place to visit.

Definitely worthy of 1star in terms of the techniques shown and attempt to elevate the dishes.  A bit of a pity due to clashing flavours and having too many things going on in most dishes. Overused of decorative flowers. A bit of a waste for natural tastes of the good ingredients to be overwhelmed instead of complemented by the sauces.

Bread was absolutely fabulous. Chef engagement was great.
All the best!

My favorite restaurant of the year… well deserved for the recent 1-star Michelin award. The chef was so creative and his menus are very unique, interesting, and yummy. None of the dish that I don’t like and I love many. The main desserts and the 36 months Comte was MVP. Definitely worth a try and coming back as he will keep changing his menu based on seasonal ingredients.

I went to a restaurant that was on the “world’s 50 best” list in Bangkok the night before I went to AVANT. Let me tell you, AVANT was miles ahead of them in every single aspect of quality from the service, the ambiance, and most importantly the food. It was one of the best meals I’ve ever had in a fine dining establishment and it currently ranks number 2 on my Beli list. If you are in Bangkok, it would be regrettable not to try for a reservation.

Highly recommended by locals, and it’s easy to see why it has earned its popularity because it focuses on strong and bold  traditional flavors dishes.The restaurant are packed with people in the weekend, if come in group then reserve is recommend (otherwise you have the option to pay 30THB per person to go to the air conditioner room) and other everything in one go otherwise the queue will definitely delay.

The standout for me was the squid ink squid,  texture of the squid was tender without being rubbery.

This was our second time here. I can't say enough about how delicious the food was, as well as being very reasonably priced. It's a bit out of the way from the tourist spots in Pattaya but we'll worth a visit
This restaurant serves small portions, so you can order many dishes. The food is delicious, the prices are friendly, and the ingredients are fresh and high-quality

I went to this place from review. It’s bigger than I expected. All the table are full at peak hour so I recommend you come early and there’s no air condition. If you want to sit in the room with air condition, you need to pay extra 30 bath for that service. The outside is not that hot but still not chill enough. However, the food test great so that’s the whole purpose of being here.

Really recommend the Stir-fried squid with back sauce!

And lastly, it’s a local restaurant so everything is super affordable!

Sure, it’s a Michelin Guide place, and if you’re in Pattaya, it’s definitely worth giving it a try.
That said, maybe we didn’t order the right dishes when we visited. We might come back again to see if we missed something!
The service was good though as the staff were friendly and quite attentive.

We made our way here today for a late lunch cos I wanted to try another Michelin Guide establishment. This was our 3rd Bib Gourmand which was located in Jomtien.

I had ordered 2 mixed beef noodles (for me and my wife). I had the medium sized bowl with kueh teow while my wife had the small bowl with sen lek. We had also ordered 2 watermelon smoothies when we saw they had it on the menu.

The beef was very fresh and you could taste the quality of the meat. The “restaurant” definately lived up to its hype. FYI - the restaurant also serves Thai food if you don’t feel like having noodles.

I would recommend this place if you are near the Jomtien area as it’s not very far away from the beach.

Like others have said get their house specialty steak soup that has to do with the very thin high-quality steak or beef. Very thin and tender. It's very good and you can see pictures here on the website. It's very good the meat is ultra good.  We also got another soup that had fish balls, beef, vegetables and I think pork. That too was very good. The place is very clean the people who work there are wonderful and will tell you about the food and the experience is exceptional. This is a 10 out of 10 restaurant. If it helps I am foreigner and my girlfriend is Thai and we both loved it. We live nearby and we will probably eat here a couple times a week 🙏
Cheap prices and delicious food that's simple formula for Michelin plate. Inside is clean and service is polite. Highly recommend to eat here.
Very relaxed and friendly Michelin Gourmand rated eatery. Owner Is very friendly. Soup was tasty and really good quality. Very well minted and high standard of hygiene.

Food was 5/5
Drinks were 5/5 too!

It's a no frill place to get good quality beef. We tried their noodles both the soupy one and dry one. Didn't disappoint at all.

Place was super clean. Service was good and quick. Many cats around the area and they are friendly.

Super affordable if you consider the high quality of beef they use.

The watermelon slushie was heavenly. It's very refreshing for the hot summer weather. What makes it even better is it has No sugar, no ice, all natural. Try yourself and you will agree.

Will come back again and hope to meet Jiew the cat again ;)

It a good chicken rice but not the best . A far away from town. So if you are in the near it ok to come.But if you have to come from far.It not worth .Since in BKK got a lot of good chicken rice or even better if you need a good place not only follow Michelin guidelines

Easy-going, traditional settings restaurant of how chicken rice restaurant should be, where you will expect no A/C. Since there is no wall, wind will do the work on the hot day. But come to the chicken rice, this place is exceptional, this restaurant rise to my top chicken rice list. There are 2 types of chicken, singapore’s and traditional, I haven’t try the traditional but I think the different is the sauce and dip (may be next time), but the place is far from where I live (Samutprakan), but I’m certain that I’ll find a chance to go there again. Please find a chance to try as well.

PS. It open around 8 am and chickens is runs out around 10 am, thus, plan carefully.
PS1. The price is very reasonable for me. And try chicken joint!!!

The chicken thigh meat is tender, reminiscent of a fine dining restaurant or an international recipe. The rice is perfectly cooked—not too oily, not too hard, and not too mushy. The liver is fragrant and delicious, cooked to perfection. The dipping sauce is bold and flavorful, and the soup is well-balanced.

Really good chicken rice, worth for long journey. A bit difficult for queing and ordering systsm, once understand the system okay. Both singapore version and hainan version are good. Well cook rice and tender chicken. Chicken liver is also good. One room toilet may not suitable for busy customer in peak time.
All good

The local food restaurant in the Phuket city. If you want to go in weekend, I would like to recommend to come early before noon. The most delicious menu for me is “Moo Hong”. And the staffs in this restaurant are very kind and humble. Really love it.

Food was 10/10

Amazing authentic Southern taste. Every taste was super saturated and intense.

We went on a weekend evening, we were able to get the last parking spot in their lot with a wait of 2 groups ahead of us.

Food was very delicious but extremely slow. I think because it was quite busy that evening but I wish they can manage to get a little more efficient since they’re quite popular.

Kua Kling was extremely spicy, even for a spicy lover native Thai like me. Just thread with your own caution. The staffs already let us know it will be very spicy, I appreciate the heads up!

No AC but the fan was able to keep us breezy during the rainy wind.

This is another go-to restaurant in Phuket that I genuinely have to visit every single time! It's all thanks to the intense, bold flavors, charming prices, and, most importantly, excellent ingredients served without holding back.

Every Southern Thai dish here is incredibly "authentic" and well-executed. The curries, in particular, are packed with flavor and truly spicy. If you're not great with heat, you might want to let the staff know when you order.

For all these reasons, this place has become an absolute favorite of ours! Just a small heads-up: if you come in the evening, it can get quite busy, so you might need to circle a bit to find parking.

Here is my first time in Phuket, and after researching the best restaurants in Phuket, my friends and I decided to try this restaurant before my flight back to Bangkok.
Here are some local dishes on our table, which looked delicious.

Especially the crab curry with rice vermicelli is my favourite dish. I’ve never had the taste of curry in Bangkok, but chef cooked the curry sauce perfectly with crab meat 🦀.

My second favourite dish is stir-fried Malindjo leaves with eggs; it’s a good combination of vegetables fried with eggs. This is a must-try menu as well; it’s one of the local vegetables in southern Thailand. 🥬🍳

Overall, for the dishes I tried, it was impressive with the authentic Southern food; the taste of curry that they made was flavoured.
Thank you for the nice recommendation and service from the staff as well; they are genuinely kind and welcoming. 🙏🏻☺️

The food was incredibly delicious and comforting, made with only the finest, raw ingredients. This place offers amazing and thoughtful service. If you’re in the area, I highly recommend checking it out! If you come around noon prepared to wait an hour!

What an amazing restaurant! Went today and had the special jay menu during the jay festival. It was absolutely delicious! You can really tell the amount of labor and dedication that goes into making the dishes. I’m so happy that they have a vegan option all year round. Will definitely be back!

Absolutely exceptional! Our dinner at Igniv Bangkok was a true culinary delight from start to finish. The tasting menu showcased imaginative and beautifully balanced flavour profiles - every dish felt thoughtfully crafted, with high-quality ingredients shining in creative combinations. The staff was extremely helpful, attentive, and genuinely friendly, contributing to the seamless, enjoyable evening. What stood out was the relaxed yet refined atmosphere; it’s the perfect blend of fine dining and comfort. Without a doubt, this was our best fine dining experience so far, and we’re already looking forward to coming back. Highly recommended!

My first time at the Swiss-influenced Restaurants. Great food, great Swiss wines that you can taste by glass.

The combination of food and wines was memorable.

The chef and Sommerlier were very nice and shared with you the detailed story of each wine.

The Summer Tasting Menu was a stunning celebration of seasonal flavors.

Every shared dish was beautifully balanced — fresh and inventive. The service was doing an amazing job, always there when you needed them.

The signature Candy Store at the end added a perfect touch of joy.

An absolute gem. The meal started off with an amuse bouche. Each bite was briefly described and we were recommended to eat them in order, but they under-sold the experience. I knew I was in for a treat as soon as I started with the lobster kadaifi. Each of the four snacks were just sublime but the Egg Royal was a favorite. The asparagus starter was recommended and rightfully so -- it was so good that I mopped up the remaining traces of sauce with a bite of bread. Was excited to try pizokel, which was new to me, and it was well executed but not particularly rememberable. The red mullet with crispy chorizo more than made up for it. We were each served a side of polenta which helped to alternate between flavors. The restaurant has an  intimate vibe with a beautiful glass wine cellar and garden view (where herbs for the menu are grown). Service was impeccable with glasses kept full and tableware quickly rotated. At the end of lunch we were taken to a dessert/candy cart and encouraged to fill up a small take-away container. I will definitely be back to try more of the menu.

View of the Wat Ratchaburana was awesome, and the chicken noodle soup was definitely extremely value for money. It had more ingredients (chicken) than the actual noodles, and would highly recommend it!

~ hello from sunny ☀️ Singapore, May 2025
Chicken noodle soup 60 baht. So tasty, very filling. I was very hungry and one bowl did the job. Very satisfying, loads of chicken! Great service, nice views, plenty of space.

I’m not joking! This was the best meal we’ve had in our 5 week stay in Thailand! And such a good price and amazing service! The service girl has absolutely excellent attitude and English! 😍 thank you so much!

Highly recommended. I ordered a padthai and a noodle soup. The waiteress warned me, if i really want both because its a lot. I wondered, because i often ordered 2 or 3 dishes and never got a warning. When its served i understood, the portion is big. Big bowl of soup and the padthai more than the double you usually get. And in the soup was so much chicken, it must be 1/2 of a whole chicken and only pure meat. The padthai came with a lot peanuts in an extra bowl. The taste was just good.   The Coke in can was 15 (!) Baht... Thats cheaper than 7/11.... It will be maybe not the best food in your life but i doubt you will find a better value for money for good food.

And ... You sit in front of a world heritage site and enjoy the view

Amazing food the best food I had in Thailand
Incredible chicken noodle soup ended up adding on 4 more extra noodles (10B each)
That one lady giving 4 star has no taste of food btw
This is 10/10 just go here super reasonable price too I would pay way more for this

Visited 3 times in April 2025.

This is an incredible Thai restaurant with a homely atmosphere. It was walking distance from where I was staying so that's how I stumbled upon the place. And boy was that a good decision.

The Pad Krapao Moo is super reliable and always well made. It's definitely on the spicier side (which is how it should be I would say) so let them know if you don't want it super spicy.

I tried a couple of salads here and it was my first time trying any Thai salad that was not a Som Tam. I got one with Chinese sausage - the savouriness and chewiness of the sausage really goes well with the freshness of the cucumbers, tomatoes and onions. Their salad vinegarette is incredible and the tomatoes they use are so fresh and tasty. I wonder what a Marinara sauce made with these tomatoes would taste like, they were that flavourful.

I also tried a boiled shrimp salad, which was very good but I wish they'd seasoned the shrimp separately so it would've gone well with the fresh vegetables.

Tried the turmeric (that's what it said in the menu, maybe it was part of the batter?) fried fish. I don't remember now if it was a mackerel, sea bream or grouper but the pieces were flaky, perfectly seasoned and fried to a crisp.

They do have an English menu on request but I couldn't shake the feeling that it didn't have all the dishes. I think the clams or mussels are really famous here but I didn't get to try because the portion looked quite large and I was dining by myself.

A Thai-style restaurant offering delicious seafood dishes, each menu item is flavorful and satisfying. The prices are quite reasonable. Highly recommended are the stir-fried clams with chili paste and crispy fried pork belly. Pair them with steaming hot rice for an absolutely delightful meal!

A local eatery that has a few Michelin related awards! However, at least for me, this is a place where locals go for simple dishes that otherwise  they probably cook at home. We can see mostly locals when we were there. The staff are very accommodating. They did go out of their way to dig out and clean a few wine glasses for us to enjoy Pinot Bianco with the foods!

A local Thai restaurant that serves Thai foods. This restaurant also got in a Michelin Guide.

I tried their famous fried mackerel fish with soy sauce, and that was the best fried mackerel I have ever tasted. The mackerel is crispy outside and very tender + juicy inside.

That fried mackerel is a must try menu!

The food was authentic and excellent! Michelin star well deserved. It is quite spicy. I really liked the overall atmosphere of the restaurant. It was like sitting on a streetcorner. We were the only tourist group there. Almost full restaurant. Only one waitress spoke English. They all were very nice though. This is a must visit in Phuket!

Solo dining. Excellent attentive service, well paced meals. Burst of flavor in every bite. Chef created a tour of Thailand, with local ingredients and classic recipes presented in fine dining format. All well explained, and I had a chance to see some of the raw materials used, staff was fantastic in answering my queries.

Some I really loved, some not so much- but that’s personal taste. Remarkable wine pairing.
Had the chance to try something exotic (for me!)- crocodile tongue!
Highly recommend to anyone who wants to try Thai fine dining!
Final souvenir with small bottles of mango jam and chilli was so thoughtful

A pretty central location for this fine dining restaurant.
Went for a 11-course set dinner for a rather large table of 12 persons.
Atmosphere is slightly underwhelming in the private room which really offers nothing special.
Luckily  the chef is able to surprise with some creative dishes. Some are outstanding while others belong to the "good effort" category. Overall, we had a good time...
Service was absolutely first class and the story telling is second to none.
Keep it up !

Authentic Gem Thai Fine Dining @ Khaan 💫

First time here and it was mind-blowing! 🤯
From the presentation — every dish was crafted with such passion and precision, full of flavours taste to your palette. The ambience is elegant yet private, service team is warm and attentive.

Dining at Khaan was truly a next level unforgettable experience!!! Enjoy the whole visit with my family! Highly recommended you guys to try! 😋♥️

We had such a wonderful experience at Khaan. Thai flavors are something we already love, but here they were elevated. Thai dishes reimagined in a WHOLE NEW WAY. The team was incredibly hospitable, really nice and attentive, and the ambiance gave you a sense of space, so you could focus on your table and fully enjoy the experience they were serving you. Every ingredient was thoughtfully sourced locally, which made each bite feel even more authentic and special. 🙏🏼

I dont want to call the feeling of eating at this restaurant a scam because that would be too harsh. But it's fair to say spending an evening here is an incredible waste of money and time. If you enjoy very little food and a very nice lady tells you a story about every dish in broken English, then this might be for you.

Lets talk about the dishes. Its not bad but not good either. I was with wife at the North restaurant the other night for their course meal. If food at the North can be rated at 8.5/10, then food here is 4.5 at best. Its not that tasty and portion is laughablely underwhelming. To call this 11 course meal is a crime in itself. We also ordered the tea pairing and juice pairing. It was a huge disappointment. It didnt elevate the paring dish in anyway and one of the green color coconut juicy tasted straight up gross.

Then let's talk about value. Me and wife had two course meal for 3850 each plus tea paring at 690 and juicy paring at 980. Plus tax and service fee. Everything comes out 11240. The entire experience was so bad that we asked to just send out rest of 3 dishes together to save time so we can make it to another restaurant before it is closed.

I can't understand why there are so many good reviews. Maybe it's emperors new cloth kinda of situation. People convinced themselves is good because they are told its good. But If you ask for my honest opinion, I say its 2.5 of 10. Food is pretentious and subpar. Its the most disappointing restaurant we ever visited in Bangkok. The only good thing I can say is the staffs are very friendly.

We went to PRU to celebrate my boyfriend’s birthday and had such a special evening. It really felt like stepping into a whole new food experience with a Michelin One Star Chef.
The drive from Chalong took about an hour and it was raining, but the restaurant was beautiful and welcoming once we arrived. Huge thanks to Alberto, Khun Ton, and Khun Jennifer for the warm service and thoughtful arrangements, they really made us feel comfortable the whole time.
We really enjoyed the way they presented the raw ingredients before each course, and the team did a great job introducing the dishes together with the chefs. The garden-to-table vegetables were excellent, and the non-alcoholic pairing was a lovely touch that went perfectly with the menu.
The timing between each course kept us excited to see what would come next. Not every dish was exactly to our taste, but overall it was a memorable experience — and the little birthday ice cream at the end made it extra sweet.

an absolute joy and experience dining here. we were served by the most professional and attentive team!  we had the opportunity to visit the kitchen, where the food prep was eye opening. we were also pleased to learn how they minimised food waste by creating new purposes for parts of the ingredients that would otherwise be discard, sustainability was on the top of their priorities. view was gorgeous of course and we will return another time perhaps in the evening to catch it with sunset. The wood that was used to smoke the meat added a lovely scent to the whole place. one of us were particularly enamoured by a local fruit that we never had before, and the chef surprised us by an extra serving it right at the end. all these little touches were wonderful, thank you!

A must-do for any foodie visiting Phuket.
PRU is more than a restaurant — it’s an experience. Every dish is a masterclass in refinement, showcasing local ingredients elevated through months (and often years) of thoughtful development. The flavours are everything delicate and subtle to bold and inventive, making it utterly unforgettable. From the story behind each plate to the flawless execution, this was easily one of the most memorable meals I’ve ever had. The team behind the experience are warm, friendly and generous with their knowledge! Loved it!

Summary:

- Complex and inventive food that often strays into “challenging” territory, for better or worse.
- Warm, professional service. Beautiful space.
- Overpriced?

Service:

Excellent, from start to finish. Not just warm and friendly, which is par for the course in Thailand, but professional, engaging and attentive. Thank you!

Food:

Photos below.

Everything is carefully prepared and beautifully plated in the open-plan kitchen, with many of the ingredients coming from Pru’s nearby farm.

I unreservedly enjoyed 4 of the 8 dishes that we were served: the orange curry, lobster, and aged duck being standouts for me.

The other half of the meal left me with mixed feelings.

Setting aside the amuse bouche and petit fours, which played it quite safe, the first and last courses are a durian dish (an infamously love-it-or-hate-it delicacy), and a kimchi ice cream (the second to last dish, also a dessert, included shallot ice cream with sweetened fish sauce).

Pru describes itself online as serving inventive food.  It does, for sure, but I think that a few too many of the dishes stray into challenging territory, and perhaps intentionally so - the kimchi ice cream was introduced as something they made “because they could”; the shallot ice cream because “why not?.  This was all meant in good humour, and the chefs are very charming, but it’s a slightly unusual ethos. Art for the artist, I guess.

In conclusion, whilst I do appreciate experimentation in fine dining, especially in “awardsy” type tasting menus, I still want the majority of what I’m served to be, for lack of a better description… delicious. I can’t say that  Pru wholly delivered in this respect, although there were individual dishes that I loved.

All very subjective, I know, and my girlfriend felt differently, happy to view it as more an artistic experience than a traditional meal.

Pricing:

We paid USD700 for two, including two glasses of champagne and three glasses of wine (total, not each). This is more or less what I would expect to pay in Singapore or Hong Kong, for something similar, but an equivalent restaurant in those cities would be likely to have higher overheads (e.g., big city rent and more imported ingredients). USD5-600 would have felt fairer, but the place is busy, with few direct competitors, and Phuket is booming. The demand is clearly there.

Nice and Comfortable Atmosphere just like other Michelin star restaurant and portion control is the main factor of the restaurant like this. (Optional either GAIA (More into Vegan) or PRU (Main Option non vegan) Restaurant will be opened From 18:00 - 22:30 and 4 hours time spent in eating there. Staff will great you in front and Escort you in every places (Entering restaurant, lounge, main dining, etc)
One of the best omakase ive had in bangkok. The staff is friendly, chef is very professional, and food is awesome. They only serve 6 seatings per day.

Sushi Saryu is one of my favorite omakase restaurants in Bangkok. With just 8 seats, the restaurant offers an intimate experience and is willing to accommodate private bookings for groups of 6 or more. They only open for one seating per day, so I highly recommend reserving in advance. The chef is not only friendly but also meticulous, and the staff pays great attention to detail. The ingredients are exceptionally fresh, as the chef sources seasonal selections directly from Japan’s fish markets.

The granddaddy of omakase in Bangkok has finally been conquered after months of anticipation. Patrons familiar with Sushi Saryu will recognize its renowned reputation for delivering some of the finest omakase in the city. Well, ladies and gents, suffice it to say that Chef Sudo does deliver on the hype. Every bite is meticulously crafted by him alone and the quality speaks for itself. Freshness from premium fish like nodoguro, kinmedai, and abalone was an absolute delight. He also excels with hybrid pieces like the snow crab and anko fish mix which packs a powerful punch.

Now my reason for knocking off a star. While the flavors were there the overall symphony did not leave a lasting impression. My dinner party and I were left feeling somewhat unfulfilled and there was not a single bite that gave us that rare omakase ohooo ahaaa moment, though I will refrain from naming those special places that have. Also the corkage charge for a big magnum? Understandable but absolutely insane. There should be a policy that allows an opening fee waiver if you purchase a bottle from the shop. Just something to think about.

Tonight was a wonderful night of dinner with my husband on our anniversary night.  I have spent many happy moments eating at Sushi Saryu. All the ingredients for sushi here are fresh.  Personally, I liked Nodogudo. I even had to ask for one more bite. I also liked the uniqueness of the restaurant with only one chef serving the food, which made me understand the attention to detail that the chef gave me.  There are also staff, they explain about the food in each dish what is chef be service us and all staff have very good service.  It made me realize the delicacy of eating sushi to a whole level.

I recently dined at Sushi Saryu with good friends of mine and it was a fantastic omakase experience from start to finish. The intimate setting made it feel like I was having a private culinary journey through Japan, right here in Bangkok The ambiance was elegant yet cozy, with soft lighting that perfectly set the mood for an exquisite meal.

Food & Presentation: Each dish was a work of art, skillfully crafted by the chef right before my eyes. The sashimi was incredibly fresh, with the perfect balance of texture and flavor. Highlights included the melt-in-your-mouth otoro and the delicate uni, which had a rich, creamy taste that lingered beautifully. Every course was thoughtfully plated, making each piece almost too beautiful to eat.

Service: The chef and staff were attentive and friendly, guiding us through each dish’s origins and preparation. I appreciated their passion and knowledge, as it added depth to the overall experience. The pacing of the meal was spot on, allowing just enough time to savor each bite before moving on to the next delightful course.

Atmosphere: The small, intimate seating arrangement allowed for a closer connection with the chef and the artistry behind each dish. It felt like a very personal and engaging dining experience. The background music was subtle, letting the focus remain on the food and the dining experience itself.

Value: While omakase can be a bit of a splurge, I felt that sushi saryu offered excellent value for the quality and craftsmanship of the meal. It’s definitely worth treating yourself to if you’re a fan of sushi and Japanese cuisine.

Overall: If you’re looking for an authentic omakase experience where each bite transports you to Japan, I highly recommend here I’ll definitely be back for another visit!

Stylish steakhouse with a great selection of Wagyu and premium cuts. I loved being able to choose both the cut and even the knife. My steak was perfectly cooked: juicy, flavorful, and tender. The trio of salts (Thai sea salt, Himalayan pink, Mongolian brown) was a thoughtful touch that elevated every bite. The space is elegant and service is professional, though prices are definitely on the higher side. The cheese dessert is an absolute must try: I’ve never had anything close to it before. A good spot for a special night out in Phuket.

“The Sunday brunch at Wagu Steak House is exceptional. The food selection is premium, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, and it truly makes for the perfect weekend experience. Special thanks to Khun Khem and Khun Aek for their excellent service.”

# Wagyu Steakhouse Phuket Review: An Impressive Fine Dining Experience

## Just went yesterday! 🥩

: This place is worth every baht! Great atmosphere, excellent food, and options for every budget.

-----

## First Impressions

Loved the atmosphere the moment I arrived. The garden in front of the restaurant is beautiful and lush, making you feel relaxed before even entering. The bartender recommended cocktails to start with. I went with a basic gin - simple but well-made.

**The wine room = absolute highlight!** I requested a table in the middle of the wine storage room because I love that atmosphere. Surrounded by vintage wine bottles, it feels like sitting in a European wine cellar. Soft lighting and attentive service throughout.

-----

## Menu Selection - From Budget-Friendly to Sky’s the Limit

You can enjoy this place even if you’re not looking to spend a fortune. They have options ranging from budget-conscious to unlimited budget dining.

Tried the **Thai Jasmine Wagyu** - Thai beef at world-class level. Absolutely beautiful presentation and taste.

**The Good News**: You don’t need to order expensive items to have a great meal, but if you want to try premium offerings, they have plenty of choices.

-----

## Things to Know

- Book your table in advance (especially for the wine room)
- If coming with children, only available 5:30-7:30pm
- No valet parking - you’ll need to park yourself

-----

## Summary

**Perfect for**: Anniversaries, business dinners, special occasions, or anyone who wants to try genuinely good beef.

**Will I go again?**: Absolutely!

**Rating**: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
**Recommended budget**: 2,500-4,000 baht per person for a great experience

We had a wonderful evening at Wagyu Steakhouse. The service was truly top-notch — attentive, professional, and warm. The cocktails were delicious and well-crafted, and the atmosphere was both pleasant and perfectly suited for a relaxing dinner.
While the steaks were slightly overcooked despite ordering them medium rare, everything else was excellent and enjoyable. Overall, it was a great experience. Thank you!

Traveled all the way there for the Japanese Miyazaki Wagyu A4 (grain & corn-fed), escargot, and foie gras.
The taste was great .. but it took almost an hour for the steak to arrive.

Pa Porn Tom Yum Noodle is a local gem recognized by the Michelin Guide. The flavors are authentically Thai, and the prices are very friendly. Their signature bowl comes with red pork and bouncy meatballs, served in a tom yum soup that’s slightly sweet, followed by savory notes, with a mild tang and just a touch of spice.

They also offer tasty side dishes like fried meatballs, fish cakes, steamed dumplings, and Thai-style snacks and souvenirs.

If you go during peak hours, it can get quite busy and the wait may be a bit long. The indoor area can feel quite warm, especially on hot days — so plan your visit accordingly!

This local noodle spot offers an interesting experience. Despite often being packed, a morning arrival can be surprisingly peaceful. The noodles have a noticeably sweet taste, and a good variety of side dishes are available to order. This establishment also holds a Michelin recognition.

Delicious noodles with generous portions and great value for money. The roasted red pork is especially tender and flavorful, and the deep-fried fish cakes are also a must-try. Ordering is easy via QR code. It can get busy around lunchtime, so expect a wait. Parking is along the street, and some locals offer spots in front of their homes for 20 baht.

Nothing special here.
Food is soaked with oil. Taste no special.
No sauces are available here like spicy or ketchup.

I the menu the food costs 70 bhat. They asked in cashier 100 baht. I didn't agree to pay, you also don't agree to pay prices higher than the menu indicated.

Not recommended...
Ba Mee (Pork noodle) very delicious, Thai tea with milk very smooth and good to drink when eating together with the fried fish-paste balls.

I had the chance to dine here January 2025. From the moment you walk in you are taken on an amazing food journey. I would say this restaurant is worthy of 1 or 2 Michelin stars. The view and setting are one of a kind. The food is exciting and creative. The wine list was spectacular. I would happily return and I encourage you to go and experience their hospitality.

The food was wonderful. However, I think too much was given for chance of complain, e.g. the dish with 4 finger food (Peanut relish, … thai green banana chilli relish … fermented fish … sweet dancing shrimp)was of my favor and the ocra and star fruit with the fish was not too good either.

The presentation was great. I love seeing all ingredients. Just be a little careful as one came with a small cockroach.

It is still 9.5/10!

Highly recommend this place!
Authentic Thai flavors with a modern twist — everything was beautifully balanced. The dishes were packed with flavor, and the ambiance truly reflects the charm of Thai culture.
Perfect spot for a special celebration or when you just want to treat yourself to something memorable. ✨🇹🇭🍽

Our dinner at Nusara was absolutely fantastic. The food was amazing, the space is beautiful and the staff is lovely.

The whole dining experience was very well curated, with a first part being guided to different parts of the restaurant (kitchen, a bar area at the top floor), and the rest at the table.

The staff guides you through every dish, bringing to the table what was used, with details and origin of the dish. The entire menu is an explosion of flavors, spices, textures. My whole group was very happy.

Everything was amazing, from beginning to end. For sure I’ll be back!

A Thai fusion restaurant opposite Wat Pho, nearby Grand Palace and Emerald Buddha Temple. Stunning view especially dinner time. Creative Thai food. Most dishes could be too spicy for foreigners, even for few local Thai. Attentive service. Very nice ambiance.

A friend of mine came to celebrate her birthday at this restaurant. They recommended it because it's a Michelin-starred restaurant, and I was very impressed. The food was delicious and flavorful, the service was good, and the atmosphere was very relaxing. I will definitely come back here again. 🙏💙

Outside of southern Thai food and the gems in Kanchanaburi, this spot is next level. Every single dish bursts with bold, fiery flavor. It doesn’t just taste good, it hits you. Hard. And the craziest part? The more you eat, the more addictive it gets. From tender deer and rich ostrich to wild boar and fresh fish, every bite is a knockout. It’s wild, exotic, and insanely delicious. On top of that, the service is friendly and attentive. If you’re a true flavor hunter, this place is a must. One visit just won’t be enough.

FABULOUS food!! The best local dishes I have ever tried as a local I dare to say. I waited in the queue for 20 mins and waited for 4 dishes I ordered for just 15 mins. I got some local fish, fried frog, local spicy fish soup and local spicy sauce stirred with deer. The vibe and staff here are also great. They manage everyone’s queues accurately even if there are many customers in the queue. No matter if you come alone because I came alone but I got a big table for 4 people before many groups of customers, of course, I came before them. Restaurant of the word FIRST COME FIRST SERVE! This is called RESPECT! The bill is reasonable if compared with everything I mentioned, you can pay by credit card as well. By the way I didn't see the menu in English, BUT BUT you must TRY!

The wild food dishes are easy to eat, adjusted for those who can’t handle spicy food. You can order with mild spiciness. The prices are reasonable. There is parking, and the queue and food waiting times are short.

Food definitely lives up to the hype. Spicy, bold and rich in flavor. They have an English menu and while the staff doesn’t speak much English, it was still easy enough to communicate with them. Good could be a bit too spicy for most foreigners so maybe ask them to turn down the heat level a bit. I would recommend the green curry as well as the stir fried deer with cumin leaves. I was sweating but still delicious.

I booked Signature restaurant for the first night in Thailand with my husband, we were celebrating our new marriage. From the moment we entered the restaurant, we felt welcomed. The staff were incredibly attentive, kind, and helpful. We had the 8 course menu which was absolutely incredible. We were blown away by the service - incredible attention to detail which also showed itself in the food. The chef, Thierry Drapeau is excellent - his themes were gardens and herbs and freshness which translated in every dish. Each dish was more beautiful than the one before. We had the pleasure of being served by Bastien who was phenomenal. His knowledge of the food, techniques, and his kindness shone through every single moment. We were able to meet the kitchen staff, including the chef, and look around the kitchen which was a lovely touch and really brought us full circle to the food we were eating. The evening was made even more special when the staff presented us with a bouquet of flowers and a chocolate brioche as a way to celebrate our honeymoon. Overall, we had an amazing experience at this restaurant and I am so happy that we booked this place for our first night in Thailand. I highly recommend!

My husband and I had a fabulous meal at Signature last night (04/09/2025). The restaurant is beautifully designed, with a lovely bar area to relax in on arrival.

The service was first class — we were warmly welcomed and given a wonderful introduction to the menu and Chef Thierry’s background. We chose the three-course menu, which, with the added canapés, was more than enough food for us (though they also offer longer menus for those who want the full experience). My husband also added cheese to his meal.

The food itself was spectacular. Every dish was immaculately presented and bursting with flavour. Our standout dishes were the lamb and the rice pudding.

We’re returning to Bangkok in February and will definitely be coming back to Signature.

A special mention as well to the team’s flexibility — we thought we might not make our reservation and contacted them at 2pm the same day. Instead of keeping our deposit, they kindly offered to move the reservation to another date. In the end, we did make it, but their understanding and accommodation really impressed us.

We’re already looking forward to our next visit!

We recently enjoyed an 8-course dinner at Signature Bangkok. We had a wonderful evening with delicious food. The staff is super friendly and explains the ingredients and how each dish was created. They really put a lot of care into it. It's striking that several ingredients come from France, but the overall experience is a mix of local and French ingredients. The flavors are delicious, and the overall experience has been well thought out. We opted for the 8-course dinner, but even a 5-course meal would have been more than enough. However, we do find the menu a bit pricey for an Asian restaurant. For the same price, you can enjoy a 7- or 8-course meal in a Michelin-starred restaurant in Europe.

That evening, we were the only guests, which we found a bit disappointing. Nevertheless, the service and the food were good.

However, for a Michelin-starred restaurant, we did find a few things disappointing. They have an open kitchen, which is a great idea. Make sure that if the kitchen isn't open yet, guests don't have to listen in on the chef's FaceTime call. That doesn't belong in a restaurant, any restaurant. Chef Thierry should also be focused solely on the preparation during the meal and not visible on their phone. Do that behind the scenes, or simply don't do it at all. Of course, things can sometimes fall over; that's human. But don't take too many risks when bringing tableware and cutlery.
One dish was missing an ingredient. We reported this, but they didn't do anything with it, which we found a shame.
If you don't use the accompanying wine menu, nothing else is offered. They could have accommodated this by offering something else. In this case, we had to ask for it ourselves.
Finally, we found it a shame that the chef didn't come to the table himself, chat, and then leave before the last dishes were served. He also clearly told his staff that. If you're the face of the restaurant, you stay until the last dishes are finished.

Despite the feedback above, we had a wonderful evening and would recommend dining here if you want the Michelin experience.

I attended the Wine & Cheese event yesterday and was absolutely blown away. As a true cheese enthusiast, this evening was nothing short of heavenly, the cheese selection was exceptional, offering an incredible variety and presented beautifully.
The freshly baked breads by Chef Erwann were outstanding and paired perfectly with the cheeses – soft, crusty, and full of flavor. The canapés by Chef Thierry, Chef Gary and Chef Syrco were an absolute delight – beautifully crafted, bursting with taste, and a wonderful complement to the wines.
A special shout-out to Chef Thierry for bringing this sensational event together. And a big thank you to Das, whose expertly curated wine selection elevated the entire experience.
This was a masterfully hosted evening of indulgence and elegance. I can’t wait for the next one in September!
We celebrated my wife birthday here. We had 8-course dinner. Delicious and beautiful displays. It’s really worth 1 Michelin  star!

25 unique dishes presented during a show/lecture that is like nothing I never experienced before. So many interesting combinations of flavours and textures in a totally different way. It’s brave to start something like this, and it’s not for everyone. Me personally loved it. I was here a few years ago and it’s even better today. They really nailed it. The combination of food and drinks, colours, textures and the music! I left happy, the team really gave everything here.

Mixed thoughts on our visit here. The service and food is absolutely outstanding, no doubt. The team has put in a lot of thought into developing the menu in a very unique way, with a story behind each dish. The wine pairing was on the money for each dish. Loved the community style eating with Gaggan and the staff engaging with everyone during the meal.
The only thing I found overwhelming was the music and clapping - it felt like a cheap Arabian Nights type show - that's not what I expected from this restaurant, which is supposed to be fine dining. That said, I understand that while Gaggan was preparing the last dish, the staff needed something to keep the diners engaged - but music and clapping? Just made it feel like a cheap theatric parlor trick. That said, Gaggan did say at the beginning of the meal that this was all about chaos - and that's exactly what this felt like!
Overall a lovely dining experience, could've been better had it been less loud, and more controlled. But that's a personal preference. If you're visiting Bangkok, you kinda have to try to get a reservation here. Price tag is not that crazy considering how much you would pay for Michelin star restaurants in other parts of the world!

First time in Thailand – just two weeks.
I wondered how to wrap up this trip, and eventually decided to book a seat for myself at Gaggan in Bangkok.

No wonder it’s ranked #1 in Asia and #6 in the world.

An out-of-body, multi-sensory experience—unapologetic and uncompromising.
Step inside and everything else fades away—
flawless wine pairing
phenomenal music pairing
dynamic lighting
and of course, 25 unforgettable courses.

An absolutely insane way to end this trip.

This is hands down the best food experience I’ve had in my entire life. I’ll be looking for more and better, but I’ll be hard pressed to find it. No wonder Gaggan made it to the #6 best in the world.

Amazing attentive and personalised service, awesome food journey across India, Japan and Thailand, and a multi-sensorial stimulus that makes the 25 courses a happy and cheerful walk in the park.

Fantastic experience! Worth the wait, the travel and money. Each and every plate was very well studied and put together. And not at all what you would have thought. Mind blowing creativity of massive team of talented professionals. Loved the music too.

I came across this stall in old town and it looked unassuming - i thought how could something so simple be good.

One bite and i was blown away. Soft center, crispy sides and subtle sweetness - tasted out of the world.

25 baht for 6 pieces.

It’s like Indian dosas or appams rolled. So so so good.

Every time I ate here, it left me with a smile and wanting more. During our 5-night stay in Old Town, I noticed the long line and decided to give it a try and I’m so glad I did! It was absolutely lovely, and I found myself craving it every single day.

Pancakes made in heaven…
Imagine a street stall with repeated recognition by the Guide Michelin… On this street corner in Old Phuket Town this has become reality. And with good reason: here you can have the best pancakes ever. They are prepared over a set of charcoal fired pits inside small domed kettle like pans. The routine between the chef and her assistant is itself a mesmerizing spectacle reminiscent of street hustlers’ cup games.

Fantastic pancakes and an incredible experience watching them being made, you buy 6 for 25thb there is no seating but they are a traditional snack so you can eat while walking. There is normally a 5 minute wait but is you place your order when you arrive they will eventually serve you. Definitely worth seeking them out and having this traditional experience. The pancakes tasted as though they had sweetened milk and coconut in then. Delicious 🤤

- A Must-Try local sweet treat in Phuket
- Best eaten fresh while it is hot and crispy
- Good with some hot coffee or tea
- Long waiting time as this is quite well known place for both local and foreigners
- 6 pieces for just 25 thb at a Michelin quality

If you’re on the hunt for a truly satisfying bowl of noodles, this place is a hidden gem that’s earned its spot on the Michelin Guide from 2021 all the way to 2025 — and for good reason.

The grilled pork is smoky, tender, and bursting with flavor, served atop perfectly cooked noodles that soak up all the goodness. The portion? Generous enough to leave even the hungriest diner satisfied — no skimping here! What makes the experience even more memorable is the owner’s warm hospitality and attention to detail. You’re not just having a meal; you’re being looked after.

It’s the kind of spot where quality meets heart — and you’ll taste it in every bite. Definitely worth a stop on your food journey.

Phenomenal noodle dish. I ordered the egg noodles with pork and crab. The soup was one of the best I've had in Thailand, rich, light but so flavourful. The noodles were cooked perfectly, as was the pork and the stuffed wantons were sizable. The crab and the soup together were umami heaven. I can recommend this place enought. 120 baht.

They got michelin 2021-2025
Super delicious noodle with pork grill with crab
No MSG… but the Soup is very nice

I will be back here again

Price is cheap,, suitable with dish
Around 60-100 thb/dish

Beverage 25thb/glass

I visited Boonlert Egg Noodle after reading its Bib Gourmand mention — and it lives up to the reputation. The egg noodle soup is deceptively simple but masterfully made: the broth is clear yet deeply savory, with a clean umami kick, not over-seasoned. The noodles themselves are springy and soft, giving just the right chew without being gummy.

Toppings like grilled pork, roast pork, crispy pork belly, and wontons round out the bowl beautifully — the textures contrast nicely, and the pork has that slightly sweet soy glaze that adds depth without overwhelming the delicate soup. The serve is generous for the price, and the atmosphere is humble, family-run, genuine.

If you’re craving a comforting bowl of Thai-Chinese noodle soup that’s flavourful, affordable, and authentic, Boonlert is a must-visit.
Just not meet my taste bud. Charsiew rice sos gravy too sweet, noodles bring some 碱水味，just win over crispy roasted pork.

I would say the thing that makes it delicious is their chilli sauce. I wouldn't say the omelette itself has no difference from others but the chilli was the stand out. The vibe where you see the chef dance to it while cooking was worth it as well.

The food stalls there is quite unique. Every stall sell different food or clothes and i haven't tried most of them in Singapore or China.

We tried the jimjum(hot pot in a clay pot) and avocado fruit juice. Both are super nice!

Entertaining but tasteless

During my visit to night market, I stopped looking at a man and a lady completely enjoying the cooking, with dancing on the beat. And the dish getting fried on the large pan looks no less attractive. They were making Crispy Mussel Omelet, topped with bean sprouts. It is also included in the Mchelin guide.

The omelet is served with chilly sauce (dip). It's crispy as the name suggests but too greasy and  Pretty bland & tasteless. I hated this feeling to eating too much oil with every bite.
This place is mentioned in the Michelin Guide. Although the food is not the best you can eat in this neighbourhood, the ambiance certainly is. The dancing chef enjoys his job and we loved being here
Mussel hot pancakes and the chef dance in front of large pan. Love him and his dish.
Lady boss can speak fluent English, which is helpful. The noodles tasted sweet compare to other stores. The dry egg noodle is a must try. Recommended to visit if you are in Ayutthaya!

Our third food stop of the day brought us to Pa Lek Boat Noodle, and stepping in felt like diving straight into a truly local Bangkok experience. The place had that comforting, slightly chaotic buzz—locals chatting over steaming bowls, tourists snapping photos, and the unmistakable aroma of rich broth and spices filling the air.

The boat noodles here are the real deal—deep, savory flavors that taste like they’ve been perfected over generations. They keep it simple: pork or beef, that’s it. No overcomplication, just pure, authentic taste. The portions are small (as boat noodles traditionally are), which makes it perfect to try a few bowls and mix things up. Honestly, it’s part of the fun—slurping one bowl, ordering another, and before you know it, you’ve lost count of how many you’ve had.

Service? Lightning fast. Bowls arrive within minutes, and despite the crowd, everything runs like clockwork. It’s no wonder the place is so popular—it proudly wears the Michelin Bib Gourmand badge, and every spoonful proves why.

Pa Lek Boat Noodle isn’t just a meal—it’s an experience. The kind that leaves you full but still wanting “just one more bowl.”

Very easy system, a manageable menu of different boat noodle options, with English descriptions, 20 baht a bowl. Couldn't be easier, relaxed friendly staff. Great for experimenting with the different types of boat noodles. Not as challenging as some dishes can be, so definitely more foriegner friendly. Found the taste here just right and ready to eat. The dry noodles were great, definitely recommend.
Don't miss all the desert stalls outside, everything we got there was excellent.
Great experience for lunch while in Ayutthaya.

Famous boat noodle spot famous among the locals located right opposite of Wat Mahathat. The small size of the bowl allows you to slurp it very fast. Both the rice noodle soup and dry noodle is good. However, broth is a little bit sour.

Can't beat boat noodles at 20 baht a bowl. Also the location makes it super convenient, it's a perfect pitstop after exploring the ruins (just across the road from the Wat Mahathat complex).

For me personally the must-order is dry pork noodles!

Tempted to just review with one word “mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm” cos’ that pretty much was the conversation at the dinner table.

You know some Michelin’s have amazing ambience and service but while the food is good, it just doesn’t commensurate? That’s NOT the case at Baan Tepa. 5 stars in atmosphere, service AND food.

Every dish had interesting flavours and a story, and the flavours melded together well so it wasn’t just funky interesting food, but made you go “eh?” and yet “mmmmmmm” and want to lick the plate (I almost did but caught myself, so made do by scraping the knife across the plate to pick up every bit of the sauce.)

Service was impeccable.

One of the very few Michelin’s I would come to, again. Even if it was to have the same menu.

Had the 4 non-alcoholic tasting pairing which came with quite tart flavours that complemented the food well. Lovers of Kombucha, don’t miss this option.

The house is gorgeous; wish I saw more of it but we spent too much time savouring the food and had to rush off after 3 hours for a booked massage; so didn’t ask for a full tour.

My friends and I enjoyed a wonderfully innovative and delicious meal at Baan Tepa last night. From the very first course till the last, we were wowed by the thoughtfulness, intentionality and sheer genius of each dish. (I don’t eat prawn, but the River and Land course turned out to be my favourite!)

Chef Tam and team, you are doing an outstanding job! We love the focus on sustainability and showcasing local produce too! We will certainly be back and in the meantime, we will encourage others to savour the rich and exciting flavours that Baan Tepa has to offer.

An amazing and truly beautiful experience from start to finish. The restaurant is housed in a space full of history, and you can feel the soul of the place in every detail. The dishes are even more impressive, creative, imaginative, and full of clever ideas that surprise with every bite. Service flowed like a perfectly composed symphony, each element fitting seamlessly into the next.
Everything felt balanced and intentional, exactly the way a Michelin starred dining experience should.
I wholeheartedly recommend a visit to anyone looking for an unforgettable culinary journey ✨

I had the pleasure of dining at Baan Tepa this past week (Sept 2025). When you arrive to the property you are immediately transported to a well landscaped garden oasis. They have done an amazing job of using the space on the property. You could easily forget you are in the middle of a major metropolis. This continues into the back with the Baan Tepa herb gardens. A space they cultivate herbs for the kitchen. The building the restaurant is housed in feels like an old house, charming and warm. The staff were incredibly professional and warm. It felt like being welcomed into someone’s home. The food was creative and tasty, this particular menu featured a lot of seafood and ingredients from all over Thailand.  They have a very respectable wine list and waved out corkage from on a bottle we brought when we ordered another from their menu. All in all a wonderful experience and I would highly recommend visiting this establishment on your next trip to Bangkok.

2 Michelin star for 2024 and 2025. One of the best that we have dine in anywhere around the world. There is so much attention to details that it puts other similarly rated restaurant to shame. The chef manages to bring out so much flavors from the ingredients a couple of dishes evokes memories from our childhood. All these make the dining experience really amazing. Worth the long travel from the city.

Once a highly popular and renowned Thai restaurant, this place truly lives up to its reputation. The food is exceptionally flavorful and well-crafted, making the dining experience thoroughly satisfying. It’s a place that leaves a lasting impression.

Special Thai food that you should try. It's worth waiting in line. Local ingredients are combined with flavors. Some dishes may be too spicy for those who can't eat spicy food. The food comes in sets every two months and the menu changes regularly.

Sang Tha Tian is a Michelin Guide gem serving authentic and unique Thai cuisine in a cozy, intimate setting. The dishes are bursting with bold, spicy flavors, featuring specialties you won’t find elsewhere. Every bite is fresh and unforgettable, but the small space means reservations are a must. A must-visit for Thai food lovers

Very popular Thai cuisine, all dishes are delicious, use local and fresh ingredients in the cooking, mix durian and mangosteen for a nice touch - see pictures

It is a small restaurant and limited space between seating, chair is small
Beware: reservation only! No parking

If you’re craving an authentic Thai family meal, Sang Thatien is the place to go. Walking into this spot feels like being invited into a local Thai home for dinner, with such a warm and cozy atmosphere that instantly makes you feel at ease. There’s no signboard outside, so I hesitated for a moment before stepping in, but that hidden vibe only adds to its charm.

This place seems to be a favorite among locals because the night I visited, the small dining area was filled entirely with Thai guests. I heard it’s so popular that they’re fully booked until the end of the year. They don’t have a fixed menu, which I found so unique. Instead, the chef serves whatever they’ve prepared for the day, and this month’s dishes were inspired by Isaan cuisine, the region famous for Somtum. The table was soon covered with a variety of dishes, each one looking more delicious than the last. I wanted to try everything, but there was so much food that I ended up too full to finish it all, which was a bit of a shame.

The dish that stood out the most for me was the strawberry salad paired with caramelized pork. It was such an unexpected combination, yet the flavors worked so well together. Another highlight was the durian curry. I was a bit nervous to try it at first because durian can be intense, but it turned out to be amazing. The durian added a subtle, creamy richness with a light fragrance, and it was cooked with pork belly that reminded me of a comforting braised dish. The grilled river prawns and a crispy fried fish were also incredibly flavorful and left me wanting more. For such an incredible dining experience, the price felt very reasonable at around 1300 THB per person. If you’re looking for a true taste of Thai home cooking in a setting that feels like a local’s dining room, this place is a must-visit. Just be sure to book well in advance!

What an excellent spot for beef noodles!!! Great value for the price. Very delicious broth, perfectly cooked noodles, and succulent cuts of beef! We loved all the herbs they served with the noodle soup. There are so many wonderful flavors going on here! The lovely people running the restaurant are so very sweet! The chili sauce on the side was also incredible!! Don't miss this spot if you're in Udon Thani!!!!

When I missed Udon, I miss most about beef noodle soup at Pa Noi 😋.
I walked nearly at noon from my hotel to this one for lunch. Omg, so worthy. Chewy & tender stewed beef shank, beef tendon & beef ball as well. Too much topping in a bowl. Many noodles but I picked yellow egg noodle. I fell in love from first spoon from broth, beef, peanut, garlic. Fresh herbs to mix together. Nothing to complaint.

Btw, service here is 10/10, very supportive bc Im Farang 😆. You must call Thai lemon iced tea in order to quench your thirsty with Thai heat.

Very cheap for combo: 60 Bath for bowl and 25 Bath for tea.

Good local beef noodles. I ordered small but still filling enough for me, loaded with braised and stewed beef, beef balls, beef tendon, etc. They provide a kind of fermented mildly spicy tofu sauce in a saucer, but has bottles of chilli sauce, nam prik, chilli vinegar in a glass, fresh green chilli, and of course a dish of fresh vegetables. Definitely worth coming back for more next time.
Maybe the best noodles I've ever had anywhere in the world... Amazingly soft need, tasty broth. Wow!
Great quality beef noodles, service with a smile, what more could you want. Highly recommend

We have spent many wonderful dinners at be friends and every single time it has been a great experience. Everything I have tried so far was absolutely delicious. I usually eat a lot so every plate I tried was full of flavor and perfectly prepared.

The restaurant itself has a great atmosphere, especially in the evening when the lights create an inviting ambience.

A special mention goes to the team: always friendly, attentive, and truly giving 100% to ensure every guest has the best possible experience. We will definitely keep coming back on next vacations.

Thanks for the best banana fritter and springs rolls!

Stopped here for a quick lunch while staying at the Outrigger nearby.

We all got pad Thai, which was great. Not as much flavor as we’ve had at other places around, but still really good and a great price.

The service was great - everyone was kind and helpful, plus the views were amazing.

We sat right on the beach and enjoyed the sound and view of the ocean.

We stayed in la flora and this was our go to restaurant for the time. The food is just amazingly delicious. Just a lot of playground for the kids so did the parents can enjoy the sunset. The staff was very friendly. They heard from my little daughter that we are leaving the next day and they all gathered to greet us and even gave us a handmade bag as a present. I can only recommend this restaurant.

Had dinner here with my daughter when staying at a local 5 Star hotel. The food was great and the service was very good as were the prices. Its on the beach so the atmosphere is lovely. It started to rain so they approached us and moved us in side. Great service 👏

Be friends restaurant offers a truly unique and delightful dining experience. The atmosphere transports you to a realm far beyond the ordinary. You'll discover an ambiance that feels wonderfully out of this world. It's a place where you can truly escape and enjoy yourself. We invite you to discover this magical destination.

Lumdee Te Khuadang is one of the well-known Northern Thai restaurants in Chiang Mai, recommended by the Michelin Guide. The food is authentic — my friends loved their Khao Soi, though I enjoyed some dishes more than others. What really stood out for me was their longan ice cream with puffed rice crisps — it’s absolutely delicious and the reason I’ve gone back! 🍨
The restaurant has ample seating and parking, great for families or groups. Service is friendly and the atmosphere relaxed — definitely worth a visit if you’re exploring Northern Thai cuisine in Chiang Mai.

From my first time visiting this restaurant, it has right away become my most favorite place in Chiang Mai. There are very wide selection of Northern Thai cuisine with supremely authentic taste, even for a Thai like me. Service is also very warm with a lot of smiles from staffs!

Dined as a couple & spent ~$750 baht.

Not the cheapest of places but food quality more than makes up for it! Do note that their kitchen closes at 9.30pm!

So many interesting dishes that we wanted to try but we eventually decided on

1) Young Jackfruit Curry with Pork: Unless you like really strong, sour, fermented flavours, avoid this! This is not for the faint of heart
2) Hors D'oeuvres Meung: Loved this! Great platter of meats, vegetables + thai chilli dip! Chilli dips weren't super spicy, so that's a plus for us
3) Fried Opilia Leaf: This was our favourite of the night! Crunchy, savoury, slightly sour. Must order!
4) Longan Ice Cream with Young Coconut Sago: This was another winner for the night. Wish we had stomach for another dessert!

Will come back again when I'm in the area!

Simply delicious!
Authentic northern Thai dishes, popular for locals. Huge playground, children friendly!
Beautiful presented, delicous food. Amazing quality and variety. Indoor air conditioned area and outdoor area overlooks garden and a large lake.

Amazing Amazing Amazing! What a great restaurant! Set beside a beautiful lake next to the jungle, in a traditional style building with kingfishers flying across the lake. We were the only ones there that afternoon and the service was impeccable and prompt. The quality of every dish was outstanding and so beautifully presented. We don’t know a lot about traditional southern Thai cuisine, but it felt like a creative take on traditional dishes. The standout dishes were the crispy prawn and leaf, the braised belly pork and the fish/crab steamed parcels, Ngob-poo. To top it all, this is the cheapest Michelin rated restaurant we have ever been to! Such great value! We would definitely recommend it.

Hidden up in a forested area, but easily accessible by car and with a scenic vista of a lovely lake with majestic mountain behind it.

Their food are authentic Phuket, with many items that can only be found here in Phuket. We ordered a few of their Michelin signature dishes like the Gaeng Ti Mi Pla or the Phuket style curry fish which has a slight sourish taste it but but have hint of sweetness from coconut cream too, and their deep fried shrimp with garlic and chili, which I think was on point but not one to shout about.

Another dish that we ordered was their Hoi Wan  Tom Ta Krai or the clams in lemongrass soup, superb, love the fragrance of the lemon grass, the flavor of the basil leaf and chili while the soup is full of the umami from the clams.

Their Ngob Poo or a similar Malaysian otak with fish and crab steamed in curry paste within a banana leaf. Another very delicious dish.

My friend ordered their Naam Prik Ka Yum Gung Sod, not really my type of dish but she loved it.

Service is good and fast but our overall bill with 3 drinks + 3 rice + 1 bottle of water was about 1700b.

Do not follow Google map if it tells you to make a u-turn after the light. That’s a long way around with less travel road through the wood.

Just drive past the traffic light and the first u-turn. There is another u-turn that run beneath the main road once you come up on the other side just turn left and the restaurant is a mere 300 meters from the main road.

See images for reference.
Beautiful and very tasty food.  A$100 for two with six dishes.  Lovely lake view.   Highly recommended

Hidden gems. They offer southern style Thai food. The restaurant is located inside the forest area. If you’re not into that spicy, don’t forget to tell them the spiciness level you’re up to. Too bad, too many menus were out of stocks and was not in season when we were there. They also got Michelin guide, which they deserve it! Overall, highly recommended!

There are meals, and then there are Potong moments — you know the kind that linger long after, tugging at memory. Chef Pam (Pichaya “Pam” Soontornyanakij) has turned her family’s century-old, Sino-Portuguese, herbal medicine shop in Yaowarat into just that kind of place: a living bridge between past and future, between the intimate and the spectacular.

Chef Pam—Asia’s Best Female Chef 2025—transforms her family’s century-old Sino-Portuguese building in Yaowarat into something rare: a Michelin star, five-floor story of heritage and imagination.

Our journey began at the Sino Bar on the ground floor, with its nostalgic wooden ceiling, before settling into a tasting menu (curated just for us by Chef Pam on a special request) on the second floor. Chef Pam graciously curated a full vegetarian experience for two, and every course was both inventive and deeply rooted in her Thai-Chinese philosophy. From delicate seasonal vegetables prepared with surprising textures to brilliant substitutions for the signature 14-day Aged Duck & Blackened Chicken with Chinese Herbs, each plate was thoughtful, balanced, and distinctly hers.

We chose the sommelier selection for our pairings, beginning with a bottle of Dom Pérignon, and over the next two-plus hours, the meal unfolded like chapters in a book. Highlights? The artistry of the five-element philosophy—salt, acidity, spice, texture, and the Maillard effect—woven into dishes that honored tradition while gently pushing it forward.

Our evening ended high—literally—first at the Opium Bar on the fourth floor, with its surreal escape of cocktails, and finally on the rooftop, gazing over the rare, quiet views of Chinatown.

A special note: don’t leave without sipping Chef Pam’s house-made kāng pǔ chá (kombucha), crafted in her dedicated fermentation room—it’s a signature memory in itself. 😉❤️

Can’t wait to see you again Chef! 🫡⚡️
You are incredible.

We had a very good and unique food experience. The story telling during the course and the atmosphere was well tailored and very creative. A great experience to try Thai Chinese cuisine. My favorite dishes were the Pad Thai and thai main course with very yummy crispy skin duck

A unique experience. Overall enjoyable but a little mechanical in delivery. It would have been better if the messaging came from the heart with a bit more personal touch. But throughout the dinner, the explanations and steps seemed more rehearsed than sincere.Situated in the middle of Chinatown, the restaurant is charming and the entrance inviting. But the entry welcome is a little like waiting to see a Dr at a medical surgery; professional but it lacked the warmth.
It is interesting to note that the Tiger features heavily in the storyline of the restaurant & we were told of the Tiger Room on the 3rd level where 5 tigers are supposedly painted on the walls - only to find that 5 leopards were painted instead!
The food was good, beautifully executed with tastes that were familiar yet presented in a different way. Kudos to Chef Pam for her creativeness yet not straying too far from her Thai Chinese roots. We learnt the menu is changed only once a year - enough time for the culinary team to experiment and come up with thoughtful menus!
We enjoyed dinner but at over Bht 10K a head (with drinks), it is pricey. Professionally executed but lacking the wow factor or surprise or the simple heartfelt gestures that elevate a good experience to a great one. We left satiated but not over the moon.

⭐ Restaurant Potong
Just learned they’ve curated a vegetarian set menu — and wow, what a journey it promises to be. The food here is bold, inventive, and deeply rooted in Thai‑Chinese traditions. Each course feels like a chapter in a story.

Potong sits tucked in Bangkok’s Chinatown in a beautifully restored old Chinese‑Thai building, giving you walls that whisper history as you dine. The ambience is intimate, elegant, and full of character.

Their tasting menu is built around 5 elements & 5 senses — every dish plays a balance of texture, flavor, and surprise. Even if vegetarian is a request, they take it seriously.

If you’re in Bangkok and want a dining experience where every bite matters — Potong’s vegetarian set menu is a brilliant pick.

Excellent service team
Thanjs Dennise

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
A Truly Unforgettable Dining Experience at POTONG – Bangkok’s Hidden Culinary Gem!

Dining at POTONG was one of the absolute highlights of our trip to Bangkok. From the moment we stepped into the beautifully restored heritage building, we knew something special awaited us.

We were first brought to the rooftop bar, where we enjoyed a stunning sunset view paired with a refreshing welcome drink, the perfect way to begin the evening.

After that, we slowly made our way down through the different floors, each level offering its own unique ambiance and story. From the bar to the chef’s table and the dining room, every space felt thoughtfully curated, blending tradition with modern design and energy.

The tasting menu was a spectacular journey through flavors, textures, and Thai-Chinese heritage. Each dish was a piece of art creative, beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. Chef Pam’s passion and storytelling were felt in every course.

Service was flawless, warm, knowledgeable, and attentive without being overwhelming. The team walked us through every dish with care and enthusiasm.

If you’re looking for a fine dining experience in Bangkok that’s immersive, culturally rich, and incredibly delicious, POTONG is an absolute must. An unforgettable evening from start to finish!

This really is untarnished, authentic Southern Thai cooking. The restaurant is simple,rustic and charming. The food in a similar vein. Great punchy flavours but still wonderfully balanced and very well priced. It was clear that all the locals regard this place as being truly authentic. Always a great sign.

The rating is above average, the reviews are only positive, so we expected more than we got: the tom yum was sour-salted with overcooked tough shrimp, large chunks of onions, there was no sweetness, spiciness, the taste of lemongrass and greens. The green mango salad was sprinkled with sugar on top and was far from the original taste. There was delicious fish, but for some reason it was brought completely cooled ( I've never eaten before such a small portion of pad kaphrao😅  In addition, they forgot one order, but at least they did not include it in the bill. Therefore, decide for yourself whether to visit this restaurant with a Michelin star
This is proper Thai food. Very authentic. If you’re in Samui get yourself down here. Highly recommend the octopus and pineapple. Massaman curry was great too. Michelin guide rated and I can see why.

This is one of the best Thai food places I’ve been to. It offers a simple and nice sitting area m, not too much of a “vibe” but a pleasant atmosphere for dining.
The food is TOP: very tasty, extremely fresh, with generous big portions.
Always a good option to have a casual lunch or dinner or to order delivery from. Always good.

Me and my partner came here after seeing the Michelin guide mentioned for here. We were very happy with the food and service. We had the deep fried shrimp cakes, chicken panang curry and southern thai curry with ribs.
We'd definitely recommend the panang and shrimp cakes they were lovely.
Service was great and for 2 large beers and a sprite the bill total was 910 baht.

I got red wine watermelon smoothie medium rare steak coconut curry and finished with a Thai tea tiramisu. Everything was perfection. The meat was cut with a spoon it was so tender the curry had amazing flavor. The wine was so nice and the smoothie was so refreshing. The dessert had multiple different custard toppings from a coffee flavored one to a raspberry flavored one. Not my favorite in the world but it was different and it was super good and for somebody else they may love it. All in all it was delicious. Pricey but delicious. That meal came out to be around 1200 baht. It was super good however and if I wanted to splurge on a nice dinner again I would return.
