The restaurant is beautifully designed to resemble a train carriage, creating a unique dining atmosphere. Service is attentive, and the selection of alcoholic beverages is impressive. Prices lean on the higher side, but they remain reasonable given the quality. The restaurant itself is relatively small, and it’s a bit disappointing that there’s no dedicated parking available.

Burapa Eastern Thai Cuisine – Flavorful, Elegant, and Seriously Spicy! 🌶️🇹🇭

As a Thai person who loves Thai food, I can say this restaurant truly hits the spot. The flavors are authentic, bold, and beautifully presented. It’s exactly the kind of food I personally enjoy.

BUT! A spicy warning:
Even if you ask for “mild,” the food here is still quite spicy — at least by international standards.
If you can’t handle chili at all, I highly recommend avoiding dishes with chili entirely, because even their “less spicy” is still pretty spicy. 🔥

On the other hand, if you love spicy food — go ahead and order freely! You’ll be in heaven.

My top recommendations:
•	The grilled beef – so tender and flavorful.
•	The grilled squid – a must-order! Seriously, don’t miss it.

Honestly, every dish we tried was excellent. No wonder they’ve earned a Michelin star — it’s well-deserved! 🌟

The atmosphere is elegant and classic, with a unique interior that feels like dining on an old-fashioned train. 🚂
Staff were incredibly helpful — we were overwhelmed by the menu at first, but they guided us through with great suggestions.

Parking is available right next to the restaurant, which is super convenient.

Prices are on the higher side 💸, but considering the quality, service, and special experience, I’d say it’s worth it — especially for a special occasion.

First time experiencing Eastern Thai food in a cocktail bar. Restaurant located in Nana district with loads of pubs and bars around.

The prawn with papaya salad was super unique and memorable. Never had papaya salad served this way.
The soft shell crab was well fried, not too oily but nothing much to rave about
The beef with rice was flavorful. The rice was fried in beef fat giving a punch and the beef was medium rare to perfection.
The beef curry was also different from the usual. The spices used made it unique and delightful.
The grilled pork was well marinated with a sauce that was so good. I can’t make out what it’s made of but it really complimented the dish.
Dessert ordered was their speciality. Another never tried nor common found. We enjoyed the shredded coconut, mixed with coconut sugar and peanuts on top of rice pudding.

An Unforgettable Journey Through Eastern Thai Flavors

Burapa offers more than just a meal - it’s a complete sensory experience that transports you to the golden age of luxury travel. The moment you step into their beautifully appointed train car dining room, you’re immersed in an atmosphere of vintage elegance that perfectly complements their exceptional Eastern Thai cuisine.

Ambiance & Setting:
The restored train car interior is absolutely breathtaking. Rich burgundy leather banquettes, warm wood paneling, elegant table lamps, and those gorgeous purple curtains create an intimate, sophisticated atmosphere. The attention to detail is remarkable - from the vintage suitcases displayed overhead to the classic table settings with blue and white china. It feels like dining aboard the Orient Express.

Food Quality:
The Eastern Thai cuisine here is outstanding. Every dish we tried showcased authentic flavors and beautiful presentation. The grilled beef dish was perfectly cooked with a beautiful char and vibrant accompaniments including what appeared to be a perfectly runny egg yolk. The variety of dishes, from the aromatic curries to the fresh vegetable preparations, demonstrated the kitchen’s expertise in balancing the complex flavors that make Eastern Thai cuisine so special.

Service & Experience:
The unique setting makes this perfect for special occasions or when you want to impress someone. The intimate booth seating and romantic lighting create an ideal atmosphere for date nights or celebrations.

Overall:
Burapa successfully combines exceptional Eastern Thai cuisine with one of the most unique dining atmospheres I’ve experienced. It’s not just dinner - it’s an adventure. The combination of authentic flavors, impeccable presentation, and that incredible train car setting makes this a must-visit destination.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for an extraordinary dining experience that engages all the senses!
Note: Reservations likely recommended given the intimate setting and unique concept.

Great Value for Money and Amazing Thai Food at Dhabkwan Resort!

We had a wonderful time at Dhabkwan Resort. The atmosphere was peaceful and charming, and the Thai food was absolutely amazing my family loved it here!
.
It’s very good value for money, with authentic dishes, lovely surroundings, and friendly service. We’ll definitely come back again!

A beautiful, old traditional style, property and rooms.
The grounds are old, and areas in serious need of major repairs, which seem to be happening

This place is absolutely stunning. The staff are so attentive.

Authentic Thai baths with the balcony overlooking the pound really made it hard for us to leave and explore the city. It was fantastic. 1000 times recommend. I can't believe its so reasonably priced.

The restaurant served us food  that was amazingly tasty. We actually returned to eat after we left we enjoyed it that much.

One point of improvement this is a very specific to me. They don't know how to make hot coffee I would recommend just getting an automated machine as then hot coffee wasn't nice.

Don't show up before calling. They don't indicate anywhere on social media if the whole place has been booked for an event. That's what happened to me, made my way to the boondocks to have lunch to be turned away. Irresponsible.

Amazing place to stay. It’s gives you a traditional vibe with how the private houses are built. Well maintained, Super friendly and helpful staff. Amazing restaurant within the hotel with great flavors.

This Michelin-listed restaurant (2021–2022) is located not far from Phetkasem Road, easy to get to. The place is peaceful, shady, and not too hot even during the day.

When I visited, I ordered the deep-fried sea bass with fish sauce, stir-fried squid with curry powder, and steamed egg. Everything was tasty, reasonably priced, and the service was great.

If you’re heading to Nakhon Pathom via this route, it’s definitely worth a stop!

A lovely outdoor restaurant by a fishing lake with great seafood options. Everything we had was great, not overseasoned and done freshly. They keep live seafood in tanks behind the restaurant. The menu is only in Thai which is already a huge sign of quality, as it caters mostly to Bangkokians on their weekend trips. Usually not busy during the week.

The food here was absolutely amazing. There are so many great options to choose from and they are all amazing. If you're looking for seafood you will not be let down. Even the more exotic foods such as frog legs are fantastic. Hands down a great experience and the atmosphere here is beautiful. I will certainly be coming back. As you can see in the photos, we were ordering a large amount of food for the entire family and we didn't spend much considering the amount of food.
A super delicious lunch at a very picturesque spot on the edge of a pond - great ambience and everything was just perfect. Highly recommend !!!
This place truly deserves the michelin star is has received. The service is wonderful, friendly and attentive. Food is SOOO good. Flavourful and tasty. MUST STOP

BEST VERMICELLI and best meal this trip!!!

Initially ordered only 1 portion of the crab vermicelli (med size 650baht). Waited approx 15-20 mins to be served. The crabs were so fresh and sweet, not the biggest crabs but it’s very fleshy. Vermicelli was well soaked with the yummiest sauce. Halfway thru my first dish, I quickly ordered a 2nd portion and I tried the tiger prawn vermicelli (310 baht) Prawns were HUGE and fresh! I topped up 20baht for extra glass noodles but there seems to be no difference even after adding the noodles.

The prawns here is even fresher and better than puponfai (in my opinion)

I will totally come back for this on my next BKK trip! I hope they can have an option to add extra prawns/seafood too

The food was exceptionally good. Both crab and prawn claypots were executed very well.  Not over cooked but just nice and juicy. The noodles are very tasty too. Waiting time can be easily 30mins for the crab dish. I would recommend the mussels. Not to our liking. There's a cart along the street selling grilled squid. Worth a try too.

Ordered two crabs and mid-size prawn dishes. Waited for 45mins despite reaching around 530PM. Outstanding flavours but don’t think will be visiting again as the location is pretty far from the city centre. Good to try out at least once!

I ordered the crab with roe as i thought it would be nicer, abit dry and hard for the roe, the transparent noodles was yummy and flavorful with a little overkill of pepper.
The crab was very sweet but small though!
Waiting time was 1hr for the crabs even though not much people!
I would rate it 6/10, not as nice i thought it would be! Then again, maybe it’s individual taste, i am fussy on food taste!
Traveling was like 45 mins for me to the shop not including the waiting time, was expecting something more exciting! Worth a try still as the staff is very polite!
Paid 600 baht which is a reasonable price!
And gosh it’s a Michelin star shop as well hoping they will improve on their roe texture especially for roe lovers!!

Dine in at the road side. Portion just nice for 1person. Choose prawn vermicelli. The prawn is fresh and big. Can choose size for crab too. Got to wait up to 30mins to serve. Suggest to come before hungry and starved. Repeated this place after few years. The taste and everything still the same. Bravo for their work.

Michelin recommended, tasty, clean, spacious, fast service. Also cheap, traditional dish that is perfect for lunch. Tom Yum soup is not the soup you think about! It’s just normal soup with very clean broth. Better order pink noodle soup, it’s tastier. And don’t forget to put some spices in it that are in the table.

🔥 Fireball Noodle Review – Not Quite the Explosion I Expected 🔥

Tried the Fireball Noodle today, and honestly… it wasn’t as fiery or flavorful as I hoped. The packaging promised a punch, but the taste fell a bit flat. The spice was mild and the noodles were just average — not the “wow” moment I was expecting.

If you’re a spice lover looking for real heat or bold flavor, this one might not satisfy your craving. Still, it’s okay for a quick bite when you want something easy, just not the “fireball” experience the name suggests.

I chanced upon Jay Jia Yentafo while taking a 30-minute walk from my hotel to clock some steps before dinner. Along the way, I noticed this humble spot with a Michelin Guide logo and decided to give it a try—and I’m so glad I did!

I ordered the dry noodle dish and initially thought it might be bland since there didn’t seem to be any chili sauce. However, it turned out to be incredibly flavorful! The noodles were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of chew, and the seasoning was well-balanced, with crispy garlic and shallots adding great texture and aroma.

The toppings were fresh and generous—fish balls, fish cake slices, crispy wonton skin—all of which made the dish a delight to eat. The portion size was satisfying without feeling heavy, and the flavors were surprisingly complex for such a simple dish.

The staff were friendly and attentive, and when they noticed I was a tourist, they even provided an English menu, which made ordering so much easier. The quick service and nostalgic floral bowl added to the charm of the experience.

A gem worth visiting!

Magical! Best yen ta fo I have had. Flavour is perfect, not too sweet, a good kick, ahhhh delicious!!! Noodles are a great size. 60 baht.

Wantons… man these are good. Stuffed with shrimp. Pair really nicely with the soup.

Takes about 10 min to prep the soup. Pretty happening on a Sunday afternoon. Filled with locals. Just delish!

Saved this place for quite some time. Finally, I had a chance to visit this place this eatery. It is located near Sanyan railway station, a bit of distance but walkable. Reached the place slightly past 9am, place wasn't crowded and there were only a few tables of customers.

Menu was pretty straightforward and easy to  understand for a foreigner. Ordered the yemtafo and a bowl of fried wanton and shrimp ball. Food didn't take long to arrive. Noodle was not bad, soup tasted a little tangy after mixing with the sauce. Fried wanton and shrimp ball was tasty as well, it goes really well with the tangy chili sauce.

Overall, the dinning experience was pretty good. Food was good and the place was clean. In total, paid 120baht for my meal.

restaurant_name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Bang Khae Road)
review_text: Accept the people said, i.e. having good taste.

restaurant_name: Jao Nai Fish Ball (Bang Khae Road)
review_text: I moved from Bangkok's Chinatown to the suburbs, where there's a Michelin Bib Gourmand-recommended fish ball shop. It's too far away, and not very tourist-friendly.
Nice place for authentic Thai food. The dishes are tasty. The restaurant has a local vibe with good, friendly service.

Took this effort to try this restaurant recommended by The Michelin Guide. While they get it right 90-95% of the time, this was a miss for me. The  yellow chicken curry was watery and tasteless, portions were small and the signature crab curry was served cool and not warm/ hot. It was definitely pre-cooked and served from a pot that was left for a while. Another challenge was a full menu in english and lack of English speaking (even basic) staff. This to me was a real let down. Only the fried garlic squid was good. Plus, pricewise this place was on the high side. I would  rate the food a 2.5/5 not 3/5 as have written
I love the food here, it always good and fresh. The staff is also friendly, will recommend dishes and provide good service.
both the hearty beef and sour seafood soup war very nice, the chicken&kale in soy sauce was tender and flavourful - good place to eat!

One of my top picks for authentic local cuisine is this restaurant, which specializes in Southern dishes. They offer both indoor and outdoor seating, and the staff is welcoming while the place maintains a clean atmosphere.

Don't miss out on their exceptional crispy pork belly with fish sauce—it's a must-try!

I would rate this as one of my worst fine dining tasting menu Experience so far. When the food tastes horrible with zero harmony of flavors everything comes down. The service and plating was ok though.

I have to say, if only talk about food, this could be my favorite during this trip. But then again overall experiences wise, probably not the best (still very enjoyable though).

I was here for lunch and, I was the only guest of the entire restaurant for the time I was there, I wonder why. Food is fantastic, innovative, yet incorporates local flavors very well. Good flow and balance among the dishes. I truly enjoyed the 16 course menu. It's pescatarian, no meat was served, only seafood, but I didn't even realize till later as I enjoyed almost every dishes. The main dish served as rice with soup and some side dishes were fantastic.

Surprisingly the wine list was also more extensive than most of the restaurants I have visited in Phuket. I ordered a good Italian which is very enjoyable and pairs well.

Service, on the other hand, was lukewarm. Polite but, feels lacking. There was not much interaction between staffs, chef and guest, even I was the only person there. It felt like I walked into a random store and they just have to open the shop for me (which is true actually haha).

Maybe it would be different during dinner or when there are more guests, but to go up another level, services definitely needs to be improved. Again, food was fantastic.

This restaurant is an extraordinary culinary gem, offering an intimate dining experience with only a few seats. The menu is a celebration of authentic Thai cuisine, featuring local dishes crafted from seafood freshly caught by local fishermen each day.

The chef adds a personal touch by visiting each table to introduce the dishes, sharing their story and inspiration. The setting is beautifully decorated, creating an atmosphere of elegance and warmth. Combined with impeccable service, this is the ultimate destination for discovering the finest local flavors.

Wonderful food with lots of seafood ingredients showcasing strong southern Thai  and bold flavours (some food were quite spicy haha). Service was attentive and good, they cared to introduce the food design and engaged in further conversations. Spacious and relaxing atmosphere. We had the tasting menu with 16 dishes, we left with a full stomach. It was a good value for money experience.

Samut was probably the most incredible dining experience I’ve had. We were expecting regular fine dining, but this was above and beyond your usual fine dining dinner. This was an experience.

We went for the samut experience and each dish arrived individually and had its own unique flavour. The staff were very attentive, and took their time to explain each dish and tell you how to eat them and advise on the best order to eat them for the perfect flavour combinations which was amazing!

The combinations and flavours were some of the most fresh and most unique I’ve seen and truly, each dish was a small explosion of flavours. My partner and I especially enjoyed the fish ham and mango dish. The final dessert was absolutely beautiful. 4 small desserts on a plate ending with a white chocolate and shrimp dessert. Who would have thought?

We loved the personal touch of the chef coming out at the end of the night and talking to us about the dishes!
Absolutely worth the money in my opinion and if I could give them an 11/10 I would! Cannot wait to visit again!

Enjoyed the 5-Course Signature Menu with wine pairing which was absolutely fantastic and a great treat for our anniversary. The food was outstanding and the hospitality incredible.

Special shout out to Khun Am out waiter and Khun hut our sommelier (apologies if spelling is wrong).

Overall excellent quality and value for money considering the standard of experience.

I’ve been to this restaurant several times, but this was my first time trying their Sunday lunch buffet—and I’d definitely recommend it. While the selection isn’t huge, every dish was excellent, more like a fine dining buffet than a typical one. The chef was generous with the caviar add-on. Service was outstanding, especially from K. Amp, who made us feel special and completely at ease—even when we ordered a lot 😆.

From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere was welcoming and full of joy. The service by K’Am was absolutely delightful — warm, attentive, and thoughtful, making the entire dining experience even more memorable.

Compliments to the chef and the entire team: the food was nothing short of perfection. Each dish was delicately prepared, beautifully presented, and bursting with flavour. The balance of creativity and refinement truly reflected fine dining at its best.
🌟🌟 🌟  "Cauliflower  veloute " from heaven!

An unforgettable experience — we’ll certainly return! 🌟
Some of the best food we have ever had. This was a real dining experience. The staff was exceptional and the wine pairing enhanced the flavours nicely.

Before we went, we could not find out much about the monthly brunch, so here it is. Once a month on Sunday at THB1800++. They send the menu in advance and you pay a THB2000 deposit for 2 pax.

The menu is set and not al la carte buffet (which is what we had expected). It took a mind-bending 3+ hours. I think the whole event is a staff training exercise!!

The staff are amazing and the environment nice. The food was OK. Most dishes were just OK but the ham and cream cheese sping rolls were not restaurant-standard food. Dessert was good and the Thai Granmonte wine a revelation! OK for the money but would not repeat.

The photos - for some reason -are in reverse order 😁

I stumbled upon Osha Restaurant in Bangkok simply because it was near where I was staying, and what a fortunate discovery it turned out to be. Already recognized with a Michelin star, it hardly needs my evaluation—but what I can say is that dining here was a truly memorable experience. If you ever find yourself in Bangkok, it’s a place you should experience at least once. Some meals fill the stomach, but this one also lingered in the heart.

Highly recommended! every dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented, the staff were friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. Prices were reasonable for the quality you get. Will definitely come back again 💯
Beautiful environment from the moment you walk in, and the food is a true representation of traditional Thai food. We will be coming back for the tasting menu.

15 mins walk from Ploen Chit BTS station, along the stretch of Embassies. Michelin star restaurant serving Thai-Fusion. Food was not spectacular but accompanied by dramatic presentations & aesthetically pleasing plating, and impeccable service that completes the Michelin experience. It's much like common dishes elevated through quality ingredients such as Hokkaido Scallop, Canadian Lobster and huge River Prawns. The soup for example, was a typical Tom Yum soup but the wow came in the presentation where the soup was heated in lab-apparatus-looking device, gets sucked into the container above to be infused with the spices there, then flowing back before it's being poured into our bowls.

I like that we got a whole private room (glasshouse that's beautifully designed set in greenery) to ourselves. Being in the private room, we also had a visually impaired pianist playing exclusively for us all night.
Very nice place, the architecture is super special, the service very attentive and of course, the food is delicious, I’d also say the prices are fair and moderate.

We had a premium omakase dinner here. The experience was wonderful.

Due to the traffic jam we were a little late, we were so worried that we would be rejected by being late. Luckily the reception was nice and  considerate and we were still welcomed.

The seat was a little tiny but it’s ok that we got to know the process of the chef making our food. They would introduce the materials before serving each dish. We learned a lot of knowledges while we were eating. Lol

The food was fresh and delicious. Around 20 dishes. The drink was very 👍. I liked the green grapes which were sweet and crispy!

The sushi lunch is good. Every sushi is very tasteful and beautifully presented and prepared.

Price wise it is slightly more expensive than the other omakase. Most likely because they were a 1 star michelin in the past. Sake drinks menu for glasses could be more elaborated.

At end I did have extreme stomach pain though (one hour long diarrhea) and I have eaten dozens of sushi omakase throughout the world. The person I was with was okay so perhaps some of my dishes were tainted but overall it tasted fresh. Kitchen should check their equipment and storage of food perhaps.

Sushi Masato is a solid name in Bangkok for sushi omakase. I have been here several times and Chef Masato never disappoint.
Top notch seasonal ingredients, best techniques to bring out the best quality and taste.
Since its always what's in season, you will never be bored of what you get here.

Of course reservation needed. And parking is not the most convenient here

Had the most memorable omakase here—and it’s absolute paradise for sushi lovers. Every piece of fish was so fresh it tasted like it had just come off the boat: the buttery toro melted smoothly on the tongue, the briny uni had zero fishy aftertaste, and even the simple tuna nigiri shone with its bright, clean flavor.

The chef’s craft made it even better—each sushi had the perfect balance of vinegared rice (not too sticky, not too sour) and perfectly sliced fish, so every bite felt intentional. If you live for that “just-caught” freshness in sushi, this spot is non-negotiable.

I can only praise how delicious the omakase was. Highly recommend to try. They change the menu by Japan’s season. That’s every 2-4 months. I had the spring set this time.
The ingredients seems to be sourced from Japan so the they’re adapted the menu accordingly. Excellent Omakase experience.

For the serious foodies:
The technical execution is not good enough for the price

This is a weird place because they have a lot of English and the prices are sky high, so you'd think they appeal to tourists, but the dips are so ridiculously spicy that you'd think only a true Thai can stomach them. Wtv the case, it translates to an absolutely empty restaurant during lunch

The dry aged beef tongue has the super bouncy texture from the dry aging, which is not good it has way too much bite. The unpleasant glaze? on the surface of the tongue completely overwhelms everything, so it's not good.

Duck heart chimichurri is pretty good, their duck heart is decent and the chimichurri is seriously good. However the duck hearts were way too hot when served, making for a very unpleasant eating experience when the dips were so spicy

Second visit:
Northern hot dog was a blast of flavours, pickle was brilliant, but it needed a bit more balance. Also, the sausage itself is served way too hot, since it's spicy

Pictured is their Jasmine wagyu bms11 oyster blade. Looks good enough but I find it hard to spit out 2500thb for a 200g piece of Thai wagyu, that's pretty much Japanese wagyu prices, except that this is only oyster blade, not ribeye

Pork skewers has a nice fish sauce marinade but very similar to the duck heart. Moreover, it also has the overly bouncy bite. I've seen a few people complaining about the bite of their food in the reviews

Banana dessert was not good
Their ice cream was way too cold and not smooth. The banana crisps were too big to eat properly, and despite one component, the juicy bananas intriguing me, the flavours just doesnt pop at all. Plus, the coconut milk was nowhere near viscous enough to work as a sauce

The quality of the food does not justify the price. No wows, and some execution aren't good enough, so really no reason to visit. If you think I'm being too harsh, this is a place that serves 500thb appetisers and 1000 thb mains, so they're fine dining, and should be critiqued as such

A modern restaurant that relies on authentic Thai cuisine with a twist.

We got a lot of recommendations on it, and the experience was very good, except we were kind of disappointed with the food and it didn't meet our expectations after the hype we heard this restaurant has.

After ordering the food, they serve a complimentary set of appetizer dishes - a classic papaya salad (was too spicy in my opinion), a papaya salad with fermented fish sauce (we couldn't eat it at all as it had a strong fermented flavor), pork cracklings with 3 dipping sauces (all three tasted good but 2 of them were way too spicy so we couldn't really enjoy them).

From the starters section we ordered a larb kon muang pork which is a warm salad made from ground pork meat and some green herbs. The flavors were good, but again it was also a bit too spicy to our palate.
Another dish we tried was the mok pla which is fish pieces sticked together and steamed in a banana leaf. This one was also ok, but it had dill in it (which we absolutely hate), and it kind of ruined the dish for us. We never imagined we'll be served dill in a Thai cuisine restaurant.

For the main dish we ordered the fermented pork ribs which were by far the best dish of our lunch, as they were perfectly cooked & seasoned, so that one single dish saved lunch for us.

The service was kind and professional, but the prices were quite high and I'm not sure it was the best VFM for us, considering we didn't like most of the food, as well as portion sizes weren't so big.

To conclude, if you're planning on coming here, I'd recommend checking out the menu in advance and making sure you relate to it, otherwise you'll leave somewhat disappointed like we did.

Love a restaurant that not only champions local produce but champions nose to tail, stalk to root cooking so that nothing gets wasted in the cooking.

100 is both familiar yet totally modern in its menu. You taste familiar Thai flavors but with modern elevated takes on the dishes.

While I am tempted to say the star attractions of the restaurant are its beautiful meat selection ( especially the beef) and their incredible grill mastery ( trust me, they were very very good),

The hidden gem was their very clever dessert selection. Again, taking the theme of familiar flavors and putting a spin on it. Green mango salad as a dessert? Amazing ...

Service was attentive, knowledgeable and unobtrusive, just the way I like it.

A must visit ...

P/s: come as a party, so you can try and share more dishes

A solid casual dining experience with a good drink selection and an interesting / varied Menu.  The Grilled Braised Ox Tongue is a bit tough for my taste and neither I nor my partner really continued on with it.  The Thai Beef Jerky was what we fought over instead.  Excellent selection of dry aged meats.

100 Mahaseth really lives up to the hype. It’s not your usual Thai fare for tourists — they focus on nose-to-tail cooking with strong Isaan roots, but done in a way that’s modern and super well-executed.

Everything was flavourful, punchy, and well-balanced, like how Thai food should be. Even the sides and complementary dips show character.

Vibe-wise, it’s trendy but still got that relaxed Bangkok charm. Service was friendly and knew their stuff, gave good recos without being pushy.

Definitely not the cheapest Thai meal in town, but if you appreciate quality ingredients and a different take on Thai food that still respects the roots, this place delivers. Would bring friends or visiting colleagues here for something a bit special but still grounded

I'd like to recommend this restaurant to someone who loves seafood. The freshwater prawns and cockles were exceptionally large. However, I found some of the menu items to be quite overpriced; for example, a plain egg omelette cost 130 THB

Kin Kub Koi: Incredibly Fresh Seafood, Incredibly Fast!
What an amazing find! I had a fantastic meal at Kin Kub Koi on Phutthamonthon Sai 2. This place is a must-try for seafood lovers.
The food is not only incredibly delicious but also comes out remarkably fast—perfect for when you're hungry! The highlight was definitely the seafood; it was all so fresh, you can taste the quality in every bite. I particularly loved the flavorful salty stir-fried prawns, which had a truly great taste.
We also enjoyed a plate of juicy stir-fried squid, perfectly cooked cabbage, and a delicious bowl of rice topped with fresh crab meat. Everything was a testament to the freshness and quality. I highly recommend this spot for anyone craving top-tier seafood with lightning-fast service!

Kin Kub Koi Restaurant has three expansive dining areas which quickly filled up as the lunch crowd came in. Food is delicious specialising in seafood. Good place for large group meals. Their dessert station near entrance has a lot of choices. The sticky rice mango and cooked bananas were good.

Mantis prawn is fresh and lightly cooked tender 9/10
The water mimosa is young and tender unlike most other places. Nice👍🏻 9/10
Kheng som with chaaom and fried egg 8/10
Spicy fried rice with a hint of sour, had petai and huge prawns  10/10
Spiced cuttlefish 8/10
Squid egg, bouncy like fishball. Very nice texture and not fishy. 8/10
Their other seafood dishes were all decent as well.

We had the grill river prawn. Its very tasty but slightly under cooked. The spicy pork belly is very tender and crunchy. Highly recommended. The best dish is the curry crab with egg. This is absolute must try, prefect with rice and everything is just right. Not too much cumin ...The perfect dish !!

Before eating at Kin Kub Koi (KKK), I’d never been to Pinklao. And for good reason, because besides massive gated housing communities, there isn’t much there.

It’s also off the beaten path. However, it is home to KKK, a sprawling Michelin-starred seafood restaurant that is hugely popular.

KKK’s size and scale are immediately apparent - the restaurant car park is nearly the same size as a small city airport car park. Entering, I like how the staff line up to greet you as you enter one of the several large dining spaces.

We had a big party of 19, enabling us to order a lot - crab, river prawns, prawns, cockles, clams, crab eggs, mantis prawns, and more. They were fried, spiced, steamed, deep fried, baked, etc, and while I liked most of the dishes, my faves were the steamed crab with dipping sauce and mantis prawn stir fried with garlic - simple, simple, simple.

The quality and freshness of the seafood were top notch and Michelin-worthy indeed. Would I go again? Not sure as I like my seafood cooked as simply as possible- but KKK is definitely worth visiting once at least.

But note, they do not take bookings, so try to avoid the dining rush hours.

The room was spacious and incredibly clean with a comfortable bed and a smart TV. It is centrally located with easy access to nearby attractions.

The service was excellent. They cared for our family and did a great job making us feel welcome.

The breakfast was really nice. There is a variety of dishes to choose from on the breakfast menu, and a very nice breakfast bar featuring fresh fruit and vegetables, crepes, and a host of other items. We enjoyed our stay and will visit again when we return to Khon Kaen.

Our experience at this establishment in Mana hotel was highly positive. The staff provided exceptional service, and the accommodations were modern, exceptionally clean, and well-maintained. While the color-coded room identification system presented a unique approach, the quality of the breakfast was also commendable.

I stayed here for seven days, starting August 16, 2025. The room was spacious and clean. The bathroom had good water pressure and no sewer odor. The floor was tiled, not carpeted, which was really nice. The smart TV worked well with Netflix and YouTube. The only downside was the small refrigerator and limited space. The breakfast was fantastic. There was a wide selection to choose from, and the cheese, shallots, and various dressings were delicious and clean. If I ever return to Khon Kaen, I'll definitely be back.
This was outstanding! Room was topclass, bed was really comfortable. Clean and very modern. The breakfast was excellent, the best breakfast I've had in Thailand. Video uploaded.

Everything about this hotel is top class! Definitely a hidden gem, well worth staying. Beautifully designed, spacious room, delightful staff, fantastic food (European & Thai, french cheeses!), quiet location. Very highly recommend.

This was our first meal in Chiang Mai and we drove about 45 minutes from the international airport.

There are dining facilities inside but we chose to sit outside as the evening was cool.

Service was friendly but a little slow as the place was around half full.  They have a plaque showing they received Michelin recognition in 2020, and the food was mostly nice and tasty.

We enjoyed the fried glass noodles so much that we re-ordered the dish.  The omelette and the small shrimp dish were also nice, as was the starter plate featuring pork crackling and the delicious local issan sausages.

The larb, which came with a hugh plate of vegetables and which included innards, was more of an acquired taste.

Prices were reasonable and you also get to enjoy sitting surrounded by ponds.

Our hotel manager recommended this restaurant.  We love their tomyum gung!! This Muchelin guide restaurant lived to its name. Given that we could only order seafood n vegetarian dishes,  we opted for the fried tilapia with garlic, omelette,  morning glory n kale. Definitely worth going again!

And we went on the second time ...very happy with our dinner!

The menu photos doesn’t look attractive at all but the foods turns out to be quite decent other than the sweet and sour fish which was really so so……..service wise is really a “basic services” restaurant………..it is a really fair priced restaurant which is good resting place if you are nearby…….

I love all their dishes but my favorite was the glass noodles and the snail curry. I highly recommend the indoor seating area as the flies in the outdoor area were really annoying and affected our dining experience. The indoor area was full when we arrived so it's better to make reservations first.

One of the better Michelin restaurants I’ve been in chiang mai. It’s a bit far from the city and the food presentation is not as nice, but I like the taste. It’s worth a visit.

Their pan fried dishes have the “wok hey” taste. They have good cooking equipment at a high temperature that is hard to make this taste at home. Not all the restaurants can do that.

Food are all delicious and authentic. Had a great time dining in. We did walk-in only here and the staffs are super accommodating to us. Ambiance add up to overall experience. Next to the pier going to Wat Arun. Highly recommended👍

Restaurant was small, but cosy. The first floor dining area basically looks out to the Tha Thein Pier for the ferry service to Wat Arun where the monument can be seen across the river
Was probably placed at the most strategic viewing corner for our table of 4. Best views at the 2nd level terrace which was hot and humid.

Food was good, ingredients were fresh. But not mind blowingly so.

Would I go back? Maybe.

Amazing overall dining experience. My only feedback is the table is a bit small for all the food we ordered lol had to scramble to finish some so they can place more on the table. Loved the food and chill atmosphere with the riverside view. The highlight dishes were the seared pork slices and the Thai tea pana cotta - would come back for these!

Food wasn't the best, it's either too salty or too sweet. We ordered all the recommended dishes, turns out only the beef salad was okay. Staff attitude and services were top notch. As for restaurant's atmosphere, choose indoor level 1 area. The 2nd floor rooftop was so clustered, barely able to let anyone move around plus the heat, don't worth the hype. In summary, an overrated and disappointing experience.

Supanniga serves flavorful, simple Thai food that masterfully exemplifies the "less is more" approach. The dishes showcase a disciplined focus on highlighting proteins and bold, authentic flavors rather than relying on culinary gimmicks. Standouts include the fried rice, reminiscent of bagoong rice, a creamy seabass soup, and a meaty crab omelette.

While the drinks and dessert were unfortunately a bit forgettable and could be more distinct, the warm, fast, and topnotch service was impeccable. Food is then 4.5/5.

With its perfect ambiance overlooking the temples, it is an essential stop to carve into your Bangkok itinerary for a memorable temple day.

Came here wanting to eat Thai food, but it is much more Thai Chinese. Curry crab was good, pork satay was good. All the rest were alright. Good meal on the whole, just don't expect to be mind blown. The wait was decent at about under 7 minutes. But the place is small, so if you hit a crowd, expect to wait.

I honestly can’t believe this place is only rated 4.1 stars! Out of all the restaurants I tried in Thailand, this one is definitely my favorite. Instead of sticking to the classics like Tom Yum or Pad Thai, I went for different and unique dishes and they were amazing.

The staff is incredibly kind and helpful, the prices are very fair, and I just simply loved the whole experience. The oyster egg is an absolute must-try!

Difficult restaurant if you travel by car. We parked at BigC nearby. The portions size here is massive. We ordered their signature curry crab and the crab was huge! Very tasty dish, quality ingredients for the price of 2,000thb. Our other favorite dish was the fried pork, very aromatic, not too tough to bite into. However despite their delicious food, we dont really appreciate the service, it's a mostly self service.
Absolutely delicious!!! Start to finish best food we’ve had in Bangkok so far! They were kind and patient with us as we ordered.

reviewer: TommyV wwg “Tvwwg cmpse Net Review” GT NetRider
review_text:
10 tables only Restaurant !!!
Food 6* original taste
Mid service 3* but quick
Old-school, Classic style restaurant.  It the Ú unique style Seafood & Chinese shop.

A great local restaurant that has received a Michelin award.
The restaurant is quite small with only a few tables, so you might have to wait for a table during the evening. Recommended dishes include tamarind sauce prawns, clear soup with minced pork and pickled mustard greens, and there are other delicious item feel free to ask the staff. The food doesn’t take too long to arrive. The place may not look very clean, but the food is tasty.

Came back a second time for the famous Tamarind Prawns and Fried Rice.

Food was definitely delicious and well worth coming back again...
Bummer was they got another couple to share table and the couple, obviously from China, was rude... guy took my seat when I just walked away for a while!
Also, my fried rice was served fast after taking my order but the Tamarind Prawns came 20 minutes late. Saw customers who came later having their  orders served first before me... was annoying and don't know if they forgot my order or otherwise. They started preparing only after I reminded them that I had one more dish....

The famous tamarind prawns were a little too sweet for my taste!

Fried rice was good.

Service by the aunty was super friendly.
This is local restaurant in Phuket town, there are cooking with fresh ingredients seafood, so it’s tasty, there are 6-10 tables.
Overall, it was good. We ordered the medium size shrimp, which was really big. It cost 550 Thai baht.

It was wonderful meal and service. I went there with my mother for her birthday, and ordered Le Grand Voyage course. I didn't regret any second in that 4-hour long meal. Thank you to Chef Dunand, all other chefs, and service staffs.

The food was a great experience. All dishes are wonderful journey. My favorites are the bluefin tuna and the blue lobster. It's one of the best lobster I've ever had.

Le Grand Voyage took around 4 hours. As my mother prefers not to finish a meal too late at night, so we booked a lunch. It was only 2 groups in that lunch time, with only us in the second floor.

Also we got a delicious birthday cake for my mom as a complimentary.

From start to finish, our experience at this restaurant was truly impressive. The ambiance was elegant yet inviting, with thoughtful details that set the tone for a special evening.

The service stood out immediately—professional, attentive, and perfectly timed. Staff were knowledgeable about the menu and wine pairings, offering just the right balance of warmth and refinement.

Each course was beautifully presented and full of flavor, showcasing a clear mastery of technique and a deep respect for ingredients. Every bite felt intentional, and the pacing of the meal allowed us to fully enjoy each dish without feeling rushed.

Overall, it was a seamless and memorable dining experience. Whether you're celebrating something special or simply looking to enjoy outstanding food and service, this place delivers on every level.

This one-star Michelin restaurant is a true all-rounder — not only for its refined cuisine, but also for its serene ambience, immaculate service, and flawless presentation. Every detail is executed with precision, making it an experience of complete perfection.

Chef Dunand’s French cooking is elegant and distinctive, marked by fresh ingredients, refined technique, and creative pairings that set his dishes apart. From starters to mains, bread, desserts, and petits fours, the consistency is remarkable.

At about USD 130 per person for the set lunch, it offers not just a meal but a beautifully curated dining experience — calm, memorable, and thoroughly commendable.

What an experience!
Chef Arnaud food is excellent! The story telling is really enjoyable, for each dish.

Every plate come with small postal card explaining where inspiration come from - this touch make me feel special connection to food.

The taste are nothing like other restaurant I visit before - real mountain flavors but with Michelin star quality! First time I was experiencing alpine cuisine, but I’ll be back 🥰

The service is also excellent, explaining and coming to your table to cut, prepare some dish. The venue looking like a luxury chalet.

I recommend if you’re passing by Bangkok or if you live here and haven’t try it yet!

☆☆☆ Food
☆☆☆☆☆ Atmosphere
☆☆☆☆ Service
☆☆☆ Value

On the day of visit, chef Arnaud Dunand was away oversea with collaboration. We should have called ahead to inquire. This restaurant is beautifully decorated, good service, however we left disappointed. We ordered a la carte as we want to enjoy the premium ingredients.  Perhaps high expectation, the Brittany lobster, came in a tiny portion  (Thai Baht 2,800++) and was prepared with Indian Kari Gosse and chopped up Thai larb salad style. The spices being overpowering, didn’t enhance the natural flavor. However the lobster was lukewarm and not fresh to begin with.

For souffle, we only tasted beaten and baked egg white, no flavoring. One bite and we had to return it.

This was our second visit. For an esteemed fine dining establishment and price to match, these two unremarkable visits left an unpleasant experience.

Exceptional. Big fan. Was here in 2021, and just had to come back as soon as I can. So much care is put into the food. Everything tastes amazing. I find the dishes and seasoning refreshing creative as well. The fresh tofu was amazing.

Generally speaking, the food is of very high quality.  The setting is designed in a Japanese style.  In accordance with the norms of Japanese cuisine, each dish is prepared with great care. There is not a lot of space available at the restaurant.  The environment is clean and comfortable to be in.  Even though the portion sizes of each dish are fair, some people who consume a lot of food could find them to be too small.  Because of the great quality of the food, the price of the cuisine is fairly high; however, it is well worth the money being spent.  Perhaps you won't be able to consume it on a daily basis.  The service at the restaurant is very courteous and of high quality.

Very friendly people. All the food was freshly prepared and tasted amazing. The atmosphere was cozy and comfortable, and the air conditioning made it even more pleasant. I would definitely recommend this place to others!
If you go to Chiang Mai, do not miss this small gem.  The food are so fresh and lovely.  Everything about this humble, cozy shop is pure magical.  Highly recommended and I will definitely come again.
Japanese food served at a very high quality. Everything is fresh and delicious.
A nice Michelin Authentic Thai restaurant definitely to visit in Khao Yai. Their fried items are so well done. The service is great. Plenty of parking and pet-friendly.

This restaurant is very crowded. The staff, though not rushing patrons, efficiently clear and manage tables to accommodate the waiting line. It's recommended to arrive early, ideally around 11 AM or earlier, as they do not take reservations.
The food is spicy, made with fresh ingredients, and delicious. While the prices are on the higher side, they are reasonable for the quality. Service is good, and it's important to note that they are cash only.

What a fantastic lunch we had at Yungkhaow Khao Yai before heading back to Bangkok! With a group of 17 adults and kids, it can be tough to please everyone, but Yungkhaow nailed it. The food was absolutely incredible, and the customer service was top-notch, handling our large group with ease. We were told this place was a must-visit, and we all agree—so glad we finally made it here.

If you look for Thai-Southern food in Khaoyai, this should be one of your lists to try. I like the food here which tastes like authentic southern food but not too spicy. I tried a few times with different menus, of which my favorite is Krua Kling Nua (Beef in stir-fried chilli), the texture of the beef was so tender that it was stir-fried well. Price is acceptable, but not cheap. If you come during a busy weekend, it may take a while to get a table. I would recommend trying, if you want to break from Pasta or Steak in Khao Yai.

The menu here is quite unique and noticeably different from typical Thai cuisine. If you’re visiting Khao Yai, it’s definitely worth a try. Many people travel here specifically for the food, so be prepared for a potentially long wait.

This is one of my favorite restaurants, and I always recommend it to friends, clients, or any foreigners who want to try authentic Thai cuisine. It’s one of the few places that still serves traditional dishes like Kratong Thong, Mee Krob Chao Wang, Moo Krajok, and Por Pia Tod a great starter set that lets you sample a variety of flavors at a very reasonable price.

The ambiance is classic and elegant, almost like stepping back into a Suntaraporn-era Thailand, with live piano music and traditional Thai singers performing classic Luk Krung songs while you enjoy your meal. It adds a nostalgic and sophisticated touch to the dining experience.

Today, I ordered some of my favorite dishes. The Green Curry was a hit, mild enough for foreigners to enjoy while still keeping the authentic Thai flavors. The Gaeng Kua Pu Cha-Om (Crab Curry with Acacia Omelet) was rich and flavorful, and the Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup) was another must-try dish. If you’re looking for something special, the Yam Sam Grob (Three Crispy Flavors Salad) is a standout, offering a perfect balance of sweet, sour, and spicy.

This restaurant is a true gem, perfect for introducing foreign visitors to traditional Thai cuisine in a setting that feels both nostalgic and elegant. Highly recommended! 🎶🍛

I come here often because of the food and atmosphere, its like you are in another era of Bangkok.  The food was excellence as always but service is very sloppy, not sure about Michelin star they got.  First we have to move our plate for the new food, which often done by waiter/waitress.  Second they ask for the glass to refill our drinks.  Third they never inform us about what is out of order on the menu, and they will come back later to tell us that this dish is out.

The rest of the night was fantastic, good food, good music.

The flavours were amazing and blends so well together within each dish. Ingredients used were fresh too.

While the plating and ambience was not the same as what one would expect of a typical one star Michelin restaurant, the flavours and the warm response of the staff made up for it.

Definitely worth a try!
All dishes are authentic taste👍 we're enjoyed the food and live music. See you next time!

Recommended by our tour guide.

Wouldn't say the best best Thai restaurant but was still very good and accessible.

Family members - Europeans and Asians. many of who didn't have Thai food experience before - all enjoyed the food.

Strongly recommend!

Thom yam, Pad Thai, and khao pot were all good. Good value for money!

The ingredients are top-notch and incredibly fresh. Prices are reasonable for the quality you get. If you sit at the counter bar, you can enjoy watching the chefs in action.

Beef tongue is a must-order, perfectly cooked and packed with flavor. We also tried the grilled Gindara (black cod); the fish was very fresh, though slightly too salty.

One small hiccup: we ordered oysters but they didn’t make it to the kitchen. Still, the overall experience was excellent.

This authentic Japanese restaurant is highly recommended and better to have a reservation. I will definitely be back!

I've had lunch here many times because it's convenient and offers high-quality authentic Japanese dishes. The lunch set is great value for the price, which is average for Japanese restaurants in Bangkok. The food is fresh and tastes like it's made by a private chef. For one price, you get rice with fish or pork, a salad, a soup, a side dish, and your choice of hot or iced tea. They also offer coffee or tea after the meal.

BTW, dinner is another level, there are many many menu I can recommend here.

If you are looking for high quality Japanese cuisine in Bangkok, you are at the right spot. From appetizers (sashimi), to main dish (all Japanese skewer and seafood bbq) and the best dorayaki I have ever tried in my life.

The sweet potato and dorayaki skin are fluffy, the cream is not light and they also put some honey inside and it balance the entire flavor of the dessert 👌🏻

It is very rare to found a Japanese restaurant giving you surprises in every dish, I am dying to come back again! 😋

I was here for a breakfast buffet and a dinner.
The buffet breakfast consists of the Japanese, Thai and Western food. The cooked Japanese rice is so nice! Assorted Furikake to sprinkle on. The coffee from the coffee machine was also nice.

As for dinner, I ordered Tori Ramen and Grilled Shimahokke fish. The Tori in the ramen are a piece of charcoal-grilled chicken and another one is a piece of smoked duck. They were both nice! There is charcoal aroma to the grilled fish!
Charcoal-grilled Chicken Skewers Set of 5 were really nice, so tender inside!
Salmon spicy rolls were fresh and tasted good, just a little bit spicy, not strong.
The Salmon Potted Rice for two people was really nice, big serving and tasted good.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
True Japanese precision with a smoky soul—an omakase-like yakitori experience in Bangkok.
Tucked inside Sotetsu Grand Fresa, Gen is a hidden gem for those who appreciate fine ingredients, quiet ambiance, and authentic Japanese grilling.

🔥 Every skewer was grilled to perfection over real binchotan charcoal, with standout dishes like tsukune (served with raw egg yolk), chicken wing, and asparagus wrapped in pork.
🥚 The tamagoyaki was soft and silky—an impressive balance of savory and sweet.
🥩 The wagyu steak? Beautifully marbled, medium rare with crispy edges and paired with Himalayan salt, wasabi, and garlic chips—simply unforgettable.
🍣 We also sampled rare cuts of tuna (kama, noten, cheek), each with distinct textures and clean, umami flavors.
🍚 Their claypot-style salmon ikura rice (kamameshi) was fragrant and satisfying, served tableside with a rustic presentation.

🎎 The vibe was calm and cozy with Japanese hospitality at heart. Staff were knowledgeable and attentive, explaining the cuts and sequence of service like a quiet omakase.

💴 Price is upscale, but absolutely fair for the quality. Best for special dinners or quiet celebrations.
📍Located just a short walk from Asok BTS and Sukhumvit MRT.

Stand alone in the field restaurant. By the ways, many people still try to find the way to eat Chicken rice at this restaurant. Boiled Chicken meat is squishy and fresh. Rice is also delicious. They claimed that their chicken is well-feeded by themselves so their meat is very high quality. If you have chance to pass around Nakhon Pathom, cannot miss this place.

This restaurant is the one of the best chicken rice (in list top10 of my chicken rice).

Mr. Ho is an owner of recipe, he has chicken farm for supply to the restaurant.

Boiled chicken is the best!
Oily rice is good
Overall is over expected and worth it!

Recommend!
Come here before noon, they always sold out in 1pm

This is an interesting Thai-style chicken rice shop. The chicken is tender yet not dry, while the rice is not too greasy but still moist. The ultimate highlight is the dipping sauce. If you’re in the Nakhon Pathom area, I highly recommend stopping by to try it!

It’s worth waiting for over 1 over for this the must chicken rice in Nakorn Pathom. They raise their own chicken of this chicken rice. I order both leg quarter with back bone parts (more tender and chewy) and breast with wing parts (more dry). I like both. Serving with chicken broth and free spicy sauce on the table. That are great combination. 😋

• A well-known spot, but a bit out of the way. The food is average—not bad, but nothing particularly memorable.

• Worth a stop if you’re already in the area, but probably not worth a long trip just for the meal.

reviewer: สุภัสสรา เลี่ยนกัตวา
review_text:
Highly recommended local restaurant in Phuket!!! Food is sooo delicious and not expensive at all.
The service is so good, people are very kind and nice,I love their smile!! The vibe of this restaurant is also comfy, shady like a you take your meal at your asian friends house! also you have to order “Moo Hong” very delicious menu! Highly recommended guys!!!

This is an honest review, with no judgement of you or your background. This place probably serves the best iteration of the dishes available that you will ever have. For me, they are top 5 or top 10, but I've been eating them for many years. Soak in the culture here and have some good eats!

A very homie place. All staffs aka auntie and uncle were very nice. They serve free mango with Namplawhan sauce as an appetizer. The foods taste  delicious, flavorful and very authentic. Big portions. Would definitely come back here again

🌿🍤 Ton Mayom – Phuket’s Best-Kept Thai Food Secret! 🌟🇹🇭

Okay foodie fam… if you think Thai food is just Pad Thai and Tom Yum, it’s time to level up your tastebuds! 😮‍💨 I just visited Tonmayom, a local Michelin-recognized Thai restaurant tucked away in Phuket – and WOW, my world has changed.

This isn’t your tourist menu stuff — this is the real deal, the kind of flavor that only locals whisper about. I heard about it from a friend, and now I’m officially spreading the good word. 🙌

✨ The highlight?
🌶️ A Thai veggie dip that made me rethink everything I knew about veggies (how is it THIS good?)
🍳 And the dried prawn with egg and Thai leaves? I could eat it every day and never get bored. Fragrant, savory, slightly crispy – perfection.

If you're visiting Phuket and only know the classics – GO HERE. Your tastebuds deserve an upgrade.
This is Thai food that tells a story — and once you’ve tried it, you’ll never forget it.
Must visit! We had a Tom Yam soup (out of this world), port and fish, equally tasty.

Good atmosphere, especially at tables by the sea. We were the only guests and the experience was disappointing. Below average pad thai, squid green curry was okay and salat was an absolute joke with canned tuna fish. Authentic flavors were missing.. not worth the time. Michelin guides should brush their tongues. Overall underwhelming experience.

Excellent example of southern Thai flavours and produce freshness. The quality of the food reflects nicely for me as a Michelin recommended establishment on Koh Samui, and as someone who dined in a lot of local eats around the island.

Came here for lunch in good, clear (but hot hot) weather, and the cozy ambiance is just sublime with nice sea breeze and the island's beautiful beachfront views.

Many menus to choose from and this place does it true and authentic for southern Thai spices. Really nicely executed dishes, although timing felt a little tardy and inconsistent with the delivery of each dishes; but the dishes were just all so enjoyable nothing felt at all lacked.

Personal highlight is the Gaeng Pu, the crab betel leaf curry (I believe) - so packed with the herbals and spices, and southern curry flavour.

Edit: visited here again for dinner and the same nice experience is just consistent at this lovely beach Thai restaurant.
Wow is all I can say! Amazing food and atmosphere. If you great seafood this is the place! Shrimp with deep fried garlic so good and the crab with yellow curry was probably my favourite dish.
Beautiful quiet little restaurant we found on the Michelin Guide with delicious local cuisine! Do not regret! Best fish I ate in Samui 🩵

I'm not sure what happened  but our meal was very average and atmospherewas even worse. Kitchen didn't seem to be running at full capacity,  had no grill? But it was very empty for dinner time, we were the only table despite them saying they were busy? We got garlic prawns which had all the right things but it came out barely warm. Tom yum soup was what was a bit better, served with a generous amount of prawns and we got a steamed small 200g crab which was average.  Unfortunately the alfresco dining did not work for us. Make sure you bring insect repellent or you'll be the meal for mozzies, but also there were like a million bugs over our food... I had to pick it out of my rice because they kept flying into it. In the end we left early because the bugs were so bad. Plus our meal costed little over 1500 which I thought was more on the expensive side for what we got. Slightly underwhelmed sorry, maybe got a bad day?

The atmosphere here is absolutely incredible! The staff goes above and beyond with their amazing service, making you feel right at home. And the food? It’s a must-try—every dish is a delightful experience! This is undoubtedly the best spot in Chiang Mai!

The ambiance was decent amongst the Chiang Mai restaurants. We killed two mosquitos while waiting for the food.
The service was disappointing and nonexistent, although the staff was quick to rush us out.
I agree with the other reviewers that the food was not deserving of the Michelin Bib Gourmand.
We got the "Panaeng" curry with chicken and there was a raw piece of chicken.
The curry sauce was too oily.

Overall: There are better options in town.

Note: you have to spend over 1,000 baht to use a credit card.

My friends and I decided to visit this restaurant on our last night in Chiang Mai. We had been enjoying the local street food for the past few days, but we felt a bit tired of the bustle and wanted to have a more relaxed, refined meal. So I searched online and stumbled across this place.

Magnolia Cafe was an extremely suitable place for us. The Michelin ranking is well deserved, as both the restaurant’s staff and the decor make you feel very well taken care of. The food is excellent and reflects a healthy balance of creativity (watermelon cubes with salmon!) and authenticity. Everything we had was cooked to perfection, and the prices were extremely affordable. A restaurant of this stature and quality could easily charge more, and it would be well justified in doing so.

We even got complimentary canapés and desserts - totally unexpected and very well crafted. Do visit Cafe Magnolia if you have the chance, it will be worth it!

We went for dinner without reservation, fortunately server helped to arrange a table at the room of the back side which is very exclusive and nicely decorated.

I have no ideas that it was a Michelin restaurant but the signage posted on the entrance really impressive.

We ordered the following,
Watermelon cubes with crispy fried salmon floss, it's very common now in Chiangmai, salmon floss taste rich.
Penang Curry, mildly spicy and with a hint of nutty flavor, however the chicken didn't taste much.
Fried Mackerel with Nam Jim seafood , the fish fillet is fried to crisp, taste fresh but a little salty.
Grilled Pork Neck with Nam Jim Jew, the most tender pork neck I've ever taste, the meat is very tender and slightly pink in color, thank you for server's recommendation.

They offered complimentary welcome canapes, which was a tiny meat ball on pineapple. Also complimentary dessert,  gluey pandan coconut cream per guest. But I still ordered durian sticky rice which is too tempting. The medium soft durian laid on a bath of warm coconut milk and sticky rice which was a perfect finish of our dinner.

Servers were all very polite and attentive, you will not listen to anyone talking around you.

The whole restaurant full of collections of glasses and pottery wares and plated which are hand made. It's enjoyable for eating and appreciating those beautiful items.

Thank you for such a good dinner.

Don't mistake this place for a "cafe" as the name suggests. It's a Thai restaurant with a well deserved Michelin guide status for 3 years. It feels like eating at a friend's (who can cook incredibly well) home. The food is authentically Thai that brings to life the best of local ingredients and culinary creativity. Since it's contemporary Thai food, you won't find the usual popular Thai dishes here. I also love the homey atmosphere and great service. Recommend to come in group so you can taste many dishes!

See Na Nuan Café is more than just a café.
It’s a true dining experience. The food is beautifully presented and full of local flavor, no wonder it’s been in the Michelin Guide for 3 years straight! The place has a warm, natural vibe with great service and calm surroundings. Perfect spot for a relaxing but memorable meal in Khon Kaen.

yellow curry contained a lot of egg and onions, very little and small prawns. a few small squid pieces. disappointing
the fried fish had almost no taste, small. seemed not to be fresh.
the prawns in dough were not pealed. taste thanks to the sauce / dough.
price value does not match. absolute disappointed

A well-known restaurant in Khon Kaen, recommended by the Michelin Guide ⭐. Visited for dinner and found the decor elegant and upscale, with food that truly lives up to its reputation.

The place welcomes a steady flow of both small and large groups. Open until late as it also serves as a semi-bar. The menu offers a wide variety of traditional Thai dishes—fried, spicy salads, stir-fries, soups, curries—and even Isan specialties 🌶️. Options include prawns, shellfish , crab , fish , pork, and chicken.

Prices are on the higher side, but portions are generous, ingredients are high quality, and the flavors are exceptionally delicious.
A most beautiful set up restaurant accompanying great food, service you would expect from a Michelin awarded establishment …5 stars everyday of the week, we will be coming back🙏🏻👍👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻
Very nice place and the menu is absolutely mouth watering. The food was good but did really rise up to the initial impression.

This really is untarnished, authentic Southern Thai cooking. The restaurant is simple,rustic and charming. The food in a similar vein. Great punchy flavours but still wonderfully balanced and very well priced. It was clear that all the locals regard this place as being truly authentic. Always a great sign.

The rating is above average, the reviews are only positive, so we expected more than we got: the tom yum was sour-salted with overcooked tough shrimp, large chunks of onions, there was no sweetness, spiciness, the taste of lemongrass and greens. The green mango salad was sprinkled with sugar on top and was far from the original taste. There was delicious fish, but for some reason it was brought completely cooled ( I've never eaten before such a small portion of pad kaphrao😅  In addition, they forgot one order, but at least they did not include it in the bill. Therefore, decide for yourself whether to visit this restaurant with a Michelin star
This is proper Thai food. Very authentic. If you’re in Samui get yourself down here. Highly recommend the octopus and pineapple. Massaman curry was great too. Michelin guide rated and I can see why.

This is one of the best Thai food places I’ve been to. It offers a simple and nice sitting area m, not too much of a “vibe” but a pleasant atmosphere for dining.
The food is TOP: very tasty, extremely fresh, with generous big portions.
Always a good option to have a casual lunch or dinner or to order delivery from. Always good.

Me and my partner came here after seeing the Michelin guide mentioned for here. We were very happy with the food and service. We had the deep fried shrimp cakes, chicken panang curry and southern thai curry with ribs.
We'd definitely recommend the panang and shrimp cakes they were lovely.
Service was great and for 2 large beers and a sprite the bill total was 910 baht.

Loved the vibe of this place — stylish decor, spacious layout, and great natural lighting during the day (perfect for photos!). The food was authentic and tasty, though portions were a bit on the small side, so best to go with a group and try more dishes. Staff were super polite and friendly, and the whole dining experience felt relaxed. Just a heads-up: there are two ways to get in — the first one is super narrow (barely fits one car), so it’s better to use the second route.

I have a wonderful experience with the food and almost everything is enjoyable. Some of the menu are sweeter than my liking but other than that it was one of the notable food place from this trip.

The place are crowded so you are likely getting a menu in 10-15 minutes of waiting for some menu. I was fortunate with a good seating but some I would say that not all seating vibe the same 😅.

The taste was okay overall — I liked several dishes. My favorites were the grilled chicken and the minced pork in plum soup. If you want a 10% discount, you can buy a drink from the café and use the coupon for a discount. At first, I just casually asked the staff if there was any discount, and it turned out there really was! So I said, “Wait a sec,” then went to buy a drink before coming back to pay for the food.

The food was delicious, with a wide range of options. I visited on a weekend and there was a long queue, but it wasn’t too long, taking about 15 minutes to get a table. We decided to take advantage of a nearby cafe’s 10% discount coupon and enjoy a coffee there instead.

The service was okay, but the staff wasn’t very proactive. We had forgotten to collect the coupon from the cafe, and they refused to give us the discount even though we had purchased six glasses of coffee from them.

The location was good, right next to the cafe.

Value 7/10
Service 10/10
Taste 7/10
Price 8/10
Vibe 10/10
Cleanliness 10/10

I don't know why there’s some of the negative feedback for this place because personally I don't’t think it’s that bad.
Considering that I was hyped about this place and the impression was a bit underwhelming.
But it’s not bad at all!

A true hidden gem in Bangkok! This under-the-radar Michelin-starred restaurant offers a beautiful blend of Japanese and Thai inspiration. Chef Shun crafts every dish with precision, high-quality ingredients, and refined techniques that highlight both flavor and artistry.

Michael, the sommelier, made our wine pairing experience unforgettable. Each pairing complemented the dishes perfectly, and as a wine lover, I was impressed with the quality of the wines offered—well beyond what I expected at the price.

If you’re looking for an intimate, world-class dining experience in Bangkok, I highly recommend this place.

A lovely place for a special meal! The course menu comes at a reasonable price with good-sized portions — you’ll feel quite full. Some dishes were super tasty, while a few were a bit on the salty side and flavors were somewhat similar. But the dessert was absolutely amazing! The staff were really friendly and made sure we had a great experience.

We had 12 course dinner and enjoy every bite of it.

We felt that the food tone has a distinct Japanese taste with warm, rounded taste with deep Umami forward flavor which different from French based fine dinning experience that usually use a lot of acidity to open up your pallet follow by savory taste.

Another point that make Resonance food unique was the subtle use of local ingredients / flavors and twist that was not obvious but usually hidden in the underline flavor. It is familier yet different. It is simple but yet deep and complex.

We especially love Aji with Blueberry and seaweed, Akagai, Kuruma Ebi, sweet prawn and the Duck. All the desserts are also very good.

The service we had was also very good combining the best of Thai friendliness with professionalism of Japanese hospitality.

Overall we truly enjoy our experience and planing to visit again in the future.

While the food is excellently cooked and well presented, it still lacks some wow factor in my opinion. Maybe I have been to too many fine dinning places that I become desensitized.
The service is somewhat strange. While they are very observant and attentive to our needs. There is minor things like not letting us know in advance that tea pairing must be reserved a few days in advance. When I express dissatisfaction, the service staff also expresses a bit of shock, which is unseemly.
But apart from that, it’s quite a decent place to dine.

For my first fine dining experience, it was an unforgettable one.
Cant say enough good things about Resonance, the food and the service.

12 course tasting menu, dish after fish gets better and better.

Brie cheese ice cream was the highlight, so unexpected for me, really love it.

Very tasty modernized E-San, Thai and Local food.
Every plate must have passed a lot of trial and error to be this good and balance.
Food portion is a little bigger than most of thai shared food.
Delicious food, drinks and dessert, truly worthy of its Michelin Bib Gourmand status! Food was served fast, staff were really attentive and friendly! Must visit when in Ubon Ratchathani!
The restaurant served a good recipe made with quality ingredients and provided excellent service.
Delicious "Thai-Isaan" fusion dishes.   Will need to return to try other dishes.

Central Thai food with isan twist. There are steak available if you want to order but we stick to Thai food. All the dishes were delicious, well cooked with good ingredients. The drink menu was surprisingly good. Great service with reasonable price.

Great Michelin rated stand. Super cheap local prices. Come early to make sure you get it cuz it runs out quickly. We got 16 pieces + 3 cheese sausage rolls + 3 sauces for 145 baht total!  The sauces they have is condensed milk, pandan, and coconut. If you’re not used to Thai flavours I recommended trying all three. The sausage rolls are nothing special
Usual streat stall but taste is a bit above other places. I would say their pandan custard is unique.
This is a fantastic Patongo I ever had. If you go to Old town phuket, MUST TRY!!
Good food and good service.

Thai short fried dough sticks? They come with three sauces: the white one is condensed milk and slightly sweet, while the other two are Thai-style with a moderate sweetness. If you live nearby, give it a try.

I saw this place on YouTube so wanted to check it out. I got the Deep Fried Dumpling with creamy crab and scented truffle. These were delicious and I could have ate more if I hadn't ordered another dish.

I also gor the Claypot BBQ Pork with Chinese Sausage and egg. It came in a sizzling pot, the egg yolk was runny to begin with but with the residual heat it went to a more hard boiled consistency. The pork was tender and the sausage had a great flavour.

At the bottom of the pot the rice had stuck a little, but this rice had a toasted flavour so changed the dish as you ate down the pot.

There's only 4 tables so I imagine it can get full quickly, but it was well worth the trek over from Sukhumvit.
A small and cozy place! It’s become one of my favorite go-to spots for homey and delicious Chinese food! Love their shrimp dumplings and BBQ pork!
I love this place’s employees. Some of them are ladyboys and really exciting to engage with. Scientifically, most of the workers are male and they give special treats. You should try this!!

Famous for Cantonese pork BBQ, guaranteed by Michelin guide from 2022 to 2024. There are limited space inside the restaurant with just only 4-5 small tables. Delicious but I deducted 1 start due to a bit sweet taste of pork BBQ. There is no parking space but if you are lucky, you’ll fine free parking space along the street in front of the restaurant.

Take away review.

Currently one of the best BBQ pork! very soft, tender, and flavorful, however, each piece is a bit too small. The noodle is perfectly cooked and their rice is amazingly yummy, glutinous-like texture. Their fried rice menus are recommended as well as the BBQ menus.

Only 4 tables for sit-in so reservation is a must.

Amazing staff. The food was delicious and was presented really well.
We were surprised that we were the only ones there but it was a weekday and early evening.
Being included for American Express Dining Credits is a bonus, but we would happily pay full price when we are in Bangkok again.

Absolutely luxurious decorated restaurant
European-Thai style
All dishes were well decorated and delicious
I impressed Tenderloid steak with medium rare, It was very intense, but meat was still soft - It was amazing dish!
In part o f desserts, chocolate souffle was No.1 that I would recommend.

This restaurant was recommended by American Express platinum card. After tasting the set menu with main selection of grilled seabass, the entire set from appetizer, salad, soup, main, dessert and after meal drink were all good. The only thing I was unhappy about is the staff did not offer free drinks(hot coffee or tea) but suggest me to order coffee martini, without mentioning me this is a chargable item. When I receive the bill and found this costs 420Baht (if need to pay extra I definitely will not order this).
I really don't appreciate this dishonest behaviour.

All the dishes look delicious and taste delicious. Really dig the food presentation asking with the modern and luxurious vibe. Ideal for a date night. Cocktail was alright but not outstanding. They no longer have set courses menu anymore due to the chef's contract being over. But their a la carte menu is still outstanding regardless.

Very impressive restaurant with a reasonable price. I’ll definitely come back here again.

Maze dining is very close to my work place but I have to admit that i have not heard about it until now. We, a group of three people, went there for brunch/lunch. The place is consider fancy for me. The food is great. I love all the dishes we ordered. Egg Benedict is cheap, 390 baht, and it tasted great! I would like to highlight the sweets. They have like four or five people working on two dessert dishes. Both of them worth all the calories 😂

They also have a complimentary cake for birthday.

The place is very quiet. Only us, a table. I think it would be crowded during night time so if you go for the dinner, you would need booking in advance.

In short, love the place, highly recommended.

Our anniversary dinner was absolutely amazing. The food was out of this world,  and the service was fabulous.  We had the 6 course meal and the taste, the way it was prepared was magnificent . We got to meet the chef and he was also very friendly and answered all our questions.  I highly recommend this restaurant. We give it a 5 star since Google doesn't have more stars. I would give it a 10!

Savelberg is truly one of the finest fine dining experiences. The restaurant is beautifully designed with an elegant atmosphere. In the evening, soft sunlight filters through the glass windows and reflects on the lush garden, creating a serene and romantic setting.

The service is impeccable — every staff member is courteous, attentive, and knowledgeable, providing excellent recommendations and explanations about each dish. The drink menu is also well-curated with plenty of options to pair perfectly with the meal.
