Every plate served was a masterpiece, full of refined flavors and creativity. An unforgettable culinary journey — without a doubt, one of the best fine dining restaurants worth experiencing.

Savelberg delivers an outstanding dining experience, featuring fresh, expertly crafted dishes and a well-curated wine selection. The sophisticated yet inviting ambiance makes for a relaxed, professional setting. Parking is conveniently located, with a golf cart service available, though I personally enjoy walking after a great meal. A must-visit for those seeking refined cuisine.

Savelberg brings Michelin-starred French cuisine to Bangkok in a refined, elegant setting. Each dish is crafted with precision, highlighting fresh, high-quality ingredients. The tasting menus are sophisticated and balanced, offering a mix of classic French techniques and modern innovation. The staff are knowledgeable and attentive, ensuring every course is perfectly timed and paired. Ideal for romantic dinners, business meals, or celebrating special milestones.

We had 6 courses dinner and everything was beyond our expectations. Everything dish was crafty prepared and cooked to perfection. The service was top-notch and the ambience was very pleasant. Highly recommended and definitely come back.

my local friend here in Phuket told me about this restaurant many many times ago and I did not have a chance to visit until today. First bite i was like whatttttttt its super yummy. One of the top 3 southern cuisine for me. Disclaimer is that it is for people who love strong taste like salty and spicy and sour. If you love those, you would be totally satisfied!

This place left us controversial. The atmosphere was pretty nice, very peranakan style, authentic and just vibe.
🔒However the half of the restaurant was closed, especially the second floor for some reason.
🚽🧻The toilet didn’t have paper neither for hands and for general use at all.
🥘The food was okay. We really enjoyed squid with salted egg sauce and shrimp cakes. Pork and Pad Thai didn’t meet our expectations. Lemonades were cool.

I’m not sure I can recommend to COME AND VISIT this place on purpose, but if you live nearby, why not.

Came here on Friday, 20 June 2025 for lunch. Restaurant was quite empty, but yet the order took very long to arrive. I mean there was only 1 other table for 3 gentlemen. The worst part is that we ordered takeaway, some dishes including an omelet crab fried rice but when we got home, it was just plain white rice with an omelet. Our friends who were waiting for the food were so disappointed. Yes I should have checked my order before I left but I don't think I needed to do this for a Michelin guide restaurant.

The food was excellent!  I made a reservation for 5 people via google map chat and it worked well.  Turns out that a reservation was not necessary as the restaurant was pretty much empty when we went for dinner.  There were 2 people sitting at another table in the garden but we were seated inside so we didn't see them.  It was a little odd eating in an empty restaurant but the food was great so that's all that matters right?

We tried a bit of everything...soup with coconut milk, pad thai omelette, basil chicken, stir fried pork, curry, pineapple fried rice, etc.

We had a slight communication issue trying to explain the difference between flat water and water with gas (carbonated water) but some pictures and google translate, etc. seemed to help.  We ordered carbonated water first but the kids wanted flat water so when we ordered flat water, they gave us more carbonated water.  But not a big deal.

I highly recommend this restaurant for anyone who wants a nice meal in Phuket.

The prices were reasonable and on par for a restaurant of this quality.

Lucky to discover this gem of a restaurant while we were in Phuket. We are big fan of Thai recipes and we wanted to have something authentic Thai food while we are in Thailand.

Place-wise, this place is amazing and huge seating capacity with beautiful gardens and small pond filled with colorful fishes. They have tables for couple as well as for small and huge group.

We had a couple of beers, chicken starter with something named Krua Praya, yellow curry chicken and pad thai rice noodles with chicken. Staff was sweet and accommodating. And they were open for suggestions too!

Stepping into this old store felt like traveling back to the 1980s. My dad and I ordered the Crispy Pork Rice, and while it looked simple, the taste was anything but. It reminded me of home-cooked meals from my childhood, especially the red sauce—familiar yet distant in a way I couldn’t quite place. The true standout was the clear chicken soup, which captured the soul of the chicken and brought deep comfort. A nostalgic, heartwarming experience.

The taste of childhood.  To me, the best is the sauce.  It really reminded me good bbq pork rice when I was young. It is hard to find the sauce like this. All 3 type of pork were good.   But wonton was average
The signature dish is good. Show them the picture on the wall or phone to order.
Best Chinese noodle in this district.

If you’re passing through Phang Nga and looking for something simple but truly satisfying, this is it.
Delicious Hainanese chicken and BBQ pork at a fair price, served with warmth and care.
It’s not fancy, but it’s full of heart.
A humble local spot that delivers big on flavor. Worth the stop.

Touched down and first place for a meal. Wasn’t sure about the food until we tasted their Yellow Powder Crab & Tomyam Soup! Super creamy tomyam and fresh ingredients, super flavourful for crab dish. 750 baht for 3ppl.

It is Michelin rated (I dont think starred only saw signs hanged), so it justify the price i think. But the taste is definitely matching their price.

At first, the restaurant’s outside look didn’t really catch my attention, but I decided to give it a try – and wow! The food was absolutely incredible, way beyond expectations 🤩🔥. Forget about Michelin stars, this place has its own magic. Step inside, taste the dishes, and you’ll see what I mean – truly amazing! 👏👏
Unassuming appearance but the food is deserving of its Michelin recognition. Authentic Thai food at almost street food prices. Love the 50s photos on its walls.  Hope it stays the same.

We visited this restaurant not knowing its outstanding food quality. Each dish came in large portions, with fruitful flavour that can be one of the best Thai food I have had in Thailand. Truly a hidden gem!
Reasonably priced food for the price. Although I might have ordered something more spicy than I could handle and the menu did not show that, haha.

Amazing and delicious seafood at affordable prices! Ordered 1kg of crab, 1kg of prawn, 1kg of clams and medium size crab fried rice with other drinks. Costs us less than 4,000 baht total for three pax.

Prices varies for different type of crabs and prawns ordered, so please do check with the staff on the prices.

We came here for lunch and it was the highlight of our trip in Phuket. The boat rides back and fro from the dock to the restaurant is covered by your meal. The whole journey is such an experience. We do not speak Thai and there was no clear signs of where and how, but people there were friendly and pointed us the directions. Just go with the flow... The only problem is getting a ride back to the city. The signal is spotty, so it was tough to get a taxi or Grab ride, it took us 30 minute to wait for our driver. It was a Thursday late afternoon in June so perhaps you'll have better luck on the weekends. Note that this is not a fancy restaurant, so expect wooden benches or tables and uneven wooden decks, but you can't beat the experience of eating fresh seafood in the middle of the sea. The food is excellent. Will definitely return.

We picked this as a must-go destination thanks to the recommendation from Marion Grasby. We are happy to say that this floating restaurant satisfied our Thai seafood cravings really well!

Here's some tips from our experience:
- if you're heading there via a rideshare service, your driver may presume that your destination is Laem Hin Seafood Restaurant
- fortunately, the actual Laem Hin pier is a quick five-minute walk
- the longboat ferry service runs every ten minutes or so
- the ferryman would ask for your destination as there are three offshore locations including this restaurant
- "khru vit seafood" and you should be right
- the return ferry is the same deal, every ten minutes or so
- this floating restaurant provides an interesting meal experience as you'd feel the raft movement from the wake of passing vessels; neither of us are prone to motion sickness but your mileage may vary
Amazing seafood restaurant on a floating raft between Phuket and Coconut island.  The food is amazing and the location cannot be beat.

"Piar khru.Witt" restaurant won Michelin guide rewards since 2019 consecutively. The seafood likely they catching after your order. The fish, shrimp and squid were unbelievably juicy and naturally sweet, easily among the best I’ve had in Phuket.
The journey itself is part of the magic, a local fisherman would pick you up from the pier without fee (if you order exceed 1,000 baht. Trust me, you will exceed it; the seafood is impossible to resist)
While you having meal, take a moment to glance beneath your feet would meet school of fish ,swim gently.  That’s more captivating than any screen.

I visited this restaurant after seeing many good reviews on blogs. It’s located by the river, so the atmosphere was really nice. The restaurant has a Michelin mark, which raised my expectations.

However, the server who looked after our table had some trouble understanding us, and there was a small mistake with our order. For a Michelin-rated place, I think the staff could be trained a bit better in communication.

The food was generally tasty, but nothing particularly special considering it’s a Michelin restaurant. I feel you could find dishes of similar quality at local spots for the same price. It’s worth visiting once for the experience, but I probably wouldn’t come back again.

Rongros is a riverside gem by the Chao Phraya River that truly lives up to its Michelin recognition. The view is absolutely stunning.
You can enjoy a breathtaking panorama of Wat Arun while dining. Every dish is beautifully presented and full of authentic Thai flavors with a refined touch. The food tastes incredible rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced.

It’s the kind of place where you can sit back, relax, and savor both the scenery and the taste. Perfect for a special evening or anyone who wants to experience Thai cuisine at its finest.

⭐️ Michelin-awarded taste, mesmerizing view, and warm Thai hospitality 👏🏻

The view and decoration are beautiful, and the food is truly delicious!

However, everything was completely ruined by the service from some of the staff. I could clearly feel a difference in how Thai customers were treated. The attitude, the looks, and the manners from certain staff members were very disappointing. My mum and I both felt upset by how we were treated.

For the price, I expected much better service and proper Thai hospitality. Sadly, it was far from that.

It’s such a shame because the food and atmosphere are wonderful. But the service left such a bad impression that I don’t think I will visit again, no matter how good the food is.

I was so excited about this and it did not disappoint! The food is excellent although the price matches the prime viewing location. Getting a rooftop table can be risky as there is definitely no rain plan and the restaurant is always booked solid so you can’t simply move inside. Luckily it did not rain on us. The service is not Michelin quality but the overall experience is well worth it.

This restaurant was really close to our hotel and had great reviews, so we decided to come here for our one 'fancy' meal of the trip. Everything on the menu looked great so it was hard to choose. In the end I had the rib-eye steak green curry. Everyone enjoyed their food (the green curry was the spiciest thing I ate all trip though for sure!), however we all agreed the food was good but not amazing, so it definitely seemed overpriced. We had better food for so much cheaper elsewhere. Service was good and of course the view was nice.

This local Hainanese chicken rice restaurant lives up to — and even goes beyond — the consecutive Michelin Guide recognitions it has received. It’s not just about the accolades; it’s about the consistently outstanding quality of the food.

The poached chicken is exceptionally tender and juicy, perfectly complementing the fragrant rice cooked in rich chicken broth. What truly elevates the dish is the restaurant’s signature spicy sauce — a bold and flavorful accompaniment that adds the perfect kick. Served alongside a light, savory soup, the meal strikes a wonderful balance of comfort and complexity.

A dish this well-executed is increasingly rare to find, which explains the steady stream of customers from morning until late afternoon. Whether you’re a local or a visitor, it’s a culinary experience that captures the essence of traditional Hainanese chicken rice done right — simple, honest, and deeply satisfying.
Small shop around 10 tables, no own parking. Quite salty. Soup was just basic. Liver is ok.
Family restaurant with Michelin Bib Gourmand. It really deserves this Award. The food is delicious and very cheap.
No doubt why they earned a prize from Michelin. Boiled chicken on rice worth to wait because they may sold out and cooked during the day. You can enjoy their foods on a budgets.
I like soup and rice but for the chicken and fried garlic minced pork just so so for me. Btw for service, they forgot my order even though the restaurant was not crowded at all.

I dropped by this stall around 3:30 PM, just before they were about to close—lucky timing! If you happen to miss it, don’t worry—there’s another stall just across the road next to 7-Eleven with a different vibe.

I ordered the dry noodles, and they were cooked perfectly—springy and just the right texture. The meat was fresh, and the fish dumplings are a definite must-try—so tasty! The staff were very friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better.

Prices are very reasonable for the quality. The only downside is the traffic—it's quite jammed in the area, so plan accordingly.

If you're looking for good noodles and warm service, this stall is a great choice. And if you're in the mood for something different, the one opposite offers a nice change of scenery too.

Delicious soup noodle and I personally prefer the soup noodle to the dry noodle.

I tried both stores (this one and the sister store across the street with Michelin rating) in 2 consecutive days.  Although they serve the same dishes, I personally prefer this store as the soup is hotter and tastes more peppery and their noodles and minced pork are cooked better.  Pictures attached are the store I preferred (ie without the Michelin rating).

Came after 1pm and still crowded. This is an excellent and very popular Michelin rated restaurant that serves street food noodles.
The noodle was exquisite and tasteful even without soup.
Pork balls were cold but yet delicious.
The drinks were extremely soothing particularly in this heat and spicy dish (I added myself their homemade chili).
Service was fast and obviously efficient.
Advice: choose small portion and with soup, particularly if it’s your first venture into Thai street noodle style. If you crave for more, try other noodle and soup type. Like this you can easily try a variety of them. The price is very affordable especially for a restaurant

Cheap and good. Recommend to order the big size if you're hungry if there is, I ordered the medium and the portion is rather small for a guy. If you go during peak hour there will be queue, for context two same store and both have queue. Life hacks go during off peak and immediately walk in. 1 noodle 1 drink 90 baht.

My favorite and best of my Bangkok trip!!! I had it two days in a row! Go for the thin beehoon, it soaks up the soup perfectly and every bowl is packed with ingredients. Absolutely delicious and something I’ll definitely return for! I ordered Grab delivery, still SO GOOD.

Like So Many of Bangkok Fine Dining Restaurants they are Tucked Away from the Hustle & Bustle of the main Streets.

The Restaurant has be on Our Radar for a While & was recommended by a Friend who previously Dined & found it to be pretty Decent

So we ventured for a Good Night Out of Drinks & Dinner.

We opted for the Smallest 7 Course Menu to keep it Light as we have been Eating & Drinking None Stop for the past few Days.

Additionally one of our party was a Vegetarian.

Up pond arriving we were usher into a small Dark Cozy Bar Area for Aperitif

Cocktail Menu with Some Classics with Twist.

After we were lead by Vishvas to our Table explaining the Name & Concept.

Neo Indian they grow what they cook

As we knew our menu we only had to choose the Mains Chicken, Beef Or Lamb.

Small Bites came in Quick Succession

And the Show began

All dishes was a Wack Bang of Colours & Flavours

The Table was in agreeance dishes had some hits & misses but well presented and overall good.

Service was Good at the beginning but lagged as the night wore on

Overall a Great Experience & Night Out

Came here for the weekend lunch tasting course and it surpassed my expectations.

Excellent service, high quality ingredients, very authentic food experience (I lived in India so can judge).

There’s nothing that I can deduct in any of the categories. Restaurant is in a nice, walkable neighborhood and the exterior has plenty of green.

Really enjoyed my visit during the rainy season 😌 Strongly recommend to book in advance!

During my two-week trip to Thailand in May, I dined with friends at Haoma and was captivated by the exceptional tasting menu. The restaurant’s elegant ambiance, with its lush greenery and sophisticated decor, provided a perfect backdrop for a memorable meal. Each dish was a masterpiece of flavor, thoughtfully crafted and perfectly paced, accompanied by engaging stories and beautifully designed postcards that added a charming, personal touch to the experience.

The wine pairing was a highlight, elevating the meal to new heights. Each glass was expertly selected to complement the nuanced flavors of the dishes, creating a harmonious balance that enhanced every bite. The sommelier’s choices showcased a deep understanding of both the cuisine and the wines, with each pour—from crisp, aromatic whites to robust, velvety reds—perfectly accentuating the ingredients and culinary techniques. The seamless integration of the wine with the menu added a layer of sophistication, making each course even more memorable.

Haoma delivered an outstanding dining experience that I highly recommend for anyone seeking a refined and unforgettable culinary journey.

This is another off-radar fine-dining destination. It carries the essence of Indian cuisine, but with the complexity and refinement of a Michelin-starred experience. Their commitment to preservation is truly outstanding, as they reuse various natural resources, and grow some ingredients, from their farm and in the restaurant.

North Indian Fine Dining – 11-Course Meat & Seafood Experience (Visited September 2024)

visited this North Indian fine dining restaurant in September 2024 and had the 11-course Meat & Seafood Experience. This Michelin-starred establishment (1 Star, Michelin Guide 2023 + Michelin Green Star for Sustainable Gastronomy) offers an impressive, curated tasting menu in a warm, intimate setting — pre-booking is essential due to limited seating.

Upon arrival, the staff warmly guided us into the restaurant and led us to a bar/lounge area for refreshments and starters — not part of the 11 courses, but a delightful prelude. We were served two starters and a refreshing drink, which were beautifully presented and enjoyable. The staff explained the ingredients and inspiration behind each item, adding depth to the experience.

Before being ushered into the main dining room, we passed through their on-site herb and spice garden, where the team introduced their sustainable practices and how they grow many of the ingredients themselves — an engaging and thoughtful touch.

Once seated, a dedicated server accompanied our table, explaining each course in detail, including the chef behind it and the ingredients used. The 11-course menu included:

1. Pani puri, Vada Pav, Raw Mango Panna
2. Smoked Mackerel Bati, Bombay Sandwich Wagyu Corn Tea Pie, Dry Aged Scallop Tart
3. Tear Drop Peas
4. Squid
5. Goby Fish
6. Crab
7. Citrus Sorbet (to cleanse the palate before the mains)
8. Lamb
9. Yakhni Pulao
10. Chocolate Dessert
11. Petit Four(dessert)

Most dishes were flavorful, beautifully plated, and thoughtfully constructed. The flavours were robust, with some courses presenting surprising, unique twists that made the experience memorable. The Citrus Sorbet served before the main course was refreshing and served its purpose well.

The only dish I didn’t quite enjoy was the Petit Four, which had strong Indian spice notes that felt slightly awkward in a dessert context — but this comes down to personal preference.

Despite the higher price point, I felt the quality, portion size, service, and attention to detail made it well worth the try. This restaurant offers more than a meal — it’s a culinary journey that’s both immersive and thoughtful. Highly recommended for food lovers seeking a refined Indian dining experience.

It was once the best hotel in Thailand for so many years. I hadn’t been back for a long time, and I wasn’t sure if I had missed anything. The hotel has had a facelift, but it seems to have lost its soul.

Maybe it’s because I’m from the ’70s, when going to the Mandarin Oriental was reserved for the most special occasions — when every guest was treated like the most important person in the world. The service was impeccable, and even if you visited only once a year, they remembered you.

My family used to celebrate my father’s birthday at the Normandie Grill every year until he passed away. I went back this time, but it wasn’t the same. The view is still priceless, but I wish I could say the same for the food and service. The newly renovated Grill Room, with its bare tables and no tablecloths, no longer felt luxurious. Perhaps it’s more sustainable now — less detergent going into the waterways — but the French-fusion menu was bolder than I prefer. The staff was friendly, but not quite the top-notch team it once had.

I will always treasure my memories of this place and accept that my time with it has passed. I hope the new generation finds joy in what it has become. For me, though, the legend has lost its charm.

An exceptional fine dining experience in Thailand.
We indulged in the Voyage Set Menu — a seven-course culinary journey masterfully curated by Head Chef Anne-Sophie Pic. Each dish was exquisitely crafted, showcasing remarkable balance, creativity, and depth of flavor. The service was impeccable, attentive yet unobtrusive, complementing the sophisticated ambiance perfectly. While the price is on the higher side, the overall experience and the exceptional quality of the cuisine make it truly worthwhile.

We did a full tasting menu, its no longer the Normandie we known and love, the place got changed to a fine dining place its not french, its not charming, it became an everywhere u can find just another fine dinning.
Service was ok but its all new team from none MO staff, some staffs you can immediately ask if they arent from MO and u guess it they are from other outside restaurants or 4stars hotels. I would prefer older gentlemen from previous normandie.

Food was (im sorry) mediocre, its not french its more japanese than anything else. Its japanese fusion with french cheese pretty much that. It might work in France if you use japanese ingredients they might find it interesting but we did not.
Its really japanese fusion with french cheese. The atmosphere has zero vibes of french high end restaurant.
They saying they still fine tuned to the local pallets, its not that, just give us french cuisine
We truely miss the old Normandie
we stayed a night here so decided to have a lunch to celebrate my birthday. great food and superb service! 🥰😍

Le Normandie, located riverside at the Mandarin Oriental, offers classic French fine dining at its best. Every dish is expertly crafted, from seafood to perfectly cooked meats, and plated with elegance. The service is impeccable, with staff providing attentive guidance throughout the meal. The riverside view adds a magical touch to the experience, making it perfect for anniversaries, business dinners, or special celebrations. A true icon of Bangkok’s culinary scene.

Lunch was mostly enjoyable. Although majority of the food I found to be quite salty. The big crab was freshly prepared and nicely grilled. The river prawns were great and so was the panfried vegetable with eggs. Although the papaya salad could use fresher preparation; the papaya was old or either premade. Overall, a good stop over in Surat Thani for fresh seafood menus with very fair pricing.

Lovely riverside setting with a relaxed atmosphere. The food is delicious and fresh - with the salted-egg dish being a definite highlight. 🤩🤩🤩
A must-try if you’re in town!

Lamphu 2 Seafood is a renowned seafood restaurant in Surat Thani province, highly regarded by both locals and tourists for its fresh and flavorful dishes, offering a wide variety of menu options.

Atmosphere and Location:
The restaurant is conveniently located along Pak Nam Tapi Road, making it easily accessible with ample parking space.

Menu and Taste:
The restaurant's highlight is its fresh seafood, prepared into a diverse range of delectable dishes.
Must-try menu items include fresh oysters, stir-fried sea catfish with chili paste, stir-fried Melientha leaves with eggs and shrimp paste, and steamed pomfret with plum sauce.
Additionally, the restaurant offers a variety of flavorful local dishes.
The seafood dipping sauce is another highlight, enhancing the taste of the fresh seafood.

Price and Value:
The restaurant's prices range from moderate to high, but considering the quality and freshness of the seafood, it offers excellent value.
Fresh and good quality seafood restaurant. Best somtam I’ve ever had. Very spacey and big tables available. River view. Attentive staffs.

Food really good and fresh.

We sit on riverside, a little hot but it is good atmosphere.

Overall service is good, staffs are very kind.

restaurant_name: Khun Jaeng Guay Tiew Pak Mor Kao Wang
review_text: The restaurant here serves a mix of Thai and Vietnamese food. Many Thai celebrities have dined here, and the restaurant has won numerous awards. You can try the clear soup if you don’t like spicy food, or if you can handle spice, you can try the spicy version. It’s really delicious!

restaurant_name: Khun Jaeng Guay Tiew Pak Mor Kao Wang
review_text: On my gosh, its my first time ever of this kind of noodle. It is so good, so many varieties of inside noodle such as vegetables, corn, mince pork and etc. The queue were long during lunch time plus grab line. However, it worth to come. The owner, he us so kind and helpful which very enjoyable of eating here. Ps.there is lot of mosquitoes 🦟 a bit boring 😝

restaurant_name: Khun Jaeng Guay Tiew Pak Mor Kao Wang
review_text:
Simple but good Pak Mor restaurant. The menu is in Thai only, however you can look at the pictures - which are real depictions of what they sell.
The owners are very friendly and accommodating to Farang that need a bit longer time to order.
The different kinds of Pak Mor are quite interesting: we ordered the veggie sampler platter, which included carrot, corn, cabbage, and morning glory rolls. We also tried the traditional Pak Mor Moo (Pork), which was more to our liking than the vegetable versions.
There is free ice and water (self-serve) for customers.

restaurant_name: Khun Jaeng Guay Tiew Pak Mor Kao Wang
review_text: Local Thai eatery. These are what the locals have been eating for years. The chef speaks English, so you can order from him.. he might be busy ..

restaurant_name: Khun Jaeng Guay Tiew Pak Mor Kao Wang
review_text: Very fair price while compared with the quality. Recommended to taste duck noodle (アヒル麺) by 70 baht per bowl. The location closely with the Kaen Na Korn swamp but quite hard to parking. The restaurant has no air conditioning.

Now here's an experience!
Walk past on the pavement and your order will be underway. Your seat will be allocated and service will start.
It's quite a loud affair, so don't be shy.
Everyone gets the same treatment, local or tourist. Fantastic red or crispy pork with rice. The sauce bottle placed before you is hot. Not spicy...high temperature. It's gravy. Not spicy, just very tasty.
Not to be missed!!
Oh and set aside less than 2 dollars for the bill

Found this from Michelin guide.

Cheap and good mix pork rice@50thb

Garlic pork rice quite salty, below average.

If you wanna try some simple Thai streetfood dish, I would definitely recommend you to come here. Order the red pork with crispy pork with rice or stewed sweet pork leg with rice (you won’t see the leg, it‘s just purely meat, no worries 😂). The price as of March 2023 is still 50 baht per dish… very reasonable I would say. Their brown sauce for the crispy pork is gold! The soup/broth to eat along is also very tasty, no MSG as what the owner claims.
The pork leg (ข้าวขาหมู) was delicious. The two outside tables can seat two or three people, and there’s inside seating too.

reviewer: ธเนศ คุณามาศปกรณ์
review_text:
The owner is very friendly and helpful.
Good local food.
Good price.

Sripol Seafood is an absolute gem for seafood enthusiasts, and my experience here was nothing short of incredible. I had the privilege of indulging in a massive 3.6kg lobster, and it was a meal I’ll never forget. The lobster was cooked to perfection—succulent, tender, and bursting with flavor. Every bite was a testament to the freshness and quality of the seafood served here.

What makes Sripol Seafood truly special is the way they prepare and present their dishes. The lobster was served with just the right seasoning, enhancing its natural sweetness without overpowering it. The cooking technique was flawless, preserving the delicate texture and ensuring every bite was as enjoyable as the last.

The restaurant itself is welcoming and unpretentious, with a lively and friendly atmosphere that adds to the dining experience. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, offering excellent recommendations and ensuring everything was cooked exactly to my preference.

If you’re a seafood lover, Sripol Seafood is an absolute must-visit. The quality, freshness, and sheer size of the lobster I enjoyed were unparalleled, and I can’t wait to return to explore more of their incredible menu. Highly recommend this spot for an unforgettable seafood feast!
Gigantic-sized seafood restaurant. The owner had the good network to source wild (non-farm) seafoods. Food was fresh and big size. Expensive.

BEST FRIED RICE in town. It's a MUST! Gaelic giant grouper is also on the list. Everything is quite gigantic with top quality indeed. It's always better to come in a large group. The place also offer private seating or rooms. Make sure advanced booking is made and prepare to spend big bucks!
The size is matter! The place you find jumbo size of clam, river prawn, grouper & crab. Bring 7-10 people to enjoy variety of food with huge portion! Prepare to pay 3000 baht per person or more.

Must reserve very important
There’s no fish unless they know your coming
It’s sourced per reservation

We were hungry and so we googled. We went with no expectations. Nestled in a quiet road opposite Maya Mall, we were their first guests of the day.
Upon opening the door, then we realise it was an award winning Michelin restaurant.
We went for their tasting menu,couldn’t drink as I had to wake up early.
The moment we sat down, the wait staffs were extremely friendly and courteous which makes it very welcoming.
Every dish was explained thoroughly and in detail.
Every single dish and drinks was delectable and scrumptious! Though on the slightly pricier side, it is well worth every penny spent.  Words cannot describe the taste  at all.
A very unique dining experience you cannot miss in Chiang Mai.
Kudos and Special thanks to Chef Dan and his team for making my birthday a pleasantly wonderful surprise!
We hope to come back again in future.
Meanwhile, keep your creative juices flowing and continue to curate innovative cuisine.

Warm and friendly

The starter really highlighted Thai flavors with a fresh, modern touch—light but full of impact. From the main course to dessert, everything was spot on. I always bring guests here, and they’re never disappointed.

Not recommended as this is certainly a tourist trap. Some concepts are nice, but nothing too worthy. The worst part is that they will try to take as much money from you as possible, for even a simple pot of tea that was not mentioned how much it would cost and whether we would be charged for it.

The price is way too high for what you get although we don’t mind paying even more for food and dining experiences that are worth it, so it’s not surprising that there were only two other tables that were occupied throughout our dining time. An ideal pricing point would be half of what is charged (we paid around 15,000 baht with only one small bottle for wine which was not that high anyways).

Some dishes were amazing, and many others a total failure. Presentation was stellar, but taste was below average. However, the river prawn dish was honestly amazing! Hands down the best one we had in Thailand! The tenderloin itself was not tasting good at all and was cooked quite badly. It tasted like a cheap supermarket meat, but the sauce was nice. The prelude was not so good, we didn’t like most of them. The scallops were nice, but a bit too heavy. The fish and chips were a unique combination. The roti and naan breads were not good at all.

We came here before several time. Would we come back? Certainly not. We like trying Michelin recommended restaurants, but this was a bit absurd for what you get.

This was, simply put, the best dining experience we’ve ever had in Chiang Mai.
Cannot praise it enough. Beautiful decor, stunning menu, awesome food quality and presentation and world-class service. It easily deserves a Michelin star in our view.
Please don’t miss out. You won’t be disappointed.

I’ve tried Redbox across a few seasons, and this season’s “Nature and Culture” is truly amazing. The journey begins with a playful regional welcome of small bites and continues with a starter that’s simply outstanding. every dish delights the palate with beautiful plating and flavors. And don’t forget to try their signature blend tea perfect finishing with petit fours.  ❤️

The food was amazing and very authentic. Every dish was prepared with care, the flavours were rich, the portions were generous, and everything was beautifully presented.
The restaurant had a charming, homely vibe, and it felt more like dining in someone’s home than a typical restaurant.
Gianni and his wife were very friendly, welcoming  and happy to chat.
Booking in advance is recommended, as it’s a fairly small restaurant.

We had an unforgettable dining experience last night.
Every dish we tried was truly exceptional — from the variety of delicious starters to the perfectly cooked, flavorful pastas that were some of the best we’ve ever had.
The atmosphere was warm, welcoming and unique, making the whole evening even more special.
And to top it all off, we ended with the most incredible tiramisu — the best we’ve had in Phuket!

I've been here several times and every single dish has been exceptional. The atmosphere is homey, the owners are so welcoming and the service by the team is absolutely stellar. I recommend booking in advance (the best way is to call), especially if it's during the weekend or public holidays. I really recommend you to experience this restaurant when you visit Phuket.
Absolutely fantastic! We had a group of 7 to celebrate a friend’s birthday. The food was amazing and the restaurant was so cute! The owners are so nice and friendly. Will definitely come back!

The restaurant is located at the Bang Neaw intersection, directly across from the shrine.
Parking is available along the street or inside the shrine grounds.
The owner, originally from southern Italy, has lived in Thailand for many years and speaks Thai fluently.
It is highly recommended to order wine here, especially selections from southern Italy, with a particular focus on wines from Sardinia.

Heard about this restaurant for a while and today we get a chance to try. We recommend reserving a table in advance since this place is really popular especially for travelers.

Overall, all dishes were delicious and i really liked grilled pork neck and coconut pancakes.

The service was okay and food came quite fast. Lots of parking was also available.

This place is good for company party and friend catch up.

My favorite restaurant for this trip to Bangkok. I was very hesitant to order the usually simple but good, BBQ Grilled Pork Shoulder, especially since it is also Michelin Bib Recommended. But to my pleasant surprise, super delicious. Soft, juicy, thinly sliced pieces of meat infused with a smokey fragrance; and served with a delicate and tasty tamarind sauce. The fried snakehead fish with the herbal &  vegetable special sauce was perhaps one of the best I've tasted. The Papaya Salad was also fresh tasting and refreshing, full of light Thai flavors . Traditional Thai cuisine,  delicately and elegantly prepared with a modern flare. All completely delightful.  Must come back!
My trip to Thailand wouldn’t have been complete without coming here. Every dish was perfectly seasoned, my family and friends truly enjoyed our time dining at this place
Tasty food.  Fresh crab and shrimps.  Good service.  Nice atmosphere.
Delicious like a Michelin restaurant. The service was good, and the food came out quickly. It's a great time.

Baan Kun Pra is a lovely restaurant by the river in Ayutthaya. It is in a traditional Thai wooden house with a warm and peaceful feeling. The outdoor seating by the river is very relaxing, especially during sunset. The place is clean, beautiful, and full of plants. It’s a nice spot to enjoy with friends or family.

The staff were friendly and helpful. The food was tasty, with many Thai dishes full of flavor. The tables were set nicely with flowers, and the service was quick. Overall, it was a great experience, and I would recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Ayutthaya.

Quality restaurant with friendly staff and beautiful scenery. Had to ask them to spice the food up a bit because they'd instinctively tuned it down for me as a foreigner, but overall a great experience.

The restaurant is designed simply but is eye-catching thanks to the decoration and display of architectural models.  There is a beautiful view of the river towards the river which is very nice and romantic.  In the evening, there are beautiful and small lights suitable for dating couples.  The food was delicious and beautifully displayed, we had a wonderful dinner together while on a trip through Thailand.

The local food was okay, but not suitable with the price. Cozy terrace along the river to enjoy the food and company. Nice arranged dishes on classic china with a good service. All in all an okay experience, but the thing I give ⭐️⭐️⭐️ for is the Lemongrass lemonade with cardboard straw!! Creative and good initiative 👍
Food was good! The only problem is that they didn’t accept card.

Nice Thai food. Good price , good taste and quite clean. Famous for its roasted chicken (as the restaurant name stated). Papaya salad with salted egg, rosted pork neck, fried pork are also recommended. Soup is average. Overall if you come by, give it a try!
The food is delicious, served very quickly, and the service is good.😍
One of the best kai-yang(chicken barbecue) in Thailand. Good e-san food.
Local Korat foods, recommend to order Pad-Mi-Korat and Grilled chicken

Always the best North-Eastern Thai foods in Nakhon Ratchasima. I have been know this restaurant since I was 5 years old and they still serve the best tasty foods to the customers. Love the Flammable Grilled Chicken, Papaya Salad with Fermented Fish, and Namtok Pork. Nice place to bring your colleagues or your whole family to spend the time in this restaurant together.

Love this spot so much I came back twice! Did not go anywhere else twice during my stay in Bangkok. I regularly eat a lot of incredible Thai food so it was refreshing to find a spot this good for a change.

The crab fried rice here is a dream and the Thai iced tea is perfection. Service was very good both times from the younger girl. Would love to come here again!

The food was okay. We came due to the reviews but my Khao soy was too sweet and the beef in it didn't taste fresh and Was really tough. The place was also empty compared to others in the neighborhood. Their complimentary watermelon slices made up slightly for the disappointment in the food. It also tasted heavily of msg. I think it caters to the western palate and not as authentically local as we wanted.

By far, best thai we had in 4 days Bangkok. Don't hesitate.  When taking a spicy dish,  go for it but ask maybe to go mild. The standard is quite hot but still edible. We love it. They are also very friendly. Also the cocktails are top notch...
This café was right across from our hotel. Breakfast was good and very filling. The staff were extremely kind, a very friendly young man gave us great advice, and a lovely girl was also very sweet!

Had mango sticky rice and very good the stuffed egg wrap, the mango itself could have been better but maybe it’s off mango-season.
I also got the steamed rice with a hair in it but they noticed as soon as they sat it on the table and got me a new portion of rice, but the new portion had also a hair in it, looked like the cats one…
But it’s thailand so just take it and eat it.

So in total food was very good

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The Smokaccia Laboratory in Phuket is an absolute gem. This place isn’t just a restaurant, it’s a full sensory experience. Every dish was a masterpiece, and the wine pairing elevated the whole evening to something unforgettable. The service was flawless, attentive without being intrusive, making us feel completely taken care of.

What impressed me even more was how light and balanced everything felt. Despite enjoying a world-class fine dining experience with multiple courses and wines, I didn’t walk away feeling heavy or drunk: just happy, satisfied, and grateful.

The ambiance is absolutely on point, and the great music selection offers even a better vibe than you can expect.

Congratulations to all the team.

We had a wonderful night celebrating my husband’s birthday with a group of friend someone travelled far. The whole restaurant experience at the Smokaccia with chef Luca and his team made our trip so special. This is my by far best Michelin star experience, every dish is very creative and full of surprises. The one amazed me most is the lasagna and you wouldn’t be able to tell the actually taste if simply look at its presentation. Chef Luca is passionate about his food, he also shared some background stories of the dishes that’s elevated whole dining experience.

This restaurant is truly phenomenal.
The creativity behind each dish, the perfect balance of flavors, the precise control of temperature, and the uncompromising quality all shine through.
I’m so glad we chose this place for our holiday that it turned out to be the perfect dining experience.

I finally visited after hearing many recommendations. The food is creative, with Italian flavours presented in thoughtful ways, and the team shows real ambition. They also make an effort with food waste and chicken  farming which is great to see. But I felt the message came through more in the storytelling than in the dishes but it’s still early days and they are on a very good path. With a little more refinement, I believe this place has strong potential for even greater recognition in the future.

I’ve been to Michelin-starred restaurants all over the world — but Smokaccia is an entirely different experience.

Often when you go fine dining, things become a bit mechanical. The food is, of course, excellent, but somewhere along the way, the experience and the menu lose their soul. Many fine-dining establishments today seem afraid to take risks, afraid to innovate. They care more about following the certain formula that gets them that michelin star, rather than being unique. Smokaccia is the complete opposite.

I have never entered a restaurant that so completely embodies the mind and spirit of its chef. It’s unmistakably Chef Luca’s baby — his lifelong project and artistic expression. You can taste it in every flavor, see it in every architectural detail, sense it in every interaction with the staff, and hear it in every story told about each dish that arrives at your table.

The staff is incredible — super attentive, deeply present, and genuinely in tune with every guest. You can feel that the vision here isn’t about efficiency or getting people in and out the door. It’s about being fully present with each and every customer, creating an experience that feels personal and alive.

Smokaccia and Chef Luca are the purest examples of what humanity can create when we focus on one thing and pour our heart and soul into our passion.

As much as it was a culinary experience of a lifetime, it was equally an inspiration on how to approach life itself. The passion and dedication poured into this project are truly motivational — a reminder of what it looks like when someone follows their true calling without compromise. And I am 100% sure, that it’s only a matter of time before you will hear Chef Luca’s name everywhere.

If you’re in Phuket — and if you truly enjoy food — then Smokaccia is an absolute must-do. I’ve lived here for almost four years, and I can say with full confidence that this is not something to miss out on.

Do yourself a favor and experience it for yourself. Bring your loved ones and share the journey — it’s one that will stay with you long after the final course.

Thank you, Chef Luca, and thank you to everyone on the Smokaccia team.

What you’ve created is not just dinner — it’s art, heart, and soul on a plate.

Vietnamese cuisine has a lot to offer, but I had to first try out the Pho… and disappointment it certainly did not. The broth was flavourful yet subtle - elegant yet simple. The herbs and sprouts so fresh, I could feel the crunch in  every single spoonful. The sliced beef definitely took the spotlight though. I ordered the “rare beef” pho - so the meat came on the side. It was ready to be enjoyed after but a short dip in the steaming bowl of broth. Perfect!

Will definitely repeat.

Nice and cozy Vietnamese restaurant.  We have been here so many times. They keep their standard quality of food. Pho was really nice soup. The broth was tasty. The beef was tender.  For weekday,  there are choices of lunch sets. It is worth for money. The service was good.

This is hands down my favourite restaurant in Bangkok.
The food here is so good it honestly brings tears to my eyes every time I have it. I can’t even begin to describe how amazing it is. Everything tastes so authentic, and my one and only go to is the Bún Thịt Bò Xào Nam Bộ with Hành Tây 😍
The waitresses are always so lovely and greet you with a warm smile, and the restaurant’s decor is really nice too.
Also, the cold water they provide outside for riders is such a thoughtful touch.
Side note: Please open a branch in Phuket 🙏🏼😭

Was so happy to find this cute and deliciously authentic taste restaurant!  I have been coming back regularly since I discovered it. The staff is so nice, the service is rapid, there’s a great variety of dishes much more than pho.  Most dishes come with plenty of vegetables.  It seems that many people come back regularly also as some faces are quite familiar.  They also have takeout with grab if you want.  The prices are quite reasonable it usually comes out to about 400 baht per person.

When ‘Michelin’ Doesn’t Warm the Heart
— A Disappointing Visit to , a Vietnamese Restaurant in Bangkok

One evening during my stay in Bangkok, I found myself craving a hot bowl of pho. Not the Thai version, but Vietnamese— with a clear, deep broth, and the delicate aroma of coriander weaving through each sip.🥢

Luckily, just a short walk from where I was staying, there was a restaurant marked MICHELIN Guide Selected. With quiet anticipation, I decided to give it a try.

A stylish space, buzzing with people. Enough to stir my expectations.✨

But… perhaps I was expecting too much?

I didn’t even take a photo of the pho. The broth was lukewarm, lacking depth, and the noodles—far too soft, almost soggy.

From the potato croquettes and bún chả, to bánh xèo, spring rolls, and other Vietnamese home-style dishes— each dish left little impression, and together, a lingering sense of disappointment.😔

Maybe it was because I came after peak dining hours, but most of the food arrived cool, and the prices felt steep in comparison to what was served.

What left me most disheartened, though, was the absence of sincerity behind it all—
not just in the food, but in the service, too. It wasn’t about comparing it to a meal in Vietnam, but rather… the gap between anticipation and reality.
Most reviews for this place are glowing,
so maybe it was simply a matter of taste,
or bad timing in the kitchen that day.

But for me— this was a meal where the ‘name’ remained, but the heart was nowhere to be found.

Sometimes, it’s not fame or recognition that touches you— but the quiet care of a hidden kitchen down an alleyway,
where sincerity is the warmest thing on the table.🫶🏻

Location was absolutely stunning, views breath taking and grounds emaculate  and we were beyond excited to eat once we arrived at the banyan tree. The staff  were exceptionally Lovley but seemed to lag with service  not what I have experienced at other fine dining restaurants. We ordered the 4 course set menu and NOT  ONE dish we rated or would order again (some I couldn’t even finish and I’m not a fussy eater and normally would try to out of politeness ) . At a normal restaurant I would have been ok with this disappointment but it was a celebration  and we chose a Michelin star restaurant because we wanted a true culinary experience. Unfortunately we walked away knowing it was not deserving of its star and thinking the Lamai fresh food market stall  deserved the Michelin star and our fondest food memory’s while in Thailand

We had a truly memorable evening at Saffron in Koh Samui. The setting was stunning—perched high above the bay with breathtaking views that made the whole experience feel extra special. The staff were absolutely lovely from the moment we arrived, welcoming us with warmth and genuine care. It was my son’s birthday, and they went out of their way to celebrate the occasion with thoughtful touches that made him feel incredibly special. Their attention to detail and friendly service really stood out and added a personal, heartfelt touch to the night.

The food was nothing short of outstanding. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of bold, authentic Thai flavours. You could tell that a lot of care had gone into the preparation and ingredients. From the delicate starters to the rich, flavourful mains, everything we tried was exceptional. It was one of the best meals we’ve had, and the overall atmosphere was calm, elegant, and joyful which made it even better. Saffron is a perfect choice for a special occasion, and we’ll definitely be returning when we’re next in Koh Samui.

Excellent view, perfect service.
Food was only okay for the price point and hype.
Tuna larb and crab rolls were good but rest of the items missed the mark.
Can’t speak highly enough of the service!

Saffron offers a beautiful ocean view, impeccable service and delicious Thai food!

Each dish of the Thai tasting menu was delicious and flavorful. The galangal-coconut broth of the Tom Kha Gai cappuccino was outstanding as it was light but rich in flavor. The roasted peppered pork spare ribs slid of the bone and had the perfect spicy-sweet combination from the black pepper and honeycomb sauce. Each dish was prettily presented and the portion sizes were extremely generous. Needles to say, we left the restaurant satisfied and happy.

The service is impeccable: professional, very attentive and friendly. Whilst the prices are not cheap, they are justifiable for the quality of the food and the location.

To make the dining experience a notch better, it would be great if there were fans outside on the terrace. On an evening with no breeze, it is a bit too hot outside.
Our friends stayed at the Banyan Tree and we came for a visit, to spend a wonderful evening with very attentive stuff and an excellent dinner. Would definitely recommend that place.

If you’re looking for a truly local dining experience in Bangkok, Ann Tha Din Daeng is a must-visit. The place feels very authentic and not touristy at all. The highlight here is definitely the crab – it’s fresh, flavorful, and absolutely worth trying. The owner and staff speak very limited English, but don’t let that hold you back; ordering and enjoying the food isn’t really a problem. One tip: come early. I visited around 7 PM on a Sunday and many dishes were already sold out.
The food was great. The squid was  sooo good.  Small downside, cash only! Please make sure u bring enough cash.

One of the best crab fried rice dishes I’ve ever had! The crispy pork belly was perfectly done, and the tom yum soup was packed with flavor just the right balance of spicy and tangy. I didn’t get to take many photos since we were all too hungry to wait, but every dish was worth it. Highly recommended, and I’d definitely go again if I’m ever in the area!

Always​ here​ for​ foooodie!!
Dont​ forget to​ order​ anything​ with​ crab  meat  🤩🤩🤩
Service: not a​ Five​-Star​ on​ Service.​  Most​ of​​ staff​ are​ polite.​ Yet,​ they​ seemed rush​ all​ the​ time.
Atmosphere: normal for​ street​ food.​

Nothing special with the michelin star dishes and overpriced. 1550 thb for 3 water and 2 dishes, 1 prawn is 600thb and crab was 900 thb very expensive for the quality of food. Save yourself a hussle and go somewhere else.

A Unique Culinary Journey at Blackitch

We didn’t go for the full pairing, but took the sommelier’s suggestion to try orange wine — and it paired beautifully all the way through the meal!

The tasting course was crafted with unique local ingredients from across Thailand, north to south, as shown clearly in the menu. It really felt like a food journey through the country.

Some dishes were easy to enjoy, while a few were a bit challenging for my taste — especially the one with blue cheese (not my favorite, but interesting!).

Desserts were lovely, especially with the refillable tea pairing from the restaurant — a nice touch.

The atmosphere was intimate and quiet. We started around 5 PM and finished by 7:30 PM. Considering the experience and creativity, it’s definitely worth trying at least once.

This restaurant was the highlight of my trip to Chiang Mai!

Definitely the best meal of the journey, Blackitch Artisan Kitchen’s Regional Thai Essence tasting menu (May edition) features 13 creative courses inspired by the flavors and ingredients from all over Thailand. It reflects the chef’s deep respect and understanding of local produce, with each dish thoughtfully composed.

The entire experience breaks away from the usual heavy handed Thai flavors. It still captures the soul of Thai cuisine, but with a delicate, inventive twist that really hit the sweet spot for me. Every ingredient is sourced from organic farms across the country, and I can truly taste the seasons and the land in every bite.

A journey across Thailand … In one dining.

Incredible meal. Stunning presentation. And soooooo tasty. Yum!
Got so lucky this trip in Chiang Mai that managed to go twice within a week! The restaurant is incredible and praised highly amidst foodies across the world, Thailand including… so getting the reservations is getting challenging.

Incredibly high quality of ingredients, lavishly extensive and ‘just right’ menu. And the wine pairing is unusually good. Coming from England and dining in places like L’Arpège, KOL and The Ledbury, I got used to the fact that Thailand has high tax on wine imports and I usually don’t expect much from wine options/pairings … however this time the wine pairing was just really good. I went for the wine pairing both visits. Also, rather surprisingly the price was really low compare to what I’d normally pay when dining in Thailand with wine pairing.

The meal in itself made me feel like my tastebuds went to the Disneyland! Some dishes were so yummy that I had to ask for an additional serving on my second visit, that I have actually slightly regretted as I struggled to finish my meal. Some dishes were really new to me and I wasn’t accustomed to the tastes.. even though I have had meals of various nature across Thailand… so I just went with the flow and eat them anyway… and then my body had this happiness. It’s hard to describe. My tastebuds didn’t know what to do about these new flavours, but my body felt at home, nurtured and somewhat deeply happy. A new level of food experience unlocked for sure!

I have been going to this restaurant every time I am in Chiang Mai, pretty much since they’ve opened. Yet I feel this trip round the restaurant truly exceed my expectations.
I am very much into Bangkok food scene and particularly favour this year Soma Bangkok, and Ore… I have to say Blackitch Artisan Kitchen is a one of a kind… It’s Thai food yes, yet it’s so innovative and different (a little bit like Ore actually… yet different(!) so don’t expect similarities in food servings)… I feel you want to submit to whatever is given to you, consume it… and allow your body and eyes enjoy the feast on a whole new level.

What I particularly liked this time round:
no extreme sharp tastes, the food flows beautifully together
wine pairing is truly good even for any European fancy dining
still extremely affordable (the prices in Thailand have risen sharply and I have to watch my budget this trip) … it’s not CHEAP! please! if you are used to paying 10 Baht for a plate of rice on a street market - this restaurant is not for you. It is fine dining! Just really affordable one.
got lucky to eat twice within a week… :)

Ohhhhhh and DESERTS! ok, this is a whole another review … maybe next trip/visit … one desert I nicknamed “Christmas came early”… it was so good, I felt like I am opening Christmas presents… Ok, basically you can grasp that I am one very very happy eater/customer of Blackitch Artisan Kitchen.
Thank you!

ps: I've exceeded the word limit here so shared tips in photos :)

Absolutely fantastic meal, so memorable!!!
Loved the featuring of various regional produce from all over Thailand. Excellent flavour combinations, and textures too. Truly an outstanding, gastronomical experience.

You must book ahead. There are two seatings a night (and lunch apparently too).
There is a 5pm (which we went to as no other spaces were available) and a 7:30/8pm time slot.

It’s a 14 course tasting menu for about 3,000 THB $100 USD per person, alcohol and drinks extra. The pineapple basil mocktail with fresh red peppercorns was delicious!! The staff said it was their favourite too!

It is a very satisfying tasting menu and we left definitely feeling full, satisfied but not uncomfortable. Some of the dishes were slightly spicy (which we enjoyed) and you were told if it was spicy- I’d say they modify the spice level according to your preferences when booking.

Wait staff spoke English and explained each dish.

It’s very reasonable for a Michelin recommended restaurant with such excellent food. There is only seating available for 15 people upstairs (not wheelchair accessible)
But it was a pleasant area with quite nice decor.

Ideal for special night out or to impress clients as it showcases such amazing quality Thai produce.

I had an excellent meal at Blackitch in Chiang Mai. The concept behind the restaurant is super cool; it's all about showcasing unique Thai dishes from different regions across the country, and it really delivers.
With local ingredients and traditional techniques you can tell every dish has serious thought and craft behind it. You're not just eating dinner; you're getting a regional tour of Thailand through flavor. Service presentation and atmosphere were great.
Some of my highlights from the night:
• The Phang-Nga fish with ginger jime was incredibly fresh and beautifully plated. Clean, delicate flavors with a nice kick.
The slipper lobster totally surprised me. I'm usually not a big lobster fan, but when it's done well-like this-it's a game changer.
The Yornfish with wild almond and beetroot
cream was rich and balanced. I cleaned the plate.
• The stuffed chicken wing was perfectly cooked and looked like a piece of art with each ingredient separated.
• The buffalo shank was super tender and flavorful.
• The grilled rump of Kholoris beef was also a standout-no photo, though, I was too busy enjoying it.
For dessert, the palm sugar mille-feuille and pineapple ice cream were both done excellently-refined without being overcomplicated. My favorite part of the meal.
I think with just a bit more intensity in flavor and spice, this place could earn its Michelin star. Honestly, it already has that level of creativity and precision.

It's a great place to dine in. The atmosphere is great with plenty of space for you to walk around while you wait for your food. But it won't take long because each dish is fast. The price is alright and that the service is great. There's also painist to enhance your experience while dining.
The taste is amazingly good with the exception of that a lot of things are unusally salty. Like the cabbage with fish sauce. Only one leaf and I could eat with half of the rice plate. It's really really salty. They should lower the salt in every dish. Some of their dish could improve like the kaojee as they tried to create a filling, but they didn't put enough in and turned them into normal kaojee

true delight! The flavors are authentic and perfectly balanced, with dishes that are both aromatic and rich in taste. The service is warm and attentive, and the cozy ambiance makes it an excellent place to enjoy a meal.

The food tastes relatively good but the services were really bad. Plus, we were fooled about grilled shrimps prices; instead of charging per piece we were charged per grams! I don’t understand why they received Michelin rewards. Do not recommend to come here at all.

Just stumbled upon this place on a whim after visiting Luang Pu Maha Sila Monastery. The moment you enter, you feel the peaceful, serene atmosphere, surrounded by natural forest trees. They've created a very relaxing vibe, almost like being in a green forest national park! The food is good, though I wish it was a bit more authentic Thai. But that's just me—everyone in my group loved it. You have to check this place out!

Food is alright, lean toward being pricey. Service is abysmal. Doesn't seem like the past comments motivate the operator to improve their cuisine experience. Recommend to those that can wait long time for above average food with poor service. Probably not a good place for local Thai.

Great place to eat. You have to walk down the hallway to get to the restaurant area. That you wouldnt know is back there, but they a food cart by the front. Well worth it. The food was amazing the pork dumplings are so delicious. And the chicken is great 👍 👌 😋 😀

Stopped by last night with the family.  Neat place.
Food was good. We had the red curry chicken, seafood tom yum, noodle with chicken, steamed rice 🍚 and Thai iced teas.

Food is delicious, guest service is great by owners.  They speak English.

I couldn’t give it 5-stars because I found the portion for rice is ridiculously small. Rice you pay separate and it’s weirdly overpriced.  I think almost everything is overpriced so I think their price caters to foreigners only.

Mango sticky rice is over B200+ and it’s around 100-120 everywhere else.
You know the food is so good when the plates are all clean hahaha so yummy!!!! definitely a good place to dine!!! We'll be back ❤️❤️❤️

Very delicious and accommodating! My dad wanted hot coffee but they only have iced coffee. The boss was able to make a hot coffee for him.
We really enjoyed the fried sea bass a lot

Food taste so good with good portion as well
A bit overprice but we understand as it located in tourist area

Located along Silom Road, this charming restaurant stands out with its stylish décor and cozy atmosphere. There aren’t many tables, so I highly recommend making a reservation in advance. Around 7 p.m., the place gets very busy, and many walk-in customers end up waiting in line.

The grilled dishes are the highlight here — the smoky aroma from the charcoal, the freshness of the ingredients, and the chef’s seasoning make every dish rich and perfectly balanced. The restaurant beautifully elevates traditional Thai cuisine with creative twists, offering several innovative dishes that are both familiar and exciting. I especially recommend trying their signature items every plate is truly delicious.

Service-wise, the staff seemed a bit overwhelmed, probably because there were too many guests and not enough staff, but overall, they were attentive.

For parking, you can park at the Pullman G Hotel and have your ticket validated at the restaurant.

Creative Thai Izakaya dining. The seafood is exceptionally fresh, and every dish we tried was full of flavor.
The shrimp pancake is a must-try (we order two times!) — crispy, savory, and absolutely delicious. Even the simple fried rice stood out, showing how much care they put into every plate.

To finish, we had dessert, which was not only delicious but also felt unique and exotic — the perfect ending to a wonderful meal. Honestly, we loved everything we tried here. Highly recommended

Loved every bite of this meal. We ordered most of the dishes marked on the menu with a heart and were not disappointed. Oozing with flavour, the food was unusual takes and tapas style bites on traditional Thai dishes. The presentation is standout and we could easily have kept going with dessert. Depending on what city you’re visiting from, you’re likely to find this place is great value for money. I can’t wait to go back.

quality modern thai food without breaking the bank - definitely put this on your itinerary!

i think they are better known for their open flame grill and thai street food - jap izakaya fushion skewers? i definitely preferred the chicken skewers (esp the boneless chicken wing with yuzu kosho) over their signature moo peng actually.

don't skip the other dishes too.

the shrimp on coconut pancake appetiser was TO DIE FOR. mochi-textured dense pancake with strong gula melaka and kaya fragrance. odd combination with shrimp but it worked so well!

the kailan cooked with prawn paste (har cheong sauce) was super yummy too! why has no one thought of using prawn paste instead of oyster sauce to dress vegetables all this time?

the pork ribs was on almost every table, so we got one to try too. it was fork tender and really yummy but leans on the salty side, so pair it with the pickled lettuce to cut thru the salt.

pomelo and shrimp salad was alright, but the least impressive of the dishes we tried.

P.S. i counted  6 aircon units for a relatlively small dining space. be warned it was very cold and draughty which marred my experience ever so slightly

Michelin bib gourmand spot. Came by during lunchtime on a Saturday with reservation but while the place was packed there were still some seats available.

We ordered most of the items (menu wasn’t the biggest). The moo ping was great with a nice char. Actually pretty much most of the dishes had a nice char since it’s cooked over open fire. Worth a try.

Nice music sound not too high, lovely restaurant and good service.
I asked papaya salad not spicy and with no sugar, I received as I order but they kindly gave also a plate of cucumbers and tomatoes
Fish big and very good !
Vanilla ice scream is top quality of vanila
It’s a nice restaurant !

Food was excellent! All the dishes appear to be seafood / fish. Note that the menu is in Thai, but that some dishes have photos. Note also that they only accept cash, so bring cash if you go. Views are just as good as the food.

Great view. Great staff.

The food was fresh and cooked and flavoured perfectly. Of course, Isaan food is ubiquitous in Thailand. But many dishes had distinct flavours from using local ingredients and herbs. It was not just high quality but also a distinct experience.

The fried cat fish was cooked perfectly. It also came with a wonderful chilli sauce that I'd recommend to everyone.

I also had a delightful som dtam Dish that used pea shoots instead of papaya. The moo larb and prawn salad was perfect and tom yum bplaa was not just perfect but I'd never had one with those flavours before.

The staff was able to recommend the isaan highlights and also the highlights more specific to Ubon.

It was worth every penny and a special trip slightly outside of the main city.

This restaurant establish more than ten years ago which changed from resort as a retirement project of the owner. She has a friendly characteristic and welcome all customer by herself.

The very first customer intend to serve are her friends. Four food oredred are well cooked with the original taste and freshness.
The most recommende menu are frices sticky rice with shrimp, fries fish with garlic, home cooked pickle cabbage and salted fish dipping.
For soup recommended sour fish soup.

Gauranteed by Michelin Guide 2023-2024 sign.

Parking are available near by its restaurant and can be park around 10 cars.

If you visit them at the right time of sunset, you will see a very nice view too.

This restaurant also need some direction sign for pointing to its restaurant.

I had high expectations to the food here as it was michelin, but all of it was quite oily. The fried rice was very plain and nothing special, the fish and sundries beef was also very plain. The location is perfect though, so forget that it’s Michelin, come have some food and enjoy the river view.
One of the finest Thai fine-dining experiences I’ve had — every bite was delicious. The tea pairing complemented the dishes perfectly. Absolutely worth it! 💞

If your looking to dine like royalty, this is the spot. Exceptional service, great atmosphere and beautifully presented tasty dishes. Our table was blown away by the experience, well done to the whole team!

We had an absolutely wonderful experience celebrating our wedding anniversary here! The food was incredible — every dish was full of amazing flavor and beautifully presented. The wine pairing was perfect and complemented each course so well. The service and atmosphere made the evening even more special. Thank you for giving us such a memorable anniversary celebration! Highly recommend. 🍷

I struggle a lot to find positive comments for this place. Food was ridiculously bad - only the first bit was able to make me happy. Most other dishes were greasy and super salty! One of the fried dishes smell really old like it was cooked from old cooking oil. Portion wise are pretty weird: wagyu which supposed to be one bite was quite large and the duck in the curry dish was so small and thin.

Service was pretty average but the kitchen crew finished cleaning their kitchen and left the site even before I finished my meal.

Had the most incredible dining experience at Lahnyai by Nusara, one of Asia's Best 50 Restaurants by the famous Chef Ton. I went for their tasting menu, which had so many courses, and each one was a masterpiece. The royal Thai food was presented beautifully and so unique—my taste buds were in heaven! The service was top-notch, everything felt so well taken care of. It’s already in the Michelin Guide, and I’m sure it’ll get a Michelin star soon. Definitely a must-try for Thai cuisine lovers!

I had an absolutely fantastic dining experience at Wana Yook Thai Restaurant in Bangkok. From start to finish, everything was exceptional.

The ambiance is elegant yet warm. It is set in a beautifully restored colonial-style building that feels both historic and intimate. The service was attentive and genuinely thoughtful. The staff took the time to explain each course and were happy to adjust the spice levels to suit our preferences.

The food was the highlight of the evening. Wana Yook’s tasting menu, inspired by khao gaeng, is truly impressive. Each course features rice from a different region of Thailand, and the flavors are bold, complex, and beautifully balanced. Every dish shows creativity and deep respect for traditional Thai cuisine, presented with a refined modern touch.

The restaurant has earned a Michelin star, and it is easy to understand why. The use of local ingredients and the celebration of Thai culinary heritage come through in every bite.

If you are looking for a memorable and high-end Thai dining experience in Bangkok, Wana Yook is a must-visit. I cannot wait to go back!

What can I say but WOW.

We saw Mark Weins review of this Michelin  Star restaurant and had to put it on our bucket list to visit.

What an experience it was, from the moment we arrived.

The building itself is nestled back from the hustle and bustle of Bangkok.  Its architecture and design is breathtakingly beautiful with whimsical touches.  My husband especially liked Pinocchio in the waiting room.

The staff were impeccable with service and explaining the food to us.
I ordered the wine pairing package and fell in love with the Thai Sato Wine, we took a bottle home with us.

The French Sommelier was attentive and the food wine pairing was perfection.

I simply cannot fault, and I left feeling more than full.

The 10 courses were beautifully curated, and the concept of the perfect bite executed brilliantly.

Bravo and thank you for a memorable dining experience.

Thank you for such a fantastic meal from the team of Wana Yook.

The restaurant is hidden at a nice and quiet garden right next to the BTS station.

The menu consists of native Thailand elements - Seafood, especially prawns and fish sauce are well incorporated in a lot of the dishes; Curry - meat infused with lots of locally sourced fresh herbs; coconut - local specialty that gives freshness and sweetness; rice - different types of rice to compliment the dishes. Overall, the whole menu is well designed with perfect balanced flavour, texture and composition. Guests that are not used to Thai level of spiciness can request milder spice level.

I enjoyed every dish from entree to dessert!

The portion is relative big for fine dining so female guests with a smaller appetite can choose to taste a bit of everything on the spot and have the rest to-go.

I think it's just a matter of time before Wana Yook grabs another Michelin star. Highly recomment to anyone visiting Bangkok!

A fun way to enjoy Thai cuisine!
The spiciness and full flavors were an amazing experience.
The service was warm and welcoming .. definitely recommend for those who love Thai food.

Absolutely phenomenal restaurant! I think all the dishes had the most impactful flavor of most of the Michelin restaurants I've eaten at. The service was top notch and very attentive. A lot of food too, I was completely full by the end of the tasting menu. They are also able to accommodate different spice tolerances. Would recommend this place to anyone looking for a fine dining experience in Bangkok.
A local friend bring us here, the seafood are fresh and meaty, enjoy the food here very much. Good portion and price are reasonable.

My go-to spot every time I’m in Ayutthaya. The food’s really good and totally worth the price. The grilled shrimp is a must—super fresh, comes in big portions, and not pricey at all. They usually have three sizes to choose from. I also really like their fried rice, tom yum, and the seafood sauce is amazing. It’s in the market area but there’s parking, which is super convenient. Definitely a place I keep coming back to.

This one is the famous Thai restaurant of Ayutthaya. I saw so many a lot of government officer come here. The ingredient is super fresh there is seafood live stock ready to cook. The food is tastes really good and decent price. The staff fast and good service. But parking is hard to find.

If shrimp were a religion, this place would be the temple. Tucked along the road of Ayutthaya, this lunch gem delivers shrimp so fresh they probably filled out a time sheet this morning. Swap riverside with marketside.

The grilled river prawns? Massive. Like, “should I tip this prawn?” massive. Heads full of rich, golden fat that made us question everything we thought we knew about flavor—and cholesterol. We went in thinking we’d order light. We left Googling if it’s socially acceptable to drink prawn oil straight.

Sides were no afterthought either—spicy dips that slap, rice that actually compliments the meal instead of just showing up, and a riverside view that’s one strong gust away from a full food meditation session. Bonus: zero tourist-trap energy. Just good food, good people, and shrimp that might haunt our dreams (in the best way).

Come hungry, leave full—and maybe with a few shrimp shells in your pocket for emotional support.

A Must-Try Grilled Shrimp Spot in Ayutthaya! 🦐🔥

If you're visiting Ayutthaya, you can’t leave without trying some grilled river prawns—and this place is one of the best! The province is known for its shrimp, and while there are many restaurants to choose from, this one stands out with its great flavor and reasonable prices.

The restaurant is surrounded by other grilled shrimp spots, but what makes this one special is how perfectly they grill the prawns. The texture is still juicy and bouncy, and you can really taste the natural sweetness.

I ordered 1 kg of grilled shrimp (they were huge!), asked them to use some to make Tom Yum Goong (spicy prawn soup), and added a separate dish of fried shrimp. Everything was super fresh and flavorful.

This place is really popular with locals, so I recommend coming early—around 11:00–11:30 AM. I arrived at 11:10, and by the time I finished placing my order, the restaurant was nearly full. They have 3 seating zones, and two of them were packed already!

If you're a seafood lover, don’t miss this gem in Ayutthaya!

Modern Indian cuisine with a twist.
Some old favourites and some interesting appetisers with great presentation.
My wife has dietary requirements due to requiring gluten free which I mentioned in the booking and we were well catered for with the head chef confirming what they could change for the dishes we selected.
We chose a range of appetisers and dessert.
Presentation, service and taste was excellent.
A shame it was raining as it’s a rooftop restaurant with a great view.
Atmosphere was still great and would definitely recommend for an experience.
