review_text: Very good food. Very reasonable price as well. Has been rated Michelin star for many years and they remain very humble. I'll going again tomorrow, 19 Oct 2025, (today 18 Oct 2025) for another bowls of kuey chap (guay jub). It's very yummy.

restaurant_name: Guay Jub Chang Moi Tat Mai
review_text: Honestly, it tastes just normal nothing special. I’ve had better crispy pork before. Also, It’s quite expensive for the small serving size, even though I ordered the large. The soup also wasn’t to my liking it had a strange smell.

Have wanted to try this place for some time finally managed to booked it.
Pretty centrally located and very easy to get to by walking from the BTS or MRT station. I tried to Grab here and got stuck in a bad jam just turning in from the main road and I ended up walking into the restaurant.
Its a small and cosy restaurant like sitting at the counter and watching the whole team in action. Came for the 530pm first round of seating and the moment we sat they were already ready to fire out the dishes.
I have to say the dishes were all pretty good and unique. For me the flavours some of it might need a bit of getting used to, it's Thai cuisine but its not the typical Thai cuisine that you eat everyday in the typical restaurants or street food in Bangkok.
They feature the local ingredients and elements in the dishes that you sometimes will find it surprising. For me it's really an experience and a wild time for my tastebuds to get to explore the complexity in flavours and yet good food.
Of course there were a few standouts for me, especially the crab and the Thai version of their wagyu beef.
It's really pretty experimental and they change their menu every 2 months but unfortunately they do not really have a signature dish which stays on in their menu.
The tasting menu is pretty reasonable and would recommend this if you really like to take a ride to try out the unique recipes from Samrub Samrub Thai.
Reservations required. They usually have the 530pm and the 8pm seatings.

With local and fresh ingredients, flavors are so complex and full of surprises. Professionally presented on table.
Staff are super nice. Such a great dining experience.
Although some of the dishes were too spicy for me, but the food was really tasty and sensational.
Strongly recommend if you wanna try modern taste of Thailand.
Make sure to secure your table online! :)

Real good Thai food. You are sitting all together at a big table and watch the crew prepari g every single dish including presentation. It was a unique and great experience. The food was perfectly cooked - however some said it was too spicy. For me the taste was just perfect. I didn’t like the speed of serving. I habent finished one course and was already served with the next - not only did it give me a feeling of rush but also kind of pushy and request to hurry.

Extremely disappointing experience. The food was underwhelming at best — some dishes were too salty, and nothing on the menu rose above the level of ordinary Thai food except for the dumpling pork soup which was quite tasty.

For a Michelin-starred restaurant and an Asia’s 50 Best listing, this was a complete letdown. Presentation was bland and uninspired, and there was still some eggshells in our dish. To top it off, I even ended up with mild diarrhea after the meal.

The food and service lacks sincerity and feels somewhat robotic, chaotic and rushed. The head chef fawned over the caucasian or “farang” guests - having drinks with them, constantly chatting and checking in on them, while completely ignoring other asian diners as though we are invisible, making it especially akward as we were all seated on the kitchen counter. The asian diners were strangely placed all together in one section of the counter and had to make small chats amongst ourselves to make the environment less awkward as we were ignored by the head chef. Nobody even came to asked us on our feedback of the food etc. The entire dining experience was less than 2 hours as we could not bare to stay there any longer as it feels very cramped as well.

It is painfully clear who they value more as a customer. Paying the same amount of money (approximately THB10,000 for 2 pax) only to be treated as second-class customers is very insulting and shocking in such an  establishment.

In short: overpriced for the cheap local ingredients used and small portion, overrated, and utterly undeserving of the accolades (perhaps the Michelin inspectors are caucasians). If you are asian, save your money and go to other better established Thai fine dining restaurants like Sorn, Baan Tepa, Potong, Khaan where customers are treated equally with respect and you don't feel shortchanged.

Truly exceptional Thai cuisine — refined, authentic, and full of heart
I had a wonderful dining experience at Samrub Samrub Thai. The food was absolutely outstanding — full of authentic Thai flavours, presented with such care and attention to detail. Every dish reflected not just great technique, but also a deep respect for Thai culinary traditions.

The ingredients were clearly of high quality, and the balance of flavours was perfect in every course. It’s rare to find a place that delivers both depth of taste and such refined presentation.

Every dish showcased high-quality ingredients and a deep respect for traditional Thai recipes, elevated in a truly elegant way. My mom especially loved how each bite reminded her of familiar flavours, but with a refined twist.

This is Thai cuisine at its finest — elevated, yet still deeply comforting and true to its roots. A well-deserved Michelin star, and I can’t wait to return.

Super clean, delicious, and service-minded from there employees!

Every foods in this restaurant are worth to order.

If are keen to looking for a mid to high tier of restaurant in Ubon Ratchathani, you should be visit here.
It’s been 10 years since the last time we ate here, and it’s just as good as I remember. Excellent saikrok, delicious somtam and the best gai yang in Ubon.

I had the pleasure of finding this place. Its a restaurant and boxing gym.
(A) CLEAN!!!!! I cant stress how rare this is.
(B) Great Service
(C) Food was simple Issan/Thai very tasty.
(D) Beer was cold
Mostly one can see the owner (whom I did not meet but will sometime soon) clearly takes great pride in the premises and it reflects in the food. Quality simple tasty Thai cuisine. I returned several times while in Ubon and will come again. There are countless similar eateries about this area but I assure you reading this you will know once you have eaten here that they are a cut above.
Good Foods for western people.
Yummy lunch,  AC is so cool, Good sitting in the summer 36C, Wi-Fi is good enough for posting. Lovely waitress as well. ☺Highly recommend. 👍

Finally got the chance to try this well-known Kueh Chap spot in Bangkok. Here are my thoughts:

KH Guide & Rating
•	Accessibility: 4.4/5
(Located in a small plaza on the LG level. Fairly easy to find parking.)
•	Cleanliness: 4/5
(Generally clean and reasonably well-maintained.)
•	Ambience: 4/5
(Comfortable seating, with around 20 tables available.)
•	Food Quality:
1.	Roasted Pork – Not top-tier, but no unpleasant porky smell and the skin was nicely crispy.
2.	Rice Noodles – Pleasantly chewy, just the right texture.
3.	Soup – Not overly sweet as is common in Thailand. Add a dash of pepper upon serving for a well-balanced flavor. Overall, the dish came together nicely in taste and presentation.
•	Pricing: 4.5/5
(Great value for money.)
•	Attentiveness: 5/5
(Excellent and friendly service.)
•	Would I return? Yes

15 mins queue on Wed around 1 pm. Tried their noodles in “pickled cabbage soup with everything”.  The innards were prepared well that it didn’t carry any foul smell.  Good for a change from the everyday Thai boat noodles.  Roast pork was average.  Chrysanthemum tea was good, only slightly sweetened. Ask for English menu ie if you cannot read Thai.

⭐ Arunwan Michelin – Honored Every Year ⭐

After living here for over two years, we’ve found our favorites — and yes, we do our diligent research! 🕵️‍♂️🍜

Opened over 60 years ago and now run by the founder’s children, this legendary spot has perfected its signature pork offal and pickled cabbage soup, crafted from a treasured family recipe. The flavors are beautifully balanced — the tangy pickled cabbage cuts through the sweetness of the rich pork consommé for a perfectly harmonious bowl.

While you wait for your soup, don’t skip the crispy pork wontons with sweet black sauce — they’re worth the trip alone! 😋

Today in front of mine introduced me to this place and definitely I will be back!

It was not only super reasonable in price but the food was really good they were quick in service and the food came nice and hot the way I like it

I ordered the pickled cabbage soup with mince pork meatballs and crispy belly with wontons it was really good I thoroughly enjoyed it !

My friend ordered the pickled cabbage soup with intestines and crispy pork as well and it was really good made it nice and spicy 🌶️

The crispy wontons were excellent and the sticky rice of peanuts came with a sweet sauce it was OK I mean it wasn’t my favorite but overall it was really good !

Remember to follow Fauzia 👈🏽💕 for all different types of cuisines in around Bangkok and beyond they don’t just eat Asian food we eat all of the amazing wonderful cuisines that creative chefs put on and through their talent we can enjoy ! 😊

We are on Facebook YouTube for all their awesome shorts and videos as well as TikTok and Instagram !! 🦋👈🏽💞 it’s free to join and subscribe 🤣💜

Another Bangkok Michelin gem quest.
Hidden location, it is on Park X-Ekkamai basement. Quiet, cozy and cool dining area.
I ordered their Dry egg noodle with pork, wonton and stomach, the combination was superb.
Springy and chewy noodle, the seasoning oil was so fragrant and flavorful.
The wontons, both boiled and fried one were chubby, full of meat and delicious.
Clean and tender boiled pork slices and stomach, taste so good.
Service was good, staffs was polite.
Michelin can't be wrong at here.
Highly recommended.

Tasty food, cheap & authentic.
Hong Mo is perfect with rice.
The yellow curry is actually KengSom and the spicy level is definitely not for Non Asian 🤣

I’m writing this review as a serious warning to other diners. My girlfriend and I visited Ko Ang Seafood Restaurant in Phuket just a few days ago, and the experience turned into a medical emergency.

She ordered the horseshoe crab, and within 24 hours she experienced severe vomiting and diarrhea. That alone would be concerning, but the situation escalated dangerously. She began experiencing symptoms consistent with neurotoxin poisoning – her fingers swelled, went numb, and became extremely painful. We had to seek urgent medical care, and doctors advised us that the food may have caused kidney complications as a result of potential toxicity from what she ate.

This is not just food poisoning – this was life-threatening. After researching more, we discovered that horseshoe crab poisoning is a documented and very serious risk, and should never be served without rigorous safety protocols. Ko Ang failed this responsibility.

To make matters worse:
•	Dogs were seen running around the kitchen area, completely unacceptable for any restaurant, let alone one that allegedly holds Michelin recognition.
•	The food itself was overrated and not worth the hype. Poor flavor, inconsistent freshness, and unsafe practices.

This place is dangerous, not just disappointing. We strongly urge all travelers and diners to avoid eating here, especially the horseshoe crab and any raw or specialty seafood.

Ko Ang Seafood should be reassessed by Michelin inspectors immediately. Cleanliness and food safety are non-negotiable, and this establishment fell drastically short of even basic hygiene standards.

A must-try Michelin spot in Phuket Old Town! Ko Ang Seafood truly lives up to its reputation. The seafood is incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked — the crabs and seafood fried rice are absolute standouts and highly recommended. Every seafood dish we tried was full of flavor and expertly prepared. The pork dishes, however, were a bit underwhelming and not something I’d recommend. That said, the overall quality of the food was excellent, and the prices are very reasonable for what you get. If you’re in Phuket Old Town, this place should definitely be on your list!

The menu was very helpful with English. The crab curry was spicy but good. The squids with black sauce were spicy but good. The fried shrimp had a nice sweet and sour sauce to give my tongue break. I'm definitely building up my spice tolerance. I would not recommend the black sugarcane juice.

A Micheline rated restaurant where you can expect good food and friendly staff. sea food is bit expensive but taste balances that  ! The only reason, I give a 4 star Is due to higher prices on some items which did not make any sense. They should accept credit card for convenience
Good taste, recommended to try.
We had a wonderful experience here! The Thai wontons are definitely worth a try.
Good

I tried the recommended menu with a friend. It was good, but I couldn’t really see the specialty… it was basically egg with rice and a few other things. It wasn’t that cheap, but of course, it was still good! I would try other dishes next time. 8/10 😋
I’m Brazilian and have a travel agency in Peru — Cusco, Machu Picchu 🇧🇷🇵🇪 @dopkertravel. If you travel to Peru, I can help you! ✈️

The food is super delicious, especially the shrimp dumplings. The boss lady is very elegant. The store has become bigger after moving, and the whole feeling is better. You can eat here when you go to the big swing.
Has moved, near the old store Google has not been updated

A hidden gem in Bang Pho! I tried their signature the “Kai Ra Boet” congee, and it was delicious. The congee was good, the pork was tender, and the egg added a rich flavor. For the congee, the taste is quite mild, so you can add soy sauce if you need saltier flavor. They cook each bowl individually in a brass pot, which keeps the heat in.

What really surprised me was the Pu Jor (deep-fried crab roll) — absolutely delicious! Crispy on the outside, packed with flavor inside. Honestly, I think I loved it even more than the congee.

Took the sea bass soft boiled rice , fish is fresh and no fishy smell as well as the pork congee was smooth and the minced pork was well seasoned. Came back again for other menu the stir fried seafood noodle and the pork blood soup it was all great. The ingredients were fresh and tasted good.
Delicious seafood and intestine. Cooked well without "intestine" taste. Mixing it with the bean sauce was superb!

The porridge was average, I have tried other stores that are better. To all tourists who are making your way to this place, please know that they practice differentiated pricing for the English and Chinese menu. Though it is not about the actual price that matters, it just does not feel good to be treated differently just because we are tourists.

I do not recommend coming to this place.

For me congee was overrated no flavor in it I know that restaurant doesn’t use msg that is a good point. And another thing that I like is service grandma she is a kind person smile to customer I love the vibe of this restaurant too it feels like 1990 Thailand.

Food Review: Egg Noodle with Creamy Tom Yum Noodle Soup and Onsen Egg at Gim Nguan Fish Ball

If you’re a fan of bold flavors and authentic craftsmanship, the Egg Noodle with Creamy Tom Yum Noodle Soup and Onsen Egg Topping at Gim Nguan Fish Ball is a must-try dish that lives up to its reputation. Recommended by the staff, this bowl of noodles is a testament to why this humble eatery has won Michelin awards consistently from 2021 to 2024.

The fishballs are undoubtedly the highlight of the dish—juicy, springy, and free from any unpleasant “fishy” aftertaste. You can tell they’re made with care and quality ingredients, a rarity these days. Each bite is satisfying, providing the perfect complement to the creamy, flavorful broth.

The Tom Yum soup itself is a masterpiece. Infused with just the right balance of tangy, spicy, and savory notes, the addition of the onsen egg elevates it to another level. The egg’s velvety texture blends seamlessly into the broth, making it irresistibly creamy. I found myself savoring every spoonful and finishing every last drop—a rare feat for me when it comes to noodle soups.

At just 85 baht per bowl, this dish is an absolute steal considering its exceptional quality and Michelin-recognized flavor. Gim Nguan Fish Ball isn’t just a restaurant; it’s a destination worth traveling for. Whether you’re a local or a tourist, this dish should be on your food bucket list. It’s more than just a meal; it’s an experience.

This may be the best dish I’ve had in all of Thailand? Such a warm atmosphere, the fish noodle soup was such a TREAT- a party in my mouth. Such rich, unique flavors, and such a special spot. HIGHLY RECOMMEND! Service was also wonderful & such friendly workers. 12/10⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ if any foreigners are looking for authentic flavor, this is the spot!!!

This restaurant is interesting because it has a huge sunshade with full of Michelin guide marks, these marks also everywhere inside the restaurant, to made me feeling like I was in the Michelin world:)
The mama noodle mixed with various kinds of food included minced pork meat, onsen eggs and squid meat, a little bit sweet, not so spicy as I expected, so I put lots of chili in it, then became very tasty, I really enjoyed it and the owner lady was very friendly and beautiful ;)

Wayyyy off the beaten path, only discovered it after a Michelin guide nod but I'm glad I did.

Their signature thing is their maximalist noodles with everything: fish balls, some kind of crackers, quail eggs, some other kinds of meat, cheese (in a Thai restaurant?) grilled with an actual blowtorch right in front of you, and thick, savoury tom yum flavoured broth.

Unique, cool, delicious and super friendly, definitely worth a detour to this remote area.
Tom Yum noodles is awared by 3 years ( Michelin). Must come and try.

Chang Wang Imm is a traditional Thai restaurant that has a taste of authentic. All foods taste great. The riverside atmosphere adds really good vibe. I have came to this place multiple times and everytime it does not disappoint.

Highly recommend

What a beautiful ambience - right next to the river!   🛶 We got a nice seating area in the corner. It was a bit windy and quite romantic 😁

The food is good. Sautéed greens with scrambled egg is nice. 👍 😋

The steamed fish 🐟 with lime 🍋‍🟩 garlic 🧄 and chilies 🌶️ is delicious. It’s quite fragrant and was served hot.

Red curry paste chicken with yolk is good as well.

Overall I would recommend this place for great views and ambience. Food is decent too although a bit on the expensive end.

Food is great that they use good ingredients with reasonable price for Michelin star with riverside view that you can bring your family or even your date here, but i recommend dinning in the evening as the indoor area is made of wood air-con is not that cool against thailand heat in the afternoon.

reviewer: เมธาสิทธิ์ เลิศศิริสัมพันธ์
review_text: When there after my grandma ash scattering ceremony, really like the atmosphere of vintage thai style wooden architecture which was very unique and nostalgic. the location is close to the temple and there’re also a parking lot in front of the restaurant but the filled with car later on since this place was so popular

Traditional Thai styled restaurant. I think they renovated an old Thai house to the restaurant. Plenty of outdoor parking available and you easily can walk from  there. Both indoor(with A/C) and outdoor are available and some tables got view of the river. We recommend you to reserve the table in advance since it can get busy on the rush hour. Overall, the food was really amazing but we particularly love the marinated crab and Fried rice with pork cracking. The service was also great and we got the food not too slow.

I travel to Asia quite a bit and I understand that the portion size is much smaller than the West. But what caught me off guard was how small these portions are at the price that’s being charged here. It was like boat noodle sizes.

No matter. I ordered more. After all if it tastes great, it’ll justify the size. I ordered the pork and wonton with soup. Then I ordered the crab with pork egg noodles and 2 orange juices.
You can definitely taste the shrimp in the dumplings. Is it the best? Not really. Soup was good with some good flavours but I don’t even bother to drink it all. It was average.

The egg noodles with crab and pork was also very average. I expected the noodles to just punch me with flavours but sadly, it didn’t. It was bland. I’ve had these types of noodles in Thong Lo and it’s much better.
The crab was non existent. It was literally a sprinkle of it as if they scraped it from whatever’s left on a single crab claw. It was laughable. Why would you advertise this having crab to just give me something so non existent. I felt insulted.

The only thing I enjoyed was the orange juice. Though on the sweeter side but it washes that garlic after taste.

Overall I was disappointed. It was a good 11 mins to walk there. I don’t mind the portion size or the price but at least give us something meaningful. Total was 330 baht. What a waste of money and time.

Extremely expensive for the portion size.

Came here because it’s a Michelin recognised place. The menu states that the signature noodles - “Egg Noodles with Crab Claw, BBQ pork and crispy pork” and it comes in S/M/L/XL sizes.

Note that the S size starts at 220baht, with each size up coming at an additional 100baht. We thought that the size was indicative of the portion and size of the crab claw but was told that the sizes only apply to the size of the crab claw, with noodles and meat portions remaining the same regardless.

The bowls at medium size were incredibly small. The crab claw sizes did not differentiate much at all. It was like paying 100baht for the same bowl of noodles. Not to mention, even the waiter couldn’t differentiate between the size S and M bowls - which goes to show how little the differences are per bowl.

While delicious, definitely not worth the money. There was just simply not enough in the bowl for all the flavours to come together.

The sides were fine. Delicious but not so
much different from other places out there. Cash only payment.

Extremely disappointing given the hype.

We had 3 noodles, they charged 310baht. The store doesn’t need to queue, so we chose it. The price is more expensive comparing with other stores. And the taste is good but not wow. The noodles are Cantonese style, but the soup flavor is Thai.

Yummy thin egg noodles 😍
Tasty Bbq Pork and shrimp wonton.

Portion is perfect for us who wants to explore Banthat Thong area.

The Lady Boss is really kind and helpful.
She helped us dealing with the Tuk Tuk driver 👏.

Thank you so much.

Whether awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand or not, this is by far one of the best Thai Wanton Noodles in BKK!

After having read the reviewers here complaining about the small size or quantity for the price, for me, as a foreigner, its good value for the portion size considering the high quality of the ingredients in the bowl, not to mention that pork bone broth that has the words dedication and passion swimming all over within. 😉

The egg noodles here are definitely different from others in BKK.  Much higher egg and alkaline to water ratio, which gives the noodles an opaque look and a more al dente bite. 👍👍👍

The Char Siew (BBQ) Pork was thick and satisfyingly tender to the bite.  Each Wanton dumpling had a separate small prawn/shrimp within, aside from the minced pork that gave it a good substantial (and satisfying) chew.  Apart from a few pieces of crab meat, the crab claw was meaty and tasted fresh!  👍👍👍

Like all Thai Wanton Noodles in BKK, it is a little bland despite being lightly coated in a tinge of garlic/onion, and perhaps pork lard oil.  For those who enjoy stronger tasting food, the blandness could be cured by the chillies, sugar and soya sauce condiments freely available on the table.

The star of the show is definitely the pork. One broth!  Murky with pork bone goodness, it wasn’t salty, but the Umami was just right on my palette, and it didn’t taste of artificial MSG as well.  Kudos to Sawang Noodle for this! 👍👍👍👍👍

This Sawang Noodle outlet has only has 5 or 6 tables, and I was lucky enough to get a seat with another single customer @11.30am…. 10mins waiting time for my food.

Young lady who attended to me was extremely patient and kind with my 20/20 questions.  And I was extremely happy with her recommendations.

Whether 405 Baht is considered expensive for the Wanton Noodles and soup I had, I was happy to pay for it, and for the experience. ☺️

And yeah, I will definitely be back again when I am next in BKK!

Came over past dinner time so it wasn't too crowded.

The boss and workers were very friendly and accommodating. The shop isn't air conditioned, great for those seeking an open authentic experience.

The seafood served was very fresh. Groupers, prawns and pealed crabs were absolutely amazing.  Being a sucker for mama noodles, the shop offers mama noodles as a carb selection together with rice. Not to be confused, the noodles are served plain without it's typical tomyum soup.

Would recommend the experience overall to those looking to try.

Really good local spot! The restaurant is listed in the Michelin Guide, and it totally deserves it. The rice soup is delicious, seafood is super fresh, and the braised pork is tender and comes in big chunks. Prices are reasonable too — definitely worth a visit!

It is a restaurant that has received awards for several years in a row.I tried ordering a variety of dishes because I came with a group of friends and found that most of the dishes tasted good.But it must be admitted that the amount of food received and the price paid are quite high.Pickled crab meat Baked shrimp with glass noodles and stir-fried morning glory with chili paste are my three favorite dishes.Another thing I don't like is that the shop is quite hot even with many fans, the air is still hot.

We came with some expectations this being a Michelin restaurant 7 years in a row.
We ordered the boiled rice fish soup (Grouper). The fish was far from fresh, chewy, and the boiled rice soup had a texture and taste like something done in a rush without care. We received our food less than 5 minutes after ordering.
The total price for two fish soups - 690 THB.

This is a disgrace and no where near the standard of a Michelin restaurant or any restaurant for that matter.
Being a fan of good quality- and fresh food, I cannot recommend this place.

I hope however, that they will step up and try to earn back the Michelin they have received.

In the restaurants' defence, we didn't complain which we probably should have done, giving them a chance to correct their mistake.
This is a good place to enjoy authentic Thai food. As is situated next to a street, it may feel a bit noisy, but it is a part of an experience 😀

This place serves authentic Northern Thai food that truly hits the spot — full of flavor, tradition, and warmth!

🥗 Nam Prik Num Set: Freshly made chili dip served with a colorful platter of steamed vegetables, crispy pork cracklings, and boiled egg. Everything was well-prepared and balanced — spicy, savory, and comforting.

🌶 Tam Khanun (Young Jackfruit Salad): One of the best we’ve had! Bold, smoky, and a beautiful mix of textures from crispy shallots and roasted chilies.

🌭 Sai Oua (Northern Thai Sausage): Rich in herbs and perfectly grilled. Each bite packed a punch of flavor. Truly a must-order dish!

🍗 Fried Chicken Wings: Crispy, golden, and juicy. Comes with a tangy dipping sauce that goes so well with sticky rice.

🧑‍🍳 The overall presentation, flavors, and attention to detail really show the love for Lanna cuisine here. Every dish reminded us of home-cooked Northern Thai meals but elevated in taste and quality.

💬 Whether you’re a local or just visiting, this restaurant is a wonderful place to explore Northern Thai flavors. It’s perfect for a family gathering — just like ours. We’ll be back for sure!

We went to this restaurant based on a recommendation from a local youtuber in Chiang Mai. The recommendation was spot on. the food was absolutely delicious. We had about five dishes and all were wonderfully prepared. The Moo Larb was amazing. this is my first time trying it and i am definitely hooked on it. We also had Pork curry with roti, stuffed peppers, Fried Chicken, and Omelette. Definitely recommend this place.

Cute restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating. We were the only diners at 3pm. Vast menu. Excellent food. Quick service. Good value. I’d recommend the pork curry with roti, sticky rice and fried cabbage. Simple but delicious.
Everything we order was super delicious , nicely presented dishes. All taste fresh made. Staff are attentive and sufficient. Will come again to explore more menu items.

One of the local food that I love. Small portions that allow you to try more dishes. I like the menu with photos. It helped you to order easier as some guests may not be familiar with northern food dishes.

A hidden gem for authentic Southern Thai cuisine with breathtaking views and wallet-friendly prices.

Note: the road there is not that great, but there is a resident cat who’ll happily greet you and show off its catwalk - an unexpected little bonus 🐱

This place offers a rewarding experience. While the journey to get there might be a bit of an adventure, the spectacular view is definitely worth the effort. Additionally, the food is reported to be good, making it a well-rounded destination.

Ps. Plenty of parking space.

Restaurant located in a middle of nowhere on a hill overlooking vast flat landscape. Food is comprised of local flavors. We went mostly for seafood, fried fish with turmeric, crab curry, fresh salad with squid and prawns. All what we had was very tasty and fresh. Prices are very reasonable. There’s a lot of car park space.
Delicious and fresh. The complimentary chili paste with fresh vegetables was a great touch. The flavors were well-balanced—not too spicy, just right

I love the food here. I ordered signature dishes, and I really loved them. Price is 150-180 per dish, value for money. Landscape View is also magnificent. Eating food with good view.  I will definitely come back.  Taste=5, view =5, price/value =5.

restaurant_name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
review_text:
Not sure if it is common dish but its the  first time i eaten this. Pork slice & kang kong in coconut milk with chilli spread on top. Strangely there is no single overpowering taste - just slight fragrance from the coconut milk & the chilli is not even spicy. The boss recommends adding the cut green chilli & thats where it all taste so much better with the sourness as it wakes up the tastebuds. The pork slice is tender & the kang kong is crunchy - a single dish with rice.
The one i ordered is big plate 55 baht.
As in pic the total price with satay & coffee 105 baht - very affordable.
PS the noodle stall next door seems very popular with locals & it only has 1 review

restaurant_name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
review_text:
Swimming RAMA : Ancient Food
(Pra ram long song, Blaned pork with peanut sauce and chinese spinash)

restaurant_name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
review_text: Food really delicious i like the beef soup and it’s Michelin restaurant 2014

restaurant_name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
review_text: Amazing tasty Satay!!!! 8 pieces and water cost 48 THB only!

restaurant_name: Khao Phra Ram Long Song Lao Ohw
review_text: Excellent beef noodle soup. The owner is very kind. Recommended!

We’ve bad experience at this restaurant Unbelievable the restaurant is not far from the fish market but they serve their food with Freshless Fish in the Soup tom-som without any tasty.

Big disappointed Driving from bangkok to the restaurant more than hr. to get those kind of low quality.
Please double check your materials every single piece before cooking.

Customers pay you the money by expect the quality on every dish they’ve ordered.

food was great, tastes good and fresh! Service can be improved, we sat in a different area where there were no staff and they did not check in on us aside from serving the food. Fish is big and so were the prawns - but also the two priciest items. I feel that they should have warned us about the size portion. Additionally, they did not inform us about extra charges such as the water, ICE and the AC room - though we did not mind but something for others to keep in mind

The price is very high but very reasonable because ingredients very fresh ,high quality great cooking .

Every dishes I’ve ordered is very delicious.

And eating room like a classic thai gallery.(add on price)

** restaurant used to be win a 1 star michellin in 2019
*** if you don’t read a first page of menu , it might more delicious than you read a rule and warning.

Foods are extremely impressive, especially prawn and crab menus.
Fried prawns with salt is very good, the size of prawns are amazingly huge.
But, the cooking and service are quite slow, it would be nice if booking and making order in advance.
I love all of the food I order; it is very delicious. However, as I arrive, there is a sign that says you need to wait for the food because there are not many waiters. But it is worth it.

This restaurant is local and quite small. However, food was phenomenal. I got Roti with chicken Massaman curry topped with fried egg. They made the fresh Roti right in front of you. It was so tasty. I liked their homemade soy milk. You can adjust the sweetness which I like it about. The price is reasonable.
The service was excellent. I went there with my baby in a stroller. They offered me to sit out front for some breeze. I definitely like to support local food and recommend this place

My friend recommended this store to me and it was a very good recommendation! The service is fast and the food is really good! I ordered the roti and two eggs and the beef curry. The portion of meat in the curry is really generous and the flavor is amazing. It has flavor but it isn’t so spicy. The have fans inside so it doesn’t feel too hot but Sensitive Sallys might complain about the “heat”.
Be sure to try this restaurant during your stay at Phuket Town!

Food is nice, but not exceptional. What’s exceptional in the temperature in the shop. Like a big oven. Besides that, walls and environment is visibly aged. Michelin star but can’t afford air conditioning?

The Michelin rating is annoyingly spot on. Best Massaman curry I've ever had. Roti was perfect, delicious and proper. Beef Curry was also yummy. Prices were very very good considering the PRICE vs. QUALITY ratio.

Do not miss trying this place if you're a foodie. It was raining hard today, so luckily no wait and it was still packed/every seat taken. Don't be afraid to share a table folks!

The roti dough is incredibly fragrant and wonderful.  The chicken curry is transparent and not thick, yet it retains a powerful flavor and aromatic spices.  The shop is small and has a restricted number of seats.  If you go during a busy period, you may have to wait a bit.  Parking near the shop may be difficult to find, but if you walk a little down the adjacent road, there is plenty of parking.

We came the previous night but they didn’t have any tables, so we made a reservation for the following night. The food was not bad, but I wasn’t blown away, especially considering the price and portion size. For example, the “surf and turf” item only had one tempura prawn and a few pieces of steak; it was also not warm. I usually prefer a chopped liver to a parfait, but it said parfait on the menu so I can’t complain. Perhaps we didn’t order their best items on the menu, but we did order two that were from the “Chef’s Recommendations” section. The drinks were yummy though.

Amazing restaurant in the heart of Phuket Old Town. Michelin Guide rated and well deserved!!! Awesome variety of dishes with deep flavors and carefully crafted while plated nicely! Really affordable too considering the quality of ingredients and taste. Several dishes really stood out and will definitely be back!

This is my second time dining at this restaurant, and I have to say it remains one of my favorites in Phuket. However, this time, I was a bit disappointed with the service. The waitress didn’t greet us with a smile and seemed quite rushed, pressuring my girlfriend to order quickly while she was trying to decide by looking at photos on Google Maps.

As for the food, I ordered the tacos, but unfortunately, they were overcooked and had a burnt taste. However, as soon as I pointed it out, the chef immediately prepared a new one, which was absolutely delicious.

Maybe it was just an off day, as my previous experience had been much better. I’ll definitely come back, hoping to find the same warm service and consistent quality that made me fall in love with this place the first time!

The chef here has truly mastered the art of using ingredients wisely, especially in pairing local fruits with meat. One standout example is the seabass with passion fruit—a genius combination that perfectly balances crispy texture, salty richness, acidity, and fat. The menu is full of creative dishes that make dining here an exciting culinary journey. Definitely a must-try if you’re in the area!

We celebrated my birthday here and it was the best meal we had in all of Thailand, which is saying a lot because most of the food we had was incredible.  The steak and the caramelized scallops were cooked perfectly.  The seaweed roe and coconut ice cream was delicious, as it was interesting.  And the Basque cheesecake was divine, even better than the San Sebastián cheesecake a dear friend makes.  (Sorry, Ritter).

Is not a big restaurant but the dishes is delicious 😋 😍..
Is very crowded when I'm there n just have to wait in Q...
There's lots of dishes in the menu n everything looks delicious 😋...
Restaurant is just along the road...the only parking is along the road...

Price is reasonable..
Food is delicious 😋 😍
Their service is fast even when the restaurant is crowded...worth waiting.

My first time here n will sure be back again...

Stir-fried pork with basil is delicious, the basil aroma really stands out.

Crispy fish with tamarind sauce introduces a unique experience to me. The sauce is sweet, sour, and kinda spicy. The fish is crispy.

And for the oyster omelette, I'm not really a fan. The oyster tastes bitter, not sure if it's supposed to be like that. But the orange sauce is delicious, kinda sour and spicy.

Causal eatery with an extensive menu, very fresh ingredients and affordable dishes.

We ordered the kangkung (morning glory vegetables), omelette with oyster and salt pepper prawns. The prawns were superbly fresh and had bits of fried garlic, delicious!

The place was packed, service was a bit slow (only two ladies cooking) but totally worth it!

Stumbled upon this spot and due to how many locals were dining there we decided to give it a try. It was fantastic! The tom yum was incredible! We also ordered crispy pork on garlic and chilies, morning glory, Chinese broccoli,  and two large ICE COLD beers. Coldest beer I’ve had in Thailand thus far. Highly recommend.

It’s where you can find best and authentic Thai dishes, they cook fast, price is affordable, clean and see through cooking zone, all the dishes taste great. Recommended by a local friend and later found they also got Michelin stars.
I was looking around to eat before Wat Kathu and saw this in a blog. Tried their noodle and shrimp in pepper and it was superb! Worth a visit for tourists. Michelin recognized also!

If you're in Phuket and looking for authentic Southern Thai cuisine, Khrua Jongjit is a must-visit. This humble, Michelin-recognized gem (since 2019) serves bold, fierce flavors that locals and foodies rave about.

I tried their dry red curry fried fish (THB 220) – spicy, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. Also had their soup with local vegetables and pineapple (THB 220), a delightful mix of sour, herbal, and sweet notes. Their Hokkien Mee is also legendary. Pro tip: come early – popular dishes like sataw with prawns sell out quickly.

Every dish is cooked to order, so be patient – it’s worth the wait. Lunchtime can get busy, and parking is limited on the narrow street, so plan accordingly.

The restaurant has a cozy, no-frills vibe, perfect for a true local dining experience. Great for foodies and families alike. Highly recommend!

Food is great, very delicious and well deserved for the Michelin, although 4 stars because it’s a bit too salty for my liking and the place closes rather early. The ingredients were all fresh especially the fish (Pla Mong).  We ordered the food ahead of time so the service was super fast. Friendly and accompanied staff.
The kitchen closes at 6:30pm but you can continue to sit and eat till you’re done.

Street parking is not available, you have to park at the Katoo Chinese Temple just around the corner. Plenty of spaces.
The food was great, but it was quite hard to find parking nearby

Visit this place for a discerning Thai gourmet experience. It is no surprise that they have been inducted into the Michelin Hall of Fame. The tamarind prawns, tom yum goong and more importantly fried yellow noodles in gravy are the best I’ve tasted. They have not adopted Michelin prices yet so it’s very affordable.

We discovered this restaurant through the Michelin Guide, and we loved absolutely everything about it! The food was incredibly delicious — every dish was full of flavor, especially the tacos and the Tom Yum. The service was outstanding, making the whole experience truly memorable. The “Bomb Alaska” is amazing!

This was my first time, dining in a luxurious restaurant and we expected it to be amazing, yet the word "amazing" would be an understatement for a such restaurant now.

As a special day, my girlfriend's birthday to be exact, we chose this restaurant as our destination and it went unexpectedly great! The foods, for us, were incredibly good. Plus, the music and atmosphere fitted perfectly for such a occasion. I could say that this was one of the most memorable birthdays for both her and me.

Also, I would love to give special thanks to chefs, musicians and the whole team, especially P'Lily, P'Cha-aim, P'Eye, P'Benz and P'Field, for accomodating us throughout our dinner.

This was such a pleasant find! First off the restaurant surroundings are gorgeous. Place is well lit and service so prompt. The food was great too - my favourite were the tacos and duck salad. They have a pretty decent wine selection too - will be back!

I came for dinner at suay and had a bit of a higher expectation because of the Michelin recs. However, I find the food here mediocre, not bad but not great either, and quite pricey. As someone who grew up in Thailand, I think the food here taste like it’s more catered towards foreigners. I had an okay time there but wouldn’t go back personally.

Perfect dinner get together with family and friends. Food is no doubt amazing with top-tier service by the staff and restaurant owners. Recommend anyone in the area who’s looking for a splendid night out.

Our second time here, and it’s just as amazing as the first. The place is beautifully decorated, the food is outstanding, and the staff are warm and welcoming. They even recommended a full-bodied wine perfectly, just how I like it.

Listed in the Michelin Guide, and they truly deserve it.

Enoteca Bangkok is a real gem! I had a truly wonderful dinner here — the carbonara was outstanding, perfectly creamy and full of flavor, just how it should be. The insalata mista was super fresh and balanced, and the modern tiramisu was a creative twist on a classic — light, elegant, and delicious. The atmosphere is cozy yet refined, and the service was warm and professional. Everything felt well thought out and authentic. I’ll definitely be back!

Wonderful anniversary dinner with my wife.  We had a Oma gaze menu (chef prepares menu for our surprise).  Although it is Italian restaurant, the food is quite French.  But it was a wonderful meal, good wine and exceptional services.  5 stars for me.  One of a great fine dining choice in Bangkok.

reviewer: นิพัฒน์สิน ยิ้มแย้ม
review_text: This is great wine restaurant in Bangkok. Maya’s is great. She is well deserved the “best in class and kindness services” Food is great and the restaurant is very nice, quiet and well organized.
First time in this hidden Italian restaurant in Sukhumvit 31 area, the staffs were all very attentive and friendly, the atmosphere was chill and cozy. The foods were good especially the rock lobster.

✨ Best of the Best Yakitori in Town – Toritama ✨

If you’re looking for the ultimate izakaya experience in Bangkok, Toritama is hands down the place to be. Specializing in chicken, the menu covers everything from the familiar cuts to the rarest parts you won’t easily find elsewhere.

The grill master here is exceptional – every skewer is perfectly grilled over charcoal, juicy and full of flavor. I’ve been to this place several times, and it never fails to impress me.

My personal favorite is the chicken oyster – tender, rich, and simply unforgettable. Pair it with sake, and you’ll see why Toritama is often called the best izakaya in town.

Whether you’re a yakitori enthusiast or just looking for an authentic Japanese dining spot, this is a must-visit.

The best chicken in town. I don’t know how many times I’ve been here and they still have way to impress me. No doubt about their grilling skill. All skewers came perfectly with crips on the outside and juicy in the inside.

You should also try the chicken organs. They are beyoooond! I recommend edge of gizzard, chicken heart, top of heart for the chicken organs. For other parts, go ahead with chicken skin, premium chicken ball, chicken butt or your fav parts. And something I always order to finish my meal: grilled sweet potato, camembert cheese and honey. 10 10 10!
Last but not least, try the pork belly wrapped over rice. Super tasty but you need to order a bit early cuz it takes time.

One of the best yakitori restaurants in Bangkok, quite crowded so recommend making a reservation beforehand. Nothing to say much for the yakitori, I especially like the mentaiko one. The sides like salad and potato salad were excellent and great at cutting out the greasiness.

Would never expected such a high quality Yakitori in Bangkok, and this is recommended by my friend.  This is now on my must-eat restaurant list in Bangkok (BKK).  Most of the dishes i tried were chicken, but i can say that this the Japan-level food that you won't find easily outside of Japan!  I appreciated for the sake sets they offer so i can try different kinds without ordering a whole bottle for one kind (since we only have two people, and we normally have to order a whole bottle of sake in Hong Kong if you dine out).  This is highly recommended if you love Yakitori, the restaurant is nicely decorated, and the service are excellent!  I am coming back next time, so wait me!

Toritama is definitely a yakitori destination in Bangkok, the atmosphere is refined with a formal approach. The Japanese chef is grilling to perfection and the yakitori are like in Japan quality. Service is attentive and friendly. One of the top Japanese izakaya yakitori restaurants in town always packs with Japanese, Thai, and expats customers looking for a great meal.

Food: taste were really nice and delicious. My customers and myself were really enjoy the foods here.

Service: good. Except i ordered black coffee which never came.

Atmosphere: very gorgeous. All decorations made me turn back time to Thai ancient.

Price: worth to pay.

The food was beautifully presented, but it wasn’t anything extraordinary. Don’t get me wrong, it was tasty. But I suppose I expected something that would be more interesting than what I could get from the street. Nothing really impressed me.

If you’re after aesthetically pleasing dishes, this could be very enjoyable for you! However, I wanted more flavour and wow-factor. Especially as this has a Michelin Bib, my expectations may have been too high.

This restaurant serves authentic Thai food. The service began with mango and dipping sauce as starters, and within 10 to 15 minutes, all of our dishes were served. The staff were polite.

They took special care with each dish, enhancing the presentation with beautiful plating and artistic fruit and vegetable carvings.

The food tasted excellent, with flavors that were balanced, not overwhelmingly spicy or sour.

Some desserts must be ordered one day in advance.

One of the best meals I’ve had in Chiang Mai

This place is hands down the best restaurant I’ve been to in Chiang Mai. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavour. You can tell a lot of attention went into the cooking and the plating.

The standout dishes for me were the fried sea bass—crispy on the outside, tender inside, and paired with a punchy dipping sauce—and the red curry, which was rich, aromatic, and packed with ingredients.

The other dishes were also great—from the appetisers to the desserts. Everything felt authentic and well-balanced. Also loved the atmosphere—calm, classy, and perfect for a relaxed lunch or dinner.

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a solid Thai dining experience in Chiang Mai.

This is a must Thai restaurant you have to visit once if you are in Chiang Mai. The original taste and the masterpiece of each dish as we as Thai dessert that you can’t find easily now’s a day. Recommended to book in advance.

The staff was friendly and the food was good. If you order spicy, be ready, it really is spicy! If you’re not sure, better go with “not spicy” and add the heat yourself. You’ll usually get fresh chilies on the side, or just ask for them.

The view is absolutely stunning! Perfect spot to snap a few nice photos, with or without the swing.

Even though the restaurant was pretty busy, the food came out quickly.

It’s right by the road, with a beautiful view of the sea.
Great location with great view and service. The food is quite good but did not exactly meet my Michelin Guide expectation. Overall had a good dinner.

Despite the Michelin guide, the food was mid at best. We tried the pineapple fried rice paired with their signature Michelin omelet. The rice was just okay and had a mild flavor, and the omelet was very oily from being deep-fried. That’s to be expected, but I didn’t anticipate that much oil fitting into such a small space. The taste was alright to me, but my friend said it was just average.

Been here a few times over the years. I think this is a must visit Thai cuisine when you are in Samui. Reasonable price and delicious. My fav homemade prawn cakes, definitely not supermarket frozen ones.
Beautiful beach. Thank you for great service too. 🙏🏼

For a Michelin guided restaurant I was disappointed with the food. Ordered the beef massaman curry and don't believe the beef was actually beef. The pad see ew and pineapple fried rice was not bad, but have had better. Service was also quite unfriendly. The best part was the view.

The best fish wonton I’ve had so far since I was young.  Glad to see they maintain its standard and quality for decades.  Not only do I like the fish wonton, but the noodles were perfect also; the texture was right to me.  The bowl size was quite small.  If you are hungry, I believe you must order at least 2 bowls😁

Absolutely delicious- had 7 different noodle dishes (dry and soup style). Always very challenging to find quality noodles such as Keo Pla but when one finds a food establishment like this, it is worth the effort and time.

Food has to be flavoured yourself. The attention to the customers are top notch. I got a table quickly and the food came out quickly. Also cup of ice was quick. I was asked if I needed help three times. Felt like they really took care of their customers. I ordered the rice noodles with fish dumplings in a clear broth as I was told this is the least chili. Overall a good experience
First visit here because it's near our hotel in the heart of the city, delicious, nice soup and good service. Friendly atmosphere. Will come back.

The best noodle i tried in surat. The fish cake and wonton fish is home made. Their noodle is common here in southern region which is very hard to come by in bangkok.
Best! Roi Jang Hu !

Solo dining. I came prepared to wait, decided to try my luck when I realised my hotel was within walking distance!
Arrived at 11am- waited 40min, the crowd control was not bad. One staff took down initials, pax, and constantly updated on waiting time. When I asked about timing for takeaway, he also advised on waiting time (Grab is super popular also).
In the end, I over-ordered , hahaha, to make up for the waiting time.
Fried rice wok hei is good- with clumps of crab. Omelette is a flat one, with the crab placed on top- I haven’t had a chance to try Jay Fai yet, so I don’t know how it compares. But other places do it in a more fluffy omelette style. Had one river prawn— they only had the “smallest” size in stock, but it’s huge!!  And coconut water. Left most of the rice behind, and enjoyed the crab.

I think, worth a visit; I am quite happy with this, and will try again in future visits- other items that I haven’t tried yet!

Queue is definite if u want to dine here. Reason is it's super famous & also because the shop is quite small. If u go in a big group then it's quite troublesome to get a table unless you're willing to seperate. The waiting time for food to be served is also quite long. Service from staffs are really good. Though very busy, each of them are still full of manners & very attentive. Thumbs up to the team. The food is delicious & seafood is fresh. You can tastes the sweetness of the meat. The crabmeat is in big chunks & it's very succulent. The fried rice is full of wok hei as well. The king of this meal has to be the mantis prawn. It's really good, very fragrant & the best part is it's fully peeled. The crabmeat omelette is on average. The seafood sauce that goes with it is also very appetizing. Price is also very reasonable. A satisfying meal.

Here Hai in Bangkok is a great spot for crab lovers. They are very generous with the crab meat in their dishes, and the flavour of the crab is seafood sweet and savoury. We tried the signature crab fried rice, but it was a bit disappointing. Even with the plentiful crab meat, the rice was overcooked and had some charred bits that affected the taste. The egg omelette was decent, mainly because of the generous crab meat, but it was not especially memorable on its own.
The mantis prawn is overcooked also to the point it is chewy.

The service, however, was excellent. Staff were attentive, and the food arrived very quickly. Prices are very reasonable considering the amount of crab meat given. Overall, it’s a good place if you want a satisfying crab fix.

A must go everytime we are in BKK. Hands down the best crab fried rice in BKK. Be prepared to wait though..the open at 10am and queue starts forming around 930am..but, definitely worth the wait. If your spice tolerance is high, go for the crab curry. Its amazing. Mantis shrimp in garlic, crab omelette are all must orders..

I finally made it to Here Hai in Bangkok! You know, that place that's always got a crazy line and is famous for crab? 😅

I’d tried a couple times on my last trip but gave up because the wait was just too long. This time, I was like—okay, I’m just gonna go and wait no matter what.

Got there around 11 on a Saturday morning, and yeah… it was already packed. Mostly people from China, Singapore, and Malaysia—this place is seriously popular with tourists.

We ordered a bunch of the recommended dishes. Most were really good! But the gapao shrimp… wow. So spicy I could barely handle it 🥵 Still tasted amazing though!

They’ve got things pretty streamlined here—like the coconut juice comes in pre-filled bottles, and they peel all the shrimp for you before serving. I get it—they’re super busy and it helps them serve more people. But kinda makes it feel a bit less authentic, you know?

Anyway, glad I finally tried it. Worth the wait? Yeah, I’d say so—just come early or be ready to queue! 🦀

Very upset and food is very ordinary. All fried onion on the topping are very overcooked and after I advise them they said they just would told the cooking department. I won’t be back due to the taste and attitude of staff. Moo Yor deep fried is worse ever found in Udon.

This popular Vietnamese restaurant, a go-to for both locals and visitors, has earned significant acclaim, including Michelin stars in 2023, 2024, and 2025. It's the ultimate destination for authentic Vietnamese food. ($$$$)
Fast service and a very good menu with great local and Vietnamese dishes. Everything we ordered tasted great

Kao Piak Sien is my absolute go-to spot in Udon Thani for authentic Vietnamese food! I’ve been here several times, worked my way through most of the menu, and I can confidently say every single dish has been superb. The flavors are rich and vibrant, and the freshness of the ingredients really shines through in every bite.

The staff are always attentive and super friendly, making the whole experience even better. They’ve clearly put a lot of effort into the interior design too—it’s cozy and beautifully done, with a charming spiral staircase that adds a unique touch to the atmosphere.

And it doesn’t stop there! They also have a variety of snacks for sale, which are perfect for bringing a taste of the restaurant home with you. Whether you’re new to Vietnamese cuisine or a longtime fan, Kao Piak Sien is a must-visit. I can’t recommend it enough!

This is a must-try breakfast spot if you’re visiting Udon Thani. The menu offers a wide variety of options. While the prices might be a bit on the higher side, every dish is absolutely delicious.

The ambiance and decor are excellent, with a cozy café-style vibe. The staff provides outstanding service, and the food is served promptly. Highly recommended!

Local brand of Chinese noodle style with the crispy pork is very dilicious. The restaurant available for dine in, but no have air conditioning. The prices is very friendly, you will paid around 50 bath per menu. Today I had to eat pad -se-ew (Stir Fried Soy Sauce).

- Special menu was delicious !
- Noodle with beef in gravy sauce was quite salty
one of the best noodle place in khon kaen. must visit.
Serves great egg noodles. Reasonable price.

I used to go here at least twice a month and alway had the pad see ew (apologies for the spelling but this is what I say when I order it), it is a really good dish of noodles and pork. The place is usually busy at lunchtime even though they have a relatively small menu. Try it out, I don't think you will regret it.
If you wanna try original thai taste, here is the place!!!
Visitors must give this restaurant a try. I like its babeque chicken, papaya salad, and Thai black coffee. All authentic issan food.

reviewer: Pureephat “ลุงป๋อง วันนี้กินอะไร” Wangpaiboonkit
review_text:
Nice crispy skin bbq chicken, should finish it quick hence the skin was not crispy once it cooled down
Other dishes was okay

For years this place has had the reputation of making the best gai yang (North Eastern style barbecue chicken). I've certainly never tasted better but there might be one or two places that are nearly equal. Gai yang can run out at lunch time.

Their other Isan food - somtam, laab (including duck), sausage and sticky rice are just as good so you won't be disappointed if you have missed the chicken that day. The chicken is a Thai breed skinny bird. The Roadrunner, not Foghorn Leghorn 😂

It's the usual sitting on stools, open walls, drink water, low prices type place but with all food I've tried being memorably delicious. I come here every time I visit Khon Kaen and I suggest you do too.

Very tasty roasted chicken. We ordered one plate and couldn't get enough of it. Ended up ordering another plate. Charred on the outside, juicy and tender on the inside. Price as of May 2018 is 160 baht per plate. There are washing basins in the shop.

Nice Thai food. Good price , good taste and quite clean. Famous for its roasted chicken (as the restaurant name stated). Papaya salad with salted egg, rosted pork neck, fried pork are also recommended. Soup is average. Overall if you come by, give it a try!
The food is delicious, served very quickly, and the service is good.😍
One of the best kai-yang(chicken barbecue) in Thailand. Good e-san food.
Local Korat foods, recommend to order Pad-Mi-Korat and Grilled chicken

Always the best North-Eastern Thai foods in Nakhon Ratchasima. I have been know this restaurant since I was 5 years old and they still serve the best tasty foods to the customers. Love the Flammable Grilled Chicken, Papaya Salad with Fermented Fish, and Namtok Pork. Nice place to bring your colleagues or your whole family to spend the time in this restaurant together.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Such a beautiful experience! 🌿
Jaras is truly amazing, the food is absolutely delicious, and you can really taste that everything is homemade with top-quality ingredients. Every dish is crafted with so much care and passion.

I love that everything is eco-friendly and sustainable, you can feel the respect for nature in every detail.
The staff is super friendly and attentive, and the place itself is gorgeous, cozy, and full of great vibes.

A really special spot where you eat wonderfully and feel genuinely cared for. Huge compliments to the whole Jaras team!!

We visited on a Tuesday night for the 9-course tasting menu dinner along with the wine pairing option.

The food was INCREDIBLE. The flavours were bold yet balanced. Very creative dishes with clever use of local ingredients. All dishes were well executed with every component of the dish coming together harmoniously.

We enjoyed every single dish and the carefully curated wines were a nice touch. Most of the wines were meticulously sourced from less common countries and vineyards which left us pleasantly surprised.

Special shout out to Cake and Golfrey for the amazing hospitality and service. They were so passionate in presenting the dishes with a personal touch on sharing more about the local Phuket culture and cuisine. I hope Jaras continues to maintain this personal touch and authenticity even as they continue to earn more Michelin stars!

We look forward to visiting again when we're back in Phuket! I highly recommend a visit before they get too popular!

This is one of the restaurants I had really been looking forward to visiting.
I recently had the chance to enjoy a dinner at Jaras Restaurant, which features a very interesting concept—creating dishes using sustainable ingredients.
The food was delicious, and the service was excellent.
My favorite dish was the goat curry—the meat was tender, young, and had no strong odor at all.
Highly recommended!

Jaras needs no introduction — every InterContinental guest who’s stayed here has likely tried it at least once. During afternoon, they serve a mix of traditional and modern Thai cuisine. Come evening, the tasting menu takes the spotlight — my personal recommendation. The chefs get creative with spices and flavours, and they consistently get it right.

Recommended dish:
Crow Yok - Braised pork belly with its skin lightly seared—just enough to create a delicate crispness that contrasts with the silky layers of fat and meat beneath
Organic Pad Pak Miang Goong Seab(a Phuket wild vegetable and the combination of frying it with crispy garlic and small shrimps - ultimate flavour)

An unforgettable dining experience!
Everything was truly delicious, the atmosphere elegant and beautiful and the service absolutely perfect.
Our waitress in particular was so attentive and kind, she really took great care of us.
A place I would definitely recommend for anyone looking for a refined and memorable evening.
Masterpiece of southern Thai cuisine, flavours and spice like I’ve never experienced. A unique dining experience and made to feel so welcome. Highly recommend especially the tumeric fried fish.

Luang Ten restaurant is rare diamond in the jungle!! This is our second time here. This time we drove from Phuket just to have dinner. The ingredients are fresh and flavorful. The price is cheap and reasonable compared to ingredients. Would definitely come back !!!

Luang Ten – My All-Time Favorite Southern Thai Restaurant in Khao Lak

Every time I visit Khao Lak, one place I always come back to is Luang Ten. It’s been my favorite since my very first trip here, and over the years, it has never once disappointed me. No surprise that it’s been awarded the Michelin Guide for 5 consecutive years – the flavors are still as authentic and delicious as ever.

Just thinking about the food makes my mouth water. My all-time favorite dishes include:
•	Fermented Shrimp Paste in Southern-style Fish Kidney Curry (Nam Keuy Gaeng Tai Pla) – Rich, salty, and packed with flavor. The aroma of real fermented shrimp paste is unforgettable, and the dish is loaded with ingredients and local veggies.
•	Southern-style Curry with Hed Krang Mushrooms (Gaeng Kua Hed Krang) – Bold, aromatic curry with a spicy kick. The wild mushrooms add a nice chewy texture, making it truly addictive.
•	Sour Curry with Seabass (Gaeng Som Pla Krapong) – Spicy, tangy, and refreshing with super fresh fish. A classic southern curry done perfectly.

The atmosphere is warm and welcoming – no frills, just real home-style cooking made with love. It feels like a meal cooked by someone who truly wants to feed you well.

Luang Ten is not just a restaurant – it’s a taste of home. Missing it already and can’t wait to go back again!

The food was great, especially the stir-fried Malindjo leaves with egg and the stir-fried squid in black ink sauce.
We waited around 30-40 minutes for a table as it was very busy, but the friendly service and delicious food more than made up for it.

Me and my two girlfriends recently had dinner at Kru-Luang-Ten, and it was such a great experience. The restaurant serves authentic Southern Thai food with bold, spicy flavors that truly reflect the region. Every dish came out quickly, the ingredients were fresh, and the prices were very reasonable.

If you’re looking for real Southern Thai food that’s both flavorful and affordable, Kru-Luang-Ten is totally worth checking out. Highly recommended!

😘Worth the 45-min drive if you’re into comforting Thai-Chinese flavors
This spot leans into the lighter side of Thai food — not too spicy, not overly seasoned (ไม่จัดจ้าน) — just simple, clean flavors that feel like a home-cooked meal from your grandparents’ kitchen.
If bold, intense Thai flavors are your go-to, this might feel a bit mild. But if you’re in the mood for something warm, familiar, and nostalgic, this place hits the mark.
The vibe also gives off old-school family gatherings — think Grandma and Grandpa cooking up something special just for the grandkids. It’s humble, cozy, and kind of heartwarming.
Perfect for when you want food that feels like a gentle hug.
Definitely love this place. All dishes are yummy! The price is right and reasonable. Totally worth it to have a wonderful meal here.

Expect to wait at least an hour and a half, and on some days, the food sells out by 1 pm. To make the most of your time, it’s a good idea to order everything at once, then take a leisurely walk around the old market while you wait—don’t miss the grilled sticky rice there.

The wait is well worth it, with standout dishes like the deep-fried pork roll (หมูจ๊อ) and sizzling stir-fried featherback fish with chili (ผัดขี้เมาปลากราย). The food is quite spicy, and some dishes can't be toned down, so be sure to order something milder to balance the heat.

For parking, you can either park across the street and walk over the canal or park near the restaurant for just 20 baht.

I went there by myself shortly after the restaurant opened, and to my surprise, it was already quite crowded. Fortunately, I managed to get a table. I ordered the sun-dried fried snakehead fish and the stir-fried spicy fish paste with herbs, finishing off my meal with lod chong (pandan jelly in sweet coconut milk). It was a truly enjoyable meal.
Hidden gem in Rahaeng market. Homecooking style restaurant, the food was great. Dont forget to order their recommend menu. Accept cash or bank transfer only. Come before lunchtime to aware crowded.
A much better version of Gai Yang in kow soun klang compared to the korat version. I personally felt the grilled chicken here are crispy and yet juicy in the inside.
Best chicken in Thailand

reviewer: OTAN ทําแล้วดี
review_text: Incorrect information. This is the Khao Suan Kwang District Agricultural Office, not Wanna Grilled Chicken Shop.
It's delicious.

reviewer: สายชล สวงสิน
review_text: Dew

One of the nicest roasted pork in the area. Very crispy skin and the meat isn’t too fatty. The noodle soup is also really good and the intestines are very soft without the heavy porky smell. The orange juice they serve is also very refreshing and pulpy. Staff are attentive and helpful. Worth traveling here to try the food.

I had such a great experience at Mr. Joe Kuay Jab. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the service was quick despite how busy it was. The kuay jab was outstanding – flavorful, comforting, and packed with delicious ingredients. The crispy pork was a real highlight, perfectly cooked and very satisfying. The place has a lively, local atmosphere that makes the meal even more enjoyable. Definitely worth a visit and I’ll be coming back for sure!

Delicious meal! 🍜 The noodle soup with wide rice noodles and slices of crispy pork belly (Moo Krob) looks comforting and flavorful. The separate side of crispy pork belly confirms its quality—tender meat with a perfect crunchy skin.

Kuay chap, a dish with teochew origins combines flat rice noodles with variations of broth. The usual protein served will be some variation of a pork part.

Kuay Jab Joe offers a clear peppery broth option. The types of protein served comprises of some pork belly and multiple variation of pork offals.

The pork belly dish offered was surprisingly good with the skin being extremely crispy.

Overall would highly recommend the dish.

Walking in without having the fear of menu anxiety. There is only 1 main menu, pork meat & innard soup with rolled rice noodle (kway jab) or rice. The roast pork is a must try.
Soup is peppery hot paired perfectly with condiment (chilli vinegar). This is way more peppery than singaporean bakkutteh. It helps neutralize the innard smells.

Amazing place from the Michelin Guide. Super local; our waitress didn’t know much English and we communicated with her using Google Translate, but nonetheless she was amazing and very service-oriented.
Amazing food. A lot of local staples, such as river-snail curry and crabs. I got the horseshoe crab curry and the shrimp paste fried rice, which were both amazing and really well-sized.
The flavors are amazing, very deep and multi-layered.
Not many vegetarian options here, but this place is authentic and that’s the experience you should aim for.
Prices are very fair, with the most expensive dishes costing between 20–30฿ whole most classics (Phad Thai, salads) cost around 9฿.

We ordered raw crab salad and it was off! Bitter bean stir fried with shrimp paste also doesnt taste authentic as well. Maybe this place targeted foreigners. The deep fried fish was yum though. Will never come back for sure.

I have no idea how many times I come to this restaurant, only I know that all foods are super yummy, fresh, and good quality.

The most thing I like when come to any southern restaurant is the fresh local veggie served as complementary.  (Southern food is spicy!!)
Good food. Fresh ingredients. Super hospitality service by young at heart ladies. Love this place.
Food was great everything tasted fresh, staff was very kind

Had a fantastic dining experience. The restaurant is located by the pool, offering a relaxing atmosphere. I ordered a light dinner. The food was delicious and well-presented. The staff were very friendly and attentive, making the evening even more enjoyable. Would definitely come back again!

We always come here when we are in Khao Lak, every time has been nothing short of magnificent. It’s the perfect spot for an amazing night. Every meal, dessert, and drink we have ordered has been absolutely delectable and consistently prepared to a very high standard.
Our go to favourites are the cold cut & cheese board, the Andaman lobster bisque, and the Devasom citrus salad - all must-tries.
The sea breeze and the stunning view truly elevate the entire experience.
P’Tommy and her team are always welcoming and great you with a smile which makes the visit even more special ❤️

This place is above of gorgeous and high quality , Great food with a super nice service and helpful staffs specially Kh. Tommy she’s so nice. We had a great dinner time here. Strongly recommend and we will come back for sure

We had several Happy Hour drinks and meals at the Devasom Beach Grill &Bar during our stay and it was great. Beautifully located overlooking the main Resort pool and the beach allowing us to view some stunning sunsets. Tommy and her team provided excellent customer service and were always welcoming and had a very positive approach to guests. A special thanks to Pui who really looked after us on every visit. Got to see the Fire Dance performance on 3 nights which was fabulous.

Fantastic food and brilliant service.
We had fantastic meals here and would recommend to everyone. Steak was wonderful, as was the rest.

Beautiful Khun Pui looked after us every single time with a big smile 😁 We won’t forget her hospitality! 🥰🥰

Khun Bao also amazed us with his skills, including the fire show! Thank you so much for everything!  🫵🏾🫵🏾

We will see them all the next time we come back (hopefully very very soon!)

I haven’t visited this place in a long time—probably not in the past few years. The food was good and met the usual delicious standard, but somehow I felt that I’ve had better dishes here before compared to this visit. Don’t get me wrong—this place is still one I recommend if you’re around the Khao Lak / Takuapa area. The deep-fried soft-shell crab with garlic was really tasty. Most importantly, this is a cheap/affordable meal for you.
Definitely worth the drive and Michelin Guide listing. The tamarind prawns, glass noodle prawns and fried soft shell crab were very good.

We have been there twice during the stay. They won Michelin stars many years, which i think they deserved it. We like all the food. The portion is good with reasonable prices. คั่วกลิ้ง and shrimp donuts are a must try, but actually you can order anything there and would hardly be disappointed.
Chuchee Pla dish (hot and good thai southern taste) after i ate , i saw Michelin star OMG! Worth to come

Amazing food—don’t miss the signature soft-shell crab or mushroom larb. The only problems with this restaurant is that its success allows it to close from time to time without warning. So if you plan to visit, consider calling ahead to make sure it’ll be open. It’s worth the trip!

Khao serves authentic Thai flavors with a modern touch. Every dish is beautifully presented and full of rich, balanced taste—spicy, sour, sweet, and savory just right. The ingredients are fresh, and you can really feel the care in the cooking.

The atmosphere is elegant and the service is friendly and attentive. Perfect place to experience real Thai cuisine in a comfortable setting.

I’ve been in Thailand for over 14 years and traveled all over the country, but KHAO (Ekkamai) truly brings together the best flavors from North, South, and Central Thailand — every dish is outstanding! The crab meat with curry powder, crab omelette, fried noodles with shrimp, and beef green curry were all cooked to perfection. Prices are very reasonable, and they have a great wine list that’s not overpriced. The staff are friendly, funny, and speak good English — their service really makes the evening special. Simple yet elegant décor with a great ambience. Honestly, one of the best Thai restaurants I’ve ever been to in Thailand. Highly recommended!

We went there to celebrate our first wedding anniversary. It is a Michelin star rated restaurant and from the moment you get inside, you can feel the warmth welcome and greetings of the place.
We ordered salad, shrimps and cooked squid.
The food was great but we weren't used to some of the tastes especially the salad.
After we finished, they offered us some sweets to celebrate our anniversary.
The waiters and staff were all nice and smiling all the time.
Prices are expensive, but considering this is a Michelin rated restaurant, it is well priced.
Ideal for a group gathering or special occasion.

The restaurant, awarded with a Michelin star for several consecutive years, exudes an ambiance reminiscent of a modern fine dining Thai restaurant. The food is delightful, the chilli with vegetables presented attractively and bursting with flavor. However, must mention that the chilli itself lacks the desired spiciness.

The stir-fried eggplants are tasty but not spicy. On the other hand, the crab curry is the standout dish, bursting with spiciness and deliciousness. It elevates the overall dining experience.

While the prices are quite high compared to the standard Thai food in Thailand, the service is friendly and attentive.

Although being a Michelin-starred restaurant doesn’t necessarily translate to a superior dining experience compared to other Thai restaurants in Bangkok, this place is definitely worth trying.

I arrived just before the second round of service, around 5:15 PM. The staff were still in a briefing, which is totally understandable, but it felt a bit uncomfortable because the manager was giving them a rather firm talk right in front of customers. One thing that stood out was when they told the staff to try and get more order from guests since it’s holiday— that felt a bit off to hear before even being seated.

Despite that, we decided to stay, expecting good food and service, especially from a place with a Michelin star.

Sadly, the food didn’t really live up to the hype. We ordered around 10 dishes, but none of them really impressed us. Tom Yum Kung was bland. The fish wontons didn’t have much flavor, and the crab omelet felt overpriced and underwhelming.

Service-wise, I could sense the mood of the staff wasn’t great — probably because of how the briefing went earlier. It was hard to get anyone’s attention, and no one seemed very responsive when we tried to call. The staff at the bar were actually the most helpful ones, so big thanks to them.

This is just my honest opinion. I understand everyone’s experience can be different, and I don’t mean to be harsh. Hopefully, this feedback helps improve things moving forward.

A Thai restaurant with southern Thai cuisine, a wide variety of seafood and other large and beautiful dishes, and unique flavors that really cannot be found in other restaurants.
