The restaurant received a Michelin star, but I don't care about that. I ate several dishes and most of them were very delicious. Each dish comes with a different flavor and a different color. The service is great and fast and the style of the place is very pastoral. Beautiful buildings made of straw and wood that sit on the shore of the lake/sea. The place is very spacious and large. I highly recommend the chicken cashew dish and the shrimp curry dish, a unique flavor👌

Tucked away from the touristy spots, this very local restaurant serves dishes you’ve probably never tried before—authentic, unique, and absolutely delicious. 🍲 The service is simple but genuine, making you feel right at home. What makes it extra special is that it has been recognized by the Michelin Guide for many years, a true stamp of quality. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ If you’re in Phuket, this is definitely a place worth adding to your food list!

The local restaurant located near mangrove forest. There are many local foods and price is reasonable. The ingredients are very fresh. I like the squid in black ink and the shrimps fried with lemon grass.

Eat like a local: An authentic Southern Cuisine in Phuket

Tucked away in a mangrove-lined canal, Mor Mu Dong is one of those local gems that feels like a well-kept secret. The open-air wooden pavilions and rustic surroundings set the tone for a laid-back, no-frills meal, but the food is what truly shines.

The menu is extensive, with a focus on Southern Thai dishes that pack a punch in flavor. Highlights from our meal included the stir-fried sataw with shrimp (spicy, funky, and addictive), grilled fish wrapped in pandan leaves, and the signature braised pork belly in soy sauce. Everything came out hot, fast, and generously portioned.

Service was brisk and friendly, though not overly attentive, but that’s part of the charm here. It’s the kind of place where locals gather, seafood is the star, and prices remain refreshingly reasonable for the quality and setting.

Pros:
- Authentic Southern Thai flavors
- Beautiful, natural setting with private wooden huts
- Great value for money
- Ideal for sharing a feast with friends or family

Cons:
- A bit off the beaten path, best to come with a car or hire a local driver
- Not ideal for those who prefer air-conditioning or modern comforts

If you’re in Phuket and want to eat like a local, Mor Mu Dong is well worth the detour. Come hungry, come curious, and be ready for some bold flavors.

Came here after getting an accident makes the food 1000x better 😆😂

What we ordered:
1) Gaeng Som (spicy stew with fish) - super duper good. If you want to taste authentic soup from Southern, order this. But! It’s spicy hehe

2) Fried rice Phuket (?) - one of the dish that exceed my expectations cus usually fried rice in Thailand isn’t that good😭 BUT this one is soo good. Recommended to order!

3) Squid stir fried with ink - this dish never go wrong. It doesn’t taste fishy and they give quite a lot of squid!

4) Stir fried melinjo leave with egg - ordered this so we have some veggie as side dish. It’s so good to pair this with the fried rice and squid!

5) ปลายัดไส้ / stuffed fish - I didn’t expect for me to like this dish. It taste good, well balanced herbs, not too strong. 1 of them is 90/100 baht.

Oh, they also give you sour mango and sweet sauce to help you snacking while waiting for the food :’)

Overall, I finally found my favorite Thai Seafood restaurant in Phuket. Will come back kaa🫶🏼👍🏼
So simple but so good! This Michelin rated fish ball soup is a must try. The fish balls were so soft and light. Super toddler friendly food as well!

Came here to try the famous fish ball soup. It was truly amazing. A real authentic experience! Pro tip: get your drinks from the 7-eleven across the street before coming here as they don’t serve drinks

Michelin star restaurant that serves fish maw soup. Came here just because of this but I wasn't impressed, my mom makes the same soup so she probably could open a restaurant also. I think the price was 70Baht for a bowl so not too expensive. Very busy restaurant and nice Thai atmosphere. For me it was too long to walk for the food. Definitely not bad just not sure about the hype.

Absolutely loved Lim Lao Ngow Noodles! Everything was so fresh, especially the fishball, which was incredibly bouncy and flavorful (now I get why it’s called jumping noodles!). The soup was rich and delicious. Can’t wait to come back for more!

Came in with high hopes, but the noodles underwhelmed me. I ordered the most traditional noodles without soup. While, it the condiments adds a pop of flavor, the noodles itself doesn’t have much flavor. It is not bad, but have had much better noodle dishes.

Cheap and delicious hole in the wall serving pad Thai and fried seafood dishes including the "otao" their store is named after, a delicious regional take on hoi tod infused with taro paste. They deep fry the fried orders one plate at a time, so be prepared for a wait if they are busy.

It’s in between 3-4 starts however my plate of O tao oyster was served not very hot and the oysters were cold. After adding the fresh beansprouts it was even colder, on top of that the big fans were blowing on the tables which made the food turn cold even quicker.
Taste was very good and texture was spot on however it lacks omph, presentation could have been better, i noticed there wasn’t any banana leave lining the plate and there’s no coriander topping. Banana leave can also keep the food warm longer. These could greatly affect the taste, smell and presentation to the dish.
The price is cheap at ฿80.

Otherworldly pad Thai.

Found this gem on the Michelin guide while looking for street food type stalls. It’s a little rustic local spot that has a small menu.

Communication is done through pointing at pictures to order but there is no need for anything else really!

The pad Thai was amazing, would recommend the seafood option. Prices were also ridiculously low - around 60THB for a pad Thai.

Epic!

Disappointment! I had their special fried oysters and it was literally one of the worst street foods I had in Thailand. Staff was nice, prices are fair but food is just bad. I'm not even sure what was in my plate. I only had one dish so maybe something else is better but I wouldn't try anything else.

reviewer: Garry Lew Your Estate Advisory Realtor
review_text:
Visited 12 June 2025 Clear Sky Thursday Evening. The following sharing are based on our unbiased personal opinion and experience

Order a takeaway to try. My humble review after trying it out. Oyster are slightly smaller in size and not fried to crispy. Yam 🍠 is generous almost like eating yam cake instead of fried oyster.

Diff flavor from where we came from. But not bad eat as if eating yum cake.

Follow us for a gastronomic experience and discover the world finest in its purest form

My wife and I went to try this restaurant out since I am a foodie and a cook.  The food was no point!  We order three items and some drink.  The fried king mushrooms  were delicious and not so oily, we also had the chicken curry with roti.  The chick and potato was so soft and tender that it broke apart with just the touch of your fork or spoon. The Roti was light and airy not so oily. We also had fresh veggies with a tomato paste and minced pork. My wife had a brown rice smoothie drink and I had a pineapple strawberry mint detox drink. The final bill was also great we spent about 950 baht for the whole meal and drinks.  We will definitely be back and encourage others to try it out.  They have won Michelin stars every year since 2021 .

The food taste good, it's Michelin winner past few years. We love the hung lay, pot of healthy color rice, fried cows lip veg.
Tips: They have air con room away from mosquitoes bite, only 6 tables available so call to reserve in advance for dinner.
This restsurant is amazing. The setting is beautiful with the trees, lights, water etc. Seating outside and also small inside area with AC. Food, service and presentation was lovely.

After a less-than-perfect first visit last year, we decided to give Meena Rice a second chance, inspired by Mark Wiens’ YouTube review. While the food has its highlights, our experience left us feeling mixed.

The restaurant is located a bit far from central Chiang Mai, so it’s a good idea to arrange transportation both ways to avoid long waits for a driver. On both visits—once during a busy time and this time arriving before 11:00 AM—the service was consistently slow. It seems the staff lacks coordination or clear procedures for managing tables, which can be frustrating. Additionally, most of the staff do not speak English, so it feels like the restaurant caters more to local clientele.

That said, the atmosphere is undeniably charming, with a jungle-style setup and an old wooden deck that’s perfect for a relaxed meal. The food itself is decent—flavors are tasty, and the exotic raw veggies add a fun touch. The colorful triangle rice is a unique and cute feature, and their herbal drinks are refreshing. However, availability of dishes can be hit or miss, which might leave you adjusting your expectations.

Should we give it a third try? We’re unsure, but it’s worth visiting at least once to enjoy the lovely setting and unique offerings. If they can improve their service, it could become a much more enjoyable experience.
A very unique restaurant with a quiet n peaceful ambience. The food was good n the prices are reasonable. Service was great.

We specifically went to this place because of the reviews and michelin guide. We were both, disappointed, we actually tried 3 diff noodle meals and one fried rice. I don’t think there’s something extraordinary with the food. I was expecting this is one of those gold finds. But we were mostly disappointed, this is for sure subjective. But twasn’t a place I would recommend for anyone. In any case, for its price, twas an okay meal. No love lost as we didn’t spend a heaps.
moderately-priced phuket-style hokkien noodles. unpretentious and casual. hyped by some reviewers, but actually quite mid. definitely not vegan or vegetarian on average days.

Great fried rice and tasty hokkien noodles.

Loved the smokiness of the wok in the dishes! Should try it out if youre in the area.

Got simple, but tasty fried rice with shrimp, curry shrimp rice, 2 black ice tea.
Paid 200 of total. Very humble place with tasty food. Produce is very good guiltily.

It’s a typical shop where good food is the priority. Ambience and layout is irrelevant. We ordered a dry Noodle and a dry Vermicelli.  It’s tasty and flavourful.  For THB180 for 2 noodles and 2 ice tea, you can’t ask for more , and very happy to have a meal there.

This is Phuket life’s simple food at its best.

It’s kind of 🇻🇳 mix Thai!
I especially recommend Nam-cook (which is orange one) very good taste! And you can have fresh vegetables as many as you can. It’s self-service.

Phor also good as well! even the temperature is hot but we still want to have for this restaurant lol
Loved it. Free veggies and a nice vietnamese lunch spot.

At first I was confused. The restaurant was nearby. Accommodation not more than 200 meters. Press search to see a summary of famous restaurants. So I thought I had to go try it one more time. Summary of the review Anyone who comes to Khon Kaen should not miss it. Famous restaurants at Khob Kaen

Almost missed out this place. A very well-done Pho soup that will warm your rainy morning right up. The soup is a good beefy stock intensity that’s not at all fatty, but hits all the right spot. The grilled chili and shrimp paste makes the soup even better, so do try if you’re good with seafood and spices. The side vegetable, ice, and still water are self-service, but the place also offers Vietnamese coffee that you’ll want to try. Oh, and the fried spring rolls are also excellent. Pricing is very fair, too. Highly recommend this place for local breakfast fares.

This is another nice Vietnamese restaurant I know for many years. Here Vietnamese style soup, Vietnamese sausage and springrolls are my favourite. The original restaurant used to be on the other side of the road some 100m away but has since moved to a newer location. When in Khon Kaen looking for a good lunch this is a place to go.

The location is easy to find and there are plenty parking spots inside but the driver got to be careful when entering and exiting to the parking due to only one lane. This is an open-air restaurant and there are a different kinds of curry for rice noodles. Papaya salad is very good as well. Finally, the price is reasonable

Food seems to contain a lot of salt. Feel so thirsty after the meal. Quite ok fried chicken, papaya salad, rice noodles with chicken curry.
Clean fresh veggies to accompany the main dishes.
Best food in the world
Delicious and good price.
As a farang I enjoyed the experience. Many flavourful Issan dishes.

Last night, I made a special trip to the Chulalongkorn University Night Market and finally got to try the legendary Jeb O Chula Banthatthong! Even though we waited in line for almost an hour, the first bite made it all worth it.

We ordered the signature "Mama Noodles." The steaming copper pot was packed with ingredients—large, fresh prawns, tender minced pork, a runny egg, and refreshing straw mushrooms. The most amazing part was the soup: the Tom Yum base was perfectly sour and spicy, with the richness of coconut milk balancing the heat just right. Every spoonful was incredibly addictive. I especially have to praise the spiciness level—it had a strong kick but didn't upset the stomach, making you crave more with each bite.

Even though the place was packed, the service was surprisingly fast. Highly recommended for anyone who loves spicy food. This is absolutely a must-try, god-tier supper spot in Bangkok!

A very popular restaurant. Although it serves instant noodles, the ingredients are great. It deserves the Michelin name and tastes great. Be sure to use the app to queue in advance to avoid meal times. They sell whole coconuts, so you can ask the staff.

Flavourful mama instant noodles, the crispy pork was still crispy even though it was soaked in the soup. The raw salmon salad is tangy and surprisingly good.
Download the QueQ app to get a queue number before arriving as wait time during dinner was more than 30min.

Took a cab all the way to try this. As alot of people mentioned, download the queq app to get a queue number. Came on a weekend when they just opened at 4pm. Surprisingly was not that crowded and managed to walk right in. Place had ac.
Had the mama noodles with meatballs (thb150). It's ok, the soup was pretty sour and creamy. Meatballs were not bad quite flavourful. Had the shrimp cake too (thb100) it was ok.
Personally I don't think it's worth it to queue for hours or specially come down all the way just for this unless u are a hardcore mama fan

✨ Hidden Gem Food Experience! ( After disappointing experience at Jeh o chula) ✨

We stumbled upon this place after having a not-so-great experience at Jeh O Chula — and honestly, I’m so glad we did! Sometimes a bad experience really leads you to something way better.

After being Jeh o Chula regular everytime I'm in Bangkok, I'M SO GLAD I encountered such RUDE behaviour by the man who handle the queue at Jeh O Chula. Because of that I realized there is so many BETTER AND AMAZING FOOD  in surrounding area that ONLY LOCAL GOES!

I took the queue in advance at around 101 number. Made our way to the restaurant, arrived at the number was getting to 70ish so we walk in surrounding area to kill the time to only realize THE QUEUE WAS CANCELLED at around number 50ish! I went immediately to ask if the the shop or system glitched cancelled it? What happened? The man shouted YOU CANCELLED IT! SEE YOU CANCELLED IT! YOU TAKE NUMBER AGAIN! (Best part was he grinned like psychopath, seem to enjoy the notoriety of their shop having customer to have long wait, wanting to eat there) Well I was thinking it's okay, we will wait then to see the queue is at 139.

My daughter told me, mommy the food is not that good (She told me otw too but I insisted for tonight since I loves the salmon there) But my partner being German are not having the nonsense of the long queue. I wanted him to try the pork belly. But I remember last visit without my partner, my friend said it wasn't THAT GREAT, it was hard and not that good, worthy of visit (I don't eat pork so I don't know) so I didn't want to let us wait again and again for him to find out the pork aren't that good and be upset. So we let majority win and decided to check out for restaurant nearby and SO GLAD WE DID!!

Just few meter away is just this AMAZING restauran called PHAKAO with OUTSTANDING waitress name KIT who assisted us from table sitting (NO WAITING ALTHO FULL HOUSE because they are efficient with swift table cleaning, bigger space and even communicate with walkie talkie) she personally explained the menu which is partly in Thai because most of the customer are local Thai. SHE ASSISTED with true thai friendly but professional hospitality. After all our order was done, whilst waiting for food that didn't even take long. She dropped by to say goodbye as her shift is ending. I was so touched to see such personal sincere service in PHAKAO compare to Jeh O Chula low class customer service.

and when the FOOD ARRIVED, BOY WAS WE BLOWN AWAY OR WHAT??!

Let me tell you, every single dish here was an explosion of flavor!

1️⃣ Longan Blended Drink – Super refreshing and naturally sweet with that distinct longan aroma. Top up with longan on top, generous amount!! It’s not too sweet, just perfectly balanced — such a great palate cleanser between all the flavorful dishes.

2️⃣ Beef Grilled – Tender, juicy, and perfectly charred. Cooked fo PERFECTION. MELT IN MOUTH with perfect sauce at the side. I'm salvating thinking about it lolz 🤤 Every bite was smoky and rich, so addictive that we ended up ordering 2nd plate again!

3️⃣ Salmon salad – Oh my god, this was perfection! Best in Bangkok! Jeh o Chulaaa what??? The Salmon Salad in PHAKAO is  Fresh, zesty, and flavorful with just the right balance of tang and spice. The amount is generous! Look at the picture. We actually ordered this twice too  because we couldn’t get enough of it. Honestly, this salmon salad puts Jeh O Chula’s version to shame.

Sometimes the best food finds are the ones you don’t plan for! 😋💯

Isaan-style food restaurant with indoor air-conditioning and outdoor seating.
PROS: The staff are fast and friendly; the food is very good and reasonably priced.
CONS: There is only one brand of beer available; the restrooms are in need of renovation.

(Scores out of 5)
Food: 5
Drinks: 2
Service: 5
Restrooms: 2
Parking: 5

Isaan food restaurant with both air-conditioned and outdoor seating.
PROS: The staff are fast and friendly; the food is delicious and reasonably priced.
CONS: There is only one brand of beer available; the restrooms need updating.

(Scores out of 5)
Food: 5
Drinks: 2
Service: 5
Restrooms: 2
Parking: 5

The food is very delicious. Every dish is delicious. It's a good place to eat before boarding the flight back. I recommend the fried fermented fish, steamed fish, and sticky rice wrapped in banana leaves. It's very cute.

11/4/2025 The food tastes right, authentic Isaan, the dipping sauce and boiled vegetables are good. The staff provides good service, there are both outdoor and air-conditioned seats. I went to eat around 8 p.m. and didn't have to wait long for the food. I deducted 1 star because the restaurant should be careful about straws. They should choose straws that are well wrapped, not bare straws like the ones in the picture I received this time. Everything is good, I would like to ask for just one improvement, I will visit again.

Sukjai Land Branch 2, a famous Isan restaurant from Ban Fang, has opened its doors closer to the city. The taste is delicious and not too spicy, perfect for welcoming guests. The atmosphere is by a lotus pond. In the evening, there are singers singing Isan-style songs, preserving the culture. The staff are good and polite, but there are few of them, making it a bit slow.

Spicy Isaan food...everything is delicious...
Parking available...lotus pond atmosphere...
Good service...

Wanted to like the food here so much, but was extremely disappointed by the quality of food served here. I made a reservation a month back but it feels unnecessary. Came into an quiet (empty) place, the furnishing looks slightly worn but warm welcome by the staff.
Ordered 3 dishes to try, morning glory salad, an egg & pork stew as well as the pork jowl curry rice. The batter on the morning glory was too heavy and felt very greasy. The pork in the stew was tough and the gravy was lacklustre, you can get this at any street stall at a fraction of the price. The pork jowl was not fresh and had a stench to it. It felt like they were trying to cover it with the spices in the curry. All the dishes we tried were not restaurant quality food. The service staff saw that we barely touched our food and asked if we wanted to take it to go but we rejected as we truly didn't enjoy any of it. However, there were no enquiries on how did we find the food. Therefore, I decided to share my thoughts here with anyone who is thinking to visit Baan to avoid more disappointed guests. Spent ~1140b on the above and left feeling very empty and sad. :(

reviewer: yenny eko kartika sari puji astuti
review_text:
Not Recommended. Between me, you, and the food—just stay away.

We walked into an empty restaurant and still decided to give it a chance. I ordered the lamb curry, which was hyped as “the most delicious.” It was nothing close. Overly sweet, drowning in oil, and served with zero effort—no garnish, no presentation, nothing.

We spent 3,320 THB for a meal that was barely passable. The other dishes were okay at best—bland, forgettable, and overpriced.

To make things worse, the place was hot and uncomfortable, with barely any cooling despite the heat.

No, we won’t be coming back. Save your money, your appetite, and your time. There are far better and wayyy cheaper options in this city.

Came here because of the many Michelin awards, but left disappointed. The restaurant was completely empty on a Friday night.

The food, while good, was definitely not worth the price as the portion sizes were lacking. While the service was good, there is better food with similar ambience available in Bangkok for half the price
Excellent service that is only matched by the delicious food we had! Good portions too. Ordered and ate too much but worth the calories!

We came here for dinner. The foods are amazing and the service is homey. We ordered the Ka Praow and specialties of the house such as Braised Egg with Pork and Shrimp/Pork fritter. It would be better to come with larger party so you can try more dishes from the menu. The mango sticky rice is to die for as well.
@thechefoodie

Very warm welcome to their location. However unlike alll the other fine dining experiences, no welcome drink or storytelling. We went straight into business. The food was delicious. Again other than the other fine dining restaurants you can order a la carte which I did this time. I felt the menu was too much that’s why my decision was right. I ordered two starters and one main. The main portion was pretty big. Not much explanation about the food. Overall I would say good food but less of an experience - certainly no emotional touch.

Definitely will return.

Love their ambience and the thin crystal stems. Dark lattice wood made the room feeling cool, especially when one comes in from the hot weather, and the hustle and bustle of Bangkok.

Good service and great food, too much of it - we've their tasting menu.

I particularly liked the stir-fried young fiddlehead ferns and Wagyu beef. Two soups, one pungent which I like and the yellow cream was sweet, which I don't like: pretty extreme.

The outdoor section of the restaurant is on the narrow side of the rectangle pool. At night, the pool looks equally beautiful.

The atmosphere here was nice and the drinks here were amazing. I ordered an orange citrus alcoholic drink and could not taste the alcohol at all. My friends’ other drinks were also super tasty and had little alcohol or a mild yet pleasant alcohol taste. The thai tea was served in a super interesting way as well; the sugar, cream, and tea were separated so you could play around and adjust the portions. Very fun.

The stir fried prawns (gung pad chakram) were excellent. They were super large, the size of my hand, and the meat was cooked perfectly. The head butter from the prawns was mixed in the sauce to create a creamy, shrimpy, thick delicious sauce that went well with rice. The wagyu beef dish (pad nuea sai nomai nahm) that we got was also extremely flavorful and cooked to perfection. It was a melody of meat in my mouth.

The chicken dish (pad ped gai sai rew kub pak chee rai) however was just okay; it tasted similar to the stir fried chicken you would get at any Thai restaurant. I thought the jungle beef curry dish (gang om nuea nong lai bai cha muang) was okay was well, which tasted similar to any pot roast, beef stew, or bo kho dish that you might get at a restaurant.

Atmosphere and service were good but some of my friends didn’t get drinks that they ordered and had to have them taken off the bill. Acceptable for a normal restaurant but this is a Michelin star one, so I have higher expectations.

Do I think this place is worthy of a Michelin star? Maybe not but it was still a good dinner. I’m sure you will still have a good meal if you come and I have yet to try the other dishes, which they might excel more at than the ones we chose

Nahm truly lives up to the hype. The flavours were bold, authentic, and beautifully balanced—each dish felt like a celebration of Thai cuisine. From the entrées to dessert, everything was presented with care and tasted incredible.

The ambience is elegant yet warm, making it perfect for a special night out. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, adding to the overall experience. Highly recommend if you’re after refined Thai food that still honours its roots.

Lovely food, but let down by the service.

Not sure what happened, but the service team seems to be rather off-mode. It was hard to get service when no one was around. Definitely not a standard expected. The lunch service had 3 tables occupied, surely not a peak load situation.

Food wise, quality and execution are high and fresh.

However, there was none to little explanation given for the dishes served. A rather missed opportunity to introduce the local dishes and used ingredients to a guest who is not familiar with all the dishes on the menu.

Overall, acceptable food, with no outstanding dish to remember.

A beautiful, family-run property right on the river, with many different accommodation options. Small houses, lovely rooms, etc... The staff is very welcoming and the prices are very fair! The food is simply top-notch!!!

The information was not clear. We found out at the door that they did not accept walk-in customers and could not enter to dine. It was a pity.

Not only us, but there was another group of guests who also found out at the door that they did not accept walk-in customers.

good reviews don’t even do justice for how good Khao-So-I is. The food is excellent, the environment is lively and lovely. The restaurant is so busy but staff are so attentive!! Staff make excellent recommendation of dishes without upselling their more expensive dishes or anything.

We’ve had other Khao Soi, including Michelin guided shops but this is the best one for me and my husband. This may not be your everyday Khao Soi. We are tourists here and here to enjoy & experience things !! Worth every penny.

This seemed like a fusion take on khao soi, and overall it was great. The khao soi was very spicy and cover the taste of shrimp and scallops. but the staff were extremely caring when he noticed I was sweating and can’t handle with the spicy, he proactively offered extra coconut milk and pork broth to mellow the soup.

However, the yogurt dessert’s texture was too hard and not creamy enough. If you can handle the spicy soup, you might want to skip dessert at a khao soi restaurant 😆

A premium Khao Soi restaurant where the flavor is quite balanced, making it suitable for tourists to try. Honestly, the taste is pretty good, but personally, I prefer more local style places. That’s just my personal preference, so it wouldn’t be fair to judge the restaurant based on that. I recommend trying it yourself. Overall, it’s a good place definitely worth a visit if you’ve never had Khao Soi before.

I visited in the morning when it wasn't busy, and the staff were friendly, providing me with recommendations. It's a must-visit if you're in Chiang Mai; the food and atmosphere are great, making it feel like I was in Japan.

The food was incredible, delicious, and authentically Northern Thai with a hint of Japanese fusion.

The best fusion Khao Soi in Chiangmai, great atmosphere like old town Tokyo, very organised. Go early the best way is no queue and ending with soft ice cream, same quality as it in Tokyo. Don’t miss! 😆

This was worth its Michelin recognition as the food was amazing. The duck is tender, the sauce is flavourful and tangy, the noodles have great texture, the soup is hearty and soothing. The passion fruit juice is very concentrated and flavourful.

Everything we had was so good, it is a must try when you’re nearby. I would recommend the claypot duck to share for 2 - 3 people and individually order your own plain noodles (a single portion of the noodles is not much though).

Ordered their signature hot claypot duck meat with noodle and hot claypot with duck wings. Not sure if we made a mistake on putting the noodles in the claypot, the noodles were too dry. However, the duck wings was good. But as an Asian, we have tasted better braised duck.

Looking for braised duck at a no-frills local Thai eatery, then this is your eat; Except Tang Sui Heng is also Michelin-recommended for a few years now.

Duck noodle soup is their resident star. The herbal soup lifts the soft supple braised duck, especially good for a slightly cooler day (or at night when it's not crowded).

The duck blood curd however under-delivered, so I won't not recommend, since there are many options around that you can fulfil your bloodthirst at.

Soft and tender braised duck. Thai Teochew style. Near to National Stadium BTS. Worth the walk. There is a menu in front of the shop. The nice lady will take your order if there is a line. So the food can be served ASAP.

Order the claypot version  and share with a friend. The kailan vege is also very well done.

We ordered a duck meat kway teow dry and a duck rice. Had to order another claypot duck to satisfy the tastebuds.

No air conditioning, so try to stay chill yourself. 😅

Simply one of the best Duck I tasted!!!!

Soft and good

The noodles damm good too.

Must come with highly recommended michelin star

Very, very sophisticated Michelin-starred northern Thai cuisine.

Overall, the food was delicate and delicious, with the occasional punch without being overly empowering.

I chose the wine pairing menu with 3 drinks and 9 dishes (do come hungry or you might end up like me, asking to pack the final spectacular main course to take away).

The restaurant definitely utilized choice ingredients (it was especially obvious with the fish tartare, the chicken consomé, the duck breast, and the river prawn), but what amazed me the most, besides the flavors, were the creative thought that went into the presentation of the dishes, and the smooth flow of service. The decoration, music level, and atmosphere were also elegant and relaxing.

No doubt this is on the expensive side for Thai food in Bangkok, but the refinement level is also rare to find elsewhere. Happy to see (northern, Lanna) Thai food being elevated and recognized!

Outstanding experience at North. Authentic Lanna flavors elevated into refined fine dining. Each dish told a story and was beautifully presented. Warm, elegant atmosphere with attentive service. Highly recommended and unforgettable.

Came here specially for the khao soi after seeing so many glowing reviews. While the dish was beautifully plated and ambience was fantastic, honestly was pretty disappointed in it as I had better Khao Soi in other small restaurants. Expected more from a place specialising in it

A Michelin-rated gem tucked away like a quiet oasis along a busy street! The 9-course meal, inspired by Northern Thai flavours with a touch of spice, is excellent value (We especially loved the Phayao dish!)

Chef personally greeted us and thoughtfully prepared a sweet treat based on our conversation. Special thanks to Non, who patiently and thoroughly explained each dish; service was attentive throughout!

A very suitable place for a romantic night or an elegant get together with family and friends!
Authentic Northern food served in a fine dining style. I love their tableware, serving style, atmosphere, and food very much; however, the lady at the dinner reception needs to improve her attitude.

Michelin rated. Entrees starting at $2. Calm vibe and low music. Food was good. Desserts delicious. And their Busarin iced coffee delightful.

We had the Green Curry with Pork and Red Curry with Pumpkin and Pork. Durian sticky rice and Coconut Milk ice cream with Fries Sticky Rice Cake.

I love the small menu.

They didn’t put the Cash Only sign in front of the door or window, we almost didn’t have enough cash to pay for the meal.
Its ok to be cash only, but not ok if not telling customers in advance. Of coz, it will be great if they start taking credit card payments.

Crabs meat curry and fish curry both amazing, worth to try northern thai style
We had a curried chicken and squash dish and some Thai style slow cooked lamb.  They were both delicious!  This place is a little out of the way, but it’s definitely worth it.  I highly recommend!

The food here was absolutely incredible. We started off with the barracuda curry, very unique dish. Second, we had the northern Thai curry noodle with chicken, phenomenal dish. The showstoppers were the roti dishes, we had the green curry and the hunglay curry with lamb; absolutely the best roti I’ve ever had. You would be crazy not to try this restaurant, fully deserves 5 stars.
Very good taste both food and dessert, highly recommend on coconut milk ice cream , should be call for reservation due to limit tables
The best Kuayjub Namkon in Ubon. Possibly more than 50 years has have been opened since this old commercial area was the busiest in the downtown.
Good
Traditional Kuay Chap, large noodles, thick broth, served with pork offal in Chinese herbs. Super delicious. Come here and forget about Ubon Ratchathani Vietnamese Kuay Chap.

reviewer: พนาดร เย็นจิตร
review_text: Delicious, tell others. The richness of Chinese spices, the unique and delicious taste.

This long-established restaurant has been in business for over 70 years.

It's also featured in the Michelin Guide.

The kway jap is well-cooked and incredibly rich.

The offal had no odor and was delicious.

If it were near my house, I'd definitely go there.
The best noodle , the pork is so tender and the broth is so delicious and after taking a sip , i can feel it fill so much nutrients , definitely one of my top 3 noodle soup
We had breakfast at this location twice while we were in town. The food was delicious and served with extra fixing. There are varieties of jams for toast. The service was excellent.

Kway juab ubon was really nice. The noodles won’t mushy and the broth was aromatic. Ingredients were fresh too. We also ordered jok but it was appalling. It was only porridge and 2 really mini meat ball. But the price is the same as the kway jub whivh has so much more ingredients, we felt cheated.
Thai breakfast restaurant. Try egg pan and steamed bread. Reasonable price, nice taste and friendly staff.

Nice place, rival to Sam Chai. I went twice. Sorry to say I think I was 10 baht overcharged both times. Food and drink tastes like slightly too many artificial additives, if possible more natural ingredients preferred.

pleasantly surprised by the quality of this restaurant! the clam linguine was so aromatic and the pasta definitely tastes handmade as it has a great bite. tomato salad was the perfect appetizer and thank you to the restaurant for the complimentary mushroom tart! wish they had more customers as it was completely empty on a wednesday dinner

Antito features a stylish and inviting design, creating a pleasant atmosphere for dining. The staff are friendly, though they may come across as slightly unsure at times. The food is decent and reasonably enjoyable, with prices that are fair for the experience offered.

While it might not be a destination in itself, Antito is a solid choice if you’re staying at the hotel. A convenient and worthwhile option for a casual meal or drink.
Food was delicious and the atmosphere was really nice. We also received excellent service from K.Kla.

A great tasting Italian restaurant with a poolside view. The place offered easy to eat Italian food that tasted great and is well cooked. My favourite would be the pizza fritta, as the texture of the bread is excellent. Overall a great place for a nice lunch or dinner if you are nearby. However, the place is rather pricey and even with the 20% discount price.

One of the best Italian casual dinings in town. The food is authentic, delicate, and flavorful. The plating is so beautiful. Ranges are from appetizers & starters, soups, pastas, main dishes, and desserts.

The prices are reasonable. And the services from all friendly staff are very professional. Happy hour is not to be missed. You can get 50% on alcoholic drinks from 5-7 p.m.

The restaurant is located on 14th floor. You can enjoy your Italian cuisine indoors or outdoors by the pool (seating in an open air area) which offers you a sunset view of city in the evening.

Parking at hotel are available or get off the BTS sky train at Surasak Station which is right in front of the hotel.

Great food. Had duck slices with rice noodles. Broth was rich and very flavourful. The service was fast and the restaurant was very clean. First proper meal since being back in Thailand, and what a way to start! I would highly recommended

A great place to have an early morning bowl of duck egg noodle soup. Good size portion, very good service,  very clean also. The broth is amazing, so many subtle flavors that work so well together. Meat very tender, and for 50Baht, it's a great deal. Well worth a visit when in Udon

Haven't been here for a while, last time was not really pleased with the service.
Today we gave it another try, have to say the place is improved.
Tables are looking new, service is more professional.
Food is good, nice duck 🦆 food. Price is good.

Go check it out yourself.
Let me know in the comment what you think of the place.
Best duck noodle in Udon...very friendly staff...Air con eating area.. highly recommend
Love it open early

From the moment you arrive at the majestic sala entrance to the Amanpuri, you know you are in for something special. Ed Tuttle's design  has worn the years lightly since 1988.

The immense size of the open fronted structure, with its dark wooden Maka and Teak beams makes a bold statement of substance and style, complemented by palms, coconut trees, and large potted Bougainvillea

The staff are no less impressive and upon being greeted by the impeccably dressed hotel front office team you will be whisked across the traditionally styled lobby through to a large courtyard. This has at its centre a lap pool (of course perfectly lit for the night) and on the right is a raised platform, where you might be lucky enough to have a traditional musician entertaining guests. Beyond that further towards the sea is 'Nama', the Japanese restaurant known for Washouku and Omakase.

Tonight however was about Thai, so our guide steered us left, towards the large open pavilion that houses Buabok. In a handoff that was so seamless, that athletic teams would be envious, our hotel guide left us and the restaurant staff welcomed us to a table on the terrace overlooking the pool.

I've read that Amanpuri has a ratio of 7 staff to each guest and I would not be surprised. With a seemingly effortless (Thai) gracefulness the Buabok staff make sure you want for nothing.

The restaurant was busy-ish with about 30 covers at 8pm. The tables are spread out nicely, with only a couple of them eating inside whilst most enjoyed the terrace.

The menu is extensive (as you would expect), with the Aman's 'take' on traditional dishes and specialism in showcasing southern Thai, especially seafood. We tried the Kor Moo Yang (pork neck with Tamarind sauce), - rich in flavour, the texture of the pork giving body to the dish,  Pod Pia Sod Nuea Pu (fresh spring crab roll with  Tamarind and cashew), slightly thickened rice wrappers make this quite filling although the flavour was outstanding.

For mains, Khao Soi Gai, (Chiang Mai noodles with chicken thigh in a fragrant coconut broth, this one you can afford to dial up the spice a little to get fuller flavour) and Gaeng Pu Sen Mee, a signature dish, (Phuket crab with yellow curry, a clean bowl signalled a very satisfied diner),

The portions are quite large at Buabok so dessert didn't figure this time.

The food presentation was elegant, in keeping with the overall experience of the evening.

It is hard to find fault with Buabok. If you are looking for a special evening, a feeling of exclusivity (if only for a couple of hours) with amazing food, stylish setting and excellent service then you are hard pressed to find better on the island.

One to return to.

Grilled snapper fillet with lemon, delicious.
D stress cocktail, great.
Profiteroles salted caramel, oh my…! So good.
On the pricey side but the decor is top!
Enjoy
Such a special dining experience! Outstanding service, creative cocktails and food - beautiful setting with a lady playing the Thai Khim throughout!

Divine 🪷🎻 Āman vibes and hospitality.
Enjoy the crab curry, and grouper.

(4 - meets expectations, 5 - beyond expectations)
Tastiest Thai food in phuket, lovely ambience with relaxing music, best service I have ever experienced.

This is a famous, traditional noodle shop in the area that's an absolute must-try. They specialize in squid noodles, a dish that's surprisingly hard to find.
What makes their noodles so special is the fragrant soup and the generous use of both fresh and dried squid as the main ingredients. The flavor is fantastic and unique.
The prices are very affordable, so you get amazing value for your money. Since this is a popular spot, I recommend getting here early, around 8:00 AM, to avoid the long queues that start to form later in the day.
Parking can be a bit tricky, but there is a designated lot just past the restaurant on the left, though it often fills up quickly. Overall, the experience is well worth it—this is one of those local spots you don't want to miss.

Good taste strong flavor.

The owner really control good quality of the ingredients.

Good service from the waiters team.

If you want to order variety of menu, have to arrive very early morning.

Ban Bung Noodles, a hot place not to miss. family restaurant that has kept the traditional recipe three generation over decades. Jam packed small place. A go to restaurant for authentic delicious bowl of noodles soup. Opening hours 06:00-14:30. Parking is a problem but about 100mts ahead open parking space.

Having my 1st time with this special pork noodle with dried squid soup. Not sure if you can get this in Bangkok but it's worth checking it out at Ban Bung. I like the smell and sweetness of the soup which come out from the squid. Yummy!😋
Original Ban Bung Noodle tastes. New location was spacious and modernization. Love that rhis place procide very convenient parking space. Very considerable of owner.

This seafood food stall is the absolute star of the night market! The young owner is not only charming and handsome but also a brilliant entrepreneur who knows exactly how to win over his customers. The seafood here is fresher and more delicious than what you’d find in high-end restaurants, yet the prices remain incredibly reasonable. The service is warm, efficient, and always on point. Although the setting is simple, it’s impeccably clean and well-organized, making for a pleasant dining experience. It’s no surprise this spot is always packed with people—waiting for a table is totally worth it. We’ve been coming back every day this week, and it never disappoints. Truly outstanding!

It is located in the market.
Good and polite service mind

For the foods, they are too sweet. I meant it.

Smoking is allowed, lung harmfulness warning!!!!!!!!!!

The price is quite okay, not that expensive per person.

If you're craving seafood in Pattaya, Kruatabird Seafood Restaurant is an absolute must-visit. From the moment you step in, you’re greeted by the lively buzz of a packed dining room—a clear sign that this place is a local gem. The first thing that hits you is the quality of the seafood: it’s incredibly fresh, like it was just plucked from the ocean minutes before landing on your plate. Whether it’s succulent prawns, tender fish, or plump crab, every bite bursts with that unmistakable taste of the sea.

The flavors here are nothing short of amazing. Each dish is crafted with such expertise that you can tell the chefs know exactly how to let the natural goodness of the seafood shine while adding just the right touch of seasoning or spice. Standouts include their grilled fish, which is perfectly charred yet juicy, and the spicy seafood stir-fries that pack a punch without overwhelming the delicate ingredients. It’s clear that the kitchen takes pride in every detail.

The staff only adds to the experience. They’re warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly, making you feel right at home even when the place is bustling—and trust me, it’s always full. Reservations might be a smart move if you don’t want to wait, but even the wait feels worth it once you’re seated with a plate of their magic in front of you.

Kruatabird isn’t just a meal; it’s a seafood lover’s dream come true. Freshness, flavor, and fantastic service—what more could you ask for? Highly recommend!
Lovely little restaurant with their own tables located inside Pattaya Park Night Market. Sea food is sublime - fresh, creamy, full of flavours.
As a retired chef, I was exceptionally impressed with the food . The flavour , quality and size of each dish was perfect ..highly recommended. Worth the search in the market ..

Actively try and seek out the most raw and authentic dining experiences when visiting other countries.

This place is fantastic, it sits just off a hectic main road, nestled in a wooden hut are a full team of fast paced, commited duck roasting angels 😂

Ordered half a duck as I was on my own, pointed over to the seating on the other side of the road and waited in anticipation, not only did it arrive fast, it excelled my expectations. Half a duck, BBQ over coal and cut up into big portions. Two small cups of chili sauces to accompany and I went to work.

Polished it off in 5 minutes and took my plate over to then butcher the pronunciation of 'delicious' in Thai, obviously met with a chorus of giggles, paid up and off I went.

Can't beat it.

Best Roasted Ducks in Phuket

I’d heard about this stall for quite some time, especially after they received the Michelin Bib Gourmand this year (2025).

To be honest, I didn’t have high expectations at first — great roasted duck is hard to come by — but they absolutely nailed it.

The duck skin is crispy, while the meat remains juicy and full of flavour.

The duck laab is also excellent — not too spicy, with tender meat.

However, there are only a few tables and very limited parking, so it’s not ideal for large groups. The toilet could also be cleaner.

Aside from that, I really love this place. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended!

A true local gem for duck lovers! This place, recognized by the Michelin Guide, serves absolutely exceptional duck—juicy, flavorful meat with incredibly crispy skin. We also ordered a papaya salad, which was fresh and well-balanced. We specifically asked for it not spicy, and to our surprise, it actually came that way—a rare occurrence in Thailand! The staff was friendly and welcoming, making the experience even more enjoyable.

And the price? Very reasonable—we paid around 550 baht for two people.

Tip: Always call and book in advance because the place is always full! If you’re in the area, this is a must-try!

Fantastic juicy duck & chicken! Delicious!!! Our family dine like ordinary Thai with sticky rice with these poultry. The chilli is very very good!
Love it!
The bbq roast duck here is really good. Mr wife and i finished a whole roasted duck! A definite must try. Mark Wiens recommended well!
Awesome taste, quality ingredients

The shop is behind Maharaj Hospital, so it's easy to get to. However, there's not much parking. It's a small shop with only a few tables. I recommend making a reservation and ordering food before you arrive so you don't have to wait long. The owner cooks all the food himself, and everything is delicious. The seafood is fresh and clean. The shrimp are large, fresh, and bouncy. The fish doesn't smell fishy. The food is spicy. The crab fried rice has a strong wok aroma.

This restaurant is truly deserving of its Michelin Bib award.
You must book in advance and specify a time. The advantage is that it's not crowded, and the atmosphere is chill, as people arrive at specific times.
The highlight is the small plates, but the portions are overflowing.
It may seem small, but the food is actually generous.
The ingredients are fresh, and the seafood is also fresh.
My favorite dish is the crab fried rice. The crab comes in chunks.
The rice is incredibly fragrant and pan-fried, making it the most delicious fried rice I've ever had.
Another must-try is the fish and pork belly. The sauce is fragrant, sweet, and salty, perfectly balanced.
The restaurant is air-conditioned, but parking is a bit difficult, so you have to park on the side of the road.
Overall, it's excellent and well worth the price. The main dishes are 200 baht each, and the large crab fried rice is 300 baht. Five of us ate it all, so we couldn't finish it. Go for it!

They use very good ingredients: large shrimp, fresh and crispy squid, and fresh and delicious sea bass. The atmosphere in the restaurant is like eating at home, but it might be a bit slow. You have to call ahead to order to get a faster service.

This is a restaurant that requires advance planning to get a chance to eat. You have to book in advance. If you just walk in, don't expect it. But every dish is delicious. The flavors are well-balanced. Well-balanced means not too salty, sour, spicy, or sweet. The chili and garlic dishes, stir-fried curry powder, braised pork in soy sauce, crab claw fried rice, and mixed seafood tom yum were all delicious. I'll definitely go back.

⭐️⭐️ 2-Star Night at Côte

One of my friends’ all-time favorite places for special occasions like birthdays and celebrations.

Be sure to prepare your stomach — it’s a long supper! The bread and butter were absolutely amazing. Throughout the course, we had quite a few standout dishes. For us, the main course was hard to finish simply because the overall portions were quite generous. Still, we managed to enjoy the dessert and even took the petite fours home.

The service, as expected from a Michelin 2-star restaurant in the Capella Hotel, was excellent. What stood out even more was their attention to detail — they noticed I’m left-handed and adjusted the setup accordingly. That’s next-level.

We weren’t in the mood for alcohol, so they paired tea with each course — a unique and thoughtful touch.

The sunset view was stunning, and the atmosphere overall was elegant yet comfortable.

I had the pleasure of attending an unforgettable wine dinner at Côte by Mauro Colagreco, Capella Bangkok. The evening was nothing short of exceptional—from the elegantly curated wine pairings to the meticulously crafted dishes, every element was executed with precision and passion.

Each course was a celebration of flavor and artistry, harmoniously paired with legendary wines including Opus One, Almaviva, and Château Mouton Rothschild. The 2015 Almaviva and 2003 Mouton Rothschild stood out as truly iconic, enhancing the dishes beautifully and leaving a lasting impression.

The service was seamless and attentive, elevating the entire experience to one of warmth and sophistication. The attention to detail, from the presentation of each plate to the storytelling behind every bottle, made this event one of the most memorable wine dinners I’ve had in recent years.

A remarkable evening that blended fine cuisine, rare wines, and impeccable hospitality in perfect balance.

PS

I’ll continue to share more photos each time I visit this restaurant. Please note that some photos may not be directly related to the wine dinner event mentioned above.

Simple and very well prepared dishea. Service and atmosphere is living up to the 2 Stars. Very enjoyable night. However, although all the dishes were very good, they are missing the taste that make you “wow”…

Of the six restaurants from Asia’s top 100 that I visited on this trip to Bangkok, this one was my overall favourite.

It was also the second most expensive, although worth it! AUD760 for 10 courses plus optional cheese and 7 paired wines.

Service from each team member was exceptional and there was even a visit from the lovely Davide 🥰 I felt so welcome and entertained - very important for a solo traveller/diner.

Of the six restaurants that I visited, I only did three wine pairings (an effort to leave space for food!), and Côte was the best of them.

I was given a shawl and hot water and hot tea to drink whilst I acclimated to the AC. As someone who tends to drink hot water with food rather than cold, I love when there is the foresight to offer it before I even ask ⭐️

I fully intend to revisit on my next trip as I feel this one will be a lifelong favourite 🤍

If I could give 6 stars for service I would. The team is exceptional, from start to finish. Attentive, engaging and knowledgeable. What an experience! We celebrated the tomato, and the food experience was phenomenal. From taste to presentation. Well done, thank you for a lasting memory. What a culinary delight! Look forward to returning!

If you’re looking for authentic, traditional Thai flavors, this place is a must-try! Every dish is packed with classic spices and seasoning that really bring out the true taste of Thai cuisine.

The portion sizes are huge, so it’s definitely great for sharing — or for anyone with a big appetite.

I highly recommend trying the เมี่ยงปลา (Miang Pla) — it’s absolutely the highlight of the menu. Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. Definitely something I’d come back for!

This restaurant has been opened for over two years. We just came here on the recommendation of our friend. The food taste very nice home cook style. They also have Michelin on three of that dishes., we tried the Korat sausage and it was very well done and delicious. Nice Thai restaurant, should be back for a second round to try other dishes.

Everything was close to perfect! The atmosphere and seating were comfortable; staff are polite; and most of all, food were delicious. The Tom yum soup was exceptional! I also recommend the Pumpkin with crab meat chunks, Lotus stem and prawn salad, and Curry (beef).
The food here is really delicious! Everything was fresh and flavorful. The staff were super friendly and attentive. I had a great dining experience and will definitely come back again!

We ordered the seasonal dishes like the stuffed rambutans in soup and mangosteen salad in addition to the glass noodles with prawn n minced pork. For our main, we had their roast chicken. Service was impeccable , the home cooked dishes were good! And the owner, Jom popped by which was the extra touch .
The Noodle was good and reasonable price.
Great noodles.
Overall cleanness is an issue.

The noodles are delicious and generous. The meatballs are small and easy to eat, bouncy, and tender. The soup is sweet and delicious, but the end of the bowl can get a bit salty.
The shop is located in a single shophouse. It's easy to find by following the pin.
An old shop. The homemade meatballs are delicious. The soup is a bit bland. Maybe it's made slowly because the auntie is old.

Another precious gem of Thai Southern Cuisine Restaurant in Phuket. Expect a homie local vibe with affordable dishes.

They will buy fresh ingredients daily so you have to book ahead and make deposit. They are closed on Monday and Tuesday so check the time before you go.

I admire the skill of the chef, all dishes are aromatic and tasty. The fish is the star of the show, sweet meat with flavorful seasoning on top. When you eat with the warm rice, its like a dream come true.

CHEERS!

🧄🌶️The atmosphere is tranquil and breezy, even during the hot season. The décor is simple and easy on the eyes. The food truly lives up to its reputation—delicious in every bite. My personal favorites are the sour curry, fried steamed buns, and wine-flavored ice cream. The flavors reflect Southern Thai cuisine but are not overly intense. Everything is thoughtfully prepared with a unique charm of its own.

☎️I recommend booking a table and sending your order list via the restaurant’s LINE account in advance it’s a better option than just walking in.

Easiest the BEST meal we had in our 4 days in Phuket! Quality of food, depth of taste, service by the staff and the calming ambience made this place such a gem. Multiple Michelin stars and you can totally understand why when you taste the food. Aunty chef was so cool and friendly.

Local Southern Thai Food.  Highly recommended.  Cozy environment. Nice service.  Limited selections but all dishes that we ordered is tasty with generous portions.  Definitely revisit❤️

It’d be better to come with a group of 4-6 so you can try many dishes.   We came as a couple and order 4 dishes, which barely finished.  I really want to try the fried mini buns with thai custard but I was too full😔

P.S.  Advance booking via line or DM is highly recommended.  The advance deposit 500 baht will be deducted from the bill later on.

Food :
Thai-local phuket food is very good. Tasty and nice decoration. Some menu need to pre booking otherwise can't have.
Price is medium to a bit high but food is good enough, taste is unique. Like it!

Booking:
Booking is needed , they are small local shop with not many staffs. Booking is easy and convenient.

Atmostphere:
Nice and feel relax , good local decor , not hot even it no aircon. Rest room is good and clean.
*Have enough car park that is great, envn it is soil not cement but still in good condition.

Menu:
I put most of menu here so others can decide before you go.

Jay Fai’s crab omelette is a real must-try! For 1,500 baht, we thnk it is well worth it. It’s 95% filled with plump and juicy crab meat. (We actually tried crab omelette in another restaurant for 1,200 baht and it was practically just omelette with very few pieces of crab meat). We loved Jay Fai’s crab omelette so much that we ordered a second one.

Go after lunch to avoid the long queue. We went at around 2:30pm on a Thursday and got a table right away.

We also didn’t experience any of the negative reviews we read about in Google. The staff, including Jay Fai’s daughter, were efficient and polite. The place was also clean, especially the toilet.

It’s understandable that they don’t allow any photos with Jay Fai. Because if each and every customer will ask for a photo, then she will not be able to cook anymore. 😅

Overall, we highly recommend visiting Jay Fai.❤️

I had the chance to dine at Jay Fai on a Saturday late afternoon and was fortunate not to have waited long for a table. The experience was well worth it.

The crab omelette is truly excellent, bursting with generous chunks of crab meat and cooked to perfection. Another highlight is the Tom Yum soup, which is packed with flavour. The first sip comes across as salty, but it quickly evolves into a rich, addictive taste that keeps you going back for more.

The service was also commendable. The staff were very polite and approachable, making the meal even more enjoyable. Prices are on the higher side for a Thai hawker, but the quality and experience justify the splurge.

Overall, Jay Fai delivers a memorable dining experience with remarkable food and attentive service.

We visited Raan Jay Fai and finally got to try her legendary signature dish, the crab omelet. It was absolutely magical — perfectly fluffy, packed with huge pieces of crab, and unlike anything I’ve ever tasted before. Totally worth the reputation it has gained around the world.

We also ordered the drunken boat noodles, which were just as impressive. The broth carried a deep, smoky flavor that gave the dish an incredible richness, and the balance of spice and texture made it unforgettable.

The atmosphere is lively, the kitchen is open so you can watch Jay Fai at work with her iconic goggles, and the service is straightforward but efficient. Be prepared for a wait, but once you take your first bite, you’ll know it was more than worth it.

If you’re in Bangkok and love food, this is an absolute must-visit.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Worth the hype! The famous crab omelette is crispy on the outside, rich and flavorful inside — easily one of the best dishes I’ve tried in Bangkok. You can really taste the quality and effort that goes into every bite. Staff were friendly, and the open kitchen adds a fun energy. Definitely a must-try once in your life! 🦀🔥

Please, tell me what chef at 81 still being the only one cooking with this care and passion all the dishes for all the people, and after we talk.
Food is 10/10, portions are big enough, pack with flavor and not dry at all. Not salty for my taste but everybody is different, service was good, not expecting anybody coming to ask me how is everything or if I need something else when the place is pack, overall my experience was awesome.
Overpriced? Tell me what Michelin place is not, and for the amount of food, fair enough

Sea bass with fish sauce was very delicious. Sweet, mild and crispy.
Shrimp Vermicelli (Wunsen) also tasted good. The rice was overcooked unfortunately.
Nice atmosphere and decoration outside as well as great live music!
Hello from Washington State! Food is cooked to perfection. Delicious and definitely worth a visit. ❤️ Thailand 🇹🇭
Came here for lunch. Quite with few customer when I was there. Food was good. Price reasonable. Not sure what's the atmosphere like at nite.
Excellent seafood ! First time here and the food was delicious. Will be back again.
Best seafood restaurant in  Korat. Very fresh and tasty.

I am giving it all 5 out of 5 because of the big crowd of locals who were eating here as well as the Michelin Guide review, which I had already read about this restaurant.
I tried Yentafo and fish balls here. This was my first time eating this soup. The soup contains blood jelly, among other ingredients. I don't like blood, and it was quite a task to finish the meal, which I successfully did thanks to so many locals clearly enjoying their experience in the seats around me!
I am too inexperienced in Thai cuisine to be able to have a different opinion than the majority. So, yes: Highly recommended 👌

Good noodle shop close to Yamo, and very popular place with the locals. Only has two kinds of soup, yentafo (which most people were having) and a "clear" soup (which was a bit boring. Ok quality noodles, but the bamee were of the "cheaper", very yellow, variety. Meat and meat balls also ok. Not a real favourite,  but not bad.
Nice local food, service nice
Payment medthode with cash only
Came for breakfast, nice weather  today, cooling. Food was great n delicious. Nice to have someone speaking teochew since I don't speak Thai.

A friendly, clean authentic restaurant offering some great Asian cuisine. We ate a wide range of dishes including northern sausage, Khao Soi, fried pork wantons, pork larb, northern Thai curry and more. I cannot express how tasty they all were. A visit here is highly recommended

Stumbled upon this place and loved the Khao Soi!
The owner was so helpful in explaining to me the dishes in English.

Ordered:
Khao Soi Beef (10/10 Utterly delicious with a balanced taste of coconut milk with the curry. Served with thick yellow noodles with crispy noodles and huge chunks of beef, that's soft and easily chewed on.)
Nam Ngeaw Fishball (8/10 Served with vermicelli noodles with pig's blood, fish balls and crab cakes)
Northern Thai Sausage (8/10 delicious and meaty Thai sausages that aren't dry and filled with herbs)
Pork Cracklings (crispy, goes well with the noodles)

Will definitely visit again when I'm in town.

This place has been awarded a Michelin award for its top noodle dish. My wife had chicken, me pork. Both fried & steamed noodles plus pork ribs, / drumstick meat falling off the bones., Unami forward broth Pictures dont do it justice.

It’s pretty decent North-style Thai food which is rare to find outside North of Thailand. I recommend their ข้าวซอย & ขนมจีนน้ำเงียว which is ok for me. plus, the staffs are so lovely to service you. Just in case, you are looking for something for lunch, this place should be on your list as well.

Highly recommend this place for it's top notch food and friendly staff.

I had mixed meat Kao Soi which was great (as expected) but also Larb Moo. The latter is a must-taste for anyone who likes this dish because they make it pretty differently to standard Larb Moo (more spices).

A must see when in Udon Thani. And I shall also mention that their prices are very good!

Withilarb Chareonmuang feels like a truly local gem, authentic and full of Northern Thai vibes. I ordered the pork sausage has a nice kick spicy and savory with bold flavors. The chicken soup? Super spicy, thanks to the herbal mix and strong ginger notes, but it warms you up in the best way. I loved the deep-fried pork has a crispy texture on the outside but still juicy and chewy inside. And when you dip it in their green chili sauce? it's a game-changer. Everything just works together so well, it's simple, honest, and full of flavor.

The raw beef larb here is surprisingly easy to eat — the flavors are well-balanced, not overly spicy, and very enjoyable. Fresh herbs give it a fragrant touch, and it pairs perfectly with the crisp vegetables. The side dishes like the fluffy omelet, crispy fried fish, and fresh greens make the meal complete. Overall, it’s delicious, easy to enjoy, and not too intense in flavor — a great pick for anyone who loves Northern style food.

A truly deserving michelin label! The food was fantastic. I loved larp kwai kua (dried minced Buffalo beef  stir fried in Thai northern style). Varieties of som tum (papaya salad) which you accustomed to your spicy level by telling the waiter. Highly recommended!

This unassuming wooden building buried in an alley serves exceptional Lanna food. The folks at our table had an omelette with pork, chicken, fried pork belly, raw buffalo salad flavored with bile, noodles with pork curry, egg with fermented pork, and slices of buffalo. All were simple. All were skilfully prepared. All were superb. Our Thai hosts say that the dishes are very characteristic of the region and prepared in traditional style. Service was efficient, friendly, and polite. Prices were very reasonable for the quality of the meal

Small but cozy restaurant of northern Thai food.
Portion is ok, not small and not much big. This is good for trying more menu.
I do love hung-lay curry and stir-fried mined pork with local herbs.
Price is good too.

I ate here since it wasn't receive Michelin star for so long, then several years later they received the star. Anyway the food quality is still a good standard, I consider most reasonable price for this quality.

Ingredients are from local fisheries, I recommend to order prawn/ horse crab by dish (if you prefer by weight that also apply). You can ask ingredients of the day for the recommendation dishes as well.

I would recommend to check on the lunar calendar as well, for spring tide you may have abundance choices of seafood.

Pls don't expect the extraordinary treatment like you're in hotel or foreigners taste of food it's quite original Thai taste. They're friendly local doing there best they could provide.

This place is the most underrated and the most unexpected place to visit. I’ve been in a lot of places. This place is mind blowing. Go with what the chef suggests. Ask for prices before making the order. Mind blowing food.

An absolutely outstanding meal in the most humble of settings. The steamed fish with soy sauce and ginger was the most amazing fish I’ve ever eaten. It was insanely good. The very kind owner even drove us the 3km back to our villa to avoid the rain storm. For an authentic experience we highly recommend this eatery. Michelin endorsed, which is how we found it - a well deserved endorsement.
Literally one of the best restaurant I've been to in Thailand. Fresh seafood and the food is so cheap compared to Phuket! We came here 2 days in a row! Strongly recommended!!

This small, authentic local restaurant from the Michelin Guide is an absolute must-visit. It’s not about fancy interiors, but about truly delicious food and a welcoming atmosphere. The owner is incredibly hospitable, making you feel like a cherished guest rather than just a customer.
The menu focuses on seafood, and everything we tried was outstanding. We had fish and shrimp—both fresh, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor. Prices are very reasonable, especially considering the quality.

If you’re looking for an affordable yet top-tier local dining experience with a touch of true hospitality, this is the place to go!
Nice local place, popular with the locals on a Friday lunchtime.  Tasty fish, crab curry, chicken with cashew nuts. Open air with some fans and next to a fairly busy minor road.

Affordable price with very good portion
If you wanna have many dishes, this restaurant is recommended

But deep fry fish is way too cold, seems it has been prepared before we order

Kang som is a bit too sour

In total it is a good choice for Chonburi restarant
Seafood is fresh. Recommend Tamarind seafood soup, squid in any flavor. Service is passive, table is too small for more than 4 persons.

No wonder this is a Michelin listed restaurant. Amazing seafood. Known for its fried Mackerel, but the other items are amazing. Best crab fried rice that I ever have had! Order your food from the table using an app. Use Google translate to copy and paste and you won’t have any problem. They bring the food to the table and you pay the bill at the end! Worth the trip from Pattaya

Very busy and one must be observant and quick to grab any table that becomes available.  You also need to write down your selection of food from the menu on a piece of paper (in Thai) together with your table number (found printed in a sticker on the table), and hand it to any available staff. Waiting for the food took a long time (roughly 30 minutes) and it was reasonably good and low cost.  It was something I would not normally drive from BKK just to indulge in, but was a Good experience as it served fish eggs (fish roe) dishes.

restaurant_name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
review_text: Nice Khao Lam, stall vendors very friendly. Can park in front of the stall.

restaurant_name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
review_text: Following the review, it is considered delicious Khao Lam. Shots of 4 for 200 baht and small bamboo tubes of 5 for 100 baht. The price varies depending on the size of the bamboo. Shots are for those who like sweet, rich coconut milk, but it's a bit less. The bamboo tubes have soft rice inside and sweet coconut milk on top. Not too sweet, just right.

restaurant_name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
review_text:
Soft sticky rice with a not-too-sweet topping.
Deserving of a Michelin star 👑 ☺️
Eating it brings back the charm of traditional Thai desserts.
Other sticky rice brands are probably delicious in their own way.

restaurant_name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
review_text:
Stopped by to buy some before going back to Bangkok. Been eyeing it for a long time.
- We bought the regular size 5 shots of sticky rice with black sticky rice = 200 baht, and the small size 4 pieces of long sticky rice = 100 baht.
- The vendor gave us a free small shot.
The taste was delicious, a bit too sweet for us. The sticky rice was a bit soggy but soft (I like it personally) because they put in a lot of sweet coconut milk and roasted it. Compared to the regular sticky rice from the shops, the sticky rice is drier and has more grains of rice.

restaurant_name: Khao Lam Mae Khai Toon Klao
review_text: The most delicious Khao Lam in my life. Fresh from the oven, sweet, fragrant, delicious. The rice is loose and not too sticky. It is worthy of being a Michelin-starred restaurant. In addition, the vendor is very cute. Let me try the whole tube and even gave some extra.

What an incredible experience! This place redefines fine dining! It’s cool, creative, and full of energy. We were lucky enough to enjoy the creative menu by not just one, but two chefs: Roger feat. Dan Bark. The fusion dishes were packed with flavor and beautifully presented. The whole team was super professional, creating such a fun and welcoming vibe. Great music, great atmosphere. One of the best dining experiences we've ever had!

I popped into Fuego for dinner on my own and was met with such a friendly, comfortable vibe from the moment I walked in. So thankful to BJ, Laine and Chef for that.

As someone eating solo, I appreciated BJ’s spot-on recommendations (nothing too big, everything delicious). The Ankimo toast looks simple but hits like a flavour bomb — one of the highlights for me. The suggested  Bonita Mochi cocktail  was gorgeous and not overly sweet despite how it looks, its flavours were really well balanced. Every plate was beautifully presented and tasted as good as it looked.

The setting is gorgeous, the staff were attentive and friendly, they made sure the whole night felt warm and welcoming. The unexpected fire show was a nice addition to the experience. I’ll definitely be back next time I’m in town and I’ll make sure to bring a friend so I can sample more of the menu!

BUENAS!! Great vibes, super fun Spanish food. Only a few veggie options, but vibes were so good I was happy to be there. My non veg friends loved the food! Good wine, staff are very fun and open, and really good music taste! Umami Salad was delicious!!

Five-star experience all around! Ming, our server, was extremely knowledgeable of the set menu that my date and I went with. Food is deserving a Michelin starred. Drink selection is unlimited, with an amazing curation of alcohol to choose from. Lane was also a pleasure to chat with. She occasionally checked in amongst the chaos of a vibing restaurant. Reservations are hard to get during weekends, be sure to book in advance!

My recent visit to Feugo was a delightful experience. The ambiance was warm and inviting, creating a relaxing &  atmosphere. The Wagyu truffle Bikini and Ankimo toast were perfect and flavors were amazing. The service was attentive by Khun Mint (waitress at our table). Chef was friendly making us feel well taken care of. Highly recommend this restaurant for a memorable dining experience.

This charming local eatery requires advance reservations and pre-ordering of meals, ensuring a personalized dining experience. With only two exclusive tables, it offers an intimate chef’s table ambiance. The cuisine is exceptional, featuring authentic Southern Thai dishes with bold, rich flavors, served in generous portions. Due to the meticulous preparation by the two dedicated chefs, additional orders may require some patience. However, the culinary excellence makes this restaurant a must-visit destination—one that beckons for a return.
The food is really delicious; however, you will need to book a table and place your order in advance.

Very tasty and authentic southern Thai food. You have to book and order in advance. Seatings are inside Thai style house, not very comfy but taste of food is worth visiting. Been there twice and will be back again.
The local food, very delicious strong taste I like it very much. In the house you need booking in advance due to there are 3 tables only.

Tried sending a Facebook message regarding a meal reservation 2 weeks ago end June for a end July occasion. Zero response.

If they have a FB account and post on it. They must have access and should respond. Unless they provide where, how and the specifics of reservations. No one will be the wiser.

Guess they must think themselves pretty special and really above it all...

The roti that you can't miss in the city! It's so authentic and delicious. Michelin certified and halal friendly. The base of roti is like thin and soft kulit lumpia, the sweet itself comes from sugar hair shaped which is very good combined with roti. I bought 2 pcs to be taken away to Bangkok and the taste is still good 👌

Good food. Fragrant wrapping. Not too sweet. generous amount of cotton candy. Must also try the pandan wrapping. Could be better if there are more tables to enjoy the food on the spot. but overall, a very nice experience for food tasting
If you're visiting Ayutthaya and craving freshly made, delicious Roti Sai Mai, this is the place to go! We never miss it.
This shop is very famous Cotton Candy in Ayutthaya… There are many flavors of breads.. I enjoyed them…

It is the famous desert in Ayuthaya. If you visit this city you must try it. You can find many shops that sell it and many stalls beside the road but this shop is one of the most famous and you can find it near the hospital... 2 packs of 10 crepes each and sugar floss cost 100 baht.

Baan Suriyasai is an elegant Thai restaurant in a restored mansion, serving royal Thai cuisine from the Rama V era. Guests love its refined flavors and ambiance—perfect for a sophisticated Thai dining experience!

Baan Suriyasai offers an immersive experience into Thailand’s royal culinary traditions. Set in a beautifully restored heritage house, it combines history, culture, and gastronomy in a single visit. The dishes are intricate, using authentic recipes with premium ingredients. From spicy curries to delicate desserts, every plate tells a story. The staff are impeccably trained, and the whole evening feels refined yet welcoming. This is Thai fine dining at its most elegant.

Good authentic Thai food (nothing too fascinated), with a little milder taste than usual. Classical Thai ambience.

But, service is kind of rude. Our waiter has quite bad attitude regarding number of dishes we order. (We are a group of 7. we ordered 2 sets of premium sharing sets for 3 with total of 14 dharing dishes and ordered a few extra desserts, but was (rudely) asked to ordered few more a la carte dishes, when we couldn't even finish the food in the set we ordered.
Had a great authentic Thai cuisine at Ban Suriyasai. Every dish was delicious and nicely presented.
