Absolutely adore this place! 🫶 authentic Thai cuisine with recipes originating from the palace kitchens! The dishes are not only exquisitely presented but also meticulously crafted. The ambiance effortlessly captures the essence of Thai heritage, beautifully melding a vintage Thai-inspired setting. Home Taste truly represents the essence of authenticity.

Very popular local restaurant.

I don’t normally give five stars for a review. It really have to be fantastic to earn that   But this one, I rated them five stars   Since I stated in Ubon for 6 nights, I had dinner there every night.

Staff didn’t speak English much. But they were helpful and friendly, they tried hard to communicate with me.

Food was very good, 3 dishes every night by myself and no one single dish repeated.  Many choice and very good price.

Highly recommend

A lot of delicious dishes are here with reasonable price.
The free parking space is behind the store.

The affordable Michelin restaurant that we come back many times.

Parking is available at the back.

Most dishes are Thai-Chinese style, and tasty

An unassuming local eatery opens until late night with Michelin that sounds promising but disappointing

The fish was not fresh with mushy texture, while moo krop was hard. Gongpo chicken is a flop in terms of taste

Not even worth a 4 star on Google Maps

One of the best restaurant in Ubon. This restaurant also is recognized by Michelin bib gourmand in 2023 and 2024.

Food here is so tasty and service is super fast. Follow the recommended dishes and you will have such a great meal.

Will definitely be back again!

What an experience! While it may be a little tricky to find, once you arrive you step into an absolute oasis. Harry, our server, was incredibly kind—he translated and explained both the menu and the history of the restaurant with great detail. Each dish was presented with care and an in-depth explanation, making the experience not only delicious but also meaningful. The flavors were a true explosion—authentic, vibrant, and memorable.

Thank you for having us! I can highly recommend this place to both locals and visitors alike.

Very nice and homy restaurant.

It is a kind of chef table restaurant. You need to book in advance and if it is your first time, there is a set menu which chef already selected their best dishes for you. Please understand before book your table.

This is our first time too. We booked for 2 people and these pictures are the set for 2. It is more than enough for us.

All of their dishes are homemade Thai style dish, not Northern Thai food. These dishes are their own recipe which you cannot found in other restaurant. The combination of ingredients are very good. The complexity and mixture of flavour suprised me.

A must try authentic Thai food. As a Thai person, I can say that the food is very good and interesting. I didnt even know some dishes before. All dishes were made with love and high quality! When we were there it was 600THB per person (4 dishes + 1 dessert) but can refill everything. The garden was so beautiful. The entrance is quite hidden and deep but very good experience.

A fabulous setting matched only in the bold flavours. This restaurant combines a family feel with historical grandeur. The owner is warm and friendly and does everything to make you feel like part of the family. The fact you also have the option of dining within the family home gives a unique experience for travellers who may be missing the family feel. I highly recommend the pork ribs and cabbage a dish that reminds you what cooking is about, soul and passion.

A great place to have a traditional Central Thai cuisine. If you come for the first time, they will provide you with a standard set of four different menus. All can be refilled with a flat price of 500 baht per person. For your second visit, you can contact them in advance to choose different menus available from the list in the last picture. The vibe is awesome. The place is located in the woods with great sound of nature.

They serve traditional Phuket-style stir-fried noodles from way back in 1952 ⏳and it even won a Michelin award!🌟 Pad Thai was so good, seriously impressive. I also tried boiled black sugarcane juice for the first time here — kinda mildly sweet and a bit unusual, but actually pretty good. Food came out fast, and the staff were super friendly. Loved it! 🫶🏻

**Phuket Local Noodle (Sapam Noodles)**
Staff: Great service.
Food: Tasty! They serve Sapam noodles, Pad Thai, and other local dishes. The fish balls are delicious, and they also have *Oh-Eew* and *A-Pong*, traditional Phuket dessert.
Parking: Plenty of parking lot

Nice traditional Thai restaurant, recommended by the Michelin guide. The cuisine stays true to the authentic flavors of Thailand, with a perfect balance of sweet and savory. The dishes are well-prepared and flavorful, with particularly tender and tasty meat.

The location is simple, situated along a road, with tables both indoors and outdoors. If you choose to dine outside, the noise from passing traffic can be noticeable, but the atmosphere remains pleasant. The service is kind and attentive, and the prices are fair.

A great choice for those looking for an authentic Thai culinary experience!
This has become my second favorite restaurant in Phuket. The food here is cheap and very delicious, and the staff are also friendly. I will keep coming here.
Very local authentic hokkien mee. Very delicious fish ball. Yam fried with oyster and many many good food !!!

Riverside Thai restaurant with their famous grilled River prawn. If you plan to come here after 12:00 I’d recommend reservation in advance(River prawns also should be reserved too). They offer variety of Thai foods which were all very delicious with reasonable price. The grilled river prawns have many sizes/prices to choose from. They were heavenly tasty, juicy and perfectly prepared! After you order Grilled river prawns, they will be a menu which the prawns’s claw meat will be used to make such as stirred fried with seasonings, omelet and etc. for a special price.
If you have UOB credit card I highly recommend to use them as they likely are main sponsor for this restaurant and have special promotions.

As a chef, I Definitely recommend this place foods was Delicious!! Flavour full and authentic Thai food.

Prawns in tamarind sauce well balanced with fresh pineapple and crispy fried Betal leaf.

Spicy Pork minced stir fried  lots of heat and chilli but you got a side herbs fresh Cumin leaves,cucumber,snake beans,white turmeric and pickles garlic OMG you don’t want to miss this one if you are a chilli eater like me.

Tom Klong catfish ,  fresh herbs clear broth with deep fried catfish. Like no other Thai curry,none coconut base soup but light and fresh herbs plus a kick of chilli makes it incredible dishes.

Fast and kind service good atmosphere family friendly you name it.

All in all, you won’t be disappointed if you pick this restaurant for your lunch or dinner.

Recommended!!!

It was a fantastic dining experience! The food was excellent, and the service was both efficient and genuinely warm. The staff were very friendly and accommodating. The seafood was particularly impressive and could be adjusted to suit our spice tolerance.

The ambiance captured an authentic provincial Thai feel, which added to the charm. We appreciated the option of an air-conditioned area—a welcome break from the heat—while the riverside section offered a breezy and pleasant alternative for those who prefer outdoor dining.

Overall, we’d definitely rate this as one of the best restaurants we visited, especially considering the quality relative to the price.

Local restaurant just by the riverside with reasonable price and fresh ingredients. Must try the grilled fresh river prawns- juicy, sweet and well cooked. Har mok had a bunch of spices inside and was fragrant. Tomyum was kind of diluted, would skip.

Dropped by for dinner, quite a few people in, nice atmosphere, very friendly, reasonably priced and good food, have grilled river prawns, like most places priced on weight, very tasty. Overlooks river, ferry just near it taking motor bikes etc across, fascinating to watch. The frontage is set back from the road then you go through some prep/storage bit to get to it.
the food was good. i like the boiled cabbage, Hungle soup and chicken with corriander salad. the stir fried veg was good as well. The service was average. The decoration is old school vibe.

TL;DR: Elevated Thai with elevated prices.

I would rate Kiti Panit a solid 3.5 stars out of 5. This will be one of the pricier meals you'll have in Chiang Mai.

We had the Larb, Fermented Tea Leaf Salad, and Crying Tiger Beef. The Larb and Tea Leaf Salad were decent, but the Crying Tiger Beef was amazing.

Service was average. There wasn't anything that stood out good or bad.

The restaurant is set in an old general store and provided a great atmosphere. There were displays of old artifacts throughout which really brought out the history of the location.

Based on our experience, I would say give this place a try. The Crying Tiger Beef is worth it! Maybe order something else besides the Larb and Tea Leaf Salad though.

Note: Cocktails are on the light side. We could barely taste any alcohol. They were delicious, but you won't get a buzz from just one.

Went to a Michelin guide recommended restaurant. Atmosphere is good, old shop house that turned into a restaurant preserving its 5 generation of roots.

The food is alright, nothing outstanding or had a wow factor. Kao Soi was basically curry mee with mee pok [just a little overrated]. Jackfruit salad and northern pork curry were pretty good and was a little different from the standard Thai food. Jackfruit salad is a little bit nearer to the fish sauce side if you prefer less I would avoid this.

Overall a pretty decent restaurant, a little bit spenny compared to standard prices. But a nice place to bring friends/ family around for a special occasion
The food are with strong flavours. Curry slightly on salty, need to have with rice. Feel a bit uneasy as the staffs keep coming back and ask if ready to take order.

Tbh the worst food experience so far since I arrived in Chiang Mai… hot water costs 35B. Rice was hard ( in my opinion they mix new and old rice). Service is not attentive. It was basically empty and it’s still not easy to catch the waiters attention somehow. But it doesn’t stop them charging you service fee! One dish with pork and vegetables they charge 300b… and it’s tasteless! Incredible how they run the business like this.

This review is solely for the restaurant. It is amazing!  I think the secret is super fresh fiish and seafood, expertly cooked to perfection. I orgerd a deep fried catfish, it came with a saucy green papaya salad with for dipping. The catfish was cooked perfectly. Crispy on the outside and buttery moist and delicious on the inside.  Absolutely heavenly with the salad.    I apologize, I butchered the photo. I dug in before realizing that I had ruined the shot. I tried to hide my transgressions with a papaya salad. I also  got the squid and shrimp with minced pork and banana flower salad.  Delicious.
I sat on the deck downstairs. The view was amazing. The staff were equally amazing. They set up two fans for me without me having to ask. It was a memorable meal and luxurious service. Definitely lives up to its star.
Jo Bob says, check it out. That’s gen X talk. It means, it’s good go there.

This place is absolutely amazing. We stopped in today and had a very nice lunch. We ordered the fried fish, fried rice, cashew chicken and several other local dishes. It’s also very nice atmosphere and right on the water. I highly recommend.

I searched the new restaurants to try in Ayuthaya as we have been to a few places already. Overall, I’m so impressed with their design and vibe here in the evening it was so stunning and peaceful. They offer a variety of menu Thai dishes had Crab meat in yellow chili (crab deliver directly from Surat Thani), Fried fish cakes, Tom Yum (spicy soup) with River fish and Stir stir-fried spicy beef in herbs. It’s all tasty and perfectly cooked. Staffs are friendly and have great service.

I will go back and may stay overnight in a hotel as well.
Amazing, amazing, amazing! Food was so good! Everything we had was delicious and my favorite was the fried fish! I will be coming back here every time I come to Ayutthaya!
Authentic Thai food by the river. Very lovely atmosphere and decor. Want to come back for a sunset dinner or perhaps an overnight stay!
Reasonable price beef noodle. Great place for stewed beef soup and noodle if you are in Ayutthaya. Stewed beef and tendon are very tender with yummy small meatballs

Same Taste,Same Time
Wonderful,and tasty

taste never changed ,quality never down

Every time I went there,that was the time I was so happy. So delicious  and wonderful taste

Yes, agree with earlier reviews.  The beef koeyteow naam 45B here is very good and I’ll definitely be coming back for more. Having been back I gotta say this has to be best noodle soup shop I have come across in 4 days here.  I’m giving it an extra star for this. They also sell chang, a glutinous rice dumpling wrapped in lotus leaves packed with pork, mushrooms and salted eggs. Very handy for travelling.
This is delicious with tender and juicy meat. If you like it spicy, don’t forget to add the chilli paste, it’s super spicy 🥵 and 🤤 yummy
An ok place for beef noodle. Nothing to complain here. The food is worth the money?

Here Kae Pork Satay wasn’t just a food stop—it felt like visiting a friend you’ve known for years. The moment I arrived, the owner’s energy filled the place. Super lively, always smiling, and genuinely welcoming. Before I even ordered, we were already chatting, laughing, and snapping a few photos together. Looking around, the walls are absolutely covered with pictures of past customers—locals, tourists, regulars—all proudly displayed. You can tell right away this isn’t just a business for the owner; it’s a passion, a community, and something he takes real pride in.

Now, the pork satay itself—let’s just say it’s a flavor bomb. Juicy, tender pork with a hint of sweetness that hits just right. Pair that with the rich, slightly chunky peanut sauce, and you’ve got yourself a match made in street food heaven. The sweetness might surprise you at first, but it’s addictive. You’ll be reaching for stick after stick before you even realize it.

Seating here is very limited—it’s mainly a takeaway spot—but honestly, it adds to the charm. You get that bustling, street-side vibe, watching locals grab their orders while you’re soaking in the smells of fresh-grilled satay. And here’s the kicker—it’s Michelin-recognized. That little plaque by the stall isn’t just for show; every bite proves it’s well-earned.

If you’re in Bangkok and want to taste something that’s not just about the food but also the heart behind it, Here Kae Pork Satay is a must. Sweet, smoky, nutty, and served with a smile you won’t forget.

A Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant. The outside looks a little bit shabby and the menu is simple, however the pork satay I tried was really excellent. A restaurant worth visiting when visiting Ayutthaya. In addition, If you're lucky, you might meet a cute cat inside the restaurant.
Don't miss it!! The lagacy pork satay restaurant with unique taste guaranteed by Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Absolutely delicious pork satay!

I had the pork satay at Here Kae Pork Satay in Ayutthaya and it was honestly one of the best I’ve ever tried. The meat was tender, perfectly grilled, and packed with flavor. The peanut sauce was rich and creamy, and everything was served fresh and hot. You can really taste the care they put into their food.

If you're in Ayutthaya, don’t miss this place — super yummy and highly recommended!

Thai skewers at it's best! Good place! Friendly owner but limited space for dining. This dish which is featured in Malaysian, Singapore and Indonesian cuisine is basically quite similar using a peanut base sauce. This version however is pretty good, nicely charred bread goes well with the sauce. Good balance marinades with salads. Highly recommended.

Raan Tha Luang restaurant was an unfortunate stop, forced as part of a Trip Guru tour. We had to preorder meals through the guide, yet still waited 30 minutes once in the restaurant. While most guests were served quickly, one of our dishes, Pad Thai, arrived long after the first meal—cold by then. Four staff members stood watching our group rather than tracking down the missing order. Prices were fair, but a service charge was added despite the poor experience, which felt unjustified. The food tasted average, pork dish was dry, and lacked authenticity. The venue clearly caters to large tour groups over individual diners, and our Trip Guru guide made little effort to resolve the issue, preferring to enjoy their own meal. I wouldn’t choose to eat here, and Trip Guru should consider an alternative, as others in our group also found the food and value disappointing.

This was one of our favorite lunch spots of our trip. The food was delicious, and my partner specifically said this was some of the best Pad Thai she had eaten on the trip. We would definitely recommend this restaurant.

It was really quiet in terms of people present, but the guy on the guitar played in volume like it was a full stadium 🥴 (a typical Thai thing we discovered).

The morning glory was really nice.
The fried pork was not my thing, really fatty and hardly any flavor. The pineapple filled with rice was ok, but the battered chicken on top, was chewy and had a floury taste 😔

So no, we don’t recommend this place for food, service was fast and friendly and the music was better than in another place last night, but way too loud.

What an absolutely hidden gem! Live music, great food, attentive staff. Would 100% recommend. I haven't bothered writing any reviews on my whole trip, but absolutely felt I must here.

I went to 6 other restaurants looking for vegetarian food, but none of them had any. By pure chance did I find this place - they had a whole vegetarian menu! And the tofu+cashew dish was amazing.

They had live music too, and he was excellent! Created a great atmosphere. The staff brought me mosquito repellent when they saw me kill a mosquito.

A++ experience and food.

Nice place for food. We went here as part of our tour. Food ordered in advance so it came pretty promptly. I really enjoyed my pineapple rice...especially as it came in a pineapple! (Not had that before!)
Nice riverside view as well

Nice food and something diffident for us as tourists. Fish was super fresh and tender, even the fish skin is yummy. Source was different and happy we chose this place and we love all the food. Highly recommend for people who can handle bit of spicy food and explore local cuisine. We were given free papaya, even papaya was better than what we bought in other shops lol.

Authentic southern Thai seafood with great local flavors! The food is very fresh and full of spice and aroma; highly recommend the spicy stir-fried fish and the fish cakes, both delicious and perfectly seasoned. The complimentary fresh vegetables with dipping sauce were a nice touch.

The restaurant has a casual, local vibe with simple seating, and the staff are friendly and attentive. A great spot if you’re looking for affordable and tasty southern-style seafood in Khao Lak.

Definitely worth a visit if you want a real local dining experience!

Thailand has so many Michelin-certified restaurants. I've been to many of them, but a lot of places made me question their authenticity. However, the food here is truly delicious. This was my second visit, and I'll definitely go again.

Super nice roadside seafood restaurant, featured on the Michelin Guide.
The place itself is very simple, but very clean and welcoming.
I got the stir-fried fish heads with bitter lemon, and the green curry with chicken breasts.
The green curry was amazing, by far the best I’ve had. The soup itself didn’t have any vegetables. The curry taste itself was so intense, fresh and rich.
The other dish was nice as well. The sauce was very unique with the bitter lemon flavors.  It’s a rather small dish, so it’s probably better off just ordering another fried fish dish with a sweet-sour sauce.
Overall, great experience and vibe.

Overpriced but not delicious. The seafood salad only has a few seafood meats that should not cost more than 150 baht. We paid around 800 baht for 3 dishes and needed to eat somewhere else afterwards. In addition, one waitress looked annoyed all the time. The only good dish is crab fried rice. The rest you can find better in other restaurants. Don’t get trapped by “Michelin star” claim. There are so many others out there in Pang-nga. You can skip this one.

This place was such a pleasant surprise, a hidden gem. The food was so delicious. Especially the pad thai! Friendly fast service. The smoothies weren't the best, though! Low prices (100 baht for a chicken and pork pad thai or yellow noodles) . Solid portions (not huge, but adequate).

Lovely place. The service and atmosphere were great and the food was really tasty too!

Good selection of Thai food and some Western too. All available in tofu.

I ordered the Chicken Khao Soi and they offered to add more coconut cream if it was too spicy. It was just spicy enough though so it wasn't needed!

We will be back.

Little gem with delicious food!! A must when you visit Koh Tao! The atmosphere is very calming with a little jungle surrounding you, music is soothing, and the people working here are friendly and welcoming!

The service is also quite quick while serving 10/10 dishes! I wish I took photos of our main meal, bit after the first bite it was quickly devoured because it was so tasty! We had one green chicken curry, Khao Soi chicken and mango sticky rice.

Mouth watering, stylish, and friendly restaurant!

We visited this restaurant after work. It was quite busy, but we didn’t had to wait too long for our food to arrive. We ordered a red curry and prawns in tamarind sauce. The red curry wasn’t like a curry we’ve had before in Thailand, it was a bit different yet tasty. But the prawns were definitely outstanding. The tamarind sauce was so delicious. We will definitely come back just for the prawns. The service was good and friendly.

Best Khao Soi in town. Must try! Huge portions, super tasty. Very nice staff.
It got my girlfriend wet. The smoothie Passion Fruit & Mango was so yummy. Coming back again for mango sticky rice

Thai North Food Original is located in the eastern part of Bangkok. I visited the restaurant five years ago, and at that time, the queue was incredibly long due to its popularity. Recently, they’ve expanded the seating capacity to accommodate over 100 guests, making it much more comfortable for diners. The new design beautifully showcases traditional Northern Thai architecture, adding an authentic and cultural touch to the dining experience.

Despite the growth and renovations, the food remains consistently delicious, preserving the rich flavors and quality that made it famous. The menu features a variety of Northern Thai specialties, each prepared with care and traditional ingredients. The ambiance now feels more spacious and welcoming, perfect for both locals and tourists seeking a taste of Northern Thailand in the heart of Bangkok.

Rate it 5. 😋😋

• Good but not excellent

• One of the most popular Northern-style Thai restaurants in Bangkok, offering hundreds of dishes on the menu. The taste is authentic with unique ingredients, good but not excellent.

• The atmosphere is decorated in true Northern style, giving you the feeling of dining in Chiang Mai.

• It’s  5 stars, but if you come with very high expectations, it might feel more like 4.

An authentic Northern Thai restaurant awarded Bib Gourmand. The food is tasty and offers traditional flavors, though some dishes feel a bit small for the price. Service is okay but not very attentive, and ordering can be a bit slow even when it’s not busy.

You don’t have to travel all the way to Chiang Mai to enjoy authentic Northern Thai food — Bangkok has it too! From Khao Soi, Hang Lay Curry, Nam Prik Noom to Larb Kua, every dish is packed with rich flavors and aromatic spices. The cozy atmosphere makes it feel just like dining in the North.
This northern cuisine with Michelins awards was newly renovated and expanded. The kao soi beef was creamy and intense in flavor with soft tendon beef. The fried chicken was super crispy and juicy.

My boyfriend had planned a VIP afternoon cruise at this establishment, and the experience was absolutely wonderful.

Everything was perfectly arranged, from the pre-cruise communication to the reception, the cruise itself, and the restaurant. A little tip: come hungry! Upon arrival, we were offered Thai desserts while waiting for the boat. On board, several snacks were also available, and drinks were unlimited (Coke, water, orange juice, wine).

The staff was incredibly attentive, respectful, and caring. We had the option to step off the boat to visit temples or simply enjoy sightseeing from the river.

After the cruise, we were treated to a restaurant experience with a generous and diverse selection of dishes.

The staff even took photos of us to capture the moment.

And the highlight of it all… I left with my fiancé, not just my boyfriend, because he proposed to me on the boat! A perfect and idyllic moment, despite the rainy weather.

An unforgettable experience that I highly recommend!

We had an awesome experience at SuriyanChandra Restaurant in Ayutthaya, Thailand. This beautiful riverside restaurant serves some authentic and delicious Thai cuisine and desserts. While waiting for the boat ride, we were served an array of Thai snacks and desserts. Then you get to taste more unique Thai food and drinks during the river tour. And the setup for dinner was so beautiful with the nice and relaxed ambiance, the orchids, the chandeliers and lighting, the beautifully presented food all deserved a praise. The staff were friendly and attentive. Amazing service, excellent Michelin starred food, nice atmosphere… we had an amazing time here!

This place is absolutely beautiful. Great for a family trip as they also take you on a boat tour(for a price)
Food is a bit too much on the sweet side and you can pretty much get more tasty-authentic Thai food elsewhere.
The place still worth a visit though if you are already in Ayutthaya sightseeing, it’s not too far from the main attraction in the city but don’t expect anything from their food.

Thai movie stars, hi society individuals and in-the-know tourists love this unique restaurant experience. The food is delicious and must be experienced. Many dishes are from Royal recipes changing your mind about what "real Thai food" is. This is something extraordinary. If you are an expat, with friends and family visiting, take them here. Blow their minds into the environmental realm of Thai elegance. The concept is taking an old rice mill, and turning it into an upscale restaurant located on the river.
After dinner or lunch? How about renting their boat for a few hours of a luxury tour on the river. You will be pleased.

Was served a myriad of authentic Thai food. Atmosphere was quaint and relaxed. Boat trip after the lunch was also a relaxing way to spend the afternoon, but the view was monotonous and perhaps not the most exciting way to be on a boat for 2 hours... A pleasant experience nonetheless.

Let’s start off with saying that the products they use and the way they cook them is really perfect. The noodles were chewy, the broth was deep in umami flavours and the dishes were beautifully presented.

We had a booking at 1pm and got our food + the explanation of the staff on how to eat it around 1:15pm.
I was enjoying my main with stilll half of my dish left when they said the dessert was coming in 10min. I was a little shocked by this because you pay quite a lot for a premium set for Bangkok terms (around 1300 baht pp) and I like to enjoy my food and take my time to eat.

Even though we were only eating for 20min, the dessert already arrived and I was forced to mix my main with my dessert (it was a matcha sorbet so I couldn’t just wait to eat it untill I finished my main). This was just absolutely rude.

While we were eating our dessert, they already came with the bill and asked us to pay.
We were in and out the restaurant in 45min even though you normally get 1h.

It felt like a rip off… 3500 baht for two people for an awfull service is not worth it even though the food itself was lovely.

Wouldn’t recommend and wouldn’t go back. It’s not worth the hype imho.

Fantastic noodles.
Cooked with meticulously care and passion. Chef is preparing your dish in front of you. All products (except egss and chicken) are imported from Japan.
Wonderful food I will go back again!

I was fortunate enough to snag a last minute cancellation, what a fantastic restaurant this is!

The staff are all very friendly, helpful and informative. Not to mention that they do everything like clockwork, smooth and seemingly effortless.

The food itself is a spectacle, could not fault it at all. Very impressed with the service, the flavours and the assistance if needed.

Definitely a good idea to sharpen up your chopsticks skills because these noodles are going to make you work for it haha.

They explain all the components of the menu and ensure your preferences are met.

If you fancy something different from the local Thai food then I seriously suggest you try get a booking here, it is in fairness, inexpensive and the quality is truly a marvel.

Thank you to everyone and hopefully see you soon!

Got the signature premium set. It was so good and worth the try. Pricey but worth it. Prefer the beef bowl > pork bowl. Able to enjoy ramen with different condiments which make it difference. The service is top-tier. Lady took a great care of us. Definitely recommended

No Name Noodle — small, quiet, and only 7 seats.
Each bowl feels like art — handmade noodles, rich broth, deep umami.
Only a few bowls a day, so booking is a must.
Pricey, yes, but every bite worth it.
Feels more like a calm little experience than just a meal 🍜✨

Tried this restaurant after hearing it earned a Michelin 2025 award – the pasta was perfectly al dente, though as a Thai I would prefer slightly bolder flavors.

Prices are high as expected for a hotel, but the service was excellent. Special thanks to Sud for being so friendly and attentive, always recommending dishes. Nice wine promotion (though limited selection).

Atmosphere is casual not so Romantic for couple ; the garden seats are lovely if you don’t mind the heat.

Customer Experience Score : 4.5/5
Will I come again : yes, surely 👍

Andaz Jomtien offers a solid food service for gourmets and foodies with 3 kitchens 3 Italian 🇮🇹, Thai 🇹🇭 and Steak 🥩. The level of food quality is very high, and the dishes served are exquisite ❤️.

There is a lot of cooking experience in these kitchens. The service is very good and the restaurant atmosphere, both inside and outside 🌳, makes the stay at Andaz very unique.

A true moment of calm 😇 and tasty food 🥗🍤 for any day and any time of the year.

Highly recommended 😍 and open to walk-in !

Nestled within the lush grounds of Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach, La Cucina brings the warmth and richness of southern Italian cuisine to life with a refined yet welcoming ambiance. Helmed by Chef Vincenzo Gatti, this Michelin Selected 2025 restaurant pays homage to the culinary heritage of Naples with passion, authenticity, and flair.

Our meal began with a vibrant salad, delicately balanced with fresh greens, juicy cherry tomatoes, and a light vinaigrette that awakened the palate without overpowering the natural flavors. The star of the evening was the Parma ham pizza — a masterpiece of simplicity. The crust was perfectly blistered, crisp on the edges and tender at the center, topped with velvety slices of Parma ham, creamy mozzarella, and it goes well with chilli oil. Each bite transported us to the streets of Naples.

For the main, we shared a beautifully cooked beef steak, served medium well as requested. It was seared to perfection, juicy and flavorful, with a subtle char that hinted at fired technique. The accompanying roasted potatoes added depth and balance, rounding out a deeply satisfying course. The red wine sauce was amazing.

The service was warm and attentive without being intrusive, and the atmosphere added a lively energy to the dining experience. Whether seated indoors in the cozy style room or outdoors with a scenery of home grown vegetables that used for every dish, the setting complements the soulfulness of the cuisine.

La Cucina isn’t just a hotel restaurant — it’s a destination in its own right. Chef Gatti’s commitment to southern Italian flavors and his respect for tradition make this one of the standout dining experiences in Pattaya. For lovers of Italian cuisine, La Cucina is an essential visit.

Such great food here! The service from Khun Aoffy was also spectacular. The cuttlefish with mashed potatoes filling and the fish was the best part! The atmosphere was calm and relaxing. I recommend this place if you’re looking for an Italian restaurant in Pattaya.
The food and service was impeccable, especially received great service from Guy and Ning. Definitely recommend dining at this restaurant when staying at Andaz Pattaya.

This city is renowned for its famous local food, and one of the best places to try it is a restaurant that specializes in a unique kind of boiled rice. Unlike porridge, this dish is cooked to perfection, with each grain separate and tender. The seafood in this city is exceptionally fresh, and the restaurant serves a delightful selection of prawns, squid, oyster and fish. Not only do they offer meat, but they also serve other parts of the seafood such as the head, roe, and organs, making it a true feast for seafood lovers. Being a fan of this cuisine, I highly recommend reserving a slot to savor these delicious dishes when visiting this city.

I feel unfairly treated by your lies. I went to your restaurant at 8:45pm and you informed us that all seafood was sold out, except for fish. So I ordered what was available. I got fried fish with rice, which took 25 minutes to arrive. It was beyond the norm, but I felt bad when other people got other seafood, like shrimp, squid.Most importantly, they received the food after I had ordered for several tables. I felt discriminated against. You should be more honest.
Traditional porridge sea food  khao tome. Good taste, fresh. Recommend the dry fried one which never find some where else.

The dry rice with duck and the dry rice with stir-fried fish are very delicious, with a soft and smooth taste. The price is reasonable, but parking can be a bit challenging. I will find time to come back again.
Original taste of boil rice with duck or seafood.

• An old-style local restaurant located on Rangsit–Nakhon Nayok Road. I had passed by many times without noticing it, until it was featured by a youtubers.

• The menu is traditional and meets the local standard. The highlight is the roasted pork, which is good, but don’t set your expectations too high based solely on youtuber reactions.

• Be prepared for a long wait during peak hours, especially on weekends, as the restaurant tends to get very crowded.

• Parking is conveniently available near the police station.
Family business, Taste is above average, price is reasonable, no air condition, the lady owner is friendly. No proper parking area.

Old restaurant, old chef. Fresh ingredients, but mild taste for me. River prawns are fresh fried with lots of garlic, but not tasty. Seafood sauce is quite sour with a bit sweet, not tasty.  Squid is fresh stir fry with chilli paste. Taste sweet and sour. Not spicy,  Parking is quite far, not convenience.

One of the best home cook meals I ever have in my life! Hidden by roadside of Rangsit-Nakhon Nayok road is this small restaurant by aunties and uncles that remind you of your grandma's kitchen. Tom yum is not very spicy, yet it is really intense. Taste of lime and dried chilli mixed together is sooo good. A lot of fish fillets are given in just on pot of tom yum, without any fishbone. I was surprised by the size of river prawns, and even by its freshness too! Really worth the price in my opinion, though. There's also a non-spicy dish like fried mixed vegetable with vermicelli that is really delicious as well. Last but not least, don't forget about red-grilled pork too.

11/10 would recommend my friends and family to eat at this place 🥰

Food is so so. Doesn't live up to the hype
No Parking available
Crowded
No reservation taken

Not knowing what to have for dinner, the sign of Bisou caught my eye. Out of curiosity, I walked in. The location feels quite mysterious, with strong design aesthetics and a romantic ambiance—and it even holds a Michelin star for 2025. Following the staff's recommendation, I ordered the sea urchin pasta and broccoli. The sea urchin was incredibly fresh with a rich, intense flavor 👍. For dessert, I tried the tiramisu, which was prepared in a unique way but tasted delightful. To top off the experience, they offered artistically crafted macarons and Limoncello . The staff were very very welcoming and nice.—I truly enjoyed the service. I think I made an absolutely excellent choice 👍

As a Thai, I’m usually pretty skeptical about European food (I’m always worried it might be too bland for my Thai palate 😂), but Bisou completely blew me away.

This isn’t your typical French food, every dish has such clever flavour combos that just work. We tried their signature Beef Wellington for the first time and honestly, my only complaint is that I wanted more of it. Any of their crudos are also amaaazing, super fresh and tasty. And that cherry dessert… I still can’t stop thinking about it.

On top of the food, the staff were super friendly and fun, which made the night even better. Overall, just a really great experience. Can’t wait to go back!

Hands down the best bar and restaurant we’ve ever been to. For our last friendship trip (for now), this place made it unforgettable—especially for our two brides. The food was incredible, with the truffle pasta being the best I’ve ever had in my life. We’ll definitely be recommending and coming back. Huge thanks to Jack, Bank, and Pon for making our night so special! ❤️

Had a lovely birthday dinner here & I highly recommend this place. Staff service is spectacular. They were highly attentive to us from the moment we stepped in, constantly checking in  us. Food is great. Service is one of THE BEST. Thank you to the staff for the good time 😊👍🏻👍🏻

Staffs service are exceptional. Everyone here are so nice. Have to look for the guy who take a very nice shot of photo. The food is extraordinary as well. I love tomato capaccio and ototo tartare. Very  fresh, refreshing and load of complex richness of flavors

Lung Khajohn Wat Ket

109 Charoen Rajd Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50000, Thailand

This humble shop opens for breakfast. They specializes in tapioca dumplings—freshly cooked tapioca wrappers—stuffed with sweet pork and peanut, and steamed rice dumpling. Reminds me of fresh lumpia without the veggies but with coconut milk and toasted nuts and garlic.

What a good way to start a day full of explorations in Chiang Mai.

They are open 6AM to 3PM from Monday-Saturday.

PS. They only offer 2 dishes in the menu—and of course, order them all. 🤭

#BirthdayCountdown #LostinChiangMai #octobertoremember #solotravel

Super busy and seems many locals will drive by to purchase. When I came just before noon and the Khao Kriab Pak Moh was already sold out.

So opted for the Sakoo Sei Moo. The filling is slightly sweet but savory and the chewiness of wrap giving it a QQ texture.

Quite an interesting combination worth trying. They had 2 tables which you could eat there if you want.

I like  sakoo sai moo or pork rice dumpling. The flour is very soft,the stuffing is a bit salty. You can eat with vegetables and chilies. It’s so compatible. Kanom Buang Yuan or Vietnamese crepe is unique ,it’s like salad with tofu ,dry coconut ,yellow crepe and sweet dressing. It serves in the bowl if you want to eat immediately. There are only 2 tables inside. You can visit Wat Ket Karam temple ,it’s very beautiful and peaceful temple, you just cross the road from the shop to go to the temple.

They mostly sell sticky dumplings with sweet and savory fillings and prices are pretty decent.

In texture it seems somewhat like cheong fun and the fillings include chai poh, minced meat and coconut.

Yes! Yes! Yes, yes yes! This is definitely worth stopping at. They offer some thing we had never had or seen anywhere else. It describes it as dessert, but it was subtle enough to be enjoyed for breakfast. We of course tried both types. And we thought they were equally as good. And the cool thing is you walk up and they are making them right in front of you and preparing bags. And it was ridiculously cheap. You must go here if you’re in the area! It is worth trying for sure.

Review of Krua Laew Ta Arom, Pattaya: Michelin Guide 2025 Worthy!

Alright, let’s talk about Krua Laew Ta Arom—a hidden gem in Pattaya that just snagged a spot in the Michelin Guide 2025. And let me tell you, they earned it! This place is all about Thai flavors with a creative twist, and every dish has that “made-with-love” vibe.

The Food
1.	แกงส้มกุ้งไหลบัว (Gaeng Som Goong with Lotus Stems)
If tangy, spicy, and fresh had a baby, this would be it. The broth? Packed with flavor. The shrimp? Juicy as heck. And those lotus stems? Crunchy and fun to eat. This dish slaps.
2.	ซาชิมิปลาไทย (Thai Fish Sashimi)
Who says Thailand can’t do sashimi? The fish is local, fresh, and served with an epic dipping sauce that takes it to the next level. It’s Thai-style sophistication on a plate.
3.	หมึกผัดน้ำดำ (Stir-fried Squid in Ink Sauce)
This one’s a bold move. The squid is tender, the ink sauce is rich and savory, and it’s got this subtle smoky vibe. You’re gonna want rice with this—trust me.
4.	ปลาทะเลทอด (Fried Sea Fish)
Crispy, golden perfection. The fish is cooked just right, with a juicy inside and crispy skin. Pair it with their dipping sauces, and it’s game over.

The Vibes

The vibe here is super chill, like dining at a friend’s house who just happens to be an incredible chef. No fancy frills, just authentic flavors that hit all the right notes.

Final Thoughts

Krua Laew Ta Arom deserves all the hype it’s getting. Michelin Guide recognition? 100% deserved. Whether you’re a foodie or just someone who loves good food, this place is a must-visit. Go check it out—your taste buds will thank you!
Easy to park, good atmosphere,  great recommendations from chief. And yummy in the way of Thai food.
A nice and easy meal we had. Been there quite a while ago. We really enjoyed all the dishes there. Yum!
Highly recommend... Great food, good for family.

Very long wait — at least 1.5 hours, even after calling to order food 45 minutes in advance. We ordered 8 dishes but received only 3 after waiting 1.5 hours. The food was far too salty. This is my first and very last time here.

The shop is quite popular, and most of their menu items feature pork. Among the dishes we ordered, the fried rice with seafood had the most delightful flavor. The tom yum noodle had a sweeter sauce, but adding chili made it quite spicy. The pork rice was a bit salty, but not too bad.
Overall, it’s good place to try , quite many dishes to order

Excellent tasty food. The Hoijaw was soft and had big chunks of crab. The dry rice porridge was delicious. Recommended!
PS no Aircon room. Parking in compound of house immediately before the restaurant or can park off street in front of the restaurant.

I found this place while doing some research on new places to eat. The restaurant is clean and it operates from 7am-7pm and serves Thai food.

I ordered the pad krapow moo with fried egg today while the rest of the family had what you see in the photos with 3 bottles of coke and a bottle of water. The pad krapow was awesome and my wife also liked her rice dish.

The only 2 issues I had was the lack of parking lots and 180 baht for a few pieces of crispy pork (side dish). Other than that, the food was excellent. I will definitely be back here again with the family.

The outstanding menu is the fried crab ball. It's really delicious and the crab meat is big. The orange sauce is delicious too. The only downside is that it's quite expensive, 50 baht per piece 🥲

The rice soup with pork is okay.

The mixed pork soup is okay. I was probably unlucky, because some of the pork innards are smelly..

7-8 years ago the tofu skin rolls with crab was so good.  As huge as I’ve ever seen with huge crap meat inside.  All those it was quite expensive, but it was so huge and delicious that I was willing to buy it.

This month I went and bought and was so disappointed .  50 baht for just one piece and it was so tiny.  A small piece of crap meat (used to be huge ) and the rest was minced pork. Look at the picture compared to mine thumb nail and my nail is a size of a medium size man’s!!
It’s a rip off.  Will never go back to buy again.

Dropped by this place after khaosoi-i for some Michelin guide small bites ~ Fried TARO. The fried tofu is sold out, so we only tried TARO. Its flour with some small yam cubes inside. Must dip the sauce for better taste. Freshly fried cos alot ppl buying..
Can try this local snack if you are nearby.

It’s absolutely delicious. We tried the fried taro. At first, we got 12 pieces, but then realized it was amazing and bought eight more. For us, it tasted like a mix of Russian potato and mushroom pirozhki, doughnuts, and French fries. Many thanks to the staff for their attention and the excellent food. The sauce is delightful.
Crunchy… well done. Recommended

I’ve tried to come here between noon and 3pm on three different occasions, weekday and weekend, over about a week, and they have never been open. They have a sign posted saying ‘closed for one day’, but it’s obviously been much longer. Please either change your hours in google or your sign to reflect the current schedule.
The fried taro is excellent, especially with their special sauce that enhances the flavor.

We came for a quick dinner in Silom and were blown away by the place.

Beautiful atmosphere, great food, refreshing drinks and excellent service from the staff, who were fantastic with us.

It was our first time eating vietnamese food so there were some dishes which we didn't know how to prepare. Tasaporn and Thanyaret were kind and patient enough to guide us through each dish and showed us how best to prepare them to enjoy the taste to the fullest.

For those interested, this place is listed on the Michelin guide at an affordable price. All dishes that we tried were fantastic.

Definitely recommend.

We ate here in September 2024 and I forgot to do a review until I saw these pictures in my iPhone:)

4-5* for the staff, the ambience and the space - very nice and luxurious.
Unfortunately, the Vietnamese food that we ordered were very far off the mark. All dishes looked good, but taste was not only lacking, but was very inaccurate taste/flavor for authentic Vietnamese food that you might have in Vietnam, or the large Vietnamese enclave in San Jose or Los Angeles, California (we are Vietnamese American visiting from California ).  In fact, when we asked for the Vietnamese style fish sauce that goes with basically all Vietnamese food, the staff had no idea what we were talking about :/

I’m hoping the restaurant has a better Chef now to make authentic Vietnamese food.
Excellent food and great service. Nice space for relaxing meal. It a a totally different experience than when the restaurant was in the hotel.

Had a lovely first visit to this Vietnamese restaurant. The food was flavorful and refreshing 🌿🍜. Every dish was full of taste and beautifully presented. It was a great opportunity to try something new and different. Big thanks to Tasaporn and Thanyaret for the friendly and thoughtful service 🙂💚.

A beautifully & tastefully decorated restaurant in a very quiet harbored garden .very friendly service and EXCELLENT food . Everything was very fresh , refined& tasty . Great experience . One of my favorite restaurants in Bangkok .

Not sure why this place only has 4 stars in their reviews. The food is absolutely delicious, every single dish we ordered. The beef oyster sauce was fantastic! The staff is very friendly and the views on the river are beautiful too.

It is a very big restaurant suitable for bigger groups as well.
Wonderful!! Awesome. Big River Prawn. A must ! The fried noodles Out of this world ! Best best Pad Thai! Friendly Staff. And Owner. Got to visit or you did not went to Ayutthaya!
A famous restaurant in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, located by the river. The atmosphere is wonderful, every dish is delicious, and the staff provides excellent service with great attention to detail.

Opened for more than 50 years, this traditional Thai restaurant is a living legendary and continue serving their delicious menus. This place is actually one of my favorites place for my family nsine I was a young kid. Must try menus including grilled river prawn, green curry with fish ball stuffers with salted egg, Deep fried soft-fleshed fish, and many many more. Recently, Micheline Guide just have this restaurant in the list, Which make this place even more popular and hard to get the table without early booking for the busy day like weekend. Definitely go back again and again. Love this place.
Fresh grilled shrimp, reasonable price, best for couple and family, good atmosphere, nice services. Visited here for many times.

The restaurant is beautiful. The staff were great. The 10 course meal was the best executed worst food I have ever had in my life. Presentation was beautiful and creative. Taste was below average. The first two courses were promising but was a quick descent from there. We tried our best to appreciate the experience with new food combinations but it did not pan out well and by the end of the 10 course we were left utterly disappointed. I ended up sick a few hours after the meal and cannot pinpoint which dish it was particularly but if I had to guess it was the fishy tasting oyster.  Overall the meal has lasted with me for days feeling sick to my stomach and unable to eat properly. Hom's idea of unique is not one I would like to revisit.

The restaurant is very beautiful. The building is impressive, and the staff are happy to help you take a photo in front of it. Inside, there are only a few tables, which makes the atmosphere calm and special.
The service was great. The team explained each dish in good English, which made the experience more interesting.
We tried the 10-course tasting menu. Some dishes were amazing, but a few were a bit strange, like the flavors didn’t quite match.
Still, Hom is a very unique and interesting place. We’d love to come back again when they change the menu for the new season.

Last night at hom, I had the chance to experience a special collaboration with Resonance that beautifully showcased creativity, precision, and harmony.

The evening was made even more memorable by the warm welcome from Hostess Nada, the attentive hospitality of June, Bird, Min, Few, Toon and the entire kitchen team. Thoughtful wine pairings by Gowbowri elevated the journey even further. Special thanks to Chef Ricardo and Chef Shunsuke for crafting such a unique and unforgettable dining experience.

A seamless blend of flavors, artistry, and hospitality – hom is truly an unmissable destination for anyone seeking not just a meal, but a remarkable experience.

Everything was fantastic from beginning to end! Min was so gracious with her presentation of the ‘moments’ as they call their courses. Staff amazing, food exploratory and ambience to die for. Interesting choice of music that kept things perky! A must if you are in town!

It’s overpriced and overrated.
We went to Hom for dinner in a group of 8 people. (THB 7505 w/ service charge p.p.)

We were impressed by the stunning atmosphere but not the food. The fermentation heavy menus is indeed innovative but the flavours are not as appealing. Hope they can find the balance of taste and ambition.

Food is great. Crab omelet is a must try item.
However do not expect the service to be fast when crowded.
The waiter and waitress are quite very busy and seem not enough. I found only 3 staff for 9 tables. If you need something, just waive your hands stringly and tell them many times until they get the job done.
Reservation is recommended.

Tucked away with understated charm, Garlic delivers a masterclass in Thai cuisine that balances bold tradition with refined presentation. Recently recognized as a Michelin Recommended spot in 2025, it’s easy to see (and taste) why.

From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is warm and unpretentious, allowing the food to shine. Every dish bursts with flavor — from the perfectly balanced Tom Yum soup, rich with lemongrass and a whisper of heat, to the Pad Kra Pao, which brings a fiery punch softened by fragrant jasmine rice. The ingredients are clearly fresh, and the attention to detail in both spice and texture is impeccable.

What truly sets Garlic apart is how it honors authentic Thai flavors while presenting them with just enough finesse to meet Michelin’s high standards — without losing soul in the process. The staff are friendly and knowledgeable, happy to guide you through the menu and suggest the perfect heat level.
Highly recommend this everyone must try, One of the best Thai restaurants. Hot and spicy Thai food recipes. You should not miss this place! 😋

A very classic spot for decent Thai food in this neighborhood. I’ve been coming here since I was a kid, about 20 years ago, and I’ve always loved the food.

The restaurant mainly serves standard Thai dishes, with a focus on Southern cuisine. Their signature dish is the crab omelet, but personally, I really love their kaeng som. It’s one of the best I’ve ever had. Every other dish I’ve tried here has never disappointed me. Also, the rice is refillable for just 15 baht.

The place has a cozy, homey atmosphere that makes you feel like you’re eating at home. It’s perfect for family gatherings or casual meetups with friends.

I just noticed that they are now listed in the Michelin Guide, which is very well deserved.

Amazing, delicious, homecooked style, authentic Thai food in a humble, cosy setup with reasonable prices. Loved every dish, from the crab omelette to pomelo salad and even down to the ultra fragrant white rice! Absolutely recommend topping off such a satisfying meal with the signature housemade coconut ice cream topped with sweet corn and roasted peanuts, what a treat. Great service. 100% looking forward to our next visit to try even more from the menu. Restaurant was packed, reservations are definitely a must.

I like the way that food combine the taste together to be perfect match. Chef has so much skills of cooking and detailing knowledge about each ingredient  to create the paradised tasty without condiment. One main dish with condiment or sause creat the fabulous amazing taste. Should recommend for everyone who love fresh vegetables and Vietnamese food.

A delicious restaurant that you should visit at least once if you travel to Ubon Ratchatani. Mostly Vietnamese-style food. Especially, pork skewers wrapped in vegetables are delicious. Rice noodles are light and can be eaten by anyone.

The best! This Vietnamese restaurant is so traditional and delicious. Still be my all-time favorite. The most popular dish is Nam Neung. If you’re new to this, I would recommend you to order wrapped by the restaurant. It’s much easier for you to eat. Another favorite dish goes to “Deef fried minced pork rolls”. That is so crispy.

The price is above average from other vietnamese restaurant. But compared to quality, I think it’s worthy.

Long time family restaurant. I get used to Vietnamese food here than Udornthani. But lately I think the taste and raw material change, hardly have star fruit in Namnueng now, only green mango. The flour of Kanomtuay is also different. Miangtod is quite hard as well. Kanombueng doesn't look nice. People said that it's quite pricey.
Quick service, delicious naem nueng, and I really liked the Vietnamese fresh spring rolls. The restaurant is decorated in a charming old Vietnamese style — very nice overall.

A Memorable Night at Juksunchae

Chef Henry Lee personally explained every dish, which made the experience even more special.

This was the new location at Townhall 49. We had been waiting to try it for months, even through the renovation delays — and it was totally worth the wait.

Chef Henry showed such warmth and gratitude. He even treated us to a sweet wine pairing with dessert — honestly one of the best I’ve had. It made the night even more memorable.

We came for a birthday celebration, and it turned into such a lovely evening.

The food? No words — just amazing. Every dish was creative and flavorful. Juksunchae instantly became one of my all-time favorite fine dining spots.

Definitely planning to come back. I’m still thinking about that soup — I seriously wished I could ask for a refill 😅

The best Korean fine dining in Bangkok. Every dishes was precisely executed. Each dish was a modern interpretation of traditional Korean dishes.

Be prepared to be very full when you leave. Will definately be back again when the menu changes.

My first time experiencing authentic Korean fine dining in Bangkok. Chef Henry put remarkable time and effort into every dish. Each course was meticulously thought out and creatively crafted, all while staying deeply rooted in Korean tradition. I thoroughly enjoyed the wine pairing, which complemented each dish beautifully.

Highlight dishes:
▶️ Hwe
▶️ Bibimbap
▶️ Octopus Tubu Jjigae
▶️ Bone Broth Soup (Gomtang setup)

Interesting Korean fine dining concept, Chef was very thorough in explaining each dish and ingredients. Restaurant is cozy with an open kitchen, nice tabletops and decor.

Around 9.8k THB after vat & taxes for 2 people

Working as a Chef for over 40 years that was my first experience with a Korean fine dining restaurant (with some modern Western cooking techniques).
Quality of ingredients was superb. Loved the dry aged African pompano fish out of the Andaman Sea and the organic locally grown duck. The lotus root and seed dish was lovely and the egg custard with the French caviar had so many different flavour levels.

All dishes were perfectly balanced (except, perhaps the cold noodles which could have had a bit more seasoning).

Desserts were really delicious with combinations of products that usually you wouldn’t associate with desserts.

Service was superb and Chef Henry did explain every dish very carefully and you can see that he’s very passionate about his food.

Exterior is very minimalistic and fits very well with the gorgeous food presentations. We had a great view to the chefs preparing all the food.

Couple points for improvements; get a good steak knife for the duck and the pork and we sat right below the ac unit which was a bit too noisy.

Overall experience- superb and I would recommend this restaurant to anyone to try.

We will be back!

Nothing else like this in Bangkok! I’d read about SDC and couldn’t wait to try. From the moment you push the button to enter, the experience is truly unique and perfectly crafted. The downstairs space transports you to somewhere totally new with amazing organic installations and pieces to admire while you are greeted by staff. On staff, super impressive, warm, knowledgeable but not stuffy or cold like a lot of fine dining. All of this is the backdrop to the best meal I’ve had in a long time. Perfectly paced and portioned, you are hit with a series of snacks to start, eaten with just your hands and that totally set the meal off to a great start - fun, delicious and intriguing. The dishes then move around through 12 or so different courses, peaking with a 2 part duck dish that is the perfect combination of taste, beautiful presentation and concept. That can be said for the whole menu really. This is an extremely well thought out restaurant experience where everything from the design of the restaurant, the plates and materials used, the ideas and the dishes themselves and the interesting and delicious drinks. Well done Chef and team behind this. Having eaten at fine dining places around the world, I put this right up there with the best but also totally different to the typical high end dining experience. Can’t wait to return.

A crime that Sareen and his crew don't have a Michelin star yet. Bangkok's best kept secret (...until it isn't!).

Sareen has a magical and mindblowingly special way of approaching Thai food.

Using local ingredients sourced from within Thailand, he takes you on a culinary journey that both tastes amazing and delights ALL your senses.

You feel his passion for showcasing Thai food to the world - and one would feel lucky to experience this.

I can't even put into words how much I enjoyed this meal. The only sentiment that could aptly capture this is that  I have been to Michelin 2 and 3-star restaurants before, and I was no where near as delighted and exuberant about my experience than at Small Dinner Club.

Hats off to Sareen and his amazing team. The photos and videos do NOT do this place justice. This is a meal that must be experienced to be believed.

Good:
- The lobby on the ground floor was beautiful and really set the mood for dinner. It felt classy and inviting, which made us excited for the meal ahead.
- The service by the waitress was excellent. They were kind, attentive, and made us feel welcomed throughout the evening.

Cons:
- The food, unfortunately, didn’t meet expectations. The balance of ingredients and textures felt off, and some choices came across as repetitive. There were three dishes featuring ice or ice cream. While one would’ve been fine, seeing ice appear three times made the meal feel redundant. By the time we reached dessert, all my friends were still hungry.
- The first dessert, a sweet potato with a moist texture, tasted good and gave us hope for something more substantial next. But the second dessert was melted chocolate with a similar texture..
- Then, they told us there is a final "surprise" dessert and we were so excited. the reveal was a single piece of deep-fried pig skin coated in chocolate. Chocolate again ….chocolate again..

I can see that the chef has good intentions and wants to push creative boundaries, which is commendable. However, at the price point of a Michelin-level restaurant, the portions, ingredients, and overall experience didn’t justify the cost.

- The bathroom also had issues. The sink was broken, and water splashed everywhere. It was awkward to use, and I had to stand at an angle to avoid getting wet. For a fine-dining establishment, I expected better upkeep.
- There was a spelling mistake on the menu: “suprising” instead of “surprising.” While minor, it came across as careless and felt out of place in a restaurant that charges premium prices.

A delightful dining experience that took me by surprise. It truly seems as though a skilled artist is crafting each dish just for you.

Every dish was exceptional and thoughtfully prepared, incorporating unique ingredients that added an element of surprise.

One aspect of our visit that felt somewhat out of place was the requirement to choose our wine while in the waiting room, rather than at our dining table. The reasoning behind this is unclear to me.

By the way, if you are not a fan of cilantro then please do inform the chef in advance so they can make substitutions.

The experience was perfectly executed and was exactly what I expected from reading and viewing the SDC website in advance (which it appears not all reviewers took the time to do - and we all experience the world differently …clearly and thankfully). The space is gorgeous, welcoming and relaxing. The team are attentive, warm, knowledgeable, conversational, fun and funny. The Chef is extremely talented, artistic, charming and witty. The food was beautiful and delicious and the wine pairing spot-on. A wonderful non-touristy way to spend a delightful and memorable evening in BKK. Thank you, Chef and Team!

My family has been enjoying Chuan Kitchen in Mueang Thong Thani since its humble beginnings as a tiny shop, long before it relocated to its current flagship location. The food, simple as it may seem, is all expertly executed and tastes fantastic. From the perfectly cooked rice to the crispy fried vegetables and savory fried turnip cakes, every dish is well-seasoned and complements the other ingredients beautifully.

The menu is diverse, offering something for everyone to enjoy. The staff is friendly and attentive, promptly bringing the menu upon seating. The new spacious restaurant is tastefully decorated, making it an ideal spot for both small families and larger groups.

In its earlier days, when the owners' family personally oversaw operations, they were warm, welcoming, and genuinely delighted to see people enjoying their food. Their presence added an extra layer of charm to an already wonderful dining experience.

A Michelin Guide restaurant in the Muang Thong Thani area, best known for its signature dish — boiled fish with pickled mustard greens. The dish is served in a large bowl and offers a well-balanced, flavorful taste. Highly recommended for families and groups of friends, as the menu is extensive and offers a wide variety of dishes that are perfect for sharing.

As a Singaporean, it was amazing to find a Singaporean restaurant at Nonthaburi. Great representation of local Singaporean dishes like Chay Kway Teow, Bak Ku Teh & Laksa. Food was generally great (laksa gravy can do with more simmering to make it creamy) & somewhat sufficient parking around. If only there’s chilli crab! Will definitely visit when I need my sg fix. Cheers.

I recently visited Chuan Kitchen Mueang Thong Thani and had a delightful dining experience. This restaurant is a gem for lovers of Asian cuisine, offering a variety of dishes that cater to different palates. Here's a breakdown of what I tried:

**Cha Noodle:**
The cha noodles were a highlight of the meal. Perfectly cooked to an ideal texture, they had a wonderful chewiness that was both satisfying and flavorful. The accompanying broth was rich and aromatic, with a depth of flavor that suggested a well-balanced mix of spices and herbs. The portion size was generous, making it a great choice for a hearty meal.

**Hokkien Mee:**
The hokkien mee at Chuan Kitchen was another standout dish. The noodles were beautifully stir-fried, capturing the essence of wok hei, that elusive smoky flavor that defines great stir-fried dishes. The seafood was fresh and plentiful, including succulent prawns and tender squid. The dish was well-seasoned, with a savory sauce that coated every strand of noodle, offering a perfect balance of flavors.

**Mala Soup:**
For those who enjoy a spicy kick, the mala soup at Chuan Kitchen is a must-try. The soup was vibrant with a deep red color, indicating the fiery experience to come. The spiciness was bold but not overwhelming, allowing the other flavors to shine through. The ingredients were plentiful, with a good mix of meats, tofu, and vegetables, each absorbing the spicy broth beautifully. It was a comforting yet exhilarating dish that left a lasting impression.

Delicious Singaporeans style Chinese food restaurant. This restaurant has plenty of parking space and even EV charging stations. The staffs are very polite and friendly when helping us with ordering. We ordered dishes ranging from classic Singaporeans dishes as well as dimsum. Most dishes are very aromatic, well seasoned and simply delicious. We bought the 3 years old along with is and this restaurant has kids cutlery as well as many basic dishes which are young kids friendly

We chose this restaurant to celebrate our 6-year anniversary, and it turned out to be a great choice. The overall atmosphere was elegant and inviting, creating the perfect setting for a special occasion. The food was impressive, with well-balanced flavors and quality ingredients. While the pasta was just average, the main course—the Wagyu beef—was absolutely superb, cooked to perfection with rich, indulgent flavors. The price was reasonable for the quality and experience offered, making it a great value. One of the highlights was the breathtaking view of the Chao Phraya River, adding an extra layer of charm to the evening. Highly recommended for those looking for a memorable dining experience with great ambiance and excellent food!

I come to eat here regularly as a resident at the Four Seasons. I’m never disappointed — the service is flawless and the food is always excellent. I enjoy inviting friends to this restaurant, especially since there are often new dishes on the menu. The pasta and desserts are simply outstanding 🤩

The restaurant is located inside the Four Seasons Hotel. It's an Italian restaurant that pays attention to every detail. Its quality is top-notch, with fresh produce and spectacular flavor.

The food was a 10, from the complimentary bread basket to the desserts. Everything we tried was delicious.

River views are available if you dine on the terrace or in the indoor dining room; both are beautifully designed. They were very attentive and the service was fantastic. You can see them working in the kitchen, and it's a real treat! 🫶🏼

The price is steep, but it's worth it!

A chef-recommended set meal priced at 5,600 baht (without service charge or taxes) resulted in nothing but an expensive waste of intelligence, and an extraordinary experience of vomiting and diarrhea.
After the appetizer bread (this might be the most delicious thing on the entire menu), came a series of beautifully crafted dishes served from the kitchen. The ingredients were cut extremely thinly, like paper, accompanied by strange sauces of various colors that were neither sweet nor sour. They were placed on empty plates as fresh cold dishes that resembled contemporary paintings:
Three small pastries, each composed of layers of mini ingredients and sauces, measuring only the size of a coin, contain raw fish.
2. Cut the raw fish into small pieces, arrange them in a thin layer to form a cute fish shape, and decorate the top with various sauces.
3. Special homemade Italian steamed dumplings. The dough is slightly undercooked, and one thin mushroom, as thin as a bamboo shoot, is placed on top.
4. The dried mushrooms are flattened and placed on a plate. Some sauce is added on top. Only about a quarter of a salmon fillet is placed on the plate, with five shrimp grains on top and a layer of sauce (this is the only cooked food on the entire menu).
5. Making your own ice cream sorbet is not much better in taste than the double-scoop ice cream sold in the mall.
6. Cream dessert, with colorful sauce applied on the top; surrounding it are several scoops of ice cream and cream granules.
These dishes not only have an extremely small portion size, but also have a taste that can be described as unpleasant. This kind of thing that doesn't fit into any specific category and can't be classified into different schools, we call "creative cuisine" in China. And these mere six small plates of "masterpieces" took a full hour to be served.
Looking at this scene, I felt like I was a fool in the movie "The Menu".
I don't understand why the chef chose to use raw fish as the main ingredient and serve it to the guests in a country located in the tropics with frequent reports of water pollution? When the uncooked smell entered my mouth, my body actually had a physiological reaction, sending a warning to me. And I believe that a five-star hotel wouldn't make such a basic mistake as "inadequate freshness of ingredients", and would insist on stuffing uncooked food into my mouth.
Before the meal was finished, I felt unwell and went to the bathroom to vomit for over 10 minutes. After returning, I weakly explained my condition to the waiter and refused to take the remaining dishes. The lobby manager immediately came over to apologize, offered a 15% discount on my order, and provided free ginger water to warm my stomach. He also explained that it takes at least 4 hours for the food to start being digested. I was too tired to continue arguing and just pretended to be acting to avoid the bill. I merely expressed my disappointment with the meal here and then paid the bill and left.
That night, I began to have a fever and break out in a sweat. The next day, with severe vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal cramps, I directly boarded the plane back home. Eventually, it was diagnosed as acute gastroenteritis.
Thank you, Four Seasons Hotel, for giving me such an unforgettable night in Bangkok. I will never forget it.

From the moment I walked in, I was impressed. The atmosphere is so warm and inviting, and it immediately puts you at ease. The staff are all wonderful, providing excellent and friendly service. Everything is delicious 🤤

Tiffin by La Sala is a high-end fine dining restaurant with excellent service & Michelin recommended restaurant.The staff are prompt, attentive, and always serve with a smile, making the whole experience even more delightful.
As a vegetarian, I explored both the local Thai cuisine and Indian dishes – and both were equally impressive. From the local menu, I highly recommend the papaya salad, pomelo salad, Thai green curry with tofu, Phuket pineapple fried rice, and of course, finishing with the classic mango sticky rice with coconut milk.
From the Indian side, the aloo tikki, aloo gobhi, and dal Anantara paired with garlic naan were absolutely satisfying.
Overall, Tiffin by La Sala is definitely worth visiting for anyone who appreciates refined dining, authentic flavors, and warm hospitality.

We visited La Sala for dinner and ordered their Thai food, with special requests not to include sugar into the dishes and to make it spicy - and they delivered! We had the peeled crab curry with noodles, duck red curry & morning glory and everything was delicious.
The atmosphere is very pretty, especially in the evenings and the service by staff, especially our host, Khun Vam, was exceptional. She remembered our names when we came back 2 days later!
I would come here again on my next visit to Phuket.

Very good food. Well deserves Michelin recommendation that they got in 2025

We had Dhal Tadka, Garlic Naan, Lamb Rogan Gosh and Saffron Ice cream. Each dish was top marks

Excellent vegetarian food and service. Papdi chat would do better either less papdi and more yogurt. Samosas were very good. Black dal and paneer were also excellent. Overall, a high quality fine dining restaurant especially if you are vegetarian.

Best Thai food ever! The food was flavorful and full of spicy punches that will leave you wanting more. The phad Thai and crab meat curry with vermicelli noodles were especially delicious.

In addition to the great food, the restaurant also offers cooking classes taught by their amazing chef. These classes are a great way to learn how to make some of your favorite Thai dishes at home. I highly recommend signing up for a class if you love the food at la sala.

A very unique place to go if you're in Chiang Mai.

At the end of the day, it's just fried pastry, but the way they prepare it it's the reason why it's worth visiting.

There are a few animal shapes to choose from, all between 20 and 40 baht. The way they prepare it is what makes this place unique. You can see the lady carving the shapes by hand, and the quality is incredible.

Next to the market so you can do some tourism around the area.

The ginger tea was potent and delicious.

Ko Neng Patonggo is a fantastic local breakfast spot that truly lives up to the hype! The deep-fried dough sticks (patonggo) are crispy on the outside, soft and airy inside—freshly made and served hot. They pair perfectly with the rich, fragrant soy milk or Thai-style pandan custard.

It’s a simple street-side setup, but the quality and taste are top-notch. You can really feel the care put into each batch. Prices are cheap and fair, making it a favorite among locals and tourists alike.

It can get a bit busy in the mornings, so be prepared for a short wait—but trust me, it’s worth it. If you’re in Chiang Mai and looking for an authentic, delicious Thai breakfast, don’t miss this place!

Michelin or not this place has good youtiao / fried dough. This is perfect with coffee, tea, nut milk, or the traditional soy bean soup/ milk/ etc.

The place is far from fancy and the price was maybe 5x the same thing on the road side but what is life without the Dino, dragon, pig, boat, or whatever else youtiao?!?!!!!. By the way, they sell some other items in their menu but why bother…

I insist!! Must try!!!
It is fried dough, it will be an affordable snack even if you only have it once.

This place is amazing! I normally don't put much emphasis on Michelin rated restaurants, but this place is amazing! To get such a low rating is beyond ridiculous. The Chinese style breakfast is the best I had. The soy milk, youtiao, sausage, and congee were exceptionally made. This is bookmarked Chiamy Chiang Mai food places.
Amazing Chinese donuts in the shape of dinosaurs, elephants and crocodiles! Fresh made in front of you and super tasty! Thai people have this for breakfast!

This is a very popular restaurant, so be prepared to queue for a little bit when you come around lunch peak time. Though it is 1000% worth it! It is not a fancy restaurant, at all. But the food, wow. It is one of the purest, most authentic restaurants that I have been to with so much flavor in their dishes. It is not for nothing that this restaurant was in the Michelin guide for multiple years already.

The dishes are more expensive than elsewhere, but don't forget that the dishes are double size than elsewhere! When ordering 1 dish it can easily fit 2 persons. Don't make the same mistake as us as we ordered 3 dishes and it was absolutely too much. Luckily we could have it for takeaway to eat again in the evening.

Recommended!!

Traditional Thai Food from the Upper Central Region – Absolutely Awesome!

The food here is seriously impressive. It came out super fast, and there were plenty of staff on standby to take care of everything — very attentive service.

We arrived around 11 AM, which was perfect since it wasn’t too busy yet. But after 12… yep, it gets packed! So come early if you can.

I ordered all the recommended dishes and honestly, every single one was spot on. Delicious!

Heads-up: The portions are quite generous, so if you’re coming with a small group, don’t over-order — you’ll be stuffed!

Nice Thai traditional food with local ingredients. Located on the Asia road. Easy parking in front of the restaurant. On holidays, there maybe a long queue, so be sure to save some time. The food is worth waiting. Juicy, yummy, and crispy. There are open-air and A/C zones to choose from.
So Yummy Good Taste! Can call for booking and ordering in advance. Also have air condition zone provided but limited seat.

This is one of my favorite traditional Thai restaurants. They serve Thai dishes in large portions.
