We ordered the recommended dishes, such as kale stir-fried with salted fish, sun-dried squid, pork cartilage stir-fried with shrubby basil, prawn and herb with spicy salad(Sangwa Goong) and fish jungle curry. The food had a mellow taste, the ingredients were fresh, and the service was fast. Highly recommended to try at least once. It gets crowded at lunchtime, so it’s better to come early or make a reservation in advance.

Our Thai hosts had specifically intended the "Ruen Jarung" restaurant weekend-visit as the highlight of our BKK vacation. (Ruen: Home/House; Jarung: Family name.) From its website, the place would only operate on weekends and limited to three seatings a day, with pre-orders of food required.
Given Michelin-star, 2025 and other culinary-recognition awards under the stewardship of "Uncle Miao", fans have, in recent years, come from far and wide, both locals and tourists. This is despite its rather off-the-beaten track and unique location.
The environment was truly classic rustic: serene lakes with ducks and geese swimming merrily, a well-maintained variegated cacti garden, surrounding plains of padi-rice fields etc.
Our hosts had ordered some 14 types of very popular Thai food (my apologies for not knowing most of the Thai names of dishes ordered), including an evergreen Thai dessert custard. We studiously savoured each and every dish, highly "aroi mak-mak"!
The long wooden tables on the premises were able to accommodate dining groups of more than 10 people comfortably, which contributed towards a much convivial and celebratory atmosphere and ambience.
Veritably, the restaurant was able to provide the diners with happy memories and recollections of their visits!
Definitely, a must-visit again, if possible!
This is a famous traditional Thai restaurant. The food tastes delicious and well-balanced. The staff are friendly and helpful. The view is beautiful, and you can feel the countryside atmosphere.

This place offers authentic Thai food with a scenic view of rice fields. We visited during the winter, so the outdoor dining area was perfect. The food was fantastic, featuring the true flavors of Thai cuisine, with good and fresh ingredients, felt like dining with family in a countryside home. The owner was very friendly and provided excellent hospitality. I love everything about it!
Delicious with a little spicy Thai dishes with very good quality ingredients. A little hot but not a big problem.
A wonderful place, with tasty Thai local food and warm-hearted service.

Excellent traditional Thai food in a historic setting. Quality of ingredients is top notch, with an authentic taste.  The highlight is the Traditional Thai pork soup with shrimp paste, a hard- to - find Traditional dish. Be sure to call and reserve beforehand as they will escort you on a boat directly to the restaurant. Truly a great dining experience.

Compliments to service team Joe, Sandra and Chef Toon for great hospitality

A memorable evening at Praya Dining, where I chose the Praya Course (THB 1,990 per person). The experience was more than just a meal—it was a journey through Thai heritage. Upon arrival, we were warmly welcomed and invited upstairs to explore the beautifully preserved historic house. A captivating storytelling session followed, enriching our appreciation of each course. Every dish was thoughtfully crafted, rooted in traditional Thai flavors, and elevated with a refined twist. The ambiance, attentive service, and cultural elements made the entire experience truly exceptional. We arrived by cruise from Phra Arthit Pier, which added charm to the evening. Booking in advance is highly recommended for this unique heritage dining experience.

We eat a lot of Thai food, and have been privileged to dine at some remarkable Thai restaurants in Thailand and abroad, and this restaurant is my absolute favourite . The team here have redefined my understanding of Thai food. For an incredible taste of old world charm (this building is deeply historic), fantastic service, and unforgettable food please try this hidden gem. The lamb curry in particular is magical. Michelin listed but honestly, it beats so many Michelin starred establishments.

Beautiful location, superb staff and wonderful food. I'm a really plain eater & find it hard to try new foods but we experienced the most delicious tasting menu. The chef was fantastic, explaining what we were having and making sure that vegetarians were extremely well catered for. The staff were also very careful about our allergies. The waiting staff were very attentive and really friendly. We had a terrific experience and I can't recommend highly enough.

PEOPLE, GO TO PRAYA DINING
There was literally just us dining when we went and we were so spooked by that at first -- usually a terrible sign -- but then it ended up being one of the best experiences we had in our 3-week trip to Asia!!! What's up with the lack of people? I mean, yes it's out of hand, but that also makes it so special !!
Yes, we almost gave up going as we couldn't figure out where to get the boat, but decided to use our Skype credits to call the restaurant. They picked us up by boat immediately (we were in the Phra Arthit boat stop #13). The boat ride was soooo nice!!! It's such a charm.
Okay, now the food. Delicious. So good. The menu is wonderful, the extensive research done by the chef is laid out to you. I love that they divide the dishes in different eras of Thailand. I love that you can eat an ancient recipe researched by the chef.
They also were able to do actually mild food for dishes that are usually spice, so super tourist friendly!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ | Truly Impressive Thai Fusion

I would say this is one of the best Thai fusion restaurants I’ve ever tried! Every dish we ordered was absolutely incredible — full of flavor, creativity, and beautifully presented. Highly recommend if you’re looking for something exciting and satisfying. Even though the restaurant was packed, the service was efficient and we didn’t have to wait long for the food at all. Definitely worth the visit 👌🏻👍🏻👍🏻

A must-visit somtum (papaya salad) Michelin selected 2022-2025 restaurant in Ayutthaya! My top favorite is the Somtum Pla Ra (fermented fish papaya salad), along with the fried rice with fermented fish and, of course, the restaurant’s signature grilled chicken—a dish you simply cannot miss.
For international visitors, don’t worry—the menu comes with pictures, and if you don’t eat spicy food, you can always let the staff know. There are also plenty of options without fermented fish and without chili. And don’t forget to try their desserts—they’re just as delicious as the main dishes!

The first time we ordered on Lineman, the second time we had to come eat here as it was super delicious.

The larb and the chicken is very tasty. We ordered chicken, beef and also larb as a main dish. However, the larb did not show up more than 10 minutes after the chicken and beef were served. We had to ask for the larb dish, and most probably they forgot. When the larb arrived, all the rest was already cold and the rice as well. This was a bit disappointing.

The food is delicious though.

Nice and delicious food. We were there on a weekday, and there were a lot of people. Food serving didn't take too long. Salmon spicy salad was good and fresh. Beef sirloin was a bit well cooked but not chewy. So far, everything was fine. It was worth for money, good price.
I really enjoyed food here! I highly recommend som tum, it’s yami and not spicy with nuts and really good juice.

We saw Angeum restaurant listed on the Michelin Guide, so we decided to go for it. It actually was in the Michelin Guide for 4 years as I could see.

The decoration is incredibly beautiful and clean, and there is a nice atmosphere with friendly and attentive staff. It gets very busy here around lunch time.

The menu is so unique and we ordered many things. The Vietnamese soup was tasty!

There is also parking for cars, though there is not much space.

Angeum Vietnamese Restaurant (ร้านอันเกิมเวียดนามมิส) was very enjoyable. The prawn sugarcane was particularly good, and I found that wrapping many of the dishes in the traditional Vietnamese style really enhanced the flavors. Overall, the food tasted great and the restaurant offers good value for money.

Food was absolutely delicious! We ordered 5 menus, everything tastes wonderful. The restaurant beautifully design, lighting was very vibrant. Highly recommend if you’re looking for Vietnamese food or just looking for a simple one dish menu.

Parking spaces available.
This vietnamese restaurant is a michellin stars for 4 years in a row. Food are delicious and rather mild for the spicy lovers, but over all quality is great. Recommended 💯% 🚀🚀⭐️⭐️🚀🚀

Angeum Vietnamese Restaurant in Ayutthaya is a Michelin Guide-listed spot that’s worth a visit. The food tastes fresh, clean, and full of authentic Vietnamese flavor. They use high-quality ingredients, and you can really taste the difference.

The restaurant is beautifully decorated, offering both an air-conditioned indoor zone and a cozy outdoor area. Whether you’re here for a light lunch or a relaxed dinner, this place has a lovely atmosphere to match its delicious food.
A famous rice porridge restaurant in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, known for its delicious food, great atmosphere, and affordable prices.

Bustling, low key restaurant located near to the Chedi Wat Sam Pluem. The place is very popular, so you may have to wait for a table. There is no menu or pricing, the owner comes to the table to give you the options (you can check online for reviews of the restaurant to give you an idea). The dishes we ordered were pretty good, but we waited 60 minutes to get our food after ordering. A little over priced for what we ordered.

Warning: This might be a biased post, but I love the taste so much that we went there twice, even though we were staying 30 minutes away from the restaurant. (Hence the 5 stars overall!)

I heard great things about this place, so we came to try it out. And Omg! It’s so good! I’ll definitely be back next time we visit Ayutthaya. There’s no set menu—just tell them what you’re craving, and they’ll either make it or suggest something amazing.

We stayed at the classic kameo hotel and were looking at Google maps for a place to eat. This restaurant is popular and only 10 min walk from our hotel. The food was really good and lucky for us that we weren't hungry because we had to wait 75 minutes to our order. I also found it strange that there is no menu so you must know what to order and still you have to wait for the end to know how much you need to pay.

Pros:
- The food taste great.
- Easy to find
- Beer is cold

Cons:
- No menu available (that mean you have to know exactly what you want to eat)
- Quite pricey for street food.
- Extremely slow and rude service.
- Price is not known before hand.
- No omelette.
- Satay is absolutely horrible.

Had a great experience at Nitan. Service is top notch and they had a really inventive non alcoholic pairing.

The menu changes every few months, but for the menu of Sep-25, the beef dishes were excellent. There were a few dishes in the middle that were off balance in terms of texture / flavour, but the meal was generally well balanced and creative.

I would be happy to visit again if in Phuket.

My first fine dining experience at Nitan in Phuket was one to remember. The food stood out with every dish. Each bite brought out clear, balanced flavors, showing care in the preparation. The menu felt thoughtful, turning simple ingredients into something special. Every course left an impression, making the meal truly satisfying.

The service added to the experience. The staff paid attention to every detail, ensuring everything ran smoothly. They explained the dishes with knowledge and warmth, which made the meal more meaningful. Their approach created a welcoming vibe throughout the evening.

The restaurant’s setting felt comfortable and well-planned. From the lighting to the seating, the space worked together to make the meal feel like an occasion. It was a place where I could relax and enjoy every moment.

Nitan made my first fine dining experience unforgettable. It’s a place worth visiting in Phuket. I recommend booking a table and enjoying what they have to offer.

Chef Pom and team took us on an absolutely amazing culinary journey with Thai and Phuket Island specialties!

Reserve a table for dinner here in advance... and prepare yourself for an extraordinary dining experience.

I had such a wonderful experience here! The food was absolutely delicious — every dish was fresh, well-seasoned, and beautifully presented. The phuket local dish is well presented in a fusion style. The environment is just as impressive: cozy, clean, and with a warm atmosphere that makes you feel comfortable the moment you walk in. Krit is friendly and attentive without being intrusive

Absolutely perfect evening. It was our 20 year anniversary as a couple and I chose NITAN to enjoy a meal together. The food was beyond fresh, delicious and definitely fine dining. World class quality - we are from Melbourne and it’s on parr with Vue De Monde in terms of the quality, creativity, service and dedication to their purpose. We love how the chefs are passionate about playing homage to Phuket’s fishing history and how the servers explain each dish in such great detail. Not only did we enjoy 12 courses but we learned so much about the beautiful island of Phuket. The flathead lobster, duck and 4 rice dessert were the stand-outs however and to be frank, each of the 12 courses were world class. What a gem of a restaurant - very authentic in its purpose and humble in its value. Thank you for a memorable evening - one of the best meals we have ever had (and we love to fine dine across the globe).

The mood and tone of the restaurant’s decor, along with the background music, perfectly match the food concept and the location — creating a cohesive and inviting atmosphere.

The food is truly worth the price. Each portion comes with generous serving sizes and high-quality ingredients, making it feel like great value for money.

As for the service, I’d like to offer a small suggestion. Please ensure all serving wares are in good condition before using them for guests. Also, regarding service sequence — especially when clearing savory dishes before dessert — it would be nice to clear plates gradually during the meal instead of waiting until the very end when guests leave the table. And please be mindful of noise when clearing dishes, as the sound of clattering plates can be distracting to other diners and could potentially damage the wares if not handled carefully on the trolley.

Just sharing this feedback for consideration. Overall, I really enjoyed the experience — the food was delicious, and I’ll definitely be coming back!

We came here first time on a public holiday and the queue was very big, and we decided to come back another time. We came back at noon on a Friday, and it was not busy at all.

The menu is extensive and had many different  options to choose from. The pink noodle was great, and especially the pork belly was super delicious!

The food was really delicious — fresh, clean, and served quickly.
The “Pad Sam Men” was absolutely amazing, and the shrimp were super fresh!
A must-try place when you visit Ayutthaya. 😋

The place is very cozy and well-decorated. The food was delicious. It was well-prepared and well-cooked.
Seafood was fresh. The service was superb.
I really had a great time and enjoyed my dinner here.

reviewer: นิพัฒน์สิน ยิ้มแย้ม
review_text: The taste is good and unique for Thai menus. Pha-Lo is great and showing long hours efforts of boiling cooking.

Absolutely loved our dinner here. The burrata and pasta were amazing, fresh, flavourful, and beautifully presented. The seabass was perfectly cooked and full of flavour. The atmosphere is lovely and the service was friendly and attentive. A great spot for a relaxed evening by the beach.

Amazing food. All the dishes we ordered were phenomenal. Highly recommend the lobster paella! It was definitely value for money. The ambience never disappoints. We are regulars here on the island. Nong Pam and Rain served us food, and the service was above and beyond!

Ing and Rain provided absolutely superb service at this restaurant! From the warm welcome to their attentive care throughout, they made our experience truly special. A big thank you for organising the beautiful anniversary decoration — it made the evening even more memorable.
The cocktails were perfectly crafted, and the food was simply delicious — every dish was well-prepared and full of flavour.
We’ll definitely be coming back! ❤️

Had our last meal at FishHouse after our 5 day stay at Kimpton. It was amazing - the steak was cooked to perfection and the prawns were so tasty with that sauce. Highly recommend this restaurant! Although it is more on the pricier side, this is expected for a restaurant of this caliber at a 5 star hotel!

We waited 10 minutes to be greeted and shown to a table. There was no manager or waiter. All the wine glasses were dirty and had fingerprints on them. One was chipped and they pour wine in it, I asked to change. We ordered three dishes, and none of them were very tasty. The steak was well done instead of medium rare!!! And it isn't high qualuty meet... The selection of wines by the glass was meager. Michelin recimmended, seriously? What for?

Outstanding noodles, soup is very clear , clean , hint of fried garlic oil, pork patty is great texture, all in the bowl is perfect .

The shop is hidden from the main road ( GPS correct ) very small street , difficult for parking , small shop , write order first , find a sit , wait untill they call your number order , enjoy !

** Cash Only ** the shop is located in suburbs of center city , maybe find atm difficulty .

Food was the balls.
Me and the misso gave it 10/10.
It's just a bit out of the way as to where you'd normally travel, and the hours are quite limited.
Thankfully for us, we planned to come here so the opening hours wasn't so much an issue for us.
Parking is also easier than I thought, just at the front of the house you can squeeze your car there, or around the corner!
Good "Tom Yum" Noodle @ Nakhonpathom
My favorite dishes - always worth the wait. Thai iced tea, and limeade drinks are a must. While waiting, you should order delicious grilled pork balls.

Very delicious 😋
Worth the wait worth the travel from bkk
The best tomyum noodle

We had the chance to have a lunch in Vilas this Sunday.
We were a bit concerned because we were the only ones at that sitting but we had a wonderful experience.

Working in hospitality myself I cant thank more the kindness and professionalism we received by the crew.
Everything was set up by them to make us feel at home in theirs .
We went for the multiple choice set up menu and everything we got served was lovely, from really balanced to punchy!
They dont joke about taste over there.
We had a durian cracker with kinda guacamole which made me really love durian for once .
A crab bite with no joke about the freshness and amount of crab for a single bite.
A scallop carpaccio with a powerful baby mango/fermented soybeans and seaweed caviar - fresh/powerful/tangy/spicy yet super balanced
And a crispy duck confit curry with watermelon pickles, just nice, comfy and everything you will expect from it with the discovery of tangy watermelon to shake up your palate.
We also had a taste of their razor clam curry, less heavy and more elegant than the duck, both bangers.
If you wanna get hit the proper thai way try their samui sour curry and tell me more about it later.

Cocktails were totally on point, I had the coconut one and it is just as described, pure coconut no bad notes.

Once again we got welcomed like part of the crew, I cant thank them enough for all the small attention we got .

I will definitely comeback on my next bangkok visit.

Exceptional dining experience at VILAS! The food was beautifully presented and full of unique, refined flavors. Highlights of the night included the thinly sliced wagyu beef topped with glossy caviar and a delicately marinated quail egg, a luxurious bite that simply melted in the mouth, and the charred sweet corn skewers served on mini tortillas with fresh greens, crispy shallots, and pickled vegetables, a vibrant mix of smoky, sweet, and tangy notes.

Chef Bank and the team are both welcoming and incredibly talented, making the whole evening even more special. The staff were attentive and warm, creating a perfect atmosphere. Definitely a place I’ll be visiting again!

I visited Vilas, now relocated to Velaa Bangkok. The new venue offers a more casual and relaxed ambiance compared to its previous setting, creating an easygoing yet elegant dining experience.

The dishes I tried were visually stunning and full of flavor—modern, cross-cultural interpretations with a bold identity of their own. While not strictly traditional, the menu offers a creative fusion of global techniques and vibrant Thai flavors. Many of the dishes are delightfully spicy, sure to please both Thai diners and international guests who enjoy bold heat.

Every plate was thoughtfully crafted, balancing textures and colors with artistic flair. From the refreshing starters to the hearty mains, the meal was memorable from start to finish.

If you haven’t experienced Vilas yet, this is definitely a restaurant worth trying at least once. A perfect spot for adventurous food lovers who appreciate contemporary cuisine with a spicy kick.

I’m visiting from Korea, and dining here was such a special experience! The modern Thai fusion dishes were absolutely delicious, and the restaurant itself is beautifully designed. The staff were always warm, smiling, and professional, which made me feel so comfortable and valued as a guest.

Every dish was a W. Every bite was a delight. Every component on the plate felt intentional. As a tourist zooming through traditional Thai restaurants, the fusion food at Vilas was a welcome change. Expect Thai flavors and roots with western techniques.
Staff were very nice, ambience was comfortable, space and lighting were good.

What an incredible experience! We were so fortunate to dine at Jampa on Chef Rick Dingen's last day at the restaurant. This Dutch chef is truly a master - every single dish was an amazing journey of textures and flavors, perfectly balanced so that nothing dominates but everything contributes to this beautiful harmony that just excites your palate. The acidity was spot on, the spice level perfect, and there was this lovely sweetness throughout. It's sophisticated, elevated cuisine, but what really impressed me was how seamlessly he integrated local Thai ingredients and cultural touches into each dish.
Chef Rick personally came to our table and assured us that his sous chef who's taking over and the entire team are exceptionally skilled and talented, so the restaurant will continue to deliver this outstanding quality. If you're a foodie, definitely follow Chef Rick Dingen's journey - he's staying in Phuket and is definitely someone to watch.
The restaurant itself is beautifully designed - elegant but not stuffy, creating such a wonderful atmosphere. The staff are incredibly professional and genuinely warm, guiding you through the entire experience with perfect attention to detail. You really feel taken care of.
One practical tip: it's not easy to navigate from the compound gate to the restaurant itself. Our taxi driver managed to find it on the way there, but on the way back, the driver got lost and ended up waiting for us by the security guard at the entrance. I'd recommend coordinating with the restaurant staff in advance - they're happy to provide transportation within the compound, which makes everything much easier.
This is truly destination dining at its best - the farm-to-table concept, the wood-fire cooking, the zero-waste philosophy, and the genuine respect for local ingredients. If you're in Phuket and appreciate exceptional food, Jampa is an absolute must. We left feeling inspired and already planning our return visit.

Had an amazing lunch experience at Jampa! The dishes are very innovative, using local plants in creative ways—beautifully presented, delicious, and healthy. Honestly, every plate looked almost too pretty to eat. Executive Chef Rick Dingen personally came over a few times to share his food concept and check in on us, which made the whole experience even more special.
A big shoutout to Madam Patch as well—she was incredibly attentive, explained each dish in detail, and even took us on a buggy ride to tour the restaurant’s farm about 1.2 km away. That personal touch was unforgettable.
The restaurant itself is gorgeous—top-notch décor, super comfortable seating, perfect air conditioning, lots of natural light, and even the toilets are spotless and luxurious. I truly enjoyed every part of my visit here and would highly recommend Jampa to anyone looking for a unique and memorable food experience.

I recently dined at Jampa Restaurant, and it was a memorable experience that really captures the farm-to-table spirit. The chef was incredibly friendly and outgoing, which added a warm and personal touch to the evening. Our waitress, BM, was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal.

The food was outstanding the lamb neck was especially nice and buttery, cooked to perfection, and a highlight of the menu. The entire concept is the use of  fire to transform fresh, local ingredients transformed into mouthwatering dishes, that still respect the produce.

That said, I’d recommend visiting at lunchtime if possible, so you can fully enjoy the beautiful grounds and truly immerse yourself in the experience of what Jampa is all about.

Overall, Jampa is not just a restaurant, but a place where hospitality, sustainability, and flavor come together and I’d definitely go back.

What a great Sunday lunch we had🥰

The venue and the road driving into the huge greenery space is super impressive.

The food is super innovative, tasty & complex. All the dish is very thoughtful & clever.
The service is superb- very nice staff, warm welcome and super professional.
We did the lunch 4 courses menu plus little shared plates and we walk out with very full yummy tummy 😇
Definitely going back there again !!!

A very nice fine dining restaurant snuggled in the vast green land that is part of a property project - Tri Vananda. They got a michelin green star for their sustainability concept, which was well elaborated for each dish. We went in July and happened to be the only group that evening, so it felt extra exclusive. So many amuse-bouche before the first course, we liked all the seafood dishes, and the service is just the right amount. We felt relaxed and comfortable. Would love to go back to try Hideaway - their day time edition.

Went here for the lunch set for around 1000 baht. Verdict: very well worth it.

The two appetizers were some beef sate and spicy salad. All very tasteful and balanced without being too salty.

Main course you can choose out of 4 options. That's great! We had the padthai and noodle soup. The latter was very tangy and not eaten before. Pad thai was okay. I think that one was a bit on the sweeter end.

Soup was sweet salty. Fresh. Desert was the black rice ice. Yummy.

Recommended!

Wonderful Dining Experience
Deserving of a Michelin Star

We had an excellent experience at this restaurant. The sharing menu offered a very generous amount of food more than enough for two people, so we even had to take some home.

From the moment we arrived, the warm welcome and professional service stood out. The private, intimate setting made it perfect for a special occasion.

All the dishes were served at the same time, which surprised us, we didn’t know where to begin! Everything looked and smelled amazing. And the taste? Absolutely delicious! Every bite was full of flavor.
This restaurant truly deserves a Michelin star.

Highly recommended dish:
Five-Spice Egg with Kurobuta Pork.

Very nice place to have lunch with friends or family members. The spacious, decent environment is very pleasant, and the service is friendly and thoughtful.
I booked a lunch set for 2 person through Hungry Hub, which contains 3 dishes and 1 dessert. It is nice and suitable for us. Especially Blue Crab Meat with Yellow Curry and 4 traditional Thailand dessert are delicious. Only one tip, “the little spicy” is still spicy, acceptable but felt hot in mouth and stomach as well.

Everything here was good. I tried another michelin star restaurant named nahm and it was definitely not as good as here.

The dish I loved the most was actually the green curry, which was super flavorful and had a stronger herbal profile compared to traditional curries with a lot of coconut cream. I also appreciated the addition of a ton of vegetables in the dish. I’m not sure what it was named but it gave a lot of texture.

The prawns with the pad thai were cooked perfectly and were so tender. Same with the chicken curry massaman, which had a more Indian flavor curry profile but was still delightful. The chicken was extremely tender and the thick creamy sauce was lovely with rice. Every single dish here was excellent and words don’t do this place enough justice.

Atmosphere is great and the service is top notch. Essentially white glove service; they do everything from filling your water to splitting portions for the dishes you have on the table.

One of the rare places that I think actually deserves the Michelin star. The only slight con that I thought was that the drinks could’ve been slightly better, but they were still decent (pineapple freeze and thai tea). I will be back.

It’s a one star Michelin restaurant but the experience and food was honestly quite disappointing. Service is rather prompt and professional but the ambience was rather noisy. I’m not sure if it’s because of the dishes we ordered or that we ordered the wrong dishes but nothing tasted outstanding. The presentation of most of the dishes was excellent, especially the Royal Thai mixed platter and the Golden desserts.

The stir fried string beans with shrimp paste came recommended and was one of the better dishes of the night but was still a pretty average rendition. Both the.stir fried seabass and the Thai fish cake tasted rather mediocre. The platter had some nice savoury bites but was otherwise unremarkable. Finally the golden desserts were alright except the wax scented pieces we couldn’t get used to. I really wanted to like Saneh Jaan but it was a rather lacklustre dining experience for us.

Baan Heng is a true Khon Kaen treasure! The food feels like home — simple, comforting, and full of flavor. Their claypot rice with Chinese sausage is amazing — perfectly crispy at the bottom and fragrant all the way through. The signature sandwiches are fresh and packed with savory goodness, and the Thai-Chinese breakfast dishes like congee and pan eggs are light yet satisfying.

The place itself is cozy and nostalgic, with a warm family atmosphere. You can feel the history in every corner — from the old grocery roots to the neatly displayed local products and souvenirs. Staff are friendly, quick, and always smiling.

It’s no surprise this spot earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand. A perfect place for breakfast or a relaxed morning meal. Highly recommended if you want authentic local flavors and a real Khon Kaen experience!

This well-known restaurant has even received a Michelin award. Its focus is on serving rice porridge and various side dishes. Today, I ordered the kai krata (Thai-style pan-fried eggs), which tasted great. Another dish I tried was the claypot rice with Chinese sausage, but I found the taste less enjoyable. The sauce mixed with the rice had a strange smell, combined with a subtle hint of ginger that didn’t blend well. I didn’t try the rice porridge, so I can’t comment on that. Overall, it’s a decent place to grab a filling breakfast, though the prices are relatively high compared to the ingredients and portion sizes.

On the other side of the shop, there’s a souvenir section offering a variety of items, including Chinese sausages, moo yor (Vietnamese-style pork sausage), sai krok Isan (Isan sausages), and other pork products. Some are homemade by the shop, while others are sourced from external suppliers. Personally, I found the souvenir section more enjoyable than the breakfast area.

For parking, customers can use the roadside spots if available, or park at the nearby church, where the shop has put up a sign stating that parking is free for 2 hours.

We came all the way from Malaysia because of the recommendation from Art Thomya, it was the right choice.
Hot tea was free of charge.

KH Guide & Rating :-

Accessibility   : 5/5
Cleanliness     :  4.5/5
Ambience        :  4/5
Food quality    :  4.5/5 (pork floss bun is strongly recommends )
Price                 :  4/5
Attentiveness :  5/5
To visit  again : yes

Ban Heng is an authentic Chinese-style breakfast spot and souvenir shop located in the heart of Khon Kaen, now run by the third generation of the founding family. The service is quick, and the staff are knowledgeable about the rich history of the establishment. The food is delicious and light, making it a perfect option for your first meal of the day. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Khon Kaen.

It was wonderful to have a breakfast liked this. The atmosphere was nice and I was familiar this feeling from my childhood. The porridge was very good. The bread with shredded pork and butter was delicious. I liked Ovaltine. A bit crowded in the morning but the line ran so fast.
Nice restaurant , good food ,good atmosphere and reasonable price .

Great place to enjoy delicious local food. Friendly staff, menu has many options. Can't go wrong ordering any variety of fish. And the fried spring rolls are the best. Very close to the city and a must to visit.

Parking was not a problem. Quiet relaxing place. Nice to sit on the river in your own little hut eating watching the fish. I came when busy so had to wait one hour for food..however, a few drinks amd watching the fish the time soon passed. Friendly staff and good food. Not too expensive and only a 30 minute drive from city centre. Id come again
Great restaurant just a few minutes from the city, surrounded by ponds and plants.
Great place to eat Michelin starred food over looking a fish filled lake .

A local dish that I highly recommend!
The taste is hard to describe, but it’s incredibly tasty.
You won’t find noodles like this anywhere else in Thailand.

A must-try!
It’s cheap and tasty — no need to think twice!
Walked in by chance and very good food! We asked people sitting next to us to order for us as we were not sure what to get and it did not disappoint! Highly recommend!

Absolutely delicious.

We were unsure about this place as we couldn’t read any of the menus, which were all in Thai. But one of the lovely staff helped translate for us, so we got the clear pork broth, satay and mango sticky rice. All of which were fantastic.

The mango sticky rice was the best I’ve ever had, easily! Will be back to try again before I leave.

Must try Surat local food
The signature dish is " Long Tong "
3 points for the atmosphere it very hot inside.

This is a famous traditional restaurant. You can try the local food called "long tong" here. This is also my first time. I feel like it's an ordinary noodle with spare ribs instead of fish or pork balls. "ผักบุ้งไต่ราว" is not really my type, too sweet for me. "ก๋วยจั๊บ" is pretty good😊. Orange juice is nice. Satay is good😉 Mango and sticky rice is highly recommended!😋

restaurant_name: Khok Kloi Tom Yam Noodles with Eggs
review_text:
Oh my god! This place is a gem. A small restaurant that also got michelin star. Most dishes costed around 50-70 Baht and they are all delicious. The recommended dish is Yen ta fo ( noodles with red soup), but we also tried their pad thai, fried oyster omelette and chicken rice and were impressed.

The lady who took the order was very funny. We would love to come back!

restaurant_name: Khok Kloi Tom Yam Noodles with Eggs
review_text: Delicious 3 years in a row Michelin star noodle restaurant with a rich, flavorful broth! Perfectly balanced with spicy, sour, and savory flavors. The ingredients were fresh, and the noodles were cooked just right. The shop is clean and cozy, with quick and friendly service. Prices are very reasonable—just 120 baht for a big VIP bowl. Definitely a must-visit if you’re in the area!

restaurant_name: Khok Kloi Tom Yam Noodles with Eggs
review_text: Great food and super local spot. Very few tourists and great prices as well. The staff are very attentive and busy helping customers. 100% recommend this spot for a truly local dining experience!

restaurant_name: Khok Kloi Tom Yam Noodles with Eggs
review_text: On our way to Phuket, we stopped at this restaurant and absolutely loved it! I tried the Tom Yum yellow noodles, and they were heavenly—the soup and eggs were so good. My husband had the chicken rice, and he loved it too. Highly recommend!

restaurant_name: Khok Kloi Tom Yam Noodles with Eggs
review_text:
Real street food with Michalin guide .
Aroi , No need to add anything. Just perfect egg noodle.

No wonder it is on Bib Gourmand 7 years in a row!!!!
Everything is just simply spot on and clicking all the boxes. The yellow carb curry and the ink stir fried squid are definitely MUST try!!! The taste is just phenomenal, perfect combination in sweet, savory and a dash of punch from the heat. It is so hard to describe the entire experience with the words. Please just put it on your this and spare a meal from your journey it won't let you down.

Delicious Thai comfort food!
Absolutely loved this restaurant! The food was flavorful and authentic — every dish tasted homemade with love. The place had a cozy, welcoming vibe that made the experience even more enjoyable. Staff were attentive and kind. Definitely a new favorite spot!

So happy to come back after 4 years.
Still delicious as it was.
Today we order stir fried crab meat with curry powder, stewed pork Phuket style, stir fried veg with egg and shrimp, deep fried fish.
And we are so happy with food and service.

The Michelin dishes are crab meat curry (แกงปู) and stewed pork Phuket style (หมูฮ้อง).

Reservation is recommended for weekend.

4 parking lots are available in front of the restaurant :)

Loved this place! Went here for late lunch and vibe is quite relaxed and quiet. I saw it’s by One Chun (which I also enjoyed), that’s why I decided to try. Service was fast as well - I would recommend all that we ordered, but my faves were the turmeric curry with crab, grilled pork with salt, Thai milk tea with coffee jelly, and mango sticky rice. The flavor of the Thai Milk tea in Phuket is more on the roasted side and I loved it than the sweeter ones you will try elsewhere or outside of Thailand. Will definitely come again.

This renowned eatery was recommended to me by a resident in Phuket as one of the must try places when visiting the island. While the food was mainly decent, some menus I found to be inconsistent.

The Thai style omelet looked very appealing as it was nicely executed and made extra crispy. The panfried vegetables with eggs and dried prawns and the crab curry were the highlights. I tried the deep fried salted pork belly and was disappointed just how dry it was. I felt the pork was just overcooked. The rice was also a little brittle and hard - undercooked.

Waitress who served us seemed quite robotic in her approach, and it was somewhat challenging for her to show some, welcoming smile. While nothing too much to remark on the etiquette, the team forgotten one dish, which was the overcooked salted, deep fried pork belly.

The feel of the place lean towards at-home-style dining but the interior smelt damp, so it lacked a bit of an atmosphere despite properly furnished decors.

Had enjoyed the Thai tea as my dessert, while my companion enjoyed her shaved iced sweet syrup.

A good dinner at this locally praised restaurant, but the experience demands more polish if I was to call it perfect.

Great place for E-sarn food!

The food is great - freshness, taste, portion size, price... everything checked! From somtam to grilled pork, every dishes are good, if not great.

Service is fast and attentive.

The place is huge, nice and cozy, with both indoor (air con.) and outdoor (under the trees) seatings. Lots of parking spots.

Fusion cuisine in a beautiful, lush setting.
The restaurant is surrounded by large shady trees and beautifully decorated with a koi fish pond. The food is reasonably priced and served quickly — no long wait times. The som tum with fermented fish sauce is rich and flavorful, and the mieng pla (herb-wrapped fish) is fresh and delicious.

Plenty of parking is available.

...we brought family and friends for dinner. The atmosphere was great. They had live music that evening. You felt like you were sitting in a jungle somewhere in Thailand. The wait staff was okay, except they didn't bring the drinks until we had to remind them. Otherwise service was very prompt and friendly. Quite a bit menu with lots of variety. The food was exceptional and delivered fairly quick as it wasn't too busy of an evening for them. We definitely would pay a return visit here with other family and friends. Worth the trip!

If you're looking for an unforgettable dining experience, the Thai Garden restaurant is a must-visit. Nestled in a lush, natural jungle setting, the ambiance is truly magical, with the sounds of nature blending perfectly with the aromatic smells of authentic Thai cuisine. The Isan food, in particular, stands out—bold, flavorful, and packed with fresh ingredients. From spicy papaya salads to mouthwatering grilled meats, every dish is a testament to the rich flavors of northeastern Thailand. Whether you're a fan of vibrant spices or crave a peaceful escape in nature, this place offers the perfect blend of both. Highly recommended!

This restaurant has great reviews and is highly recommended by locals. It’s located not far from Khon Kaen Airport, making it a perfect spot for a first meal after landing. There’s plenty of parking available, but if you visit during peak dining hours, you might have to wait for a table. The restaurant offers both outdoor seating and an air-conditioned area. The decor is beautiful, with lush greenery and a waterfall that creates a cool, relaxing atmosphere.

As for the food, the flavors are quite mild, making it suitable for people from Bangkok, but it didn’t fully match my taste. The best dish I tried was the grilled fish with herbs. The fish was large, juicy, and tender, served with a flavorful seafood dipping sauce. The most disappointing dish was the crispy catfish salad. While it looked generous, the dish was mostly made up of batter, with very little actual catfish. It felt like eating fried flour with dressing, which made it overly greasy and difficult to finish.

The prices are relatively high, but the portions are generous. The staff is attentive, but during busy hours, service might be a bit slow and inconsistent.

Just had the pleasure of visiting R.HAAN, a legendary Thai fine dining establishment that has held two Michelin stars for consecutive years, to try their newly launched Monsoon Samrub menu — an elegant, seasonal Thai tasting that perfectly balances tradition and innovation.

R.HAAN continues to uphold its reputation as one of Thailand’s top fine dining destinations, led by Chef Chumpol Jangprai, renowned for his refined interpretation of age-old recipes using top-quality local ingredients sourced from across the country.

Booking is simple — just email them and pay online in advance. This is my second time dining at R-HAAN, and it was just as memorable as the first.

I love their signature appetizers, each beautifully presented and full of flavor. The seasonal tasting menu is thoughtfully crafted, using the freshest ingredients to highlight the rich heritage of Thai royal cuisine. Every dish feels like a story, revealing layers of tradition and creativity.

It’s truly an eye-opening dining experience — refined, yet deeply rooted in Thai culture. Each course was delicious and left us excited for the next. If you’re looking to explore Thai cuisine at its finest, R-HAAN is absolutely worth it.

Michelin 2-star level service and food. My dining companion lives in Bangkok and suggested the place.

His assessment was that the menu represents an effective distillation and reinterpretation of the essential Thai flavors.

Someone looking for a modern gastronomical interpretation of the cuisine will enjoy this.  Someone looking for classic dishes will be very unhappy. 🤣 The classic and essential flavor is there, but it's all in updated and conceptual permutations.

I thought everything was delicious. My critique, if I take the liberty, is that the cocktail pairing didn't always seem coherent with the dish. But of course all of the flavors were delightful.

The Michelin two-star Thai restaurant had mixed reviews online, so I didn't have high expectations when I arrived.
The dishes were passable, but the most impressive dish was the low-temperature slow-cooked duck yolk. The royal-certified Tom Yum Goong soup was not as delicious as what I had in a small restaurant.

We just had an unforgettable dining experience at R-Haan, a 2-star Michelin restaurant. The staff was absolutely phenomenal—attentive, friendly, and incredibly professional. A special thank you to Pik, who kindly helped us take some fantastic photos to capture the moment. The hospitality perfectly matched the elegance and quality of the food. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a world-class Thai fine dining experience!

Wow, this michelin recommended Cantonese restaurant really delivered. The interior reminded me of simple but grand dining halls, perfect for large families or groups. They are known for their tender duck and meats so I ordered the duck stuffed with taro and the pork steak in pea gravy. Both were excellent balancing sweet, sticky and savory well. Both executed perfectly. 615 baht for two generous dishes, rice and iced coffee which I consider good value.

A colleague's recommendation 😁 popped in after a near by meeting. So many awards awarded 😀.

FOOD: Chinese cuisine, Rad-na and Pad si-ewe was particularly nice 😁. Good quality, portion size is ok. 8.5/10

SERVICE: old style, attentive but on the senior side so please have a little patience 😊. 8.5/10

FACILITY: lovely decorated, enough table not to be too crowded 😊, not sure of parking though. 8.5/10.

PRICE: reasonable... 8.5/10
Nice authentic Cantonese food, a bit om the sweet side. A bit pricey but value for money. Old skool Chinese restaurant environment.
You should definitely try it! Order something that you know it’s good for you….

Great Chinese restaurant with an old traditional store.  The dishes were all very good.  Many people ordered the iced tea, which was refreshing and unlimited.  It seems to taste better than their other branches.  A little hard to get to.  But it is popular and full of customers.

Cheap and delicious hole in the wall serving pad Thai and fried seafood dishes including the "otao" their store is named after, a delicious regional take on hoi tod infused with taro paste. They deep fry the fried orders one plate at a time, so be prepared for a wait if they are busy.

It’s in between 3-4 starts however my plate of O tao oyster was served not very hot and the oysters were cold. After adding the fresh beansprouts it was even colder, on top of that the big fans were blowing on the tables which made the food turn cold even quicker.
Taste was very good and texture was spot on however it lacks omph, presentation could have been better, i noticed there wasn’t any banana leave lining the plate and there’s no coriander topping. Banana leave can also keep the food warm longer. These could greatly affect the taste, smell and presentation to the dish.
The price is cheap at ฿80.

Otherworldly pad Thai.

Found this gem on the Michelin guide while looking for street food type stalls. It’s a little rustic local spot that has a small menu.

Communication is done through pointing at pictures to order but there is no need for anything else really!

The pad Thai was amazing, would recommend the seafood option. Prices were also ridiculously low - around 60THB for a pad Thai.

Epic!

Disappointment! I had their special fried oysters and it was literally one of the worst street foods I had in Thailand. Staff was nice, prices are fair but food is just bad. I'm not even sure what was in my plate. I only had one dish so maybe something else is better but I wouldn't try anything else.

reviewer: Garry Lew Your Estate Advisory Realtor
review_text:
Visited 12 June 2025 Clear Sky Thursday Evening. The following sharing are based on our unbiased personal opinion and experience

Order a takeaway to try. My humble review after trying it out. Oyster are slightly smaller in size and not fried to crispy. Yam 🍠 is generous almost like eating yam cake instead of fried oyster.

Diff flavor from where we came from. But not bad eat as if eating yum cake.

Follow us for a gastronomic experience and discover the world finest in its purest form

Food was overpriced. It wasn't bad as the ingredients used were good, but the way it was cooked tasted one dimensional and had nothing too special going on. The vegetables in the main course including the papaya salad was exceptionally bad. Expected much more from a Michelin star menu. The best thing we had was probably the tiger shrimp in the beginning.

As for the service, the people was very friendly but the wait time was incredibly long for the food to come, there was  approximately a 20 minute wait between each meals, especially from appetizer to main course was exceptionally long and we were starting to get full waiting for the main course.

All in all, The 5000 Baht spent was definitely not worth the experience. Would not recommend.

The beef is really nice but is just a bit sweet maybe can make it a bit spicy.
Cocktail also nice. The bread also taste good with their butter and is refillable. The lamb shank is a bit gamy maybe can use more spice to marinate it. Overall is really nice

Such an amazing restaurant and stuff. We have ordered pizza and pasta, both are delicious. Also, deserts we ordered chocolate lava cake, it was super delicious and well served.

Special thanks to Mr. Bank for his excellent service.

Memorable venue for special occasion.
We celebrate 40yrs-old birthday on the lawn overlooking the sunset with champagne & canapés. Simply stunning & intimate!
Then we move to restaurant for private dinner and fireworks. Food & service, all was excellent. Highly recommended!

I had such a pleasant dining experience here. Although the weather wasn’t great, unable to see the sunset due to the rain but it didn’t ruin my mood at all. The staff especially Kim was so thoughtful and kind. He kept checking on me to see if I need any recommendation and stuffs. Would definitely come back again!

Had a lovely dinner with my girls last week at this place. The food was amazing, real bold taste of Southern Thai. After seating, chef showed and explained the local ingredients used in each dishes that displayed in the restaurant. Some of the ingredients we barely know honestly, even though we are Thai 😆
The service was very welcome and warmth. Food taste was incredibly amazing. Bold Thai taste the southern style. Many menus are developed from the ancient recipe. There’re also wine selections that paired well with These bold Thai taste, we tried Thai wine from Khao Yai, it was perfectly paired with our menus. We had a great night. :)

An unforgettable dining experience.
Thai Library combines authentic southern Thai flavours with beautiful presentation and warm hospitality. Every dish is crafted with seasonal ingredients sourced from local communities, making each bite fresh and meaningful. The chef personally came to our table to share stories about the ingredients—such a lovely touch. Highly recommended for anyone seeking genuine Thai cuisine in an elegant, serene setting.

Incredibly disappointed, the fish cake was too salty, the rice was mushy (how do you get rice wrong at a Thai restaurant?), crab tasted off, and curry was bland (all I tasted was the fishy taste of old crab sitting in the fridge for too long). I had the set menu and I had to send half dish back, it was either tasteless or tasted funky. How can this restaurant be in a luxury hotel and recommended by Michelin blows my mind away.

Also, ambience..eh normal. For the high price point, you will get better food at a street stall, don't waste it here.

For the restaurant, recommend you retrain whole staff.
Michelin 2025! Everything is wonderful! From the service, to the great presentation and the dishes! We took lobsters set! Delicious!!!!

We just had one of the best meals of our lives! Everything was spot on! The food was incredibly delicious, perfectly cooked and seasoned. We chose one sea menu and one land menu and it all tasted amazing. The service is a new level of excellence, attentive to details and super friendly.
Super recommended to anyone traveling to Phuket that wants to have an unforgettable experience!!

Probably the best authentic Thai meal we've had during our first week in Thailand.
This restaurant is Michelin recognized since 2019-2025 in a row, and for a very good reason!!
The staff was super kind and very professional, and the food was served very quickly although the restaurant was quite full (even though it wasn't peak hour).

We came for a late lunch (around 4pm) so we didn't even have to wait for a table, which is great as they don't take reservations in advance at all. If you'd like to come eat here, I'd recommend avoiding peak hours, then you can walk in and be seated very quickly.

We were very hungry so we ordered quite a lot of dishes, and every singly one of them was absolute heaven.

From the salads section we ordered the pomelo salad, mango salad & papaya salad. All of them were refreshing & very spicy, but my favorite was the mango salad as it wasn't too spicy, yet full of flavor.

For mains we ordered the yellow curry with crab meat & noodles which was so delicate & creamy, yet spicy just at the right level. It's on the recommended section for a good reason.
We also tried the classic stir fried morning glory, which is always a dish the you can never go wrong with, as well as it balances the rest of the dishes that are usually quite spicy.
The highlight of our lunch was by far the fried grill pork with chilli, pepper & garlic - it was the perfect balance of sweet & spicy with shawarma-like pork slices, and it was so good that we kept thinking of ordering another one at the end, although we were so full.

From end to end the entire experience was 10/10, so if you're in the Phuket old town area, this is definitely a must-visit restaurant.

The food was amazing but not a place for kids.

The food is very good tasting but to the spicy side, there is nothing for kids to eat. You have to be creative,  we asked for steam rice and some cooked chicken with no spices at all.

We ordered a mango Smoothie and a passion fruit Smothie,  without sugar it really don't have a taste it is more og less water, the drinks are very poor, so I recommend to order fresh coconut for your meal.

The staff is super nice and service minded.

Came here for dinner, 3 of us spent about THB 1180 with bottled water. Food was really tasty, proper local Phuket style. Service was super fast, staff friendly, and the place has a nice old Chinese-Peranakan vibe. There’s a waiting area but better come before 6pm — saw a long line forming after that, especially on Sunday. Worth it if you want authentic local food

The pork belly and pineapple rice were amazing. We got the crispy crab egg which was not my favourite. I think it would be much better regular. Otherwise this mean was amazing. One of our favourite on the trip!

Another local restaurant with a lot of tourists serving delicious dishes. Located around Phuket Old Town, this is a good-value place to eat.

I find the curry flavors spectacular, clearly spicy with aromatics. The crab is not the best, could be sweeter for me. Overall if u r looking for a easy lunch with affordable price, come here !

Thank you and keep up the standard !

restaurant_name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
review_text:
I’m giving this place 4 stars because while the food is superb, it’s on the pricey side for a budget traveler like me. The Pad Thai was excellent, probably one of the best I’ve had in Bangkok. We ordered both shrimp and pork and really enjoyed them, but for the portion size I felt the price was a little steep.

A nice surprise was the big dining area upstairs, which I only discovered when I went to the toilet. The vibe was good, and the location is very convenient with a bus station nearby and Khaosan Road just a short walk away.

If you’re traveling on a budget, just know you’ll be paying more here compared to the usual street stalls. But if you don’t mind the extra cost, the Pad Thai is definitely worth trying at least once.

restaurant_name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
review_text:
Well this is ome of the Michelin Bib Gourmand places recommended in Bangkok and I am a fan of Pad Thai so I thought I should give it a try.
Visited during lunchtime it was pretty quiet with not many customers. Had a look at the menu and stared at it very long before deciding because I had hard time coming to terms with Pad Thai with no prawns! There was one with dish but seems like most of it are with pork, so I decided to be a bit experimental and give it a try and ordered the Iberico Smoked BBQ Pork.
Took quite some time before the dish was served. In the meantime, had to endure the cold air conditioning as well and the low light which almost kept hitting my forehead.
Two pages of beverages but only a few items available. Ended up ordering the longan juice and would say it's pretty good.
Soon the noodles came. A little disappointed by the portion size but still decided to give it a try. Have to say it exceeded my expectations didn't know the pork could be so well cooked and it's such a good combination with Pad Thai.
Food was good and satisfying, enjoyed everything except for the portion. For the taste there was nothing I could fault and now I won't see prawn as the mandatory ingredient to go along with Pad Thai anymore.
Definitely worth a visit to give it a try.

restaurant_name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
review_text:
Absolutely the best dish I had during my entire Thailand stay.

I still think of this Pad Thai to this day. There was just so much flavor and the spices mixed beautifully with the dish. It was like every bite was a perfect harmony.

I recommend this place to everyone in Bangkok, as I feel like this just tops all other dishes I had during my Thailand stay of 2 weeks.

For the price you also couldn't complain, it was definitely worth the price and next time in Thailand I'm ordering three plates, minimum.

restaurant_name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
review_text:
I will start off by saying, I understand why this got consecutive years of Michelin Stars. The pad Thai dishes served here are out of this world tasty and unique toppings. It’s definitely a twist from the classic Pad Thai dishes.
That said the price reflects this as well, though I would say that the environment of the restaurant doesn’t really reflect the high end prices you pay.  It feels like a regular run down building you go up to for dinner after a days work.
Regardless it is a great experience checking out Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu, we went twice just to try other dishes.

restaurant_name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
review_text:
If you want to try a more upscale version of Pad Thai, this place is worth a visit.
In my opinion, the tastiest one is the version with pork belly—highly recommended!
The other dishes are also good, but make sure to try their signature menu.

That being said… it’s honestly very expensive 🤣 like really expensive.

Oh, and my mom uses a wheelchair, and she was still able to enter.
We just had to lift the wheelchair a little to get inside.

A wonderful spot for Northern and Eastern Thai food. The menu is extensive with so many tempting options. The taste is bold and spicy but still well-balanced and full of flavour.
-ส้มตำ​(Papaya Salad with salted egg)
-ลาบทอด (Fried​ Spicy Pork Ball with chilli dipping sauce) : My expectation on this dish might be high. I like when it crispy outside and soft center.
This one's an overly hard, indicating it may be overcooked or they make it thinner than what I expected.
-ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว​(Rice vermicelli with Northern Thai Sauce) :
-ต้มแซ่บเห็ดรวม​(Spicy Mushroom clear soup) : Like it a lot! Thai Spicy!
-น้ำพริกอ่องพร้อมชุดผัก (Spicy Northern Thai Pork and Tomato with side salad) : Expecting it to be a bit more sweeter and balance of savoury, sweet, sour and herbal favours.
-หมูคลุกงาทอด (Fried​Pork coated with sesame) : Easy to eat and tender texture.
-ข้าวหนุกทอด​ ( Perilla Rice Stick with syrup) : Soft sticky rice tossed with crunchy Perilla seed. The 1st time I have tried this menu. I thought it might be very chewy, surprisingly it was crispy outside and inside is perfect texture.

Lots of seating both indoor with air-conditioning and out door. Good —  for dining with friends and family.

Not really a fan of the Northern dishes here, except for the Northern sausage which was quite good. The Isan and Central Thai dishes were much tastier in my opinion.

Service was great and there’s plenty of parking. The atmosphere is warm and cozy, especially nice for families.

Prices are on the higher side though, with portions feeling a bit small compared to what you pay.

This Esan restaurant (Northeast Thai cuisine) is one of the best ones i hv ever eaten!!!

The atmosphere is very chilling and relax but price is totally affordable not expensive!! You can choose to dine in indoor with air-con or outdoor to experience the local vibe!

We ate Kor moo yang (pork neck), which u can request for less sweet! The sour sausage and somtum (Papaya Salad) were soooooo good, as well as kanom jeen!!! Don't forget to order khao niao (sticky rice) which is super hot and fresh ahahahaha

Overall experience was excellent, the only concern might be location, it's a bit far away from main tourist areas but it's convenient to ride GRAB to reach there!!

Northern Thai food. Recommend their roast fish, big in size, tender in texture. laap raw beef is fresh with interesting taste as well, worth a try. There is also a little cafe selling snacks and northern sausage and chilli.

Huen Lamphun is one of the Northern Thai foods in Nonthaburi. This restaurant have 3 zones provide you, either Northern Thai style zone or Air Conditioner zone.

Remark:
Here do not get credit card.

This is my favorite Northeastern Thai foods restaurant. I have enjoyed the foods here since my childhood and it's always my go-to. The place remains pretty much the same from the old days--the flavors, the food quality, and the retro rundown vibes. You should try their "Gaeng Orm" which is very unique. I hope youblove this place too.
Great local Thai restaurant. Great selection of northeastern Thai cuisine. A bit spicy. Great quality and inexpensive. Curbside parking and a bit difficult to find.

If you're looking for a cozy spot offering authentic, home-style Thai cuisine, look no further than Laeb Som Pith. This hidden gem might not cater to English-only speakers, but don't let that deter you – a little Google Translate will unlock a world of delicious discoveries.

The Grilled Pork Collar and Spicy Pork Collar Salad are absolute must-tries! The pork is cooked to juicy perfection, infused with smoky char and balanced by the fresh, piquant flavour of the salad.

This bistro is stated in town of Korat.
There's no official parking area, but you can park in front of the bistro if available.
The taste of Somtum is delicious.
fried-beef is too chewy.
grilled-beef tongue is good.
Lab is good.
The price is fair with the food quality and quantity.
Order any of their grilled meat dishes and you’d enjoy the perfectly char grilled meat with flavorful dipping sauce, paired with their soft sticky rice - mouth-watering perfection!

I had a wonderful lunch experience at Indus restaurant in Sukhumvit area! The food was absolutely delicious — full of authentic flavors and perfectly cooked.

Special thanks to Mr. Ram, who took excellent care of us throughout the meal. He was very attentive, friendly, and gave great recommendations on what to try. His service made the experience even more enjoyable.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for amazing Indian cuisine and warm hospitality!

Don't skip this place!!!!
Great service, AMAZING food, super beautiful plating. We were 2 ppl ordered 2 naans, 3 mains, 1 starter and 2 drinks and the price was great too. Will definitely come back next time I'm in Bangkok.

I recently celebrated my birthday at Indus. It was a great experience. The staff was extremely attentive, caring and kind. They treated us with utmost love, warmth and compassion. The food was good and the environment was cozy. It’s definitely an upscale place. Absolutely love and recommend this restaurant.

Just celebrated a birthday dinner here. They serve amazing and delicious food. Cheese nan is a must and their home-made chicken curry goes well with nan. Raan is also soft and tender.

Staffs are great at their services, friendly, thoughtful, and attentive. We have a great time here and definitely are coming back 🙏🏻

Terrific Indian Restaurant with 8 years of Michelin Guide to back it up. Good atmosphere and service.

We came for Sunday Brunch Buffet that only available on the weekend 11 am to 3 pm.

You can still order A la carte menu but for small group buffet is the way to go. Although you will get a limited menu but you can try many dishes as the serving is adjust according to the number of people on the table.

The food was good. The seasoning was not too heavy (not too salty) and most of them are cooked to order except for appertizer such as Pani Puri and Biryani.

The buffet dose not included water but it included indian herbal drink and dessert. Their Ice Cream is really good. At the end of the meal we ordered Ayurvedic herbal tea to help with the digestion as Indian food tend to be on the heavy side.

Great choice to introduce someone to the Indian cuisine and Long time fan alike.

I had the pleasure of dining at 80/20 in Bangkok, a Michelin-starred restaurant that offers a modern take on Thai cuisine, and it was an incredible experience. The dishes were beautifully minimalist and truly reflected Thailand in a modernized way. I absolutely loved the ambiance; it was sleek, contemporary, and very inviting. The staff were exceptionally attentive and knowledgeable, providing detailed explanations about each dish. The wine menu was also impressive, and the selections were fantastic. Overall, it was a remarkable culinary journey and a perfect blend of modernity and Thai tradition.

# Review of 80/20: A Culinary Journey in Bangkok

## Introduction

Located in the vibrant neighborhood of Charoenkrung, 80/20 is a fine dining restaurant that has garnered attention for its innovative approach to Thai cuisine. Under the helm of Chef Napol Jantragul, the restaurant aims to showcase the rich flavors and diverse ingredients of Thailand, with a focus on sustainability and local sourcing. While the culinary experience is commendable, there are areas where the service falls short, particularly for those dining at a Michelin-level establishment.

## Ambiance

Upon entering 80/20, guests are welcomed into a modern yet inviting space that reflects the restaurant’s commitment to blending tradition with contemporary design. The interior features clean lines, warm lighting, and artistic decor that creates a relaxed yet sophisticated atmosphere. The open kitchen adds an extra layer of excitement, allowing diners to witness the culinary magic happening behind the scenes.

The layout promotes intimacy, with well-spaced tables that allow for private conversations without feeling isolated. Overall, the ambiance sets the stage for an enjoyable dining experience.

## Menu Offerings

The menu at 80/20 is a testament to the chef’s creativity and passion for Thai flavors. With a focus on seasonal ingredients, the offerings change regularly, ensuring that each visit feels fresh and exciting. The tasting menu is particularly noteworthy, showcasing a range of dishes that highlight the best of Thai cuisine.

### Signature Dishes

One standout dish is the **Grilled River Prawn**, where the natural sweetness of the prawns is beautifully complemented by a fragrant herb sauce. This dish exemplifies the restaurant’s philosophy of highlighting the quality of ingredients while enhancing them with thoughtful preparation.

Another must-try is the **Fermented Rice with Mango**, which offers a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors. The use of fermented elements adds depth, showcasing the chef’s ability to incorporate traditional techniques into modern presentations.

### Desserts

The dessert selection is equally impressive, with offerings like **Coconut Sorbet with Lychee** that are both refreshing and indulgent. Each dessert is meticulously crafted, providing a perfect conclusion to an exceptional meal.

## Service

While the culinary experience at 80/20 is commendable, the service needs improvement to truly uphold Michelin standards. Upon arrival, the staff was friendly and welcoming, but as the evening progressed, there were noticeable lapses in attentiveness. For a fine dining establishment, timely service is crucial, yet there were instances where we waited too long for drink refills and course transitions.

The staff’s knowledge of the menu was inconsistent; while some members were well-informed and able to provide detailed descriptions of the dishes, others seemed unsure and unable to answer basic questions. This inconsistency detracted from the overall experience, especially in a setting that aims for high culinary acclaim.

## Conclusion

In summary, 80/20 is a fine dining restaurant that offers an innovative take on Thai cuisine, with a menu that celebrates local ingredients and traditional flavors. The ambiance is inviting, and the culinary creations are impressive and well-executed. However, to truly align with Michelin standards, the service needs to be more attentive and consistent. With improvements in this area, 80/20 has the potential to solidify its reputation as one of Bangkok's top dining destinations. For now, it remains a worthwhile visit for food enthusiasts eager to explore the best of Thai cuisine, albeit with some room for growth in service quality.

Exceptional Dining Experience – A Must-Visit!

Dining at 80/20 was an absolute delight! The attention to detail in every dish was incredible—each bite was a burst of creativity and flavor. The signature tasting menu was the perfect choice, taking us on a beautifully curated journey through Southeast Asia, with each course inspired by a different region and thoughtfully explained by the staff.

Speaking of which, the team was warm, courteous, and the service was flawless from start to finish. Honestly, the food was to die for—a true culinary experience that blends storytelling, artistry, and flavor. Can’t recommend it enough for anyone looking to indulge in something truly special!

This used to be my favourite restaurant on earth(reviews on burpple), but I'm back after 1.5years and unfortunately, the change in chef did no wonders for the restaurant. Some things stayed, including their strong flavours and unabashed heat, but literally no dish impressed, unlike the previous time I visited and half the menu made me stop and go wow.

Their prices have increased too, it's still a good restaurant but no surprises, so I'm not going to review every dish like I did before

The worst part of it is that when I last visited, there were certain parts of the menu that weren't good. Since half the menu remained, I had hoped that they would at least correct the mistakes before, but nope all the mistakes stayed.

Enjoyed an exquisite 16 course Thai fusion fine dining with wine pairing @8020bkk. Most of the dishes hit the point though not all the wine to my liking. Overall a memorable experience and it’s always the company that matters! #bangkok #thailand #foodporn #finedining #celebration

As a newcomer to Thai cuisine, this was a wonderful introduction. Translating to “heaven” in Thai, this restaurant did an amazing job of showcasing every major cooking methods used in Thai cuisine while highlighting the quintessential Thai ingredients and dishes. While it wasn’t mind blowing when it comes to taste or creativity, I think the blend of value ($100 USD per person), storytelling, and showcasing of the bright and floral flavors of Thai cuisine made it a 5 star experience. They also give you many extra courses in between that are not listed in the set menu which was a big plus.

Great experience for a special occasion! The food was so delicious. Even dishes with ingredients i usually don't like, were so good! The service was outstanding - we learned a lot regarding dishes from the different provinces of Thailand. Highly recommend!

Excellent! Definitely a 10/10 recommendation.

We (family of 4) had an incredible experience at Saawaan. The food was very good, every dish was tasty by it self - however most special was that the each of the dishes perfectly integrated into the menu, leading to a very complete experience. The portion size was very good, we left the place fully satisfied.

The service was outstanding, every dish was explained - but not too long.

We will be back!

We tried the tasting menu and found it promising. The chef clearly has great potential, especially when embracing Thai flavors—those dishes were the most memorable by far. In contrast, the more Western-style courses felt less distinctive.

Even as a French person, I believe relying on imported French meats and seafood feels a bit outdated, especially when the culinary world is shifting toward locally sourced, sustainable ingredients. Fresh, local products not only align with modern values but truly elevate the flavor.

Special mention to the pastry chef—the dessert course was a standout, with a beautiful balance of flavors and textures. It ended the meal on a wonderfully high note.

Dining at Saawaan, and it was nothing short of exceptional! From the moment I stepped into the restaurant, I knew I was in for a special experience. Located in a charming and tranquil corner of Bangkok, Saawaan’s ambiance strikes a perfect balance between modern sophistication and traditional Thai elements.

### Atmosphere:
The ambiance at Saawaan is an absolute standout. The elegant decor, soft lighting, and comfortable seating create a serene and welcoming atmosphere. The restaurant is relatively intimate, which allows for a relaxed, fine dining experience. The staff were incredibly warm and attentive, ensuring that every guest felt valued and well cared for.

### Service:
The service was impeccable. From the very beginning, the staff was knowledgeable, friendly, and eager to provide recommendations. They took the time to explain each dish in detail, which really enhanced the overall dining experience. Our server was also highly skilled at suggesting the perfect wine pairings for each course, showing a deep understanding of the menu and ingredients.

### The Food:
Now, the food. **Saawaan** offers a modern twist on traditional Thai flavors, and every dish was a masterpiece. Each course was a perfect combination of balance, flavor, and creativity. The tasting menu I opted for showcased the best of what Thai cuisine has to offer, with intricate and bold flavors presented in the most beautiful, artful way.

The **som tam** (green papaya salad) was an explosion of flavors, with the perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and sour. The **tom yum** soup, which I had as part of the set menu, was bursting with fresh herbs and rich broth – undoubtedly one of the best versions I’ve had in a fine dining setting. For the main course, the **pan-seared foie gras with tamarind and Thai herbs** was a standout, beautifully blending French technique with Thai ingredients in a way that felt innovative and utterly delicious.

Each dish was a testament to the skill and creativity of the chefs, offering a perfect blend of traditional flavors and modern presentation. The desserts were equally impressive, with flavors that lingered on your palate long after the meal ended.

### Drinks:
The drink pairings were also exceptional, with a wide range of options that complemented the complexity of the dishes. The sommelier’s recommendations were spot on, and they had a variety of cocktails and mocktails, including some unique Thai-inspired options, which were refreshing and delightful.

### Conclusion:
In summary, Saawaan is a must-visit destination for anyone who appreciates fine dining and wants to experience Thai cuisine at its finest. The combination of incredible food, excellent service, and a beautiful atmosphere makes this restaurant a standout in Bangkok's already vibrant culinary scene. It’s perfect for special occasions, romantic dinners, or anyone looking to indulge in an unforgettable meal.

I can’t wait to return and experience the menu again! Highly recommend!

Love the place! We literally ordered every food on the menu! Some dishes could taste alright but most of them are super delicious. Highly recommend to come with a group of friends so you can enjoy as many dishes as you can. We also ordered dessert which made from the real sako tree and they have homemade cola. Definitely going back there again! Highly recommend for those who wish to escape the normal northern local food!

I came here alone, so I just ordered two dishes. Personally, I liked the food. I enjoy a variety of flavors, and everything had a nice mix of sweet, salty, and bold tastes. The pomelo dish reminded me of yum from Isan food, a bit sweet and salty with that kick of kapi flavor, which I really liked. I also ordered a 600g fish. Yes, you can squeeze some lime over it and dip it in seafood sauce, then eat it with rice. So good.The only downside is the price. It’s not exactly budget friendly, but I can understand. *** I recommend booking before you go to save time and avoid long queues. They do accept walk-ins, but you might have to wait a while.

Amazing seafood!
Fresh grilled fish, tasty salads (especially loved the pomelo salad), a good crab omelet, and a 900g fish that was the star of the meal – fresh, delicate, and full of flavor.
A bit pricey (1,900 baht for everything), but worth it for a special treat. Don’t miss the lemon-honey soda – super refreshing! 🥳🥰
Realllyyy great atmosphere. Most of the people who ate here were koreans. I think it’s famous for koreans but nevertheless their fish and stir fried vegetables was good!

The dish has a good flavor and is not overly spicy. This may not the authentic flavor, possibly because it has been altered to appeal to people from other countries.  The components that are utilized are of high quality and freshness.  The shop has a nice appearance, however it can be a little on the tiny side.
