All 3 dishes I ordered were excellent. Crispy omelette can be shared portion big enough for 3-4 pax. The beef was excellent! Price is reasonable too but maybe more for tourists than locals.

What a great little place. It doesn’t look like 5 star restaurant (don’t be put off by the back street look and very glittery sign) but it definitely delivers. Recommended by Michelin year by year and it truly deserves it.
Pad Thai was best I had in Bangkok and crispy omelette delivered both on taste and texture. Prices are good and portions huge.
Service was friendly, decor very nice.

very kind and attentive staff. wagyu steak was amazing but very tiny portion would order two next time.

they didn’t have red or green curry for the day but we had delicious tom yum soup.

also got crispy omelette, pretty good

stir fried flat noodles were our least favorite.

Great small authentic Thai food restaurant with car parking available outside. The soup was on the spicy side while papaya salad was less spicy than usual. Overall a great experience and not too expensive. Expect to pay about 500 baht per person for diner without drinks. Advise making reservations ahead of time as they are always busy.

A legendary Thai-Chinese shaved ice dessert spot that effortlessly blends nostalgia, flavor, and value. Priced at just 35 THB per bowl, this humble dessert shop has earned its Michelin Bib Gourmand status year after year—and rightfully so.

The menu offers a generous variety of traditional toppings: from candied taro, ginkgo nuts, red beans, corn, toddy palm seeds, to chewy grass jelly and jackfruit—all submerged beneath finely shaved ice and lightly sweetened syrup. Each bowl is customizable and made to order, allowing you to curate your own perfect mix of textures and flavors.

Though the interior is modest and classically styled, the seating is clean and organized. Walls are adorned with Chinese ancestral prints, traditional décor, and an impressive row of Michelin plaques spanning several years—further affirming the shop’s reputation and consistency.

The shop operates only a few hours each afternoon, so timing your visit is crucial. Arrive early to avoid missing out, especially on weekends.

In short: a Bangkok institution. Affordable, authentic, and utterly satisfying—highly recommended for locals and visitors alike.

After I roamed around and so sweaty, having the dessert here was refreshing and fuel.  I like the noodle one - kinda al dente texture which was so good to me.  One of a must-try place in this area.  We dine in and the place was clean, impressive!

This Michelin-starred Thai shaved ice dessert, honored for six consecutive years from 2019 to 2025, is a true masterpiece of flavors and textures—all for just 35 baht.

Tender red beans and soft coconut meat pair seamlessly with chewy noodles and silky glass jelly, while sweet bursts of corn and fragrant jackfruit complement the satisfying crunch of fresh water chestnuts.

Served over fluffy shaved ice, it’s a refreshing and perfectly balanced dessert that proves simple ingredients can create unforgettable magic.

Never knew such a simple dessert would appear in the Michelin Bib Gourmand list. It might be one of the cheapest dishes to be in that list.
What's more surprising is that a Chinese dessert could actually be in that list! Decided to try and see what is so good about it, and there was already quite a long wait at the stall.
As a foreigner it is not easy to take an order because everything is in Thai, and I was standing there waiting for help while some people already cut me in the queue and placed order. It's not easy ordering because you have to write the order yourself on a piece of paper and pass it to one of the aunties there.
Finally one of the aunties came to my rescue and I had to point at what I wanted. She showed me the ingredient list and I told her which one I didn't one and she started preparing it for me.
What's so special was that there was this item inside which looks like the thin noodles, I think its probably noodles but I kept denying the fact because I have the impression noodles won't taste nice in desserts.
In fact, I really enjoyed it and I almost wanted to order more! It just ticks all the boxes: simple, cheap, good, enjoyable.
Definitely one of the best desserts eaten so far in Bangkok.

One of the best of Chinese sweet dessert in Bangkok
Many choices for choose in a bowl, if you can’t, they put them all!!!
Only one price is 30฿ so cheap!!
A long queue in front of the shop, please wait.
Sweet noodle is the highlight of this shop
Recommend for try
Good taste!

Super flavourful dishes at very reasonable prices. This was one of our favourite meals in Phuket. Do go early though! When we reach at 6.45pm, they had run out of crab meat and squid. Best morning glory and fried rice we have ever tasted. Full of woh hey! Friendly boss and staff. Please visit if you are in Phuket and near Phuket town! You won’t regret it!

The true local experience and well-deserved Michelin guide restaurant. We went there for 2 days in a row to try most popular items on a menu: crab dishes and menu. The taste is amazing, the portions are generous, service is fast. The special satisfaction comes from seeing how the chef does his art in an open kitchen - truly dedicated and focused. The personnel also talks in English and very helpful at explaining the dishes. Very much recommended and must-go in Phuket. Wishing the restaurant a Michelin star :)

World class crab curry, seafood with garlic which is to die for and crab fried rice that will make you dream off after you leave the restaurant. Undispute flavor and even better customer service. A must visit if you around phuket town. Price is unbeatable and absolute value for money

P/s: pls come early. I am here at 10.30 when they just open and didn't need to wait. After before we leave, the restaurant is packed with customers.

I ordered the crab fried rice and stir fried crispy pork with basil - both tasted really good. The size was quite generous and the seasoning was just right. I think it was the perfect choice for a meal for two people.
We came early at 5 pm, so the place was not busy yet and the food came super quickly.
Our meal costs ~340 baht in total, which I think is pretty reasonable. However, they accept only cash, so be sure to prepare some cash in advance.
Unbelievably good food, chef has great technique, fresh and tasty. People are nice and friendly too. Environment is correct, no air con but can truly taste the boutique Thai restaurant.
This restaurant has moved from previous site to  Eight Thonglor. Using fresh and premium ingredients. Skilled food-preparation. Good taste. Pricey though.

Spent Christmas Eve at Tempura Kanda, and it was absolutely perfect! The tempura was incredibly fresh, light, and crispy—every bite was a true delight. The chefs were amazing—authentic Japanese food experts, highly professional, and genuinely friendly. The restaurant was spotless, and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. Every little detail was thoughtfully crafted to make the meal unforgettable. If you’re looking for authentic tempura, this is the place to go!

Small, Cozy Japanese omagase restaurant, only 15 seats available during dinner service. By the way the restaurant usually not so busy and you can normally walk-in to get the seat. Don’t expect this kind of restaurant to be cheap this is one of the most expensive Japanese restaurants you can find in Bangkok, with a large variety of fishes and their freshness, made to order for each sushi you won’t be disappointed. Each sushi will be served with the best possible method to bring out the flavor specifically for each kind of fishes, they may looks similar to anywhere else you had tried on the pictures but not on their flavor. The only downside is you are not always be served by the head chef, which mean it is not always consistently best and sometimes the dish isn’t properly prepared, but it is still very good. Lastly, I highly recommend this restaurant if you want to try out one of the best.

The atmosphere is good, staffs are very warm welcome. All chefs are really nice and friendly. They created all dishes with their passionate and tender. All foods are fresh and tasty. Price is a bit expensive but worth it.You have to try this restaurant if you love authentic Japanese food.

2nd here for lunch during my hols in BKK as it's one of the sushi restaurants that are open for lunch.  Felt that the sushi was normal. Especially in BKK where fine dining is pretty affordable or worth the top dollar, this was top dollar sushi @ $3,800 baht for the special sushi set which I felt was not very worth it in my opinion. See pics attached for  11 pieces sushi + miso soup + dessert.

Overall, very good place for seafood in Bangkok. Prices are a little expensive when you get live crabs or prawns, but understandable due to the location. The service is amazing and the place is huge, so it’s fairly easy to find a table even in rush hour. Only thing we didn’t like was how loud a lot of tables were. Very noisy place so not the best to enjoy your seafood calmly, which is what we wanted. But great taste and great product!

Great dinner @ Somboon Seafood 🦀🍤 We feasted on their signature dishes. Seafood Tom Yum, Steamed Fish, Thai-Style Curry Crab, and Poached Prawns all bursting with authentic Chinese Thai flavors. Fuss free Chinese restaurant. Good for family and friends.

The fried curry crab meat was really delicious, rich in flavor and perfectly cooked. The glass noodles with fresh prawns were also excellent, full of freshness.
A great place if you’re looking for tasty seafood in Bangrak.

This restaurant outlet is Michelin selected and was the first lunch of our trip as it was very close to our hotel. I had my favourite yellow curry stir fried crab again and the rendition here was superb, possibly the best I had in Thailand so far and it goes so well with rice that I probably mopped up more sauce, gravy and rice than I should have. There were many tourists from China and Korea at this rather busy restaurant branch.

The scallops with asparagus were okay but both the curry crab and salt and pepper prawns were very delicious. The fried fish was quite tasty as well but I can’t remember the exact flavour we ordered. On hindsight, we should have ordered the crab meat version of the curry so I did not have to peel the crab and I’m sure it would be just as good. This was a very enjoyable meal and I will on the search to see if there are better versions of yellow curry crab elsewhere.

Crab meat with curry - over rated, and a bit oily, the taste is not strong either. We paid 720TB for small size but the crab meat is not as much as expected.
Trotter - soft and juicy except that the skin (end) is not well cleaned
Crab meat fried rice - must try
An overrated Michelin restaurant

Famous spot that’s been in the Michelin Guide for three years in a row! The food is delicious and the portions are generous. They open until late, which is super convenient. Highly recommend trying the fried chicken — it’s crispy, juicy, and so good!

❣️😋🍗

Food was good though they’ve been decreasing the portions over the past year. But DO NOT expect any hospitality or any kind of good service here. Just eat the food and get out. We ordered a couple of dish on second batch, with expectations of some extra time to prepare. The first dish came after 20mins. However, we had to follow up with the waitress several times for the second dish. We finally got attention on the third follow up because, ofc, the first two times they just repeated the pattern “the second batch will take some time” without even bothering to know which dish are we talking about. Finally, the dish came after we had finished everything and was denied the cancellation due to “the food is already made” policy. The lady who is older than my grandma called me P btw which is so funny.

Some of the best Thai food I've had in Thailand at an amazing price. We are like kings for about $14 per person. It is a lively and local environment with a very attentive wait staff... It felt like you were eating at your auntie's house.

Great outdoor traditional Thai restaurant that is extremely reasonably priced… $15 US for a lot of food! Food was pretty good, the calamari and tempura crab were the best I’ve ever eaten. Service was excellent. Atmosphere, well it’s an outdoor restaurant with metal tables and plastic chairs. It’s Michelin approved/rated.

Absolutely the best chicken I’ve ever had! The texture was tender, the skin perfectly crispy, and the flavor was unbelievably rich and balanced. Their stir-fried vegetables with crispy pork were also outstanding, with a perfect balance of freshness and umami. The ambiance and the two consecutive Michelin recommendations (2023 and 2024) are well-deserved. Highly recommend for anyone who appreciates high-quality Thai cuisine!

The soup and noodles are very delicious!! The bowl size is quite large and fun. Very much value for money ❤️

I am not giving a very high rating is because all of the meat is processed meat. Meat balls, fish balls, stuffed tofu are all processed, nonetheless, delicious!! I especially loved the crispy fried pork bits.

Logan juice is the best which I’ve had in Chiang Mai. Not too sweet

If you are a noodle lover, Thana Ocha Noodle is absolutely a place worth visiting! Guaranteed with many years of Michelin guide.

What stands out right away is the taste and quality of the food. The noodles are cooked well and many kinds for selection. The broth is rich and flavorful. Every bowl feels balanced, whether you go for the tomyum noodle soup, or yen-ta-four or the dry version. Their toppings are always fresh – many kinds of fish balls make a combination of tender, soft, crunchy, and perfectly seasonal that bring everything together, sour, sweet, salty, and spicy.

Portion sizes are generous, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality you get. It feels like great value for money, especially compared to many other noodle shops. You leave full and satisfied, without feeling heavy.

The staff are friendly, polite, and smile.

The atmosphere is an old noodle shop but quite clean, casual, and comfortable. It’s the kind of place that works well for a quick weekday lunch meal.

Overall, Thana Ocha Noodle combines great taste, affordable prices, and nice service. It’s one of those places you want to come back to regularly because you know the quality will always be there. Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy authentic and delicious noodles in an old style.

Thana Ocha

29 Ratchawong Road, Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai, Chiang Mai, 50300, Thailand

Every day at lunch long lines form in front of this decades-old shop selling Hakka-style noodles. House-made Hakka stuffed tofu, fish sausage and crispy wontons find their way into every dish.

I went there earlier than usual just before the line queuing starts. I ordered Shrimp WonTon Yong Tau Foo Soup with egg noodles. The serving is generous and there are lots of toppings! I can say that their homemade fishballs is way better than the Michelin Bib Gourmand rated fish ball in Bangkok.

The shop is open from 8AM to 5PM everyday. I recommend to visit between 9AM to 11AM just to skip the line.

PS. They are Michelin rated since 2020–and now that’s consistency.

A Consistent Gem! Why This is the Best Thai Noodle Place

**Review:**
If you're looking for authentic, delicious, and consistently great Thai noodles, look no further than Thana Ocha. As a regular customer who has been here more times than I can count, I can confidently say they never disappoint.

The menu may seem simple, but the depth of flavor in every bowl is incredible. Whether you're getting a rich and savory boat noodle, a spicy and sour Tom Yum noodle soup, or a comforting Pad Thai, everything is executed perfectly. The meats are always tender, the noodles have the ideal texture, and the broths are simmered to perfection.

What keeps me coming back is the consistency. Every visit is as good as the last. The service is always quick and friendly, and the place is clean. This isn't just a restaurant I like; it's a place I genuinely crave. Do yourself a favor and become a regular here too!

Very busy Michelin guide listed noodle restaurant. The food is excellent, especially the Yong Tau Foo noodles, love the sauce, sweet, slippery and tangy and the stuffed wantons are nicely balanced in fishy savory flavour. The pork and rice is very good too. My only little comment is I've always had very dismissive service, not a smile, it just seems you are an inconvenience. That being said, the food is great, as is the value for money.

We arrived around 6pm, the 1st floor was full. We ordered with help from the waitress on the 2nd floor. My daughter ordered Beef fat fried rice. She told me beef tasted bitter. I tried. It did. And I asked one of waitresses whether this is normal to be bitter or not.she said yes. Roasted beef tasted a little bit bitter as well. The only almost finished dish is the cabbage. As a Michelin Restaurant, the food is really disappointing. Even the rice itself tastes not good, sticky and didn’t feel like being fried. The atmosphere is awesome though, tiny but cozy.

Arrived before 6PM, soon after, there were people waiting outside. There is really no room for that as the restaurant is so close to a rather busy street.

As for the food, we tried two signature dishes: the beef steak was average as the meat was dry and chewy. Beef leg was tender and flavorful, tasted very similar to pig leg, though. Beef liver was good, but a few pieces were chewy as well, and finally, tea leaf salad was quite good, especially for balancing out all the protein.

Would like to come back and try the rice noodle soup. Looks better than beef steak.

Just a side note: there are two main groups of tourists in Thailand in recent years. At the day we went, almost all tables were Chinese, no Korean, for whatever reason. Maybe a table or two locals, but left before our dishes showed up.

I ordered beef soup, fried rice and fried cabbage as well. The only good taste comes from the cabbage... the beef in the soup was good, but the taste is too sour, you can't taste natural beef flavor. Basically, using overnight rice for making fried rice is common, but not here. That is why the fried rice tastes sticky and wet, btw the beef steak is well done also... I don't understand why this restaurant can be one of the Michelin guides, it is unbelievable.
Delicious Thai Beef Michelin star restaurant in Chiang Mai.
When you order liver at a restaurant, it can be a gamble — but here, it was pure jackpot 🎰. The best liver I’ve ever had: tender, rich in flavor, and perfectly balanced in aroma.

It is a nice hotel in Chiangmai and it is far away from the downtown about 30 kilometers. It spends about 20-30 minutes from driving. This place is good for people who driving by themselves. The place is quiet and clean. You can see the Mountain View from the room balcony. The food in the restaurant is also delicious.

Great hotel to relax if you drive, overall there is nothing around but a single cafe. Rooms are large and cozy, bed is comfy.

Restaurant is very expensive for the area, but nothing extraordinary.

The view is the astonishing of course, it was the main reason for me to come here.

I stayed in the Chantra Kiri Suite! big, quiet, and super cozy. The bed was comfy and I could see the mountains right from the room.

The bathroom looked amazing and had a big bathtub. Only thing: the water pressure was a bit low (just something to know).

There’s a cute dog walking around the hotel like a little host. If you love dogs, you’ll love it here.

Breakfast was a buffet, clean and tasty. They had Thai and Western food like rice soup, eggs, bacon, juice, and fresh coffee. The view from the dining area was really nice.

The hotel is also in the Michelin Guide, which means it’s known for great service and quality. The staff were kind and helpful the whole time.

If you want a peaceful and stylish place to relax in Chiang Mai, this is a great choice.

This is a genuinely fantastic hotel. The view alone is the most amazing thing and well worth the trip. Couple that with the incredible service, immaculate quality of the room and I can honestly say that this is level of comfort is unmatched.

With that said, I must mention a something that I have not seen mentioned in the reviews. The road that leads to the entrance of the hotel is steep. Incredibly steep. So steep that I can only imagine the construction of the hotel could only be achieved either via rotary aircraft or divine intervention. If you have a car that is low to the ground, do not attempt the drive up, if your car has a weak engine, do not attempt, if you drive a car with manual transmission, may God help you.

Beautiful place with a unique atmosphere!
The restaurant is Michelin-starred, offering an exceptional dining experience.
The hotel also features a fascinating collection of historical artifacts and antiques related to Thailand and Chiang Mai, adding rich cultural value.
While the property is set on hilly terrain, it's not actually difficult to get around — they provide a golf cart service for guests who prefer not to walk.
